diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_product_page.mjs b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_product_page.mjs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..90b67d2670
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_product_page.mjs
@@ -0,0 +1,497 @@
+// R10-PRODUCT-PAGE-REDESIGN (#201): the design note's acceptance list for
+// docs/index.html, the part that needs the two trees or a browser (checks 4-11
+// of design/R10-PRODUCT-PAGE-REDESIGN, section 10; checks 1-3 are
+// tests/doc_claims.py and tools/site/day_chart.mjs themselves).
+//
+//    node dev/audit/harnesses/r10_product_page.mjs [--base <ref>]
+//
+// playwright is resolved from NODE_PATH and Chromium from
+// PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, as tests/card_browser.mjs does. The working tree's
+// docs/ is served from a loopback port (so the page's own fonts and images load
+// and every request is seen); the base page is read with `git show <ref>` and
+// served from memory beside it. <ref> defaults to the merge base with
+// origin/main.
+//
+// One line per check: `ok` or `FAIL`, then what was measured. Exit 1 on any
+// FAIL. EXPECTED at a head that meets the note: RESULT fails=0
+//
+// What it does not establish: one engine (Chromium); no screen reader; touch is
+// not exercised. An engine without :has(), and one without scroll-driven
+// animation, is not run: each is SIMULATED in Chromium through the style sheet's
+// object model, by doing to the parsed rules what such an engine does to them
+// (`withoutFeature`). The styles-off check removes every style element and
+// style attribute; the user agent's own sheet stays.
+//
+// Design choices the checks encode. The 40 px floor is read on every displayed
+// link, button, summary, tab stop and radio pill, both dimensions, EXCEPT a link
+// in a line of text (computed display inline, with a text node beside it in its
+// parent): that link takes its line's height, which is WCAG 2.5.8's inline
+// exception, and the check prints how many it exempted. The keyboard check takes
+// a radio group as one tab stop (its checked radio) and a tab list as one (its
+// tabindex 0 tab), and reads a radio's ring on its pill.
+import { createRequire } from "node:module";
+import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
+import fs from "node:fs";
+import http from "node:http";
+import path from "node:path";
+import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
+
+const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
+const { chromium } = require("playwright");
+
+async function repoRoot(start) {
+  const fs = await import("node:fs");
+  const path = await import("node:path");
+  let dir = path.resolve(start);
+  if (fs.existsSync(dir) && fs.statSync(dir).isFile()) dir = path.dirname(dir);
+  for (;;) {
+    if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, "custom_components", "heatpump_optimizer", "manifest.json"))) return dir;
+    const parent = path.dirname(dir);
+    if (parent === dir) throw new Error("no repository root above " + start);
+    dir = parent;
+  }
+}
+
+const ROOT = await repoRoot(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
+const DOCS = path.join(ROOT, "docs");
+const git = (...a) => execFileSync("git", a, { cwd: ROOT, encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 1 << 26 });
+const at = process.argv.indexOf("--base");
+const BASE_REF = at >= 0 ? process.argv[at + 1] : git("merge-base", "origin/main", "HEAD").trim();
+const HEAD_SRC = fs.readFileSync(path.join(DOCS, "index.html"), "utf8");
+const BASE_SRC = git("show", `${BASE_REF}:docs/index.html`);
+
+const WIDTHS = [360, 390, 768, 1440];
+const THEMES = ["light", "dark"];
+const ANCHORS = ["top", "main", "how", "card", "features", "works-with", "install", "limits", "ai", "docs"];
+const SIZE_CAP = 70000;
+
+let fails = 0;
+function check(name, pass, detail = "") {
+  if (!pass) fails++;
+  console.log(`${pass ? "ok  " : "FAIL"} ${name}${detail ? "  [" + detail + "]" : ""}`);
+}
+
+// ---- static: links, anchors, embedding, size (checks 4-6)
+const hrefs = src => [...new Set(src.match(/href="[^"#][^"]*"/g) || [])].sort();
+const hb = hrefs(BASE_SRC), hh = hrefs(HEAD_SRC);
+const gone = hb.filter(h => !hh.includes(h)), added = hh.filter(h => !hb.includes(h));
+check("4 links: the set of non-fragment href values is the base's", !gone.length && !added.length && hb.length > 0,
+  `${hh.length} at the head, ${hb.length} at the base; gone ${JSON.stringify(gone)}; added ${JSON.stringify(added)}`);
+const counts = ANCHORS.map(id => [id, (HEAD_SRC.match(new RegExp(`\\sid="${id}"`, "g")) || []).length]);
+check("5 anchors: each of the ten ids appears exactly once", counts.every(([, n]) => n === 1), counts.map(([i, n]) => `${i}=${n}`).join(" "));
+const bytes = Buffer.byteLength(HEAD_SRC);
+check("6 nothing embedded: no data: address", !/data:/.test(HEAD_SRC));
+check(`6 size: the page is under ${SIZE_CAP} bytes`, bytes < SIZE_CAP, `${bytes} bytes; the base is ${Buffer.byteLength(BASE_SRC)}`);
+
+// ---- the server
+const TYPES = { ".html": "text/html; charset=utf-8", ".woff2": "font/woff2", ".png": "image/png", ".svg": "image/svg+xml", ".css": "text/css" };
+const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
+  const url = new URL(req.url, "http://x");
+  if (url.pathname === "/__base.html") { res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": TYPES[".html"] }); res.end(BASE_SRC); return; }
+  const rel = url.pathname === "/" ? "index.html" : decodeURIComponent(url.pathname.slice(1));
+  const file = path.join(DOCS, rel);
+  // One read decides: a missing file or a directory throws, and nothing is checked before it is used.
+  let body = null;
+  if (file.startsWith(DOCS + path.sep)) { try { body = fs.readFileSync(file); } catch { body = null; } }
+  if (body === null) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return; }
+  res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": TYPES[path.extname(file)] || "application/octet-stream" });
+  res.end(body);
+});
+await new Promise(r => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", r));
+const ORIGIN = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`;
+
+const FONTS = [...HEAD_SRC.matchAll(/url\((site\/fonts\/[^)]+)\)/g)].map(m => "/" + m[1]);
+const IMAGES = [...HEAD_SRC.matchAll(/(?:src|srcset)="(img\/[^"]+)"/g)].map(m => "/" + m[1]);
+const ALLOWED = new Set(["/", ...FONTS, ...IMAGES]);
+
+const browser = await chromium.launch();
+async function open(opts = {}, url = "/", init = null) {
+  const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 }, ...opts });
+  const page = await ctx.newPage();
+  const seen = { console: [], requests: [] };
+  page.on("console", m => seen.console.push(`${m.type()}: ${m.text()}`));
+  page.on("pageerror", e => seen.console.push(`pageerror: ${e.message}`));
+  page.on("request", r => seen.requests.push(r.url()));
+  if (init) await page.addInitScript(init);
+  await page.goto(ORIGIN + url, { waitUntil: "load" });
+  return { ctx, page, seen };
+}
+const settle = (page, ms = 250) => page.waitForTimeout(ms);
+/** Walk the whole page so every lazy image and every reveal has had its turn. */
+async function walk(page) {
+  const h = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollHeight);
+  const step = Math.max(200, Math.floor((page.viewportSize().height) * 0.6));
+  for (let y = 0; y <= h; y += step) { await page.evaluate(v => scrollTo({ top: v, behavior: "instant" }), y); await settle(page, 60); }
+  await page.evaluate(() => scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: "instant" }));
+  await settle(page);
+}
+
+// ---- 7: every text node under a source mark at the base is still on the page
+{
+  const texts = async url => {
+    const { ctx, page } = await open({}, url);
+    const out = await page.evaluate(() => {
+      const norm = s => s.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
+      const marked = [], w = document.createTreeWalker(document.body, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT);
+      for (let n = w.nextNode(); n; n = w.nextNode()) {
+        const t = norm(n.data), owner = n.parentElement.closest("[data-src],[data-copy]");
+        if (t && owner && owner.hasAttribute("data-src") && !n.parentElement.closest("script,style,svg")) marked.push(t);
+      }
+      return { marked, alts: [...document.images].map(i => norm(i.alt)), all: norm(document.body.textContent) };
+    });
+    await ctx.close();
+    return out;
+  };
+  const base = await texts("/__base.html"), head = await texts("/");
+  const headAlts = new Set(head.alts);
+  const lostText = [...new Set(base.marked.filter(t => !head.all.includes(t)))];
+  const lostAlt = base.alts.filter(a => !headAlts.has(a));
+  check("7 sentences: every text node under a source mark at the base is on the page at the head",
+    lostText.length === 0, `${base.marked.length} marked nodes at the base; missing ${JSON.stringify(lostText)}`);
+  check("7 pictures: the only alternative text gone is the removed how-it-works picture's",
+    lostAlt.length === 1 && lostAlt[0].startsWith("One optimization interval"), `gone ${JSON.stringify(lostAlt.map(a => a.slice(0, 60)))}`);
+}
+
+/** The 40 px floor's rule, stated once (the header says what it exempts and why). */
+const targetFloor = () => {
+  const inLine = e => getComputedStyle(e).display === "inline" && [...e.parentElement.childNodes].some(n => n.nodeType === 3 && n.data.trim());
+  const all = [...document.querySelectorAll("a[href], button, summary, select, textarea, label:has(input), input:not(label input), [tabindex]")].filter(e => e.getClientRects().length);
+  const held = all.filter(e => !inLine(e));
+  return { targets: held.length, inLine: all.length - held.length,
+    small: held.map(e => { const r = e.getBoundingClientRect(); return [(e.textContent.trim() || e.getAttribute("aria-label") || e.tagName).slice(0, 24), Math.round(r.width), Math.round(r.height)]; }).filter(([, w, h]) => w < 40 || h < 40) };
+};
+// ---- 8: widths x themes; no overflow, no console message, no request beyond the page's own
+for (const width of WIDTHS) for (const theme of THEMES) {
+  const { ctx, page, seen } = await open({ viewport: { width, height: 800 }, colorScheme: theme });
+  await walk(page);
+  const m = await page.evaluate(() => ({
+    sw: document.documentElement.scrollWidth, iw: innerWidth,
+    bg: getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor,
+    lazy: [...document.images].filter(i => i.getClientRects().length && (!i.complete || !i.naturalWidth)).map(i => i.getAttribute("src")),
+  }));
+  Object.assign(m, await page.evaluate(targetFloor));
+  const paths = seen.requests.map(u => new URL(u)).map(u => (u.origin === ORIGIN ? u.pathname : u.href));
+  const foreign = [...new Set(paths.filter(p => !ALLOWED.has(p)))];
+  const tag = `${width}px ${theme}`;
+  check(`8 ${tag}: scroll width equals window width`, m.sw === m.iw, `scrollWidth ${m.sw}, innerWidth ${m.iw}`);
+  check(`8 ${tag}: no console message`, seen.console.length === 0, seen.console.slice(0, 3).join(" | "));
+  check(`8 ${tag}: no request but the page, its fonts and its images`, foreign.length === 0 && paths.includes("/"),
+    `${new Set(paths).size} distinct; other ${JSON.stringify(foreign)}`);
+  check(`8 ${tag}: every image with a box loaded, theme background ${m.bg}`, m.lazy.length === 0 && m.bg === (theme === "dark" ? "rgb(11, 26, 40)" : "rgb(243, 248, 252)"), JSON.stringify(m.lazy));
+  check(`floor ${tag}: every target outside a line of text is at least 40 px in both dimensions`, m.small.length === 0 && m.targets > 0,
+    `${m.targets} targets held to the floor, ${m.inLine} links in a line of text exempt; under 40 px ${JSON.stringify(m.small)}`);
+  await ctx.close();
+}
+
+// ---- the same floor when the page's fonts do not arrive and the system's own stand in
+for (const width of [360, 1440]) {
+  const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height: 800 } });
+  const page = await ctx.newPage();
+  let refused = 0;
+  await page.route("**/site/fonts/**", r => { refused++; return r.abort(); });
+  await page.goto(ORIGIN + "/", { waitUntil: "load" });
+  await walk(page);
+  const m = await page.evaluate(targetFloor);
+  const loaded = await page.evaluate(() => [...document.fonts].filter(f => f.status === "loaded").length);
+  check(`floor ${width}px without the page's fonts: every target outside a line of text is at least 40 px in both dimensions`, m.small.length === 0 && m.targets > 0 && refused > 0 && loaded === 0,
+    `${refused} font request(s) refused, ${loaded} font face(s) loaded; ${m.targets} targets held to the floor, ${m.inLine} exempt; under 40 px ${JSON.stringify(m.small)}`);
+  await ctx.close();
+}
+
+// ---- contrast floor, from the page's own tokens in each theme
+for (const theme of THEMES) {
+  const { ctx, page } = await open({ colorScheme: theme });
+  const worst = await page.evaluate(() => {
+    const cs = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement), v = n => cs.getPropertyValue(n).trim();
+    const lum = hex => { const c = [1, 3, 5].map(i => parseInt(hex.slice(i, i + 2), 16) / 255).map(x => (x <= .03928 ? x / 12.92 : ((x + .055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)); return .2126 * c[0] + .7152 * c[1] + .0722 * c[2]; };
+    const ratio = (a, b) => { const [x, y] = [lum(v(a)), lum(v(b))].sort((p, q) => q - p); return (x + .05) / (y + .05); };
+    const body = [["--ink", "--bg"], ["--ink", "--surface"], ["--ink", "--well"], ["--ink-2", "--bg"], ["--ink-2", "--surface"], ["--ink-2", "--well"], ["--ink-2", "--hero-a"],
+      ["--accent", "--surface"], ["--accent", "--bg"], ["--accent", "--well"], ["--accent-ink", "--accent"], ["--heat", "--surface"]];
+    return { body: body.map(([a, b]) => [`${a} on ${b}`, +ratio(a, b).toFixed(2)]).sort((p, q) => p[1] - q[1])[0], title: +Math.min(ratio("--heat", "--hero-a"), ratio("--heat", "--hero-b")).toFixed(2) };
+  });
+  check(`floor ${theme}: every body text pair of tokens is at least 4.5 to 1`, worst.body[1] >= 4.5, `lowest ${worst.body[0]} = ${worst.body[1]}`);
+  check(`floor ${theme}: the title's ember words are at least 3 to 1 on the hero wash`, worst.title >= 3, `${worst.title}`);
+  await ctx.close();
+}
+
+// ---- 9: the story, down and back up, on the two-column and the one-column layout
+const vizState = page => page.evaluate(() => ({
+  s: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].filter(i => document.getElementById("viz").classList.contains("s" + i)),
+  on: [...document.querySelectorAll("#steps .st.on")].map(s => +s.dataset.step),
+}));
+for (const width of [1440, 390]) {
+  const { ctx, page } = await open({ viewport: { width, height: 800 } });
+  const centre = n => page.evaluate(k => {
+    const r = document.querySelector(`#steps .st[data-step="${k}"]`).getBoundingClientRect();
+    scrollTo({ top: scrollY + r.top + r.height / 2 - innerHeight / 2, behavior: "instant" });
+  }, n);
+  const got = [];
+  for (const n of [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]) {
+    await centre(n); await settle(page, 300);
+    const st = await vizState(page);
+    got.push([n, st.s.join(""), st.on.join("")]);
+  }
+  const want = n => "12345".slice(0, n);
+  check(`9 ${width}px: step n at mid-viewport gives the chart exactly layers 1 to n, down and back up, and marks step n current`,
+    got.every(([n, s, on]) => s === want(n) && on === String(n)), got.map(([n, s, on]) => `${n}:${s || "-"}/${on || "-"}`).join(" "));
+  await page.evaluate(() => scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: "instant" })); await settle(page, 300);
+  const top = await vizState(page);
+  const sticky = await page.evaluate(() => getComputedStyle(document.getElementById("viz")).position);
+  check(`9 ${width}px: above the first step the chart is the bare grid, and the chart card is pinned`, top.s.length === 0 && top.on.length === 0 && sticky === "sticky", `layers ${top.s.join("") || "-"}, position ${sticky}`);
+  await ctx.close();
+}
+
+// ---- 10: the fallback table
+const layerState = () => {
+  const vis = e => { const c = getComputedStyle(e); return +c.opacity === 1 && (c.transform === "none" || c.transform === "matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)"); };
+  const anims = document.getAnimations();
+  const q = s => [...document.querySelectorAll(s)];
+  return {
+    layers: q(".chart .lay").length, layersShown: q(".chart .lay").filter(vis).length,
+    bars: q(".chart .bar").length, barsShown: q(".chart .bar").filter(vis).length,
+    anims: anims.length, clock: anims.filter(a => a.timeline instanceof DocumentTimeline && a.playState === "running").length,
+    transitions: q("body *").filter(e => getComputedStyle(e).transitionDuration.split(",").some(d => parseFloat(d) > 0)).length,
+    progress: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(".progress")).display,
+    panels: q('#gallery [role="tabpanel"]').filter(e => getComputedStyle(e).display !== "none").length,
+    tablist: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(".seg")).display, theme: getComputedStyle(document.getElementById("theme")).display,
+    viz: getComputedStyle(document.getElementById("viz")).position,
+    s: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].filter(i => document.getElementById("viz").classList.contains("s" + i)).join(""),
+    on: q("#steps .st.on").length, stepH: Math.round(Math.max(...q("#steps .st").map(e => e.getBoundingClientRect().height))), vh: innerHeight,
+    hiddenRv: q(".rv, .features .feat").filter(e => !vis(e)).length, sections: q("main section, .hero").filter(e => e.getClientRects().length).length,
+  };
+};
+const choose = async page => {
+  const out = [];
+  for (const id of ["cp2", "cp3", "cp0", "cp1"]) {
+    await page.locator(`label:has(#${id})`).click();

+"""R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE: the held state's census over every bound on the reference's heat.
+
+    PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components \\
+        python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_held_capacity_census.py
+
+Drives ``_thermostat_held_state`` over a grid of installs -- no valve and the
+three throttling valve modes, both zonings, the derived and the
+``two_tank_4way`` layout, pumps of 4, 6 and 9 kW, valve targets 21 to 40 C,
+outdoor -25 to 18 C -- and books one reference step from each held state at
+``_compute_baseline_power``'s power on a one-step horizon (nothing to
+apportion). The property is the phenomenon's, not an instance's: a held state
+the reference step can keep draws no stored heat on its first booked step.
+Prints the case count, the worst first-step store change in kWh_th and the
+count over 0.02 kWh_th, then the capacity control: at -25 C a 9 kW pump holds
+21 C (valved and not), a 4 kW pump does not.
+
+Preconditions, asserted (exit 1): every grid case ran without an exception,
+every held room lies in [min(outdoor, 21), 21], and the case count is the
+grid's product.
+"""
+
+import itertools
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from heatpump_optimizer.optimizer import (
+    HeatPumpOptimizer,
+    OptimizationConfig,
+    _thermostat_held_state,
+)
+from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import (
+    ThermalModel,
+    ThermalParameters,
+    ThermalState,
+    WeatherSeries,
+)
+from profiles import house
+
+TARGET_C = 21.0
+MODES = ("none", "manual", "smart_read", "smart_write")
+ZONINGS = (True, False)
+LAYOUTS = (None, "two_tank_4way")
+PUMPS_KW = (4.0, 6.0, 9.0)
+VALVE_TARGETS_C = (21.0, 25.0, 30.0, 40.0)
+OUTDOORS_C = (-25.0, -15.0, -5.0, 0.0, 5.0, 10.0, 14.0, 16.0, 18.0)
+
+
+def first_step(mode, two_zone, layout, pump_kw, valve_target, outdoor):
+    """The held state and its first booked reference step's store change, kWh_th."""
+    cfg = {"buffer_tank_volume": 750.0, "buffer_max_temperature": 56.0,
+           "heat_pump_max_power": pump_kw}
+    if mode != "none":
+        cfg.update(mixing_valve_mode=mode, mixing_valve_target=valve_target)
+    if layout:
+        cfg["topology_layout"] = layout
+    model = ThermalModel(ThermalParameters.from_config(house(two_zone=two_zone, dhw=False, **cfg)))
+    opt = HeatPumpOptimizer(model, OptimizationConfig(
+        horizon_hours=1, time_step_minutes=15, target_temp=TARGET_C))
+    weather = WeatherSeries(outdoor_temps=np.array([outdoor]), wind_speeds=np.zeros(1),
+                            precipitation=np.zeros(1), solar_radiation=np.zeros(1))
+    start = ThermalState(room_temperature=20.5, slab_temperature=22.0,
+                         outdoor_temperature=outdoor, upper_floor_temperature=20.5,
+                         lower_floor_temperature=20.5, buffer_tank_temperature=30.0)
+    held = _thermostat_held_state(model, start, weather, TARGET_C)
+    power = float(opt._compute_baseline_power(weather, start, 0.25)[0][0])
+    nxt = model.simulate_step(held, power, outdoor, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.25)
+    return held, opt._stored_thermal_energy(nxt) - opt._stored_thermal_energy(held), power
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    grid = list(itertools.product(MODES, ZONINGS, LAYOUTS, PUMPS_KW, VALVE_TARGETS_C, OUTDOORS_C))
+    ran, worst, worst_case, over, refused = 0, 0.0, None, 0, []
+    for case in grid:
+        try:
+            held, ds, power = first_step(*case)
+        except Exception as exc:  # a refusal is a precondition failure, reported
+            refused.append((case, repr(exc)[:120]))
+            continue
+        ran += 1
+        outdoor = case[-1]
+        if not min(outdoor, TARGET_C) - 1e-9 <= held.room_temperature <= TARGET_C:
+            refused.append((case, f"held room {held.room_temperature:.3f} out of range"))
+        if abs(ds) > abs(worst):
+            worst, worst_case = ds, (*case, round(held.room_temperature, 3), round(power, 3))
+        over += abs(ds) > 0.02
+    print(f"RESULT census: cases {ran} of {len(grid)}, worst first-step dS {worst:+.4f} kWh_th "
+          f"at {worst_case}, over 0.02 kWh_th {over}")
+    for mode in ("none", "manual"):
+        for pump_kw in (4.0, 9.0):
+            held, ds, power = first_step(mode, True, None, pump_kw, 40.0, -25.0)
+            print(f"RESULT control two-zone -25 C mode={mode} pump {pump_kw} kW: held room "
+                  f"{held.room_temperature:.3f} power {power:.3f} first-step dS {ds:+.4f} kWh_th")
+    for case, why in refused[:10]:
+        print("REFUSED", case, why)
+    return 1 if refused or ran != len(grid) else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_residual_attribution.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_residual_attribution.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..d87bbca253
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_residual_attribution.py
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+"""R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE: the savings residual the valved arms leave, attributed.
+
+    PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components \\
+        python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_residual_attribution.py flat|winter_typical
+
+``r10_sav_wood_reference.closed_loop``'s valve arm (no wood, tank at 30 C,
+the arm ``valve_arm`` runs) with the plant step and the booked reference
+wrapped, never changed. Per plant step, in kWh_th: the plan's pump heat
+``cop * heat_per_cop_kw(P) * dt`` and its store change (``_stored_thermal_energy``
+next less now), so its loss; and the booked reference stepped once from its
+held state (``_thermostat_held_state`` at 21 C) at the power the harness
+booked for that step, its pump heat at ``_reference_cop`` and its store
+change, so its loss; beside the steady floor demand at 21 C and at the
+room the plan delivered (the comfort term's rule).
+
+The harness's residual is ``ref - comfort + stored - plan``. With each
+side's loss defined as its heat less its store change, the residual in
+kWh_th is ``(L_ref - L_plan - steady gap) + reference store change``: an
+identity, so its content is the two measured terms, not their sum. Both are
+the booked reference's own: the heat its booked steps draw from the held
+state's stores (a reference at equilibrium reads 0), and its loss beyond
+the steady comfort term. Precondition, asserted: the wrappers saw every
+plant step of the run (``DAYS * 24 / DT``) and a booked reference for each;
+the harness exits 1 otherwise.
+"""
+
+import sys
+sys.path.insert(0, "dev/audit/harnesses")
+import r10_sav_wood_reference as h
+from heatpump_optimizer.optimizer import (
+    _thermostat_held_state, _reference_cop, _floor_demand_at_target, WeatherSeries)
+from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import heat_per_cop_kw
+A = dict(q_p=0.0, ds_p=0.0, q_r=0.0, ds_r=0.0, st_r=0.0, st_p=0.0, n=0)
+orig = h._install
+def _install(wood, two_zone=True):
+    opt, model = orig(wood, two_zone)
+    real, real_base = model.simulate_step, opt._compute_baseline_power
+    last = {}
+    def base(series, state, dt, *a, **k):
+        out = real_base(series, state, dt, *a, **k)
+        if sys._getframe(1).f_code.co_name == "closed_loop":
+            last["booked"], last["series"] = float(out[0][0]), series
+        return out
+    opt._compute_baseline_power = base
+    S = opt._stored_thermal_energy
+    def step(*args, **kw):
+        if len(args) < 7 or sys._getframe(1).f_code.co_name != "closed_loop":
+            return real(*args, **kw)
+        state, power, out, wind, rain, sol, dt = args[:7]
+        nxt = real(*args, **kw)
+        cop_p = model.compute_cop(out, flow_temp=state.buffer_tank_temperature)
+        A["q_p"] += cop_p * heat_per_cop_kw(model.params, power) * dt
+        A["ds_p"] += S(nxt) - S(state)
+        series = last["series"]
+        held = _thermostat_held_state(model, state, series, 21.0)
+        b = last["booked"]
+        ref_next = real(held, b, out, wind, rain, sol, dt, **kw)
+        A["q_r"] += _reference_cop(model, held, out, None) * heat_per_cop_kw(model.params, b) * dt
+        A["ds_r"] += S(ref_next) - S(held)
+        A["st_r"] += _floor_demand_at_target(model, 21.0, out, wind, rain, sol) * dt
+        A["st_p"] += _floor_demand_at_target(model, nxt.room_temperature, out, wind, rain, sol) * dt
+        A["n"] += 1
+        return nxt
+    model.simulate_step = step
+    return opt, model
+h._install = _install
+residual_pct = h.closed_loop(False, lambda t: 0.0, None, 30.0, sys.argv[1])[1]
+print(f"harness residual {residual_pct:+.2f} %")
+L_p, L_r = A["q_p"] - A["ds_p"], A["q_r"] - A["ds_r"]
+print(f"steps {A['n']} | plan heat {A['q_p']:.2f} store change {A['ds_p']:+.2f} loss {L_p:.2f} | "
+      f"reference heat {A['q_r']:.2f} store change {A['ds_r']:+.2f} loss {L_r:.2f} | "
+      f"steady loss at 21 {A['st_r']:.2f} at delivered {A['st_p']:.2f}")
+print(f"loss gap ref-plan {L_r - L_p:+.2f} kWh_th against steady {A['st_r'] - A['st_p']:+.2f}: "
+      f"non-steady {(L_r - L_p) - (A['st_r'] - A['st_p']):+.2f}; reference stored {A['ds_r']:+.2f} kWh_th")
+want = int(h.DAYS * 24 / h.DT)
+print(f"plant steps seen {A['n']} of {want}")
+sys.exit(0 if A["n"] == want else 1)
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_valuation_residue.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_valuation_residue.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..e5280e98d9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_valuation_residue.py
@@ -0,0 +1,182 @@
+"""R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE: the part-load refill pricing, against the rule it owes.
+
+    PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests \\
+        python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_valuation_residue.py
+
+Synthetic throughout: ``r10_partload_pricing.solve``'s 16 installs on its
+spread and flat price days, at ``d = 0`` and at the central plant's derate
+(``r10_partload_residue.central_derate``). Three figures per solve, each the
+production figure against the tree's own part-load inverse
+(``thermal_model.power_for_heat_per_cop_kw``) applied to the same inputs:
+
+1. ``lp``: every hot-water LP the solve runs (``dhw_planner.linprog``,
+   wrapped). The LP's own valuation of the energy it bought,
+   ``c[:energy] . x[:energy]``, against what that energy costs at the draw
+   the planner publishes for it, ``sum(price * dt * P(h))`` with
+   ``h = E / (cop * dt)`` and ``P`` the inverse. The largest gap over the
+   solve's LPs, currency per day.
+2. ``terminal``: ``_terminal_cost`` on the published end state, against
+   ``refill_price * P(T_lin / refill_price, hours=H)``: ``T_lin`` the same
+   call with the derate zeroed (the linear figure), ``H`` the refill hours
+   (a quarter of the 24 h horizon, the hours the 25th-percentile refill
+   price is drawn from), sign-symmetric.
+3. ``deferred``: every ``_deferred_energy_cost`` call of the solve (wrapped),
+   re-evaluated alike: its zero-derate figure through the same rule.
+
+Null control: at ``d = 0`` all three must read 0 (``lp`` within 1e-9: the
+two valuations multiply and divide by the COP in different orders); the
+harness exits 1 otherwise. A tree that prices refill linearly reads the
+``d > 0`` terminal and deferred gaps above 0; a tree pricing it at the rule
+reads 0. ``lp`` reads the chord between segment breakpoints where the LP is
+segmented, the whole secant where it is not.
+
+Also printed per solve: ``predicted_savings``, so the flat-price day (no
+timing saving to find) shows what the derated refill moves in the savings.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+
+sys.path.insert(0, "dev/audit/harnesses")
+
+import r10_partload_pricing as pp  # noqa: E402
+import r10_partload_residue as pr  # noqa: E402
+import r10_setpoint_boost as sb  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer import dhw_planner as planner_mod  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer import optimizer as opt_mod  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import power_for_heat_per_cop_kw  # noqa: E402
+
+REFILL_HOURS = 0.25 * 24.0
+NULL_TOL = 1e-9
+
+
+def rule(params, linear: float, refill_price: float) -> float:
+    """The derated refill of a linear figure: the tree's own inverse at H."""
+    # No derate: the inverse is the identity, and ``rp * (x / rp)`` need not
+    # be ``x`` to the bit, so the rule returns the figure itself.
+    if not params.cop_partload_derate or refill_price == 0.0 or linear == 0.0:
+        return linear
+    hpc = linear / refill_price
+    return refill_price * math.copysign(
+        float(power_for_heat_per_cop_kw(params, abs(hpc), hours=REFILL_HOURS)), hpc)
+
+
+def zeroed(params):
+    class _Z:
+        def __enter__(self):
+            self.d = params.cop_partload_derate
+            params.cop_partload_derate = 0.0
+
+        def __exit__(self, *exc):
+            params.cop_partload_derate = self.d
+    return _Z()
+
+
+def solve_recording(cell, prices, d):
+    lps, defers = [], []
+    real_lp = planner_mod.linprog
+    real_plan = planner_mod.DhwPlanner._plan_dhw_min_cost
+    real_cop = planner_mod.DhwPlanner._dhw_cop_profile
+    real_defer = opt_mod.HeatPumpOptimizer._deferred_energy_cost
+    seen: dict = {}
+
+    def plan(self, ctx, *a, **k):
+        seen["ctx"], seen["params"] = ctx, self.model.params
+        return real_plan(self, ctx, *a, **k)
+
+    def cop_profile(self, *a, **k):
+        seen["cop"] = out = real_cop(self, *a, **k)
+        return out
+
+    def lp(c, *a, **k):
+        res = real_lp(c, *a, **k)
+        if res.success and res.x is not None and "ctx" in seen:
+            ctx, cop = seen["ctx"], np.asarray(seen["cop"], float)
+            x, cv = np.asarray(res.x, float), np.asarray(c, float)
+            lps.append((cv, x, ctx.n_steps, ctx.dt, cop, np.asarray(ctx.prices, float), seen["params"]))
+        return res
+
+    def defer(self, *a, **k):
+        out = real_defer(self, *a, **k)
+        with zeroed(self.model.params):
+            lin = real_defer(self, *a, **k)
+        prices = a[2] if len(a) > 2 else k["prices"]
+        refill = float(np.percentile(prices, 25))
+        defers.append((out, rule(self.model.params, lin, refill)))
+        return out
+
+    planner_mod.linprog = lp
+    planner_mod.DhwPlanner._plan_dhw_min_cost = plan
+    planner_mod.DhwPlanner._dhw_cop_profile = cop_profile
+    opt_mod.HeatPumpOptimizer._deferred_energy_cost = defer
+    try:
+        opt, res = pp.solve(cell, prices, d)
+    finally:
+        planner_mod.linprog = real_lp
+        planner_mod.DhwPlanner._plan_dhw_min_cost = real_plan
+        planner_mod.DhwPlanner._dhw_cop_profile = real_cop
+        opt_mod.HeatPumpOptimizer._deferred_energy_cost = real_defer
+    return opt, res, lps, defers
+
+
+def lp_gap(entry) -> float:
+    cv, x, n, dt, cop, prices, params = entry
+    # Energy columns are the leading n-wide blocks priced below the
+    # shortfall slack, which ``_plan_dhw_min_cost`` prices at
+    # 1000 * (max |price| + 1): one block unsegmented, one per segment else.
+    slack = 1000.0 * (float(np.max(np.abs(prices))) + 1.0)
+    blocks = 0
+    while (blocks + 1) * n <= len(cv) and np.all(cv[blocks * n:(blocks + 1) * n] < 0.5 * slack):
+        blocks += 1
+    n_e = blocks * n
+    lp_value = float(cv[:n_e] @ x[:n_e])
+    energy = x[:n_e].reshape(blocks, n).sum(axis=0)
+    draw = np.asarray(power_for_heat_per_cop_kw(params, energy / (cop * dt)), float)
+    return float((prices * draw).sum() * dt) - lp_value
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    derate = pr.central_derate()
+    print(f"central plant derate {derate}; refill hours {REFILL_HOURS}")
+    null_bad = failures = 0
+    for tag, prices in (("spread", sb.SPREAD), ("flat", sb.FLAT)):
+        for d in (0.0, derate):
+            rows = []
+            for cell in sb.CELLS:
+                try:
+                    opt, res, lps, defers = solve_recording(cell, prices, d)
+                except Exception as err:  # counted, never dropped
+                    failures += 1
+                    print(f"  {tag} {cell} d={d} failed: {err!r}")
+                    continue
+                params = opt.model.params
+                lp = max((lp_gap(e) for e in lps), default=0.0)
+                term = pp.terminal_figure(opt, res)
+                with zeroed(params):
+                    term_lin = pp.terminal_figure(opt, res)
+                refill = float(np.percentile(np.asarray(res.prices, float), 25)) * opt.config.price_weight
+                term_gap = rule(params, term_lin, refill) - term
+                defer_gap = max((abs(r - o) for o, r in defers), default=0.0)
+                sav = float(res.predicted_savings)
+                rows.append((abs(lp), abs(term_gap), defer_gap))
+                print(f"  {tag} {cell} d={d} lp {lp:+.6f} ({len(lps)} LPs)"
+                      f" | terminal {term:.4f} gap {term_gap:+.6f}"
+                      f" | deferred calls {len(defers)} gap max {defer_gap:.6f}"
+                      f" | predicted_savings {sav:.4f}")
+                if d == 0.0 and (abs(lp) > NULL_TOL or term_gap != 0.0 or defer_gap != 0.0):
+                    null_bad += 1
+                    print(f"    null row off: lp {lp!r} terminal {term_gap!r} deferred {defer_gap!r}")
+            if rows:
+                a = np.array(rows, float)
+                print(f"{tag} d={d}: cells {len(rows)} lp gap max {a[:, 0].max():.6f}"
+                      f" terminal gap max {a[:, 1].max():.6f} deferred gap max {a[:, 2].max():.6f}")
+    print(f"null rows not zero {null_bad}")
+    print(f"failures {failures}")
+    return 1 if null_bad or failures else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

@@ -167,6 +167,15 @@ MUTANTS = [

     ("S24", "seat_venv.sh", '|| die "$VENV_HA is missing a pinned homeassistant',
@@ -707,7 +716,8 @@ ENV_MUTANTS = [("S04U", "S04", {"PYTHONUNBUFFERED": "1"})]
 STEP_OF = {"prepr-9": "tools/pr/prepr.sh", "prepr-10": "tools/pr/prepr.sh",
            "prepr-12": "tools/pr/prepr.sh", "body_push-1": "tools/pr/prepr.sh",
            "body_push-2": "tools/pr/prepr.sh", "body_push-3": "tools/pr/prepr.sh", "body_push-4": "tools/pr/prepr.sh",
-           "carry_audit-1": "tools/audit/seat/bus.sh"}
+           "carry_audit-1": "tools/audit/seat/bus.sh",
+           "roster_lib-1": "roster_edit.py", "roster_lib-2": "roster_edit.py"}
 
 # The wrappers' own line is the dispatch to the self-tests they delegate.
 # S08's wrapper now runs both tallies (delivery_row.sh's and its own pushes):
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..7378ba0b6f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,222 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# R10-HOTFIX-TICK-SELFTEST-CHECKOUT: tick_loop.sh's self-test must read and move
+# no checkout but scratch clones of its own, whatever its caller's checkout,
+# GIT_DIR or PATH. The finder's control (the self-test run from a checkout
+# behind origin/main: a branch fails a row, a detached head is moved) and the
+# mutants that take each guard back out, on <rev>'s copy of the script.
+#
+#   bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh <rev> [arm...]
+#
+# Nothing runs in the caller's checkout: <rev>'s tick_loop.sh, heartbeat.sh,
+# ref_privacy.py and tests/throwaway_git.sh are written to a scratch directory
+# and every self-test runs from there or from a throwaway clone of it.
+#
+# Shape arms -- <rev>'s self-test run from a throwaway clone, its nested rows
+# skipped (the clone is the nesting); each prints
+#   <arm> behind=<n>: <the self-test's tally line> HEAD-MOVED|HEAD-UNMOVED
+# and the failing rows:
+#   branch    a branch clone one commit behind origin/main on tick_loop.sh
+#   detached  the same clone, detached
+#   gitdir    a detached clone behind, named by GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE (a git hook's environment)
+#   shim      a branch clone at origin/main, the state dir's bin holding a gh with the seat shim's marker (a live seat's)
+#   level     a branch clone at origin/main: the null control
+# Every arm but shim runs under a scratch HPO_STATE_DIR whose bin holds a plain gh, so the
+# caller's own gh, shim or not, decides nothing.
+# Mutant arms -- <rev>'s whole self-test from a scratch copy that is no checkout,
+# one guard taken back out; each prints `<arm>: <tally line> rc=<n>` and the failing rows:
+#   whole       no mutation: the control every mutant is read against
+#   nocheckout  the HPO_TICK_CODE_DIR export back below the TICK-GH rows
+#   gitenv      throwaway_git_env back below the heartbeat rows
+#   plaingh     the no-shim row's own plain gh taken off its PATH
+#   envscrub    the line dropping the caller's HPO_TICK_* and HPO_SWEEP_MANDATE deleted (a rev before envi)
+#   envi        the re-exec under env -i dropped: --self-test runs the rows in the caller's environment
+#   carry       the re-exec copies one caller variable through (SPY_REAL_GIT, round 3's first channel)
+#   pathfirst   the seat-bin PATH computed above the re-exec and carried by it (round 3's second channel)
+#   allowlist   the rows' entry point lets a name off the allowlist through (a rev before the re-cut)
+#   pipefail    the self-test's `set +o pipefail` deleted
+#   failopen    the refusal after the re-exec replaced by a run of the rows: a --self-test whose re-exec a
+#               caller's function named exec skipped runs every row in the caller's environment (round 4)
+#   bound       pr_args.sh's self-test bound (main's 38aee2235a) deleted from the rows' entry
+# Channel arm -- <rev>'s whole self-test from a scratch copy, once per channel a caller has into the
+# process before line 1 and at the re-exec, every run beside a scratch bare repository named as
+# HPO_HEARTBEAT_REMOTE and TICK_RC=1 (either acts if a row runs in the caller's environment); each prints
+#   channels <channel>: <the run's last line> rc=<n> fn-calls=<n> victim-refs=<n>
+#   fn-all      an exported function for every bash builtin but exec and every command the script runs,
+#               each touching a file when called (a bare redirection, so it looks up no command itself)
+#   bashenv-all the same functions defined by a BASH_ENV file
+#   fn-exec     an exported exec that skips the /usr/bin/env call (the round-4 attack)
+#   posix       fn-exec under POSIXLY_CORRECT, and under SHELLOPTS=posix: exec is a special builtin there
+#   noexec      SHELLOPTS=noexec: bash runs no line of any script
+#   opts        SHELLOPTS=errexit:nounset:xtrace and BASHOPTS=execfail:extglob
+#   env         ENV naming a file that touches one when sourced
+#   path        PATH led by a directory whose bash, env, git and python3 touch a file
+#   ifs         IFS=/ in the caller
+# A mutant arm needs the `# mut:selftest-*` markers and says so on a <rev> without them.
+# No arm named runs the five shapes.
+set -uo pipefail
+rev=${1:?usage: r10_tick_selftest_checkout.sh <rev> [branch|detached|gitdir|shim|level|whole|nocheckout|gitenv|plaingh|envscrub|envi|carry|pathfirst|allowlist|pipefail|failopen|bound|channels]...}; shift
+[ $# -gt 0 ] || set -- branch detached gitdir shim level
+top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) || exit 2
+sha=$(git -C "$top" rev-parse --verify -q "$rev^{commit}") || { echo "no commit $rev"; exit 2; }
+d=$(mktemp -d) || exit 2
+trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
+L=tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh
+extract() { # <dir>: <rev>'s six files, in a directory that is no checkout
+  local f; mkdir -p "$1/tools/audit/seat" "$1/tests"
+  for f in "$L" tools/audit/seat/heartbeat.sh tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py tools/audit/seat/offline_spy.py tests/throwaway_git.sh tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh; do
+    git -C "$top" show "$sha:$f" > "$1/$f" 2>/dev/null || [ "$f" = tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh ] || exit 2
+  done
+}
+extract "$d/src"
+# shellcheck source=/dev/null
+. "$d/src/tests/throwaway_git.sh"
+mkdir -p "$d/plain/bin" "$d/shim/bin"
+printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$d/plain/bin/gh"; printf '#!/bin/sh\n# hpo-gh-shim\nexit 0\n' > "$d/shim/bin/gh"
+chmod +x "$d/plain/bin/gh" "$d/shim/bin/gh"
+bare() { env -u HPO_TICK_CODE_DIR -u HPO_TICK_HEARTBEAT -u GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES HPO_STATE_DIR="$d/plain" "$@"; }
+rows() { sed -n 's/^  FAIL /    FAIL /p; s/^    nested FAIL: /      nested FAIL: /p' "$1"; }
+
+clones() { # the scratch origin, one commit ahead of the `old` clone on tick_loop.sh
+  [ -d "$d/o.git" ] && return 0
+  (
+    throwaway_git_env
+    cp -R "$d/src" "$d/n"
+    throwaway_git_init "$d/o.git" -q --bare -b main && throwaway_git_init "$d/n" -q -b main || exit 2
+    git -C "$d/n" add -A && git -C "$d/n" commit -qm base && git -C "$d/o.git" fetch -q "$d/n" main:main || exit 2
+    throwaway_git_clone -q "$d/o.git" "$d/old" || exit 2
+    printf '# ahead\n' >> "$d/n/$L"
+    git -C "$d/n" commit -qam ahead && git -C "$d/o.git" fetch -q "$d/n" main:main || exit 2
+    throwaway_git_clone -q "$d/o.git" "$d/new" || exit 2
+  ) || { echo "the scratch clones could not be built"; exit 2; }
+}
+
+shape() { # <arm>
+  local arm=$1 c=$d/c-$1 h0 h1 n m
+  local -a pre=()
+  clones; rm -rf "$c"
+  case $arm in
+    branch) cp -R "$d/old" "$c" ;;
+    detached) cp -R "$d/old" "$c"; (throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" checkout -q --detach) ;;
+    gitdir) cp -R "$d/old" "$c"; (throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" checkout -q --detach); pre=(GIT_DIR="$c/.git" GIT_WORK_TREE="$c") ;;
+    shim) cp -R "$d/new" "$c"; pre=(HPO_STATE_DIR="$d/shim") ;;
+    level) cp -R "$d/new" "$c" ;;
+  esac
+  h0=$(throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" rev-parse HEAD)
+  HPO_TICK_SELFTEST_NESTED=1 bare ${pre[@]+"${pre[@]}"} bash "$c/$L" --self-test --nested > "$d/$arm.log" 2>&1
+  h1=$(throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" rev-parse HEAD)
+  n=$(throwaway_git_env; git -C "$c" fetch -q origin main; git -C "$c" rev-list --count "$h0..origin/main")
+  [ "$h0" = "$h1" ] && m=HEAD-UNMOVED || m=HEAD-MOVED
+  echo "$arm behind=$n: $(tail -n 1 "$d/$arm.log") $m"; rows "$d/$arm.log"
+}
+
+mutant() { # <arm>
+  local arm=$1 m=$d/m-$1 rc
+  rm -rf "$m"; extract "$m"
+  python3 - "$m/$L" "$arm" 2>/dev/null <<'PY' || { echo "$arm: NOT RUN, the mutation did not apply (no '# mut:selftest-*' marker at this rev?)"; return; }
+import sys
+p, arm = sys.argv[1:]
+s = open(p).read().split("\n")
+def marked(marker):
+    g = [i for i, l in enumerate(s) if l.rstrip().endswith("# mut:" + marker)]
+    assert len(g) == 1, (marker, g)
+    return g[0]
+def move(marker, after):  # the marked line, back to where the merge base ran it
+    line = s.pop(marked(marker))
+    a = [i for i, l in enumerate(s) if after in l]
+    assert len(a) == 1, (after, a)
+    s.insert(a[0] + 1, line)
+if arm == "nocheckout":
+    move("selftest-nocheckout", 'ck "a seat bin dir with no gh shim')
+elif arm == "gitenv":
+    move("selftest-gitenv", "# The real script against a bare remote")
+elif arm == "plaingh":
+    i = marked("selftest-plaingh")
+    assert 'PATH="$t/bare:$PATH" ' in s[i]
+    s[i] = s[i].replace('PATH="$t/bare:$PATH" ', "")
+elif arm == "envscrub":
+    s.pop(marked("selftest-envscrub"))
+elif arm == "envi":
+    i = marked("selftest-envi")
+    s[i] = '  tick_loop_self_test  # mut:selftest-envi' if "selftest_allowlisted" in "\n".join(s) else ""
+elif arm == "carry":
+    i = marked("selftest-envi")
+    assert "env -i PATH=" in s[i]
+    s[i] = s[i].replace("env -i PATH=", 'env -i SPY_REAL_GIT="${SPY_REAL_GIT-}" PATH=')
+elif arm == "pathfirst":
+    i = marked("selftest-envi")
+    lit = 'PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:${BASH%/*}"'
+    assert lit in s[i]
+    s[i] = s[i].replace(lit, 'PATH="$PATH"')
+    k = marked("seatbin")
+    assert s[k - 1].startswith("SEAT_BIN=") and s[k + 1] == "export PATH"
+    block = s[k - 1:k + 2]
+    del s[k - 1:k + 2]
+    i = marked("selftest-envi")
+    s[i:i] = block
+elif arm == "allowlist":
+    i = marked("selftest-allowlist")
+    assert '*" $v "*) ;; *)' in s[i]
+    s[i] = s[i].replace('*" $v "*) ;; *)', '*) ;; *" $v "*)')
+elif arm == "pipefail":
+    s.pop(marked("selftest-pipefail"))
+elif arm == "failopen":
+    i = marked("selftest-failclosed")
+    assert s[i].startswith("case ${1:-} in --self-test) refused=")
+    s[i] = 'case ${1:-} in --self-test) set -- --self-test-rows "${@:2}" ;; esac  # mut:selftest-failclosed'
+elif arm == "bound":
+    i = marked("selftest-bound")
+    assert "pr_bounded tick_loop" in s[i]
+    del s[i]
+else:
+    assert arm == "whole"
+open(p, "w").write("\n".join(s))
+PY
+  bash -n "$m/$L" || { echo "$arm: NOT RUN, the mutant does not parse"; return; }
+  bare bash "$m/$L" --self-test > "$d/$arm.log" 2>&1; rc=$?
+  echo "$arm: $(tail -n 1 "$d/$arm.log") rc=$rc"; rows "$d/$arm.log"
+}
+
+channels() { # every channel in parallel, one line each
+  local c b=$BASH x=$d/ch o
+  mkdir -p "$x"
+  local -a names=() fenv=()
+  while read -r o; do [ "$o" = exec ] || names+=("$o"); done < <(compgen -b)
+  names+=(git mktemp python3 sed grep env bash head tr cat chmod mkdir cp rm mv date sleep timeout kill tail wc cut sort dirname pwd)
+  run1() { # <channel> [env args...]: one whole self-test under that caller
+    local c=$1 v=$x/victim-$1.git rc; shift
+    mkdir -p "$x/calls-$c"; (throwaway_git_env; throwaway_git_init "$v" -q --bare) || return
+    (cd "$x" && env HPO_HEARTBEAT_REMOTE="$v" TICK_RC=1 "$@" "$d/src/$L" --self-test) > "$x/$c.log" 2>&1; rc=$?
+    echo "channels $c: $(tail -n 1 "$x/$c.log") rc=$rc fn-calls=$(ls "$x/calls-$c" | grep -c .) victim-refs=$(git -C "$v" for-each-ref | grep -c .)" > "$x/$c.line"; }
+  fdefs() { # <channel>: the function corpus, as a BASH_ENV file's text
+    local i=0 n; for n in "${names[@]}"; do i=$((i + 1)); printf '%s() { >> %q; }\n' "$n" "$x/calls-$1/fn-$i-${n//[^a-z0-9]/_}"; done; }
+  while IFS= read -r c; do fenv+=("BASH_FUNC_${c%%()*}%%=()${c#*()}"); done < <(fdefs fn-all)
+  printf 'exec() { if [ "${1:-}" = /usr/bin/env ]; then >> %q; return 0; fi; builtin exec "$@"; }\n' "$x/calls-shellopts-posix/exec" > "$x/execfn-posix"
+  fdefs bashenv-all > "$x/bashenv-all"; echo ">> $x/calls-env/sourced" > "$x/envfile"
+  mkdir -p "$x/pbin"; for o in bash env git python3; do printf '#!/bin/sh\n>> %q\nexit 1\n' "$x/calls-path/$o" > "$x/pbin/$o"; chmod +x "$x/pbin/$o"; done
+  run1 fn-all "${fenv[@]}" "$b" & run1 bashenv-all BASH_ENV="$x/bashenv-all" "$b" &
+  run1 fn-exec "BASH_FUNC_exec%%=() { if [ \"\${1:-}\" = /usr/bin/env ]; then >> $x/calls-fn-exec/exec; return 0; fi; builtin exec \"\$@\"; }" "$b" &
+  run1 posix POSIXLY_CORRECT=1 "BASH_FUNC_exec%%=() { if [ \"\${1:-}\" = /usr/bin/env ]; then >> $x/calls-posix/exec; return 0; fi; builtin exec \"\$@\"; }" "$b" &
+  run1 shellopts-posix SHELLOPTS=posix BASH_ENV="$x/execfn-posix" "$b" &
+  run1 noexec SHELLOPTS=noexec "$b" & run1 opts SHELLOPTS=errexit:nounset:xtrace BASHOPTS=execfail:extglob "$b" &
+  run1 env ENV="$x/envfile" "$b" & run1 path PATH="$x/pbin:$PATH" "$b" & run1 ifs IFS=/ "$b" &
+  wait; cat "$x"/*.line
+  # The null controls: each channel's instrument records a call when one is made.
+  local -a fctl=(); mkdir -p "$x/calls-fn-ctl" "$x/calls-bashenv-ctl" "$x/calls-env-ctl" "$x/calls-path-ctl" "$x/qbin"
+  while IFS= read -r c; do fctl+=("BASH_FUNC_${c%%()*}%%=()${c#*()}"); done < <(fdefs fn-ctl)
+  env "${fctl[@]}" "$b" -c 'cd /; git status; mktemp; exit 0'
+  fdefs bashenv-ctl > "$x/bashenv-ctl"; env BASH_ENV="$x/bashenv-ctl" "$b" -c 'cd /; git status; mktemp; exit 0'
+  echo ">> $x/calls-env-ctl/sourced" > "$x/envfile-ctl"; env ENV="$x/envfile-ctl" "$b" --posix -i -c : 2>/dev/null
+  printf '#!/bin/sh\n>> %q\n' "$x/calls-path-ctl/git" > "$x/qbin/git"; chmod +x "$x/qbin/git"; env PATH="$x/qbin:$PATH" "$b" -c 'git status'
+  for c in fn bashenv env path; do echo "channels null control $c: fn-calls=$(ls "$x/calls-$c-ctl" | grep -c .)"; done
+  echo "channels corpus: ${#names[@]} function names"
+}
+
+echo "rev $sha"
+for arm in "$@"; do
+  case $arm in
+    branch|detached|gitdir|shim|level) shape "$arm" ;;
+    whole|nocheckout|gitenv|plaingh|envscrub|envi|carry|pathfirst|allowlist|pipefail|failopen|bound) mutant "$arm" ;;
+    channels) channels ;;
+    *) echo "unknown arm '$arm'"; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done

+    ):

+            sent = [w[1] for w in sim(limits=limits, **kw)["writes"]]
+            print(f"{label:20s} sensor {'set' if sensors else 'unset':5s} writes {len(sent)}  "
+                  f"lowest {min(sent):.1f}  highest {max(sent):.1f}")
+    # The class the part-3 review left open: a high-limit sensor reading at

+    step_up = {"plan_kw": [0.53] * 8 + [1.2] * 16, "clamp": (10.0, 27.6)}
+    for unit in ("return", "flow"):
+        for offset in (None, -5.0, 0.0, 0.05, 0.1):
+            gate = pa._gate_c(Coord(unit=unit).arbiter_inputs())

+            sent = [w[1] for w in sim(unit=unit, limits=(None, limit), **step_up)["writes"]]
+            name = "unset" if limit is None else f"{limit:.2f}"

diff --git a/dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-PUSHER-CENSUS-ESCAPE.md b/dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-PUSHER-CENSUS-ESCAPE.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..6460e7b46c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-PUSHER-CENSUS-ESCAPE.md
@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+# R10-RCA-PUSHER-CENSUS-ESCAPE: pull requests merged `instrument-self-tests` reds their own diffs introduced
+
+The root-cause seat's analysis for the class R10-INTRODUCED-REDS-BARRIER
+barriers, landed by that group's fixer in the root-cause seat's terms (triage
+`dev/programme/triage/s6-batch200.md#P626`). Every figure below was re-measured
+at the fixer's merge base `60413046e3` on 2026-11-11 (`date -u` 14:17Z), by the
+command beside it. Carried figures are marked as carried. Run and job reads
+use `A=repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer`.
+
+## 1. The defect
+
+#3425 (`ee64358be`) merged with `governance / instrument-self-tests` red on
+four steps that its own diff turned red. The four are the sweep template
+render and the three `pr_args.sh` census steps (the PR opener, the PR argument
+builder and the PR updater). From that merge on, every push to `main` reads
+red on the same four steps. Enumerator, the built check at each merge's
+second parent against the merge base of its parents:
+
+    m=ee64358be; python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py introduced \
+      $(git rev-parse $m^2) --base $(git merge-base $m^1 $m^2)
+
+It prints 4 `INTRODUCED` lines and exits 1 at `c93903f075` against
+`a7628041dc` (head job 130479299736, base job 130352715261). The same
+command for #3361 (`8652aa65ce`) prints 2 lines (the two `selftest_scope.py`
+steps) and exits 1 at `825f549270` against `b8f67a7751` (head job
+129632490622, base job 129479891231). Main was still red when this was
+measured, 3.06 h after #3425's merge
+(`git log -1 --format=%cI ee64358be` = 11:13:48Z): the push job of
+`0a2139b1d` (130543139624) is red on the same four steps plus the push-only
+drift step.
+
+Instances: 2 merges measured (#3361 and #3425). The root-cause seat counted
+3, #3425 twice because two independent causes (`c966df873`, the remerge
+exit-code change, and `c6c04f21b`, the plan-beat cap hand-off) reached it.
+That attribution is carried, not re-measured. A scan of every merge since
+the ruling was not run: 137 first-parent commits
+(`git rev-list --first-parent --count 234ff52c75..origin/main`), each one
+filtered check-run read, would answer it. Until then, 2 is a lower bound.
+
+## 2. The cause
+
+`instrument-self-tests` is in no required set: decision 0013's
+`HPO_JOB_GRADES: nothing` boundary keeps the self-tests out of any grading
+job. The 2026-11-07 ruling (`234ff52c75`, committed 2026-11-07T19:15:02Z)
+narrowed the reds a body owes an answer to the set
+`merge_train.py owed-reds` prints. The job is outside that set. So #3425's
+body owed no `## Red checks` line, `classify` printed GREEN over the required
+contexts, and no reviewer rule read the job. The merges fell 2.39 d (#3361)
+and 3.67 d (#3425) after the ruling, by the commit dates of `8652aa65ce`,
+`ee64358be` and `234ff52c75`.
+
+## 3. The process state
+
+**(d), the preconditions changed.** Before the ruling, `pr-contract` made a
+body answer every red at the head, so an introduced self-test red needed an
+answer and drew a reviewer's block. The ruling removed that obligation for
+non-required checks, correctly for reds inherited from `main`. It removed the
+backstop for reds a pull request introduces too, and no process noticed that.
+The comment above the job in `.github/workflows/governance.yml` still said
+`pr-contract` made the body answer such a red.
+
+## 4. The cost test
+
+- The defect costs main red from the merge until a hotfix lands. #3425's
+  red was 3.06 h and still standing when measured, so that is a lower bound.
+  The root-cause seat's figure of about 6 h per occurrence (main red plus
+  seat-hours), at about 0.6 occurrences per 17 h release cycle, is carried.
+- The countermeasure (C1) costs nothing on a head whose `instrument-self-tests`
+  job did not conclude failure, beyond the check-run read the caller already
+  makes. On a red head it adds one filtered check-run read at the base and one
+  job-step read per side. `review_packet.introduced_reading` at `c93903f075`
+  measured 2.53 s for its four reads, the head's filtered listing included.
+- The class reddens `main`, which meets the owner's bar without a percentage.
+
+## 5. The countermeasures
+
+- **C1, built (R10-INTRODUCED-REDS-BARRIER).** `merge_train.introduced_at` is
+  the one rule. A step concluded `failure` at the head and not at the latest
+  concluded run at the merge base is INTRODUCED. The push-only drift step
+  (`Refuse a self-test read set the committed table misses`) is excluded. No
+  base run counts every head red. A step skipped by scoping concludes
+  `skipped`, so it is never red. An unreadable input fails closed.
+  `classify --pr` reads an introduced red as RED, so `bus.sh dispatch` and a
+  cloud reviewer's wait both stop on it. `review_packet.py` refuses it as
+  `introduced-red`. `fix-review.md` step 11 makes it a block. A red inherited
+  from `main` stays unowed, as the 2026-11-07 ruling holds.
+- **C2, refused as a barrier.** A census arm in `prepr.sh` covers one step,
+  not the class. It is the recorded fallback.
+- **C3 and C5, refused.** C5 costs 431 s or more per `prepr.sh` run (carried).
+- **C4, refused.** Making `instrument-self-tests` required conflicts with
+  decision 0013's `HPO_JOB_GRADES: nothing` boundary.
+
+## 6. The detector shown to detect
+
+The acceptance pairs, all through
+`python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py introduced <head> --base <base>`:
+
+| pair | INTRODUCED | rc |
+|---|---|---|
+| `c93903f075` (#3425 head) against `cbd23f1c8b` | 4 | 1 |
+| `cbd23f1c8b` against `f24d107bd7` (both red on the drift step alone) | 0 | 0 |
+| `0a2139b1d` against `ee64358be` (both red on the same 4 steps) | 0 | 0 |
+
+The third row is the inherited-red control: removing the base subtraction
+turns it to 4 with rc 1. The second row is flat under that mutation, because
+its only red is the excluded drift step. The root-cause seat's scratch probe
+(a head-versus-base comparison of job step conclusions over saved job JSON)
+reproduced the first two rows; it stays out of the tree, and the built check
+replaces it.

index 0000000000..f30cb4c82b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-REPLAY-CLASS-RERECORD.md
@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+# R10-RCA-REPLAY-CLASS-RERECORD
+
+**Defect.** The scheduled nightly at d08ed31049 (run 42934263129) read the
+synthetic clean cpu_ratio 1.7266 at class ref40 under that class's budget
+floor 1.9937. The budget rested on two draws that predate 17bb738485 (one BLAS
+ThreadpoolController, #3349), which cut the cycle's CPU on CI's runners to
+0.61-0.66x.
+
+**Cause.** The cut is a level shift in every class's cpu_ratio. The re-record
+procedure re-derives the classes a run has drawn since the change. Its unit,
+the drawn class, is wrong: the runner classes that were not drawn since the
+shift kept budgets centred on pre-shift readings, and so will fail the same way
+when next drawn.
+
+**Process state: (c)** the stated re-record procedure was obeyed and its unit
+is wrong.
+
+**Countermeasure.** `level_shift_offenders` (tests/replay.py), the
+`cycle_cost:level_shift` control, orders each class's clean draws by created
+time. A level shift at T is every draw at or after T under the floor
+(budget/2) that the draws before T derive. Every other class must then hold a
+draw at or after T, or a declared cut (`COST_CUTS`) must explain the shift;
+otherwise it names "class X rests wholly on draws before the shift class Y
+shows at T" and prints the classes examined. Registered in
+tools/policy/field_coverage.mjs as the `replay_cuts` arm;
+`replay_draws.py shift [--table T] [--no-cuts]` runs it over any table.
+
+**Demonstration** (`replay_draws.py shift --no-cuts --table <tsv>`, tables from
+`git show <sha>:tests/replay_cost_draws.tsv`):
+
+| table | result |
+|---|---|
+| d08ed31049 | red, names ref23, ref28, ref31, ref38, ref40, ref53 |
+| 6715d97332 | green, 7 classes examined |
+| 078780e687 | green, 7 classes examined |
+| fix head, `--no-cuts` | red (the cut declaration dropped) |
+| fix head | green, 7 classes examined |
+
+**Cost.** One pass over a 7-class TSV inside tests/replay.py; no extra CI job.

diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/CENSUS.md b/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/CENSUS.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..ded48ca794
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/CENSUS.md
@@ -0,0 +1,149 @@
+# R11-PROTECTION-CENSUS (round 10): the required set, sorted by what each check reads
+
+Read-only study, no production or tool code. Written without `gh` or an API
+token. The classification below needs none: each check's steps are in the tree.
+Only the per-head check conclusions of PRs outside the ledger, and the job logs
+of the main `tests / ci-ratchet` reds, are **UNREAD**.
+
+## Rule (applied to every check, never to a name)
+
+A check is **product** when a step of its job runs the shipped code or its
+metadata: `custom_components/`, `blueprints/`, the card, the HA manifest, HACS
+metadata. It is **programme** when its steps read only the governance corpus,
+pull-request bodies, rosters, the test-selection machinery, CI timings or
+archscore. A job with both says so; it is placed by its purpose and the
+mixed part is named.
+
+## Sources and enumerators
+
+| figure | enumerator | prints |
+|---|---|---|
+| required contexts | `python3 -c "import json;r=json.load(open('tools/ci/fixtures/ruleset/ruleset_23698884.json'));print(len([c for x in r['rules'] if x['type']=='required_status_checks' for c in x['parameters']['required_status_checks']]))"` | 17 |
+| recorded test scripts / scripts whose closure reaches `custom_components/` or `blueprints/` | `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('tests/closures.json'))['closures'];p=[k for k,v in d.items() if any(f.startswith(('custom_components/','blueprints/')) for f in v)];print(len(d),len(p))"` | 33 29 |
+| the 4 scripts that reach no product file | same, `sorted(set(d)-set(p))` | `tests/arch_score.py tests/ha_contract.py tests/layout.py tests/md_tables.mjs` |
+| main-push red-job rows | `python3 -I dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/main_reds.py \| wc -l` | 28 |
+| ... by run conclusion and job | `... main_reds.py \| awk '{print $3,$4}' \| sort \| uniq -c` | 8 failure `gate`, 8 failure `tests` (the ci-ratchet job), 6 cancelled `gate`, 6 cancelled `tests` |
+| PR-head ledger | `tail -1 dev/audit/rca/ci-red/entries_v7.1.2.tsv` | `ENTRIES 18 PRS 14` |
+| `harness_headers.py` reds | `grep -c harness_headers dev/audit/rca/ci-red/entries_v7.1.2.tsv` | 4 (#3180, #3189, #3208, #3242) |
+| delivery files, all rounds | `ls dev/programme/delivery \| wc -l` | 1614 (no round-10 denominator is claimed) |
+
+Null control: `main_reds.py | awk '$1==4080||$1==4107||$1==4116' | wc -l` prints 0 (those runs are `success`).
+
+## The 17 required contexts, classified (9 product, 8 programme)
+
+Context list: the ruleset fixture named in the first enumerator row.
+
+| # | context | job (file:line) | what its steps run | side |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | `fast (3.14)` | tests.yml:163 | `tests/run.sh` with RUN_PART=fast; 29 of 33 recorded scripts reach product files; `arch_score*.py` are skipped here (run.sh:657-659), `layout.py`, `md_tables.mjs`, `ha_contract.py` run here and read no product file | **product**, mixed: also runs programme-rule scripts (`harness_headers.py`, instrument self-tests) |
+| 2 | `browser` | tests.yml:503 | `tests/plan_view.py`, `tests/card_browser.mjs` (card layout in Chromium) | **product** |
+| 3 | `typing` | tests.yml:675 | `tests/typing_ruler.py` (mypy --strict ruler, three ratcheted numbers) | **product** |
+| 4 | `mutation` | tests.yml:1036 | `tests/mutation_table.py` over production files the diff touched | **product** |
+| 5 | `hassfest` | hassfest.yml:14 | `home-assistant/actions/hassfest` on the manifest | **product** |
+| 6 | `validate-hacs` | validate.yml:14 | `hacs/action` | **product** |
+| 7-9 | `Analyze (actions)`, `(javascript-typescript)`, `(python)` | codeql.yml `analyze` | CodeQL over the tree; `tools/pr/codeql_scope.py` decides skip-with-stand-in. The python and javascript legs read product code; the `actions` leg reads the workflows (programme files). Counted product as a set; the `actions` leg is the exception. | **product** (3), `actions` leg reads programme files |
+| 10 | `briefs` | tests.yml:602 | `tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs` over wave rosters | **programme** |
+| 11 | `closure-scope` | tests.yml:1749 | `tests/lane_skip.py`, `tests/closure.py`: decides which lanes may skip | **programme** (test-selection machinery) |
+| 12 | `closures` | tests.yml:1966 | `tests/derive_closures.sh` and `closure.py`: re-records and checks the measured closures | **programme** |
+| 13 | `policy-docs` | governance.yml:61 | policy lint, rules_sync, fragments_sync, machinery ratchet, CODEOWNERS gap | **programme** |
+| 14 | `wave-script` | governance.yml:1664 | `check-wave-script.mjs`, agreement lane, `fold_ledger.py` | **programme** |
+| 15 | `env-matrix` | governance.yml:1552 | `policy_lint_envmatrix.mjs`: declared environment shapes of the governance checks | **programme** |
+| 16 | `pr-contract` | pr-contract.yml:40 | PR-body contract, figure lint, version-edit refusal, `carry_audit.py`; **also** `tools/ci/codescan_wait.py` lists the open code-scanning alerts as reds | **programme**, with one product duty: it is the only check that turns a CodeQL alert into a red |
+| 17 | `budget-raise-gate` | budget-raise-gate.yml:57 | `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py`: owner approval of a budget raise | **programme** |
+
+Sizing for round 11: the product-only set is contexts 1-9 (9 of 17, 8 dropped).
+Two decisions the study cannot make and a round-11 seat must: (a) the CodeQL
+alert duty of `pr-contract` (row 16) has no home in a product-only set unless it
+is moved into the CodeQL legs or kept; (b) `fast` still grades programme-rule
+scripts (`harness_headers.py`, instrument self-tests), so splitting those out of
+`fast` is a further move, priced by the 5 `fast` reds below that those scripts
+caused. `hassfest` and `pr-contract` also have a second definition in ci.yml
+(224, 270); the ruleset names the context, not the file.
+
+## Not required contexts that appear in the ledgers
+
+| name | read | side |
+|---|---|---|
+| `tests / ci-ratchet` | tests.yml:2301-2318: runs only on push to `refs/heads/main`, comment says not a required context; `tests/ci_ratchet.py` docstring: measures `script_runs_per_push` and `critical_path_minutes` from Actions run timings, plus archscore counts | **programme instrument**, not required |
+| `gate` | not in the 17 and its steps were not read in this study | **UNREAD**, not required |
+| `tests / replay`, `prelude`, `instrument-self-tests` | not in the 17 | not required; steps UNREAD |
+
+## Main-push reds (28 rows, 14 runs)
+
+Each of the 14 runs carries a red `tests / ci-ratchet` job and a red `gate`.
+Runs 4009, 4015, 4028, 4035, 4046, 4055, 4056, 4128 concluded `failure`; runs
+4036, 4037, 4038, 4040, 4044, 4045 concluded `cancelled`. In all six cancelled
+runs the `tests / ci-ratchet` job itself concluded `failure` (counted from
+`runs_red4.json` job conclusions by `main_reds.py`, which prints only
+`failure` jobs and printed all 14), so "cancelled" is the run's conclusion and
+says nothing of the job's cause. Cause of every one of the 14 ci-ratchet reds:
+**UNREAD** (job logs are not in the tree). No infrastructure class is assigned.
+
+Class: the 14 ci-ratchet rows are reds of a **programme instrument** that is
+not a required context; the 14 `gate` rows are not a required context either.
+These 28 rows are therefore exactly the class a product-only set stops
+grading, not rows "said nothing about". They are not a product-check signal.
+
+## PR-head reds (18 rows) re-sorted by required context
+
+Same rows and same causes as the previous cut; the new column is the side of
+the required context that carried the red (1-17 above), or "n/r" for a name
+outside the 17. Class column unchanged where the cause is read.
+
+| PR | head | red | class | context side |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 3167 | 7637d66 | tests / replay | real catch (timing budget; runner noise possible) | n/r |
+| 3167 | 4e4bb29 | gate | infrastructure (cancelled run) | n/r |
+| 3180 | 3f7777a | tests / fast, tests / closures | real catch: `harness_headers.py` rule on the PR's own harness | `fast` (product, but cause is a programme rule) + `closures` (programme) |
+| 3181 | bb730c1 | gate | infrastructure (CodeQL python cancelled) | n/r (the cancelled leg is product) |
+| 3189 | fd9c5ba | tests / fast | real catch (`harness_headers.py`) | product check, programme-rule cause |
+| 3195 | 6f742a3 | tests / typing | real catch (9 no-untyped-call) | **product** |
+| 3195 | c383169 | prelude, gate | infrastructure (prelude wait expired); also real: 8 unpinned sites | n/r |
+| 3195 | 611e1aa | gate (tests / mutation) | real catch (unpinned-site refusal; cured by bot commit) | **product** (`mutation`, via `gate`) |
+| 3204 | e5381d9 | gate | infrastructure (cancelled) | n/r |
+| 3208 | 327d83e | tests / fast | real catch (`harness_headers.py`) | product check, programme-rule cause |
+| 3211 | 1fca63c | gate | infrastructure (PR closed, run cancelled) | n/r |
+| 3217 | 1c42ca3 | gate | infrastructure (CodeQL python cancelled) | n/r |
+| 3219 | aca5009 | gate | infrastructure (+ body defect) | n/r |
+| 3227 | a52354e | instrument-self-tests, fast | real catch (`body_patch.sh:146`) | `fast`, cause is a programme script |
+| 3240 | 79cf40f | gate | grader skew | n/r |
+| 3242 | e836876 | tests / fast | real catch (`harness_headers.py`) | product check, programme-rule cause |
+| 3244 | a258212 | gate | grader skew | n/r |
+| 3244 | 8bc540e | pr-contract / gate | real catch (CodeQL alert 50, `py/jinja2/autoescape-false`) | **programme** context carrying a product-code alert |
+
+Counts, each by hand from the table (18 rows): real catch 9, infrastructure 7,
+grader skew 2.
+
+Rows moved by the re-applied rule (all prior classes kept, sides added or
+changed):
+- the 28 main-push rows: from "product check `ci-ratchet`" to programme
+  instrument, non-required (the block);
+- 3180 `tests / closures` is programme (it was not separated);
+- the 5 `fast` rows (#3180, #3189, #3208, #3227, #3242) are a product check
+  whose red was caused by a programme rule or script, not by product code:
+  `grep -c harness_headers` is 4 (the 5th is `body_patch.sh` in #3227);
+- 3244 `pr-contract` is a programme context whose red was a product-code alert;
+- `gate`, `replay`, `prelude`, `instrument-self-tests` are placed "n/r", not
+  guessed.
+
+## Which reds would have reached main under a product-only set (contexts 1-9)?
+
+Rows whose every required red is programme or n/r stop being graded: 3167
+(both), 3181, 3195 c383169, 3204, 3211, 3217, 3219, 3240, 3244 a258212, and
+3244 8bc540e: **11 of 18**. Rows with a product context graded: 3180, 3189,
+3195 6f742a3, 3195 611e1aa, 3208, 3227, 3242: **7 of 18** (11 + 7 = 18).
+Among the 11: infrastructure 7, grader skew 2, real catch 2. One real catch
+is **3167 `tests / replay`**, which is n/r today, so no required-set change
+touches it. The other is **3244 8bc540e**, the CodeQL alert enforced only by
+`pr-contract`: the one catch a product-only set loses unless the alert duty
+moves (decision (a) above).
+
+Verdict: **the ledgers do not show a product-only set missing a catch except
+via `pr-contract`'s alert duty**; 28 main-push rows and 11 PR rows are
+programme or non-required reds. Decision stays tvofi's.
+
+## Limits
+
+14 PRs are covered; per-head conclusions for the rest need the API
+(`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_red_list_lag.py --rows`, needs a token), classed by
+the table above. The `gate` job and the n/r names were not read.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/main_reds.py
@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Rows for the main-push side of the census: one row per red job per ci.yml
+push run in runs_red4.json. A run with no red job yields no row (null control).
+    python3 -I dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/main_reds.py
+"""
+import json, pathlib
+p = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "harnesses/r10_rca_ci_critpath_3/runs_red4.json"
+for r in json.load(open(p))["workflow_runs"]:
+    for j in r["jobs"]:
+        if j["conclusion"] == "failure":
+            print(r["run_number"], r["head_sha"][:9], r["conclusion"], j["name"], sep="\t")

index 0000000000..e574275383
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/governance/roles/standing.md
@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+# The standing seats' shared terms
+
+Binds `standing-merge.md`, `standing-dispatch.md` and `proposal-triage.md`.
+
+## Wait
+
+End a turn only when nothing is owed. Otherwise wait in a `run_in_background`
+shell loop that touches your alive file, and its `FILE.d/<id>` entry, every
+25 s while your pid answers `kill -0`, and exits on a queue change or at the
+window's end, so its exit wakes the turn. A detached `nohup` wakes nothing. No
+tracked loop script (P51); the loop writes no pid into the alive file.
+
+## Reads
+
+Each Bash call starts in the seat's original directory, so every read names
+its cwd-safe instrument:
+
+| read | instrument |
+|---|---|
+| a PR body | `tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --pr-body` and `tools/audit/carry_audit.py check --body` |
+| a PR's state | `pull_request_read` (`web-fragments.md`); print `UNREADABLE` on an error or an empty answer |
+| handoff refs | `tools/audit/seat/bus.sh orphans`, or `git -C <worktree>` |
+
+A hand-written pipeline (`| wc -l`, `grep -c`, a bare `git` or `gh`) is never a
+check result.
+
+## Autofix hold
+
+Dispatch a reviewer at a pull request's head H, or start a merge at H, only
+when no `mutation-autofix`, `closures-autofix` or `claims-autofix` job at H is
+queued or in_progress, and either a bot commit has moved the head (act at the
+new head) or every autofix job concluded with no push; a red one pushes
+nothing (`ci-autofix.md`). Read it with `tools/audit/seat/failure_logs.sh` or
+`pull_request_read` (`get_check_runs`). A dispatch at the handoff, before a
+pull request exists, has no check-runs and is outside the hold.
+
+## Recycle
+
+Recycle (tvofi, 2026-10-31) once your context passes about 150k tokens or you
+have run 4 h, whichever comes first, and only at a quiet point: no op of your
+own mid-step, no train, push or open you own in flight. Write a
+`STATE-HANDOFF` file in your seat directory (pending waits with targets,
+in-flight ops, queue positions, held lines and their release conditions, next
+actions), stop only your own loops by PID, and reply `HANDED`. A fresh seat
+starts from its brief plus that file.
+
+## Alive files
+
+`$HPO_STATE_DIR/alive/`, the directory `tools/audit/seat/hooks/liveness.py`
+reads; `HPO_ALIVE_STALE_MIN` sets staleness.

     "Owner specification for the savings baseline (tvofi, 2026-10-24, binding acceptance criterion). Actual consumption is calculated from the heat pump's power sensor. The baseline must use power levels similar to the ones recorded, simulated as a plain thermostat over the exact same price profile, for both space heating and DHW. The DHW baseline assumes the DHW thermostat is always on: no DHW windows. Savings are the cost of that baseline minus the metered actual cost, priced over the same profile.      "Correction to carry-d15-sav-volume-2 (D15 triage, 2026-10-24; derived ratios only). Withdrawn: \"an idle row writes no mode, so the DHW mode keeps the pump charging through plan-idle steps\". The owner's integration also owns the supply switch, and the ledger statistic it rested on, 7 of 8 idle steps after a DHW slot ran, is not evidence that the pump ran outside a planned slot. Three seams. (1) The ledger freezes `planned` at the step's first one-minute tick (`_observe`, custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_arbiter.py:1006-1010). That is the plan from before the mid-step re-solve, and the re-solve can move a DHW slot onto the current step. In the bundle, the 13:00 row reads planned dhw while the 13:13 solve's action for that same step is space 0.5 kW and dhw 0. `ran` is real metered pump draw of at least `on_threshold_kw` (0.25 kW) on any one-minute pass (pump_arbiter.py:1013-1015). `dhw` is the mode flag or a tank rise (pump_arbiter.py:1020-1026). (2) The arbiter never writes the switch (pump_arbiter.py:46). The switch is written once per coordinator cycle, from the new plan's step 0 (`_apply_action`, coordinator.py:7581-7595, after the solve at :5634). Cycles run every 15.39 min (median of 641) against 15-minute steps, at a phase spread uniformly through the step (quartiles 4.3, 8.2 and 11.4 min). So each switch-on lasts into the next step, and a slot written late in its own step starts the compressor in the following one: 3 of 4 planned DHW slots show no run in-slot. (3) Checked and refuted: the solve's switch schedule disagreeing with its ask. 0 of 672 published steps were switched on without an ask, or off with one. The bundle holds no switch-state history, so \"switch commanded off while draw continued\" can be neither confirmed nor ruled out. Owed: score each ledger step against the plan in force when the step's actuation happened (re-freeze `planned` at each cycle's adoption), and actuate the switch at step boundaries, from the arbiter's one-minute tick, rather than at the cycle phase. Controls: a synthetic install with the cycle phase at 0 and at 14 min books identical duty verdicts; a step whose plan changed mid-step is scored against the plan that actuated it; one mutant per seam. Add P7's record_row.py `HTTP Error 500` on main's push run, whose revisit trigger (\"a second 5xx instance\") is now met. The remaining 9 stops are content refusals (red CI 3, HOLDER worktree 4, stale carry 1, ledger merge 1), so 18% of train stops are pure transport. (2) The cause and the precedent. app_approve.sh l.104 `js=$(gh api \"repos/$1/pulls/$2\") || die` has three sibling reads (l.271 comments, l.406 CODEOWNERS, l.408 files), all single-shot, discarding stderr so the failure class is lost. app_push.sh already holds the house pattern (l.188-251: bounded RB_SLEEP*3^(n-1), 5/15/45 s, transport refusals distinguished from a genuine refusal, never retry-forever). Reuse that rule rather than inventing 10/30/60. (3) Classification, so it cannot mask a refusal. Retry only network/transport errors, HTTP 5xx, and 429 or a secondary-rate-limit 403 (honouring Retry-After). Anything else (401, 403-permission, 404, 422, or a body that parses but is wrong: head moved, no verdict, owned path) refuses at once, as today. After the budget it refuses with the last error text kept. Mutation-write calls (review POST, merge) are never retried by this rule; they keep their own guarded paths. (4) Ordering. PR 1, app_approve.sh's four reads plus self-test arms: no open PR or live handoff touches tools/pr/app_approve.sh, so dispatch now, ahead of R10-FLY-CARRY-DOC-CONTEXT (P17, same file), which gains an after-edge on it. PR 2, merge_train.py's GitHub reads and record_row.py's urlopen: after #2585 (CI-LAYOUT-P1: merge_train.py, record_row.py), #2584 (MAIN-GATE: merge_train.py) and #2524 (PUSHER-REAP: merge_train.py). Cost: ~25 lines in bash, ~20 in python, one shared rule stated once in INSTRUMENTS.md. Benefit: about 45 min of CI wait plus a relaunch for each transient stop (2 in about 30 h of trains), and one red main push run per 5xx. (5) Null control, in each self-test: a stub `gh` failing once with a transport error then answering passes, with exactly 2 calls logged. A stub answering 404, or a head mismatch, refuses after exactly 1 call (no retry masks a refusal). A stub failing 4 times refuses after the budget, naming the last error. A stub answering 500 to record_row twice then 200 records. Brief addition: \"bounded retry of GitHub READS only, app_push.sh's 5/15/45 s rule, retrying transport errors, 5xx, 429 and secondary-limit 403 and nothing else; fixtures: one transient then success (2 calls), 404 and a wrong head (1 call, immediate refuse), budget exhausted (refuse with the last error); PR 1 is app_approve.sh, PR 2 is merge_train.py and record_row.py after #2585, #2584 and #2524\".",

-    "Owner directive (tvofi, 2026-10-31): \"the architects 30% arch score improvement can be even higher if cheap enough, and each group that touches production code should aim to also improve the score by sound changes, gaming fully prohibited.\"\nFold into the round playbook and the contracts it names, as a policy change approved before merging:\n(1) dev/governance/roles/architect-planner.md: the dS >= +22.7 target, a 30% fall in the weighted geometric mean, is a FLOOR, not a cap. Each move past the floor carries its cost estimate beside its expected dS.\n(2) dev/governance/roles/fixer.md step 17 (and plan-review.md for the plan): a group whose diff touches production code also takes sound score-improving changes in the code it already touches, inside its size budget and seam: one owner per concern, removed duplication, fewer parameters, no layer violations. Its body states the archscore dS with its command.\n(3) Gaming stays fully prohibited, and the mechanism already exists: fix-review.md step 14 (metric-gamed: remove the mechanism; plant the same move with nothing improved), plus fixer.md 17's list of non-improvements.
