@@ -0,0 +1,118 @@
+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 159 (P571)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` line 254. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `dbd1ab5b07`. `failure_logs.sh`, `merge_train.py`, `tools/ci/gate.py` and `ci.yml`
+  are unchanged from `444cf62fab`.
+- The merge seat's own output, `s14/seat/merge/fl3355/` (`HEAD.txt` 03:56:43Z, `failing.tsv`).
+- The GitHub API, read at about 04:05Z (about 30 calls):
+  - the check-runs at `dee7a1fa45`, both pages;
+  - check-runs 130305517989 and 130305543232 by id, with their annotations;
+  - workflow runs 42818706376 and 42945740958;
+  - commits 98a544dba9 and 6f1e3cfd16;
+  - `total_count` at 15 heads `failure_logs.sh` has read since 2026-11-10.
+
+## P571: S14-FAILURE-LOGS-HIDES-OLDER-GATE
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, at a corrected cause and fix site. It repairs an observed wrong behaviour, and it
+is its own carry on R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE, not a fold into carry 18. The ruling also corrects carry
+18's deferral test, which the evidence shows never matches as written.
+
+Source: queue line 254 (2026-11-11T03:58:10Z, the merge seat, PR 3355 at dee7a1fa).
+
+Instances:
+- **The reds were real, and the tool did not list them.**
+  - Check-runs 130305517989 and 130305543232 are `gate`, `failure`, at head `dee7a1fa`, started
+    03:41:05Z and 03:43:02Z, in run 42818706376 (`CI edit`, attempt 3).
+  - The seat's `fl3355/failing.tsv` (03:56:43Z, before the 03:57Z re-runs) lists only
+    `governance / delivery-status` and `pr-contract / pr-contract`.
+- **The cause is not grouping.** `failure_logs.sh` lines 125-130 keep only completed failures
+  first, and then take the newest per name. A newer green therefore cannot hide an older red.
+  - I ran the script's own jq over the 3355 shape: two red `gate` entries, then a newer green one.
+    It prints `gate failure 2`, the newer red.
+  - A false premise would have looked like that jq printing nothing for `gate`.
+- **The cause is that it reads only the first page.**
+  - Line 125 calls `check-runs?per_page=100` with no `--paginate` and no page loop.
+  - The head holds 144 check-runs (`total_count`), and GitHub lists them by id, descending:
+    - page 1 is ids 130311468189 down to 130305614669, 100 entries, sorted descending;
+    - page 2 is 130305614454 down to 129809007326, 44 entries.
+  - Both reds' ids (130305517989 and 130305543232) are below page 1's last id. Even now one
+    green `gate` check-run, 130305563880, is on page 2.
+  - At 03:56Z the 36 check-runs the re-runs later created did not exist yet. About 90 surviving
+    entries sat above the reds, plus the failed jobs the re-runs replaced. That puts the reds at
+    or past the boundary. Today's reading shows the mechanism directly.
+  - A false premise would have looked like a head under 100 check-runs, or a red id above page
+    1's last id.
+- **How often it happens.** Of 15 heads that `failure_logs.sh` read since 2026-11-10 (the newest
+  out-dirs), 2 now hold more than 100 check-runs: `dee7a1fa45` (144, PR 3355) and `60a26fee42`
+  (121, PR 3341). The queue line's second instance, PR 3405 at `068074f0`, holds 179.
+  - These are today's totals. The totals at read time were at most these.
+- **"Newest red per name" also drops reds, as a second effect.** A head with two red `gate`
+  entries lists one. GitHub blocks on any red entry of a required context (batch 155, P567), and
+  `gate` is that context. So for `gate`, every red is the answer to "why is this PR blocked".
+- **Correction to carry 18 (P567), read from the same runs.**
+  - Carry 18 re-runs a red `gate` when "its output title is gate.py's deferral line, or [it]
+    comes from a run whose `sha=` names another head".
+    - **The title arm never matches.** Check-run 130305517989 has `output.title`, `summary` and
+      `text` all null. Its one failure annotation is "Process completed with exit code 1". The
+      deferral text (`gate.py` line 130: `run(s) [...] at this head are still being judged;
+      their gate decides`) is printed only into the job log.
+    - **The `sha=` arm matches every run.** `ci.yml`'s run-name (lines 21-32) puts `github.sha`
+      in `sha=`, and for a `pull_request` run that is the merge commit:
+      - 98a544dba9 (run 42818706376) has parents `cd36e79737` and `dee7a1fa45`;
+      - 6f1e3cfd16 (PR 3404's run 42945740958) has parents `63bcdcaad8` and `561edf4c8f`.
+  - So the arm fires on every `pull_request` run, and carry 18's real filter is only its second
+    condition (a green `gate` at the same head from a completed run).
+  - That condition is the sound one. Every gate at a head computes the same verdict from the same
+    sources (`gate.py`'s module doc, lines 30-36), so a red beside a completed green at one head
+    is a stale or deferred red.
+  - A false premise would have looked like a non-null deferral title, or a `sha=` equal to the
+    head.
+
+Cost:
+- **(1) `failure_logs.sh` reads every check-run at the head through the one paginated reader.** It
+  stops making its own single-page call.
+  - A `merge_train.py check-runs <sha> <owner/repo>` shell entry prints `Train._check_runs(sha)`
+    (line 1843, `--paginate`) as JSON lines. It sits beside the existing `job-log` entry
+    (`merge_train.py` line 653, "every Actions job-log read in the tree goes through here").
+  - `failure_logs.sh` slurps those lines into its existing jq.
+  - The paged read then follows whatever page fix carry P549 lands in the same file, in a cloud
+    seat too.
+- **(2) Every completed red of a required context is listed, not only the newest.** Today that
+  context is `gate`; the set is the one `merge_train.py` reads (`REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, line 397: `tools/policy/fixtures/required-contexts.json`), not a new list. Other names
+  keep "newest red per name".
+  - A red whose log holds `gate.py`'s deferral text prints `deferral` beside its job id.
+- **Self-test, in `failure_logs.sh`:**
+  - the fake `gh` serves 101 check-runs over two pages, with a red `gate` on page 2, and it is
+    listed;
+  - two red `gate` entries and a newer green are all listed, the reds each with their log;
+  - a deferral log is tagged and a plain failure is not;
+  - the null control: a one-page head with one red per name prints today's lines;
+  - a mutant that reads one page fails the page-2 case.
+  - The existing "red-then-green grouped to the newest" check stays for a non-required name.
+- **(3) The amendment to carry 18.** Its deferral test becomes: the red `gate` check-run's job log
+  holds `gate.py`'s deferral text (read through `merge_train.py job_log`), or a green `gate`
+  check-run from a completed run is at the same head.
+  - The title and `sha=` arms are dropped.
+  - Carry 18's self-test fixtures follow suit: titles null and `sha=` set to a merge commit, as
+    GitHub serves them.
+- Size: about 15 lines in `failure_logs.sh`, about 8 in `merge_train.py`, and the self-test cases.
+  Neither file has a row in `tests/structure_budgets.json`.
+
+Binding:
+- `failure_logs.sh` is the instrument that answers "why is this PR red". It silently answers from
+  the newest 100 check-runs, and the heads that sit longest in the train, the ones re-run most,
+  are the ones past 100.
+- Each miss cost the merge seat a hand read by job id: 3355, and 3405 before it.
+- Folding this into carry 18 would merge two different repairs, a diagnostic reader and the
+  train's re-run decision. They share one rule, so they are kept separate.
+- Correcting carry 18 now costs one sentence. Building it as written would ship a filter whose
+  first condition is always true and whose other arm is never true.
+
+Routing:
+- Two carries go to R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE, which owns `merge_train.py` and `failure_logs.sh`. It is in
+  progress as PR 3424 (handoff moved to `5e91c2cfe5`), so both carry the PART 2 prefix.
+- Carry files:
+  - `b159-P571.txt`: items (1) and (2);
+  - `b159-P571-c18.txt`: item (3), which names itself carry 18's amendment.

@@ -0,0 +1,172 @@
+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 160 (P572, P573)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` line 255. It also records the result of the P569
+sampler, which batch 157 left owed. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `dbd1ab5b07`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- Job log 130312858296 (pr-contract on PR 3424, run 42953123178), read once with
+  `gh api .../actions/jobs/130312858296/logs`, and grepped.
+- The open pull requests, read once with `gh api 'repos/.../pulls?state=open&per_page=100'`:
+  number, `base.sha` and head for each.
+- The P569 sampler's two logs, `s14/seat/triage/s14-5/rate2.log` and `s14-5/ghproc.log`, and the
+  beat journal `r10s6/beatd/*.log`.
+
+## P572: PR-CONTRACT-GRADER-SKEW
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, at a corrected cause that is wider than the proposal's. The fix goes to a new
+hotfix group, R10-HOTFIX-RESTORE-BASE-SKEW. The proposed self-test detector is REJECTED.
+
+Source: queue line 255 (2026-11-11T04:26:40Z, orchestrator s14, PR 3424 head f9c7952b).
+
+Instances:
+- **What was checked out.** pr-contract checked out the merge ref, not the head.
+  - Job log line 8746: `git checkout --progress --force refs/remotes/pull/3424/merge`.
+  - Line 8764: `HEAD is now at 427c4ca87 Merge f9c7952b... into c620ebba96...`. c620ebba96 is
+    main after #3417 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 8efacee48d c620ebba96` succeeds).
+- **What was restored, and from where.** The restore took the event's stale base commit.
+  - Job log line 8816: `PINNED: d08ed31049...`.
+  - Line 8819: `check source restored from d08ed31049...: 3 file(s) differ`.
+  - `pr-contract.yml` line 104 sets `PINNED` from `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`.
+  - Line 118 lists `tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py` among the files restored at line 135.
+  - `carry_audit.py` is not on that list. Lines 449-454 say CODEOWNERS covers it instead.
+- **Which file came from which ref.** This answers the proposal's open question. Each count is
+  `git show <ref>:<file> | grep -c`:
+
+  | ref | `def carry_receivable` in roster_lib.py | `carry_receivable` in carry_audit.py |
+  |---|---|---|
+  | d08ed31049 (PINNED) | 0 | 0 |
+  | c620ebba96 (the merge's base) | 1 | 3 |
+  | 427c4ca874 (the checkout) | 1 | 3 |
+
+  So `roster_lib.py` came from d08ed31049, through the restore. `carry_audit.py` came from the
+  merge ref, so from c620ebba96. The call at job log line 9038 then raised the AttributeError at
+  line 9040.
+- **Cause.** The event's `base.sha` is not the commit the merge ref was built on.
+  - The run checks out GitHub's merge commit, whose first parent is current main.
+  - It restores from `pull_request.base.sha`, which stays put while main moves.
+  - Files the restore takes and files it leaves are then two different mains. Any program the
+    restore leaves, importing a module the restore takes, can break when one main commit changes
+    both.
+  - The "stale-tree arm" the proposal suspected does not pick the files. Its NOTE (line 9024)
+    only chooses where the roster is read.
+- **Does a head push refresh `base.sha`?** Measured: no.
+  - For 15 of the 19 stale open PRs, the stale `base.sha` is an ancestor of their own head
+    (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <base> <head>`). The exceptions are 3382, 3420, 3425 and 3429.
+  - PR 3427's head was committed at 04:08Z, after #3417 merged at 02:38Z, and its base is still
+    stale.
+  - So `base.sha` tracks the last main the head took in, not the push. The proposal's workaround,
+    merging main into the head, is the one that works.
+- **Exposure.** 19 of 23 open PRs have a `base.sha` that lacks 8efacee48d: 3379 3381 3382 3386
+  3387 3388 3390 3391 3398 3404 3419 3420 3423 3424 3425 3427 3428 3429 3355. Command: the pulls
+  read above, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8efacee48d <base.sha>` for each.
+  - Not measured: how many of them reach `carry_receivable`. Only that step's code path calls it.
+- **The class is wider than this one pair.** The same event base drives every restore site.
+  `git grep -c -E 'git checkout "?\$\{?PINNED' origin/main -- .github/workflows` gives:
+  - budget-raise-gate.yml 1, ci.yml 5, codeql.yml 1, governance.yml 4, pr-contract.yml 1,
+    tests.yml 6.
+  - Each one carries the same skew whenever a restored file and a file the restore leaves change
+    together on main.
+
+Cost:
+- **The fix: restore from the commit the checkout was built on.**
+  - For a `pull_request` event, a restore takes its source from the merge commit's first parent
+    (`HEAD^1` after the checkout), not from the payload's `base.sha`.
+  - It first asserts that the payload's `base.sha` is an ancestor of that parent, and refuses if it
+    is not.
+  - `HEAD^1` of GitHub's merge commit is a base-branch commit. The pull request cannot choose it,
+    so the security property the restore exists for (decision 0013) is kept.
+  - `merge_group` (`base_sha`) and the `inputs.base` dispatch fallbacks keep their current
+    meaning.
+- **Do not change the diff bases.** The restore source and the diff base are two different
+  meanings that currently share one value.
+  - `BASE_SHA`, `SINCE`, `PR_BASE`, `MACHINERY_BASE`, `PAYLOAD_BASE` and `tests.yml`'s `BASE` key
+    the pull request's own diff. For a diff, the merge base is the right base.
+  - The fixer splits the two meanings and changes only the restore source.
+  - Where one step uses `PINNED` as both, the fixer separates them in that step. It does not
+    re-key the diff.
+- **Size: M.**
+  - One shared resolution of the restore commit: a single step's output, or a script under
+    `tools/ci/` that every restore site calls. It is not 18 hand edits, so the next workflow
+    inherits it.
+  - Plus the 18 call sites.
+  - None of the six workflows has a row in `tests/structure_budgets.json` (`git show
+    origin/main:tests/structure_budgets.json | grep -c workflows/` gives 0).
+  - The workflows are code-owned, so the PR needs tvofi's review or the mandate.
+- **Mutation proof the fixer owes.** Replay PR 3424's merge ref 427c4ca874 with the old `PINNED`
+  (d08ed31049) and with the new one (`HEAD^1` = c620ebba96). The `carry_audit.py check` step must
+  go red under the old one and green under the new one.
+  - Null control: a PR whose `base.sha` equals its merge parent (for example one of the four fresh
+    PRs) gives the same result under both.
+
+Binding:
+- The cost of doing nothing is a red pr-contract on every exposed PR's next body edit. It is
+  already red on 3424, which is on the critical path. Each one costs a remerge of main and a
+  re-review of carries.
+- It recurs whenever one main commit changes a restored module together with a program the
+  restore leaves. #3417 was such a commit. Nothing on the list prevents the next.
+- The fix makes the restore and the checkout one ref by construction. That removes the class, not
+  this pair.
+- **REJECTED: the proposal's detector**, a pr-contract self-test with a planted old `roster_lib.py`.
+  - It pins one file pair. After the fix the skew cannot arise, so the self-test would guard a
+    state that can no longer occur.
+  - The fixer's replay above is the proof.
+  - Whether a cheaper detector should have caught this belongs to the root-cause seat. This is a
+    red check, so the red-check trigger of `defect-root-cause.md` applies. Triage does not
+    pre-empt the cost test.
+
+Routing:
+- A new group, R10-HOTFIX-RESTORE-BASE-SKEW. Severity high (a red pr-contract on a critical-path
+  PR, and 19 of 23 open PRs exposed). Kind instrument, lane IN.
+  - Files: `.github/workflows/{pr-contract,ci,tests,governance,codeql,budget-raise-gate}.yml`,
+    plus the one shared resolver.
+  - Brief: this ruling's Cost section.
+- It does not go to R10-BODY-CONTRACT, which also owns `pr-contract.yml`. That group is in
+  progress with 45 carries, and P551's five-carry split applies. This fix spans five workflows it
+  does not own.
+- Until it lands, a red `carry_audit.py check` with `AttributeError` on a stale-base PR is this
+  defect, and the workaround is merging main into the head.
+
+## P573: P569 sampler result (batch 157's owed split)
+
+Verdict: DEFER. Batch 157's DEFER of (a), the start-of-pass rate_limit guard in
+`tick_loop.sh`/`beat_jobs.py`, stands. Its condition is met only marginally, and even or marginal
+is not an ACCEPT.
+
+Source: batch 157 (P569), owed item: the per-caller split from the s14-5 sampler (03:11:16Z to
+04:31Z).
+
+Instances:
+- **The window.** 03:24:37Z-04:24:37Z (reset 1794371077): `awk '$3==1794371077' rate2.log`.
+  - The first reading is 60 used at 03:25:21 and the last is 4001 at 04:23:42, so the spend is
+    about 3941.
+  - The peak is 80.02%. It crossed 4000 by one call, 55 s before the reset. It did not exhaust.
+- **The split.** `ghproc.log` restricted to the same range: 1132 gh process-seconds, 911 distinct
+  gh pids. Shares are by process-seconds, then calls seen:
+
+  | bucket | process-seconds | share | pids | callers |
+  |---|---|---|---|---|
+  | tick | 320 | 28.3% | 306 | `orchestrator_tick.py` 315, `pr_cap`, `approve_held_runs` |
+  | beat | 252 | 22.3% | 105 | `plan_page.py` (plan-beat) 151 s over 14 pids; `beat_jobs`; `cancel_superseded`; `outside_intake`; `pulse`; `worktree_gc` only inside the beat disk pass 03:34:45-03:37:32 (journal `PASS ... disk start=03:34:45Z dur=167`) |
+  | relay | 3 | 0.3% | 3 | `cloud_relay.sh` |
+  | train | 179 | 15.8% | 151 | `merge_train.py`, `postmerge.py` |
+  | train, inferred | 134 | 11.8% | 110 | `worktree_gc.sh` 03:27:08-03:33:44, outside any beat disk pass and during the train's run; `roster_sync.py` |
+  | seats | 184 | 16.3% | 178 | |
+  | sweep-runner | 48 | 4.2% | 48 | `blind_spots.py`, `s9/sweep-runner`, every ~15 min |
+  | unattributed | 12 | 1.1% | 12 | |
+
+- **Scheduled (tick+beat+relay).** 575 s, 50.8% of process-seconds, but 414 of 911 pids, 45.4%
+  of calls seen.
+  - The measures disagree about the half because `plan_page.py`'s 14 calls are long.
+
+Cost: nothing is built.
+
+Binding:
+- The window passes 80% by one call and the scheduled share sits on the half. The decision
+  condition is therefore marginal on both arms.
+- An 80% guard would have shed under one minute of scheduled passes in this window, saving tens of
+  calls against a 5000 bucket that was not exhausted.
+- **What would reopen it:** one exhausting or above-90% window with scheduled callers at least
+  half by calls, measured through the gh shim once PR 3427 (R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE) merges.
+  - Calls under 1 s are under-sampled here. Cloud seats spend the same token from other hosts and
+    are invisible. This is a sample, not a count.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 161 (P574)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` line 256. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `dbd1ab5b07`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The tick's live output, `r10s6/tick.txt`, copied at 04:36Z (268 lines) to the triage scratch
+  directory, and `r10s6/owed-unactioned.json`, copied there as the state.
+- No GitHub API calls.
+
+## P574: OWED-CHECK-UNKEYABLE-CAP-LINE
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT. The fix is at the writer, with a pin that drives the writer's real output into the
+reader. The proposal's reader-side alternative, skipping the exact literal, is REJECTED. The fix is
+a carry to R10-TICK-RESIDUE (PART 2).
+
+Source: queue line 256 (2026-11-11T04:31:55Z, orchestrator s14).
+
+Instances:
+- **The writer.** `orchestrator_tick.py` lines 2426-2429 emit a flagged line when more than
+  `CAP_ORPHANS` (line 182, 20) handoffs are stranded:
+  `OWED handoffs capped at {CAP_ORPHANS} of {n}; the rest print next pass once these are
+  discharged`.

+  - That is R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE carry 13 (roster 943eb224e8). The group is not started,

+    changes, the previous review can be carried". A git automatic merge of main is in its CARRY

+- About 8 lines in `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh`. Its self-test's pending-ci arms (lines

+## P577: BOTTLENECK-MUTATION-VACUOUS
+
+Verdict: REJECT both arms:

+3 of 11 uncapped. Measured, it prevents the block on 1 of the 5 PRs. Its precision is low: 47
+survivors on the two heads where it catches anything, against the 3 sites the reviewers named.
+That is marginal at best.
+
+No new root-cause seat is owed. The class has one: `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-MUTATION-VACUOUS.md`.
+Its tools/ refusal (lines 111-118) waited on one number, and this ruling measures that number.
+The number confirms the refusal.
+
+The self-test-body noise found while measuring is DEFERRED. It is noise from `mutant_run`
+mutating self-test assertions, and its terms are below.
+
+Source: queue line 259, 2026-11-11T05:01:31Z, orchestrator s14. It comes from the beat's
+bottleneck row at 05:00:23Z: `block-class mutation-vacuous 31% (5/16 blocks) vs 30%`.
+
+Instances: the 11 sites the five verdicts name. Each site was checked against what
+`mutant_run.py --diff <merge-base>...<head> --list` generates at the head.
+- **Merge bases.** Each is `git merge-base origin/main <head>`:
+  - 3419 at 30c785330f;
+  - 3425 at d08ed31049;
+  - 3427 and 3428 at 63bcdcaad8;
+  - 3431 at 40fe1cae2e.
+- **What `mutant_run` can generate.** It mutates only added `*.py` lines (`mutant_run.py:209`),
+  outside `tests/` and `dev/` (`:66`). Each line gets statement-level operators only
+  (`mutate_line`, `:245`):
+  - `if`/`elif` statements become `False`;
+  - `return` becomes `pass`;
+  - comparison bounds;
+  - call statements become `pass`;
+  - the first numeric or bool constant is swapped.
+
+  It has no conjunct drop. It does not mutate an `if` inside an expression or a comprehension, and
+  it does not mutate string literals.
+- **PR 3419 at 245ddf78: 1 of 2 sites caught, and only uncapped.**
+  - 51 mutants are listed, all in `tools/ci/selftest_scope.py`.
+  - Site 1, the `governance.yml` settle line, is YAML. It is not generated.

+    1459-1460). It is generated as GUARD_OFF and RETURN_DEL, at list positions **50 and 51**.
+  - Measured in an isolated copy (`s14-7/mr/run3419.log`):
+    - unmutated: `99 checks, 0 failed` rc 0, in 4 s;
+    - mutant 1459: `0 failed`, so it SURVIVES;
+    - mutant 1460: `0 failed`, so it SURVIVES.
+  - Both are beyond prepr's default cap: `--max-mutants "${MUTANT_MAX:-40}"`, `prepr.sh:4491`.
+  - 19 of the 51 mutants sit inside `self_test()` (lines 809-1448), and they fill the cap first.

+  - 58 mutants are listed; 16 of them are in `tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py`.
+  - The reviewer's M3, deleting the `one_pr` clear, is listed as `orchestrator_tick.py:1220

+  - `hot-render` is a conditional expression, `plan_page.py:663-664 ... if r["hot"] else ""`.
+  - `hot-gates` and `hot-discharged` are comprehension conjuncts, `plan_page.py:235-236`.

+  - At the default cap of 40, 2 of 11 sites are caught (18%). Uncapped, 3 of 11 are (27%).

+  - 3419: 35 of 51 mutants survive. 19 are in production or `main()` code and 16 in `self_test()`.
+  - 3425: 12 of 16 survive, 10 of them in production code.

+Cost:
+- **(a) handoff REFUSE.**
+  - Benefit: 1 of 5 blocks removed in the sample. That is 1 review round plus 1 repair round, at
+    the 111-minute median quoted by the RCA (`R10-RCA-MUTATION-VACUOUS.md` section 5).
+  - Standing cost: one `mutant_run --diff` per tools/ handoff, 31-116 s in the sample. It also

+  - It needs a new roster field, which is an edit to the roster schema and lint.

+    each" (`prepr.sh:4495`).

+    span, plus one self-test arm.

+- No capped file is edited by this ruling.
+
+Binding:
+- **(a): REJECT.** The binding cost is precision against reach. It prevents the block on 1 PR of
+  5. 8 of the 11 sites are outside the operator set, so no tuning reaches them. And it would make
+  47 survivors blocking paperwork on the two heads it catches anything on, 38% of them mutations
+  of the self-test itself. Its trigger field exists on 0 of 439 groups.
+- **(b): REJECT.** It has the same reach of 1 of 5. The answering cost moves to every first-round
+  tools/ fixer, and it costs a hot-file change to `cloud_dispatch.py`. That is marginal, not
+  clearly positive.
+  - The orchestrator's per-repair hand request stays the orchestrator's call, with the two limits
+    measured above:
+    - a `tests/` diff gets 0 mutants;
+    - expression-level sites, conjuncts and non-Python files are never generated, so "zero
+      unanswered survivors" from `mutant_run` does not show that a verdict's named survivor is

+- **Root cause: not newly owed.**
+  - `defect-root-cause.md:89-95`'s audit-class clause counts judged findings and sweep seams. It
+    does not count review-verdict classes.
+  - This class already went through the friction route: `R10-RCA-MUTATION-VACUOUS.md`.
+  - That record's population-T refusal is "a refusal that depends on a number nobody has" (line
+    116): the cost of a tools/ mutation arm. That number is now measured. An arm exists

+## P578: DESIGN-REVIEW-OWED-NO-BOARD-LINE

+It reuses the refs `design_builds` already lists, so it adds one fetch per pass and no API call.
+
+Source: queue line 260, 2026-11-11T05:06:21Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+Instances:
+- **The gap in the tick.** The tick prints two design lines:
+  - `DESIGN OWED:` (`orchestrator_tick.py:1608`), only when no `design/<g>` ref exists;
+  - `DESIGN-BUILD:` (`:1660`, `ledger.py:621`), only on `Design review: approve <sha>` at the
+    tip (`ledger.py:123`).
+
+  A design tip newer than a `revise` verdict fits neither. The tick has no line for it, so a
+  revised design that nobody dispatches is invisible to the board.
+- **`owed_unactioned.py`** keys only the `FAMILY` prefixes at line 56. `DESIGN OWED` is not among
+  them, so even the existing designer line is never tracked as unactioned.
+- **The three cases named in the queue line, replayed at 05:06Z.** For each group: the design

+

+  |---|---|---|---|---|
+  | R10-STANDING-CONTRACTS-P2 | a249d768 | 00:43:43Z | 00:11Z | `revise 5bcd069c` |
+  | R10-ADVISOR-STEADY-START | d2d663c3 | 00:43:45Z | 00:12Z | `revise e29f9b4a` |
+  | R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING | abc57517 | 00:50:34Z | 00:17Z | `revise edf2ceb3` |
+
+  In all three, the verdict names a sha that is not the tip, and the last dispatch predates the
+  tip. The rule therefore fires 3 lines at 05:06Z.
+- **After the orchestrator acted.** Reviewers were dispatched at 05:07-05:08Z, and verdicts
+  `approve <tip>` landed at 05:15-05:17Z. Each verdict now names its tip, so the rule fires 0
+  lines for these three.
+- **Null control, at 05:20Z.** 4 of 29 designs have a verdict that does not name their tip:
+  r10-arch-docs-first, r10-hotfix-codeql-headroom, r10-orch-machinery and r10-user-docs-final.
+  All four groups are `done` at 33adcf993e, so a stage gate excludes them. The other 25 have a
+  verdict at the tip. The rule prints 0 lines at 05:20Z.
+- **Frequency and cost of the state, measured.** For each verdict commit in every
+  `design-verdict/<g>` history, I measured from the commit time of the tip that verdict names to
+  the first `dispatch/design-reviewer-<g>` commit at or after that tip
+  (`s14-7/design-lat.txt`, 51 verdicts).
+  - 33 of the 51 have a reviewer dispatch ref. The other 18 predate the dispatch refs.
+  - Median dispatch latency 0.8 h; p75 15.05 h.
+  - **15 of the 33 waited more than 2 h, 420.9 h in total.**
+  - The longest: r10-ceiling-probe 104.3 h; R10-ADVISOR-WHATIF 96.2 h; r10-fly-standing-contracts
+    60.1 h; R10-ADVISOR-STEADY-START 25.0 h; R10-STANDING-CONTRACTS-P2 24.2 h; R10-ARCH-DOCS
+    22.9 h.
+  - Caveat: a commit time is no later than its push, so these are upper bounds. Some waits may
+    have been deliberate holds. Even at a tenth, the state costs tens of hours of L/XL
+    critical-path wall time across the round.
+
+Cost:
+- **Code.** About 25 lines in `orchestrator_tick.py`, beside `design_builds` (`:1660`), plus one

+  - It adds one `git fetch` of the design and dispatch tips, needed for commit times. That is

+Binding:

+- This is a new line for an observed silent state, not repair of a low- or normal-severity

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 165 (P579)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` line 261. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `8f97247fc1`. Every `merge_train.py` line number below is at that commit.
+- The live train's log, `~/.local/state/hpo/merge_train/train.log`, snapshot of 19710 lines at
+  05:30Z (seat copy `s14-8/train-snap.log`). Line numbers below are in that snapshot.
+- Two scripts over that log, `s14-8/waits2.py` (output `s14-8/waits2.out`, `s14-8/waits3.out`).
+  A wait is a run of `beat: waiting <what> (poll k, t+Ns ...)` lines with the same `<what>` and a
+  rising `t+`; its length is the last `t+`. The spool is tracked from the log: an entry joins it
+  on `ADDED #n to the live train` or `spooled for the live train's next batch`, and it empties on
+  the drain line `ADDED #...: batch k of this train` (`merge_train.py:3857`) or a `BATCH ` line.
+  A wait is spool-blocked from the first poll at which the spool is non-empty. Its outcome is read
+  from the 11 lines after it: `SKIP #`, `stays skipped` or `past the N s cap` is skip; `merged` is
+  merged; anything else is other (55 of 75 "other" are `#n <head> ci red=[]`, a green head that
+  goes on to its merge).
+- No GitHub API calls.
+
+## P579: TRAIN-REJOIN-WAIT-BLOCKS-SPOOL
+
+Verdict: REJECT both arms (yield the rejoin wait to a non-empty spool; move a WAIT rejoin
+candidate into the spool). DEFER a critical-path-only yield, on the terms below.
+
+The instance is not a rejoin wait. PR 3355 is this batch's serial entry (`serial: #3355`, line
+19629). It was parked `[MAIN-MOVED]` on a base-branch policy refusal (line 19646), took the
+card-5 no-recarry path (line 19648; `merges_as_is`, `merge_train.py:2553`, called from
+`recarry`, `:2494`), and now waits in `wait_ci` (`:1905`) at its own head: the gate red there is
+read as a deferral while ci.yml run 42961218591 is unfinished (`:1951`), and the heartbeat is
+`wait_ci`'s (`:1988`). `Train.rejoin` (`:3709`) prints no `beat:` line at all, and the log has no
+`REJOIN #3355` line in this batch. Both arms as asked therefore move 0 of the 1 instance.
+
+Source: queue line 261, 2026-11-11T05:23:40Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+Instances:
+- **This instance.** `beat: waiting CI at dee7a1fa`, 24 polls, t+5596 s at the snapshot, cap
+  7320 s (`wait_cap_s`, `:3703`). Spool non-empty for the whole wait (`waits2.out`, top row:
+  `line 19651 ... t 5596 blk 5596`).
+- **The rejoin wait itself, whole log.** 18 `REJOIN #` outcomes: 15 RED, 1 head moved, 2 GREEN
+  (359 s and 7229 s after the skip). The rejoin is a minor share of spool blocking.
+- **The general mechanism the instance does show: a single-head `CI at` wait in a batch blocks
+  the spool.** Whole log (BATCH 20261016-183919 to 20261111-002834-b4, 26 days; 243 waits,
+  523,303 wait-s):
+  - wait ending in skip: 78 waits, 25 spool-blocked, **47,740 s** blocked, 147,040 PR-s;
+  - wait ending in merge: 50 waits, 11 spool-blocked, 23,471 s;
+  - other (mostly green, going on to merge): 75 waits, 38 spool-blocked, 64,387 s.
+- **Last 7 days** (from `BATCH 20261104`, line 9748; 256,345 wait-s):
+  - ending in skip: 53 waits, 13 spool-blocked, **17,228 s** (4.8 h), 36,635 PR-s;
+  - ending in merge: 37 waits, 7 spool-blocked, 18,633 s;
+  - other: 14 waits, 3 spool-blocked, 2,425 s.
+- **Rule applied per instance, as a yield to a non-empty spool on any single-head wait:**
+  - skip-ending waits: a pure gain, the whole blocked span: 17,228 / 256,345 = **6.7%** of the
+    train's waiting in 7 days; 47,740 / 523,303 = 9.1% over 26 days.
+  - merge-ending waits: a reorder, not a gain. The spool batch merges earlier and the waiting
+    head merges later; only the overlap of the two CI waits is saved, at most the blocked span
+    (18,633 s), and every yield moves main under the waiting head, which owes a re-grade
+    (`:2634` path) and on a strict ruleset a recarry.
+  - Upper bound with every blocked second counted as saved: (17,228 + 18,633 + 2,425) /
+    256,345 = 14.9%.
+- **Null control.** A spool-blocked count needs a spool: the same script reports 147 of 243
+  waits with an empty spool for their whole span (0 s blocked), so the measure does not count
+  every wait as blocked.
+
+Cost:
+- A yield in `merge_train.py` (9,430 lines, the train's hot file, owned by R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE,
+  part 2 open and unstarted): a spool check inside `wait_ci`'s serial callers after one poll, a
+  Stop that re-spools the waiting entry at its head and verdict, the drain, and a re-grade of
+  the yielded head on the moved main. About 40 production lines plus self-test arms for yield,
+  no-yield on an empty spool, and the re-spooled entry's re-grade: about 80 lines in all, and at least
+  one review round on the train's hot file.
+- `merge_train.py` has no row in `tests/structure_budgets.json` at `8f97247fc1`; no capped file.
+
+Binding:
+- **Both arms as asked: REJECT.** They act on `Train.rejoin`, and the instance is a `wait_ci`
+  in the serial path. Applied to this instance they move nothing.
+- **The general yield (any single-head wait, non-empty spool): REJECT.** It is new machinery on
+  an instrument, so it must clear 20% (`proposal-triage.md`, Machinery). The measured pure gain
+  is 6.7% of the train's waiting over 7 days (9.1% over 26), and even counting every blocked
+  second, merges included, it is 14.9%. The binding cost is a re-grade-on-moved-main branch in
+  the train's hot file for a gain under the bar.
+- **A critical-path-only yield: DEFER.** The instance's real cost is that main's red repair,
+  PR 3419, queues behind the wait. That is one critical-path instance in the log. It changes on
+  a second instance in which a critical-path PR sits in the spool for more than 30 minutes behind
+  a single-head wait; the owning group would be R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE part 2.
+- **Owed to the orchestrator, not a build:** this instance's wait ends by cap no later than
+  t+7320 s, about 06:00Z, or earlier when run 42961218591 concludes. A critical-path merge that
+  cannot wait for that is the orchestrator's operational call, through the merge seat (the live
+  train is pid 90895; a stopped train leaves the spool to start a train of its own, `:3838-3842`), under the never-slip ruling for the
+  critical path.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 166 (P580)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` line 262. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `a7628041dc`. Every `cloud_relay.sh` line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` `fc68214974`.
+- `tick-loop.log` in the state dir, its `TICK-PASS` and `TICK-RELAY` lines for 2026-11-10 and
+  2026-11-11. A `TICK-RELAY <end> relay=ok started=<start>` line gives one relay pass's length.
+- The relay's last pass output `tick.txt.relay.log`, and the mtimes of the relay's fold files
+  `cloud-fold-<topic>.md` (written just before `carry_fold.py`, `:827`) and `cloud-fold.out`
+  (written by `body_push.sh`, `:840`) in the state dir.
+- One timed replay of the arm's read loop (`:812-818`), run from a seat worktree at 06:00Z.
+- No GitHub API calls.
+
+## P580: CARRY-FOLD-ARM-REJUDGES-EVERY-PASS
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT arm (3), corrected: a judged-outcome memo in `carry_fold_arm`. REJECT arms (1)
+and (2), the `dispose` widening.
+
+The cost is real, but the proposal names the cheaper part. Each pass re-fetches every
+`handoff-wip/<topic>` ref and reads its `BLOCKED.md` (`:818`), about 30 s. The larger part
+is a fold whose `body_push.sh` failed after `carry_fold.py` succeeded. Only `rc = 0` writes
+`cloud-folded` (`:843`), so the arm runs the whole `carry_fold.py` and `body_push.sh` pair again
+on every pass. That is about 3 minutes per pass for two topics today. The skip at `:821` never
+fires for them.
+
+Source: queue line 262, 2026-11-11T05:57:20Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+Instances:
+- **The read loop.** At 06:00Z, `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/handoff-wip/*'` lists 63
+  refs: 46 topics pass the `:817` filter, and 15 have a `BLOCKED.md`. The arm's fetch-and-show
+  loop over them took 33 s cold and 27 s warm.
+- **The re-run folds.** The relay's last pass (`tick.txt.relay.log`) prints 12 `OWED carry-fold`
+  lines. Two are `body_push rc=1 after the fold`, for `r10-sav-valuation-residue` and
+  `r10-train-residue`. Both topics run `carry_fold.py` then `body_push.sh` again on every pass.
+  - Fold-file mtimes in that pass: sav-valuation at 05:48:17Z, train-residue at 05:49:59Z, and
+    `cloud-fold.out` at 05:51:18Z. That is about 102 s and 79 s, **about 181 s per pass**.
+  - The refusal in `cloud-fold.out` is a body-lint error, `` `## Head` does not name 5e91c2c``,
+    together with `RED UNANSWERED` ancestry reds. The first cannot change until the kept body
+    changes. The second can clear without any ref moving.
+- **The pass it sits in.** `TICK-RELAY` relay-pass medians per hour on 11-11, 01Z-05Z: 719,
+  677, 832, 605 and 588 s; on 11-10, 14Z-20Z: 563-587 s. The carry-fold arm's measured
+  ~211 s (30 s + 181 s) is **about 36%** of a 588-605 s pass today.
+- **The proposal's symptom lines.** `relay=running` on a `TICK-PASS` line is the normal state.
+  All 79 `TICK-PASS` lines from 11-10T13Z to 11-11T05Z carry it, so it does not single out
+  this arm. The claim of a pass falling from ~10 min to under 2 min is not supported: the pass
+  ran at ~570 s on 11-10 as well, and the arm accounts for about 211 s of it. The opener
+  latency (`SKIP moved` x3) was not traced to this arm. It is not counted.
+- **Rule applied per instance**, as a memo keyed on (topic, wip sha, kept-body sha):
+  - the 44 of 46 topics whose judgement depends only on their two shas (10 BLOCKED.md not
+    naming CARRY-LANDED alone, and the topics with no BLOCKED.md): skipped with no fetch, which saves
+    ~27-33 s per pass;
+  - the 2 failed folds: retried at most once an hour instead of every pass, which saves
+    ~181 s on 5 of 6 passes, about 151 s per pass averaged;
+  - together about 180 s of a ~600 s pass, **about 30%**.
+- **Null control.** The 11-10 passes (median 563-590 s) bound what the rest of the relay costs.
+  Removing the arm's 211 s from today's 600 s gives about 390 s, which is below them. So the
+  saving is a ceiling for today's state, not a claim on every day. With no failed fold it falls
+  to the 27-33 s read loop alone, about 5%.
+
+Cost:
+- `cloud_relay.sh`, 1,871 lines, a hot file. It has no row in `tests/structure_budgets.json` at
+  `a7628041dc`, so no capped file is touched.
+- The memo is about 20 production lines and one state file, `cloud-fold-judged`, with lines
+  `<topic> <wip sha> <body sha> <outcome> <epoch>`.
+- Self-test arms beside the `mut:foldonly` cases (`:1827-1850`), about 25 lines:
+  - an unchanged nothing-folded ref is not fetched again, and its OWED level line still stands;
+  - a moved wip ref or body ref is judged again;
+  - a failed body push is retried after the TTL and not before.
+- Owner R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE (medium; not started; 22 carries), so P551's five-carry
+  split applies at dispatch.
+
+Binding:
+- **Arm (3), corrected: ACCEPT**, carry to R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE. The measure is about 30%
+  of the relay pass today, above the 20% bar on CPU and wall-clock. Its terms:
+  1. Read the shas from the `ls-remote` the arm already makes. A topic whose (wip sha, body sha)
+     is in the memo is not fetched and not shown.
+  2. Its stored OWED line is re-written into `cloud-level-fold.$$`, because `level_set`
+     (`:849`) replaces the whole carry-fold level each pass. A memo that drops the line clears
+     an owed item silently. This is the one way the arm can go wrong, and it needs a self-test
+     arm.
+  3. A failure after the fold (carry_fold rc != 0 or body_push rc != 0) is retried once its
+     memo entry is 3600 s old, never every pass. An ancestry red can clear while no ref moves.
+  4. Success still appends to `cloud-folded` as today.
+- **Arms (1) and (2): REJECT.** Admitting `handoff-wip/` to `dispose` (`:322`) and checking
+  `disposed` before the fetch puts a hand step on each wip ref to save what arm (3) saves with
+  none. It also widens what `dispose` accepts, which is another surface to pin. Once (3) lands,
+  the binding cost is all cost and no further benefit.
+- The local workaround in force (stale wip refs archived as tags and deleted) stays the
+  orchestrator's until the carry lands.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 167 (P581)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` line 264. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `a7628041dc`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` `400a014603`.
+- The beat opener's log `open-driver/open-driver.log` in the state dir: 1,556 lines, with 25
+  `RESULT` lines from 2026-11-10T09:50:33Z to 2026-11-11T06:12:15Z.
+- `s14/sweep.md`, its `beat rotated` lines.
+- No GitHub API calls.
+
+## P581: BEAT-CHECKOUT-ROTATION-BY-HAND
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, narrowed. It is not a separate rotate instrument that rewrites launch files.
+`beatd` restarts itself in place, on its own branch-backed checkout, between job instances. That
+is the mechanism P552 (`s6-batch145.md#P552`) gave `tick_loop.sh`'s `fresh_check`. The carry
+goes to R10-SEAT-IDENTITY-P5.
+
+Source: queue line 264, 2026-11-11T06:12:41Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+Instances:
+- **The refusal.** `pr_args.sh:188` refuses `STALE CHECKOUT <h> behind origin/main <o> by <n>
+  commit(s) touching tools/audit/seat tools/pr` when the checkout holding `open_pr.sh` is
+  behind on those paths.
+- **The opener's record.** `grep -c 'STALE CHECKOUT' open-driver.log` gives 8. Each is a
+  `RESULT ... rc=1` line: **8 of the 25 open attempts (32%)** in 20.4 h were refused for this
+  cause alone.
+  - The 8 fall at 11-10T10:55, 11-10T11:21, 11-11T01:21, 11-11T03:24, 11-11T03:59, 11-11T06:10
+    (two) and 11-11T06:12Z.
+  - Of the refused topics that have opened since, the delay from refusal to the next `rc=0`
+    `RESULT` for the same topic was **36 min** (`r10-hotfix-prepr-readset`) and **48 min**
+    (`r10-plan-page-residue`).
+  - The other 5 have not opened yet. 3 are `r10-process-slim-p2`, which is also blocked on its
+    carry fold (P580), so their delay is not counted here.
+- **The hand rotations.** `s14/sweep.md` logs two: 04:00:27Z and 06:12:41Z. The proposal's
+  02:04Z rotation is not in that file and is not counted. Each logged rotation was followed by an
+  opener backoff reset (04:03:13Z) or by a tick-loop rotation (06:13:50Z). The orchestrator's
+  ~10 min per instance is the source's estimate, not a measurement.
+- **Why `beatd` does not restart itself today.**
+  - `beatd.py:488-496` reads only `STALE-CODE behind=<n>` and counts every commit on main, not
+    the paths `pr_args.sh` checks. It is an alarm, not a trigger.
+  - `beatd.py`, `beat_jobs.py` and `beatd.jobs.json` contain no self-restart path (`beatd.py`'s `restart` hits, lines 24, 284 and 771-773, are job restarts)
+    (`grep -c 'STALE-CODE|STALE CHECKOUT|ff-only|RESTART|exec '` gives 0 in `beat_jobs.py`).
+  - The tick loop's `fresh_check` (`tick_loop.sh:95-112`) is the in-tree precedent. When behind on
+    its own paths, with a clean tree and the relay lock free, it moves its checkout to
+    origin/main and `exec`s itself. P552 extended it to a clean branch-backed checkout with no
+    commit outside origin/main.
+- **Rule applied per instance.** A beat that restarts itself on main, once it is behind on
+  `tools/audit/seat` or `tools/pr` and no job instance is running, reaches each of the 8
+  refusals before the opener's next attempt. The opener retries on its backoff; it does not
+  wait for a hand step. All 8 are removed. The measured delays of 36 and 48 min fall to the
+  beat's pass interval plus one opener backoff step.
+- **Null control.** 17 of the 25 `RESULT` lines carry no `STALE CHECKOUT`, including all 14
+  `rc=0` lines. So the count does not read every refusal as this cause.
+
+Cost:
+- `beatd.py`, 1,266 lines. It has no row in `tests/structure_budgets.json` at `a7628041dc`; no
+  capped file.
+- About 35 production lines, following `fresh_check`'s shape:
+  - a path-filtered behind count on `tools/audit/seat` and `tools/pr`;
+  - the refusal conditions: a dirty tree, a commit outside origin/main, a job instance running,
+    or `bash -n`/`py_compile` refusing main's `beatd.py`;
+  - `git checkout -q -B <branch> origin/main`, then a re-exec with a once-per-start guard;
+  - a `BEAT-STALE` line when a refusal persists into a second pass.
+- About 40 self-test lines:
+  - behind on the paths and idle restarts;
+  - behind only off the paths does not;
+  - a running instance defers to the next pass;
+  - a dirty tree or a local commit refuses with its why;
+  - a broken main `beatd.py` refuses.
+- No new file and no launch-file rewrite. The checkout path does not change, so `beatd.tools`,
+  `orch-checkout` and the launch files stay valid.
+
+Binding:
+- **ACCEPT, narrowed, as a carry to R10-SEAT-IDENTITY-P5.** That group owns `beatd.py`,
+  `beat_jobs.py` and `beatd.jobs.json`. It is not started, with 5 carries, and its `after` is
+  R10-TICK-RESIDUE. The measure is 32% of open attempts, over the 20% bar for adding to an
+  instrument. The two measured delays were 36 and 48 min each.
+- **The proposed form, a rotate instrument rewriting `beatd.tools`, `orch-checkout` and two
+  launch files: REJECT.** It costs a new file and four local path rewrites per run. The in-place
+  restart removes the same 8 refusals and rewrites nothing. Rotating to a new worktree is needed
+  only when an instance must keep running from the old tree, and the restart waits for no
+  instance instead.
+- The hand procedure in `s14/sweep.md` stays the orchestrator's until the carry lands.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 168 (P582, P583)
+
+This batch rules two orchestrator requests made 2026-11-11 under mandate 6715477401 (scope
+all): where R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT's open carry 6 goes, and why the plan sized that
+group as it did. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `a7628041dc`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` `de1cf3d732`.
+- PR 3402's merged body, read once with `gh pr view 3402 --json body`. The merge commit is
+  `45adb0c3b425dc44e72fd9ce4ef51f480b5a3af6`; the head is `c12789515e`.
+- `tools/plan/durations.json`, `tools/plan/replan.py` and `tools/plan/size_durations.py` at
+  `a7628041dc`.
+
+## P582: GHCP-CARRY6-MQTT-OFF-HOME
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, as a new group R10-ECL110-MQTT-OFF-NEUTRAL: size S, `after`
+R10-ARBITER-OFF-RESTORE. It is not a carry on R10-ARBITER-OFF-RESTORE.
+
+Source: the orchestrator's owner ruling under the mandate. When the optimizer is turned off or
+unloaded, no actuator arm may leave the pump displaced, MQTT included; "byte-identical" was
+W7's scope limit, not a product decision. The ruling asks for a measurement first. The carry is
+PERSISTENT's carry 6 (ghc-d02, body item 711d4be1). PR 3402 left it untouched (`## Roster
+carries`: "Carry 6 (ghc-d02): untouched").
+
+Instances, as static reads at `a7628041dc`:
+- **The MQTT arm.** `heat_curve.publish` (`heat_curve.py:237-262`) publishes the MQTT topics
+  through `publish_ecl110_topics` on every call. `mode_off` gates only the entity arm (`:260`).
+- **No publish on MODE_OFF.** `coordinator.async_publish_current_action` returns before
+  publishing when `self._mode == MODE_OFF` (`coordinator.py:7683-7687`, "off writes nothing").
+  The only other caller, `_async_peak_guard_transition`, returns on MODE_OFF the same way
+  (`:8827`).
+  - Statically, then, the last displace published before off stays the last command on the
+    topic.
+  - Retain is a user option, `DEFAULT_ECL110_RETAIN = False` (`const.py:1543`). With retain on,
+    the broker keeps that last displace for any later subscriber. With it off, the controller
+    bridge keeps whatever it last received.
+- **The null control** the brief must measure against: the entity arm (non-MQTT), which
+  `off_restore` restores to its baseline on MODE_OFF and unload since #3299 and 3402
+  (`heat_curve.py:151` registers the consumer).
+- **Existing groups first.**
+  - The only live groups naming `mqtt` or `ecl110` with `coordinator.py` or `climate.py` in
+    their files: R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT itself. It is carries-open, with a merged PR.
+  - R10-ARBITER-OFF-RESTORE (in progress; PR 3404 frozen mid conflict-repair) owns the restore
+    of the pump arbiter's set-point, a different seam. It shares `coordinator.py`,
+    `__init__.py` and `tests/features.py`.
+  - A carry there would re-open a frozen PR, or its part 2, for a seam it does not own. A new
+    group ordered after it avoids both.
+
+Cost:
+- About 15 production lines, an off and unload publish of displace 0 on the MQTT topics.
+  The coordinator's MODE_OFF transition and the `off_restore` unload path are its two call
+  sites.
+- About 40 test lines: a failing test first, with a mutation proof on each path. A test that
+  the null-control entity arm is unchanged.
+- A docs line in `docs/ecl110.md`.
+- No capped file; no row for these files in `tests/structure_budgets.json` at `a7628041dc`.
+- If the measurement shows the topic already neutral, the cost is one measurement and a
+  dismissal.
+
+Binding:
+- **ACCEPT, new group R10-ECL110-MQTT-OFF-NEUTRAL.** S, production, `after`
+  R10-ARBITER-OFF-RESTORE, because the two share three files. Its brief:
+  1. **First, measure.** On the MQTT ECL110 arm, find what value stands on the topic after
+     MODE_OFF and after unload, retained or last published, with retain on and off. Measure the
+     entity arm restored by 3402 as the null control.
+  2. **If a non-zero displace stands,** publish displace 0 on both paths. Pin it with a failing
+     test first and a mutation proof per path.
+  3. **If the topic is already neutral,** record the command and its output, and mark the carry
+     dismissed with that evidence.
+  4. **Also,** re-read #3299's merged diff (`20d96598c9` is on main) and re-check design carries
+     ghcp-03 and ghcp-r3's citations at origin/main. 3402's `## Design carries` re-checked
+     them only at `e066a630`, "to be re-checked at the merged base".
+- PERSISTENT's carry 6 is dropped once the new group's entry is read back. That is the
+  orchestrator's instruction (c).
+
+## P583: PLAN-HELD-SIZE-NONE-MEASURED
+
+Verdict: REJECT a repair of `held_rows` / `prs_of_groups`: there is no mis-map, and a
+re-measure changes this group's figure by 0 min. DEFER the held-group part granularity, on the
+terms below.
+
+Source: the orchestrator's request (d). The plan's duration basis read "8 carries, none measured
+as answered", while `cited_carries()` over the merged 3402 body returns 7 answered.
+
+Instances:
+- **Where the words come from.** `replan.held_open` (`replan.py:489-498`) prints "none measured
+  as answered" when `durations.json`'s `held_open_carries` has no record for the group.
+- **The measure is stale, not mis-mapped.**
+  - `durations.json` has `sizes_measured_at` 2026-11-01T07:38:26Z. Its last change on main is
+    `857586f29f`, 2026-11-06.
+  - `size_durations.py` runs by hand only. CI runs its `--self-test` (`governance.yml`), not the
+    measurement.
+  - PR 3402 merged 2026-11-10T14:26:57Z, after the record.
+  - Of the 8 groups now carries-open, **0** have a record. All 27 recorded groups are no longer
+    carries-open.
+  - `prs_of_groups` (`size_durations.py:197-213`) maps 3402 to the group through the roster's
+    `resume.commit`, which is the merge commit `45adb0c3b4`. Nothing is mis-mapped.
+- **What the stale measure cost here: 0 min.**
+  - `durations.json` holds `carries_per_part` 11 and `carry_part_hours` 19.8. A held group is
+    sized as `ceil(open / 11)` parts x 19.8 h (`replan.py:530-534`).
+  - 8 open gives 1 part, 1188 min. 1 open (carry 6 alone, the measured truth) gives 1 part,
+    **the same 1188 min**.
+  - The 1188 min at the head of the binding chain came from one owner-decision carry left
+    open with the group carries-open. Re-homing that carry (P582) and the `set-stage done`
+    release it; a re-measure would not have.
+- **The granularity.** All 7 carries-open groups with any open carry are planned at exactly
+  1188 min, whatever their 1-8 open carries. One part of 11 carries costs the same as one carry.
+
+Cost:
+- A repair to the mapping: none is owed.
+- A scheduled re-measure: one GraphQL fetch of every PR since `SINCE` per run. That is an API
+  cost, against a 0 min change on this instance.
+
+Binding:
+- **REJECT the mapping repair.** There is no mis-map, and the re-measure moves this instance by
+  0 min. The binding cost is a change to `tools/plan/` that buys nothing here.
+- **DEFER the part granularity** (one carry planned as a whole 19.8 h part). It changes on a
+  measured carry-part duration by open-carry count, from the merged part PRs. The owning group
+  is whichever live group holds `tools/plan/replan.py`. If the measure shows a single carry well
+  under a part, `held_open` should size by carries, not whole parts.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 169 (P584)
+
+This batch records one orchestrator ruling made 2026-11-11 under mandate 6715477401 (scope
+all): main is red, and the ruling builds the hotfix and its class barrier as one new group.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `a7628041dc`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The failing job 130352715261 of workflow run 42968587919, and its `selftest-closures`
+  artifact (`gh run download 42968587919 -n selftest-closures`), as diagnosed by the
+  orchestrator's main-red seat.
+
+## P584: SELFTEST-SCOPE-UNION
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, as a new group R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-SCOPE-UNION: class hotfix, size S,
+fixer and reviewer opus, two parts. No live group owns `tools/ci/selftest_scope.py` or
+`tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` (roster read at the time of ruling: every group listing
+them is done).
+
+Source: the orchestrator's main-red intake, 2026-11-11, ruled under the mandate.
+
+Instances:
+- **The red.** Step `drift` ("Refuse a self-test read set the committed table misses") of
+  `governance / instrument-self-tests` prints `selftest_scope check: 111 gated step(s), 6
+  refusal(s)` at `a7628041dc` (job log of 130352715261). It has been red on every completed
+  main push since PR 3315 added it. The refusal counts were 37, 1, 32, 33 and 6 (check-runs
+  per sha over `git log --first-parent origin/main`).
+- **Cause 1, a new read without its table entry.** PR 3379 added the read of
+  `dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md` in `review_packet.py:921` (`step12`). It did not touch
+  the table, so verdict-bus and review-packet miss it.
+- **Cause 2, a re-record replaces.** `record` (`selftest_scope.py:701`) does `entries.update`
+  per step (`selftest_scope.py:743`). That replaces a step's read set with what one recording
+  saw. PR 3419's off-push re-record dropped reads that only a main push makes: prepr's
+  `.gitattributes`, `tests/env_drift.py`, `tools/merge/ledger_merge.py` and git `branch`, and
+  the `-c` probe of open-pr, pr-args and update-pr.
+- **Why no pull request is refused.** `SELFTEST_TRACE` is set only on push
+  (`governance.yml:297`), and the drift step is guarded on it (`governance.yml:1496`). On a
+  pull request the step is skipped, so it judges nothing before a merge.
+- **The class.** This is at least the third hotfix of the self-test scope class, after
+  R10-HOTFIX-MAIN-SELFTESTS, R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-SCOPE-HANG and
+  R10-HOTFIX-PREPR-SELFTEST-DARWIN (roster, all done). By `defect-root-cause.md` it owes a
+  barrier, not another entry fix.
+
+Cost:
+- Part 1: one JSON file, 9 added entries, no code. It has no cap row.
+- Part 2: `tools/ci/selftest_scope.py`, possibly `.github/workflows/governance.yml`, and one
+  detector. These are CI and instrument code, outside `custom_components/`. Severity is high
+  and the class is hotfix, so the machinery bar does not apply.
+
+Binding: main is red on every push, and the merge train reads main as GREEN only because the
+context is not required. Every merge until part 1 lands carries the red. Every re-record
+until part 2 lands can recreate it.
+
+Rule per instance:
+- **Part 1.** Add the 6 measured misses to the existing entries (artifact minus table, per
+  step). Never replace the table with the artifact. Keep prepr's `required-contexts.json`
+  and git `fetch`.
+- **Part 2.** `record` unions with the prior entry, and a separate explicit operation drops a
+  read. A pre-merge detector refuses a pull request that adds a read to a gated self-test
+  without the table entry; PR 3379's diff is the positive case, and a pull request adding no
+  read is the null control. Running the drift step on pull_request is decided with numbers
+  (strace install and traced-run wall time from the main-push jobs, against the gate's
+  budget), then wired or refused with those figures.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 170 (P585, P586)
+
+This batch rules two process proposals filed by seat s14-12 on 2026-11-11, both about PR 3425.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `a7628041dc`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The tick-loop log of the orchestrator's state directory (22183 lines at the time of ruling),
+  its `cloud-relayed.refused` ledger, and the check-runs API for the heads named.
+
+## P585: PENDING-CI-RED-TERMINAL
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, re-pointed, as a carry on R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE (stage in-progress,
+severity medium; it owns `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh` and `tools/audit/seat/review_carry.py`).
+The fixer builds it with that group's P576 carry, which edits the same arm. The proposed arm
+itself is REJECTED as a duplicate: P576 (batch 162) already carries it word for word.
+
+Source: the proposal queue, s14-12, 2026-11-11 ("cloud_relay pending-ci draft is refused once a
+main merge moves the head ... PR 3425").
+
+Instances:
+- **The proposed mechanism never fired.** `grep -c "head moved under a pending-ci"` over the
+  tick-loop log, `cloud-relay.log` and `cloud-relayed.refused-why` gives 0 in each. The die that
+  message belongs to is `cloud_relay.sh:268`. Had the claim been true, at least PR 3425's line
+  would have matched.
+- **What did fire is the RED arm, `cloud_relay.sh:273`.** `grep -n "pending-ci draft is not
+  posted"` gives two refusals, and these are all of them:
+  - **PR 3425.** At 04:39Z its draft (`probe/rev-3425-5c9958ba`, verdict `8e4b9d262c`,
+    `Fix review: merge c6becb3175`) was HELD (classify WAIT). At 04:49Z it was REFUSED with
+    "CI is red at c6becb3175 (classify RED)" (tick-loop line 21910). The failing check-runs at
+    c6becb3175 were `gate`, `pr-contract / pr-contract` and `governance / instrument-self-tests`.
+    The `gate` failures print only `FAIL pr-contract / pr-contract: failure`. The pr-contract job
+    (130328018313) died in `carry_audit.py` with `AttributeError: module 'roster_lib' has no
+    attribute 'carry_receivable'`. That is a version skew: main's `carry_audit.py` calls a
+    function main added on 2026-11-10 (`e08425e904`), after the branch's merge base `d08ed31049`.
+    The branch's diff (`git diff d08ed31049...c6becb3175 --stat`, 9 files) touches neither file.
+    The third red is main's own (P584). The fixer's main merge at 05:54Z (`c93903f075`) cured the
+    skew: `gate` and pr-contract are green there (06:54Z-07:05Z). `review_carry.py c6becb3175
+    c93903f075 --verdict-only` answers `CARRY` (rc 0).
+  - **PR 3430.** Its draft (`probe/rev-3430-6a421a63`, verdict `58b7ef6110`) was HELD at tick-loop
+    line 22140, then REFUSED at line 22161 over a red at `ba0ed526cc`. Two check-runs were red
+    there. `gate` (job 130351017244, 05:52Z) printed `run(s) [42968003278] at this head are still
+    being judged; their gate decides`. `tests / nightly-status` is main's nightly and is not
+    required. A later `gate` at the same head is green (06:41Z), with no new commit.
+- **Both drafts are stranded.** `cloud_relay.sh:371` appends the refused pair to
+  `cloud-relayed.refused`, and line 343 skips any pair already listed there. Both pairs are in
+  the ledger (`grep -c 'rev-3425\|rev-3430'` gives 2). The log has no line for #3425 after line
+  21910, and none for #3430 after line 22161. The refusal text says "the PR goes back to its
+  fixer", but nothing sent it back. Both PRs are open with no review at the current head
+  (`gh pr view 3425 --json reviews` is empty).
+- **P576's fix as written would cure neither.** It keeps "RED at the live head still refuses".
+  It also only acts on a moved head, and both drafts were refused before any head moved.
+
+Cost:
+- **Benefit.** 2 of 2 RED-arm refusals in the log (100%) were reds that cleared with no fixer
+  work. Each costs a second reviewer turn (the group's opus reviewer) and leaves the PR waiting
+  until someone notices, 2 h or more in both cases.
+- **Fix.** One arm in `cloud_relay.sh` (about 10 lines), next to the lines P576 already edits,
+  plus three self-test checks that reuse the classify stubs at lines 1183-1205. API cost is one
+  extra classify per held draft per relay pass, the same as WAIT's today.
+- **Gate.** No capped file is new, and no new file is added. The group's severity is medium, so
+  the machinery bar does not apply.
+
+Binding: a terminal refusal of a draft whose head still has the review's answer wastes a full
+opus review each time. This is the arm that has fired, while the proposed one has not.
+
+Rule per instance:
+- **RED on a pending-ci draft holds the draft, like WAIT.** It returns 75 and prints one
+  `HELD-PENDING-CI-RED #<pr> <head>: <red contexts> (classify RED)` line per pass. It refuses
+  only on one of two conditions:
+  - the PR's head moves to a head where `review_carry` does not answer CARRY (P576's arm);
+  - the head has read RED with no check still running for 6 h since the first RED read.
+    The first RED read is recorded in the state dir and keyed `<ref> <sha> <head>`.
+- **On the final refusal, print an OWED line naming the PR.** It reads `cloud_relay: OWED
+  re-dispatch #<pr> <head>` and replaces the claim that the PR goes back to its fixer, which no
+  code carries out.
+- **Run against the two instances, result beside each:**
+  - PR 3425: RED at 04:49Z is held. At the next pass after 05:54Z the head has moved, and P576's
+    arm runs `review_carry` (CARRY). After 06:56Z classify reads `c93903f075` with `gate` green.
+    `instrument-self-tests` is red on main too, and `nightly-status` is not required. The draft
+    posts, and no second review is needed.
+  - PR 3430: RED at its refusal pass is held. At 06:41Z the same head reads `gate` green and the
+    draft posts. It was held for under 1 h, inside the 6 h bound.
+- **Self-test.** RED, then GREEN at the same head, posts. RED for longer than the bound refuses
+  and prints the OWED line. As a null control, WAIT behaves as it does today. A mutant that
+  restores the die at line 273 makes the first check fail.
+
+## P586: CARRY-FOLD-PR-SPELLING
+
+Verdict: REJECT. The claimed mechanism does not exist. The PR's spelling never changes the
+answer, and the 1-versus-0 the proposer saw comes from two different inputs, not from the
+spelling.
+
+Source: the proposal queue, s14-12, 2026-11-11 ("carry_fold.py --pr 3425 (no #) reports 0 missing
+while carry_audit landed --pr '#3425' reports 1 ... PR 3425").
+
+Instances:
+- **Replay on the roster from before the carry landed.** The carry is `From #3425, body item
+  09380b99`, and it landed on the round roster at `d611071d86` (04:40Z). The replay ran against
+  that commit's parent, with PR 3425's current body.
+  - `carry_audit.py --roster-ref <it> landed` and `carry_fold.py --roster-ref <it>` were each run
+    with `--pr '#3425'` and with `--pr 3425`, each with and without `--topic r10-tick-residue`.
+  - All 8 runs agree between the two spellings. landed gives `CARRY-LANDED: 0 missing` every
+    time, adding a `CARRY-STATUS` line when the topic is given. fold gives `0 item(s) folded`.
+  - On the current roster, landed with `--roster-ref origin/main` and with the round roster gives
+    `0 missing` for both spellings.
+  - Had the claim been true, the bare-number runs would have differed from the `#` runs in at
+    least one of these pairs.
+- **The code agrees.** A bare number reaches `own_group` (`carry_audit.py:601-609`), which skips
+  `#`-prefixed tokens and resolves bare ones through `pr_group_of`. `own_group(dests, ['3425'])`
+  and `own_group(dests, ['#3425'])` both return `None`. Only the topic resolves
+  (`R10-TICK-RESIDUE`). In the source-token match, a bare `3425` cannot equal the whole token
+  `#3425`. So a bare number could only report more items missing, never fewer.
+- **Where the 1 came from.** At 03:37Z the bus ran `carry_audit.py --roster-ref origin/main
+  landed --pr "#3425"` with no `--topic` (`bus.sh:236-237`). It printed `CARRY-LANDED: 1 missing`
+  (tick-loop lines 21767-21768). That was an hour before the carry landed at 04:40Z. A fold run
+  after 04:40Z correctly finds nothing to write.
+
+Cost: normalising or refusing the argument means code in two tools for a behaviour that measures
+identical. It would buy nothing.
+
+Binding: an unreproduced claim. 0 of 8 replays differ. If a later instance shows two runs at the
+same roster ref and body, differing only in spelling, that reopens it.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 171 (P587)
+
+This batch re-rules queue line 266, which batch 170 rejected as P586, after the orchestrator gave
+the replay condition P586 missed. P587 supersedes P586.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `a7628041dc`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- PR 3425's body as the fold read it, byte-identical to the body P586 replayed (`cmp`).
+- The round roster at `e60ea43333`, the tip before the fold's write `f63227bd43`.
+
+## P587: CARRY-SOURCE-BARE-NUMBER
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, as a carry on R10-CARRY-AUDIT-P5 (stage not-started, severity medium, size S;
+it owns `tools/audit/carry_audit.py`). This supersedes P586's REJECT.
+
+Source: the proposal queue, s14-12, 2026-11-11 (line 266: "carry_fold.py --pr 3425 (no #)
+reports 0 missing while carry_audit landed --pr '#3425' reports 1 ... PR 3425"). The orchestrator
+corrected the measurement on 2026-11-11.
+
+Instances:
+- **Why P586 missed it.** P586 replayed with `--roster-ref <one ref>` against the roster from
+  before an earlier carry, `d611071d86^`. That flag reads only the named ref. The fold reads
+  main plus the round roster, and the round roster was at `e60ea43333`.
+- **The replay that reproduces it.** A shared clone (`git clone --shared --no-checkout`) has
+  `origin/main` at `a7628041dc` and `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `e60ea43333`. Running
+  `carry_audit.py --git-dir <clone> landed --body <body>` gives:
+  - with `--pr '#3425'`: `CARRY-MISSING R10-TICK-RESIDUE body item 09380b99 ... CARRY-LANDED:
+    1 missing`;
+  - with `--pr 3425`: `CARRY-LANDED: 0 missing`.
+  This matches the orchestrator's 07:11Z runs. The `#3425` fold folded 1 and wrote `f63227bd43`.
+- **The mechanism.** `landed` (`carry_audit.py:620`) treats an item as landed when any source
+  token is a whole token of its group's text (line 650, split on `[^\w#-]+`).
+  - R10-TICK-RESIDUE's carries at `e60ea43333` contain the prose "handed off as PR 3425" four
+    times, and `#3425` zero times (`jq` over the group, `grep -c '#3425'` = 0).
+  - So a bare `3425` matches that prose, and the item reads as landed by its source although no
+    carry holds it.
+  - `own_group` and `pr_group_of` are not involved: both spellings resolve to `None` in the
+    clone.
+  - Had the bare number not matched prose, both spellings would have printed 1 missing.
+- **Consequence.** A fold run with a bare number reports success and writes nothing, so a
+  missing carry stays missing. A run with the documented spelling `#N` (`carry_fold.py:4`,
+  `carry_audit.py:965`, `bus.sh:237`) is correct.
+
+Cost:
+- About 5 lines in `carry_audit.py`: one normaliser, used by both `landed` and `land_ops`, that
+  maps an all-digit `--pr` value to `#<N>`. `carry_fold.py` calls both functions, so it needs no
+  change.
+- One self-test pair.
+- No new file, and no capped file is new. The group's severity is medium, so the machinery bar
+  does not apply.
+
+Binding: a fold that silently writes nothing leaves a carry missing while every reader sees
+success. The fix is a few lines in a group not yet started that already owns the file.
+
+Rule per instance:
+- **Normalise the source.** In `carry_audit.py`, an all-digit PR source becomes `#<N>` before
+  `landed` splits sources, and before `land_ops` writes `From <pr>`. Any other spelling, such as
+  `PR3425`, is refused with rc 2, naming `#<N>`.
+- **Run against the instance:** with the normaliser, `--pr 3425` reads as `#3425` and gives
+  `CARRY-LANDED: 1 missing` at `e60ea43333`, the same as the `#3425` run. The fold writes the
+  carry once.
+- **Self-test.** A group whose text says "PR 3425" but holds no `#3425` carry:
+  - `--pr 3425` and `--pr '#3425'` both report the item missing.
+  - Null control: a group holding a "From #3425" carry reports 0 missing for both spellings.
+  - A mutant that drops the normaliser makes the bare arm report 0.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 172 (P588, P589)
+
+This batch rules queue lines 267 (the orchestrator's rate-limit intake) and 268 (s14-12), 2026-11-11.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `a7628041dc`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- A 600 s process sample of `gh` invocations (07:25:05Z-07:35:05Z) with the core `rate_limit` read at both ends.
+- The relay and tick-loop logs of the orchestrator's state dir.
+
+## P588: GH-BUCKET-SPENDER-UNLOGGED
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, as a PART 2 ITEM carry on R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE (stage in-progress, severity
+medium). That group owns `tools/audit/seat/gh_calls.py` and `tools/audit/seat/shims`, and holds
+P449, the same drain on 2026-11-08. Its PR 3427 is handed off, and its body dismissed P449's
+"install reaches every daemon PATH" half as having "no tracked caller". This is the second instance
+of that drain. No call cut is accepted on this sample: the named spenders are a minority of the
+bucket, and the rest cannot be attributed until the log reaches the loops.
+
+Source: the orchestrator's queue line 267, 2026-11-11 ("GitHub core bucket hit 0 at 07:19Z ...
+gh_calls.py --top --since 06:24Z reads '0 calls' ... name the spender, propose the cut"). It is
+ruled under the owner's 2026-11-08 no-API-hammering order.
+
+Instances:
+- **Why the log is empty.**
+  - `seat_venv.sh --install-shims <dir>` installs the shim as `<dir>/gh` (`seat_venv.sh:304-307`).
+    `~/.local/state/hpo/bin` holds only `python` and `python3` (installed 2026-10-14) and no `gh`.
+    So every caller resolves to `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`.
+  - `$HPO_STATE_DIR/gh-calls.log` does not exist under the orchestrator's state dir.
+  - `gh_calls.py --top --since 2026-11-11T06:24:00Z` prints `(none)` under both tables with
+    rc 0. Had the shim been reachable, it would have listed callers.
+- **Which loops would log, by `ps eww` PATH.** The merge train's `merge_train.py batch` and
+  `beatd.py run` have the seat bin dir on PATH. The tick loop (`tick_loop.sh`), `wake.sh` and the
+  dispatch seat's `watch2.sh` do not.
+- **The spender, sampled.** `ghsample.py` polls `ps` every 50 ms for 600 s from 07:25:05Z and
+  attributes each new `gh` pid to its parent chain.
+  - The bucket went from 4987 to 4424, so 563 calls in 10 min, about 3380/h.
+  - 240 `gh` processes were sampled:
+    - `orchestrator_tick.py`: 121, about 21% of the bucket. Of those, 31 are `check-runs` reads
+      over 31 distinct shas, 10 are `search/issues` (the search bucket, not core), and 4 are
+      `--paginate --slurp` reads of the #201 and #3394 comments. One of those passes
+      `since=2026-10-28`, which is 4 pages of #201's 2500 comments.
+    - `blind_spots.py`: 42, about 7.5%. This script is the orchestrator's own out-of-tree sweep
+      runner, not in the repository. 19 of its calls are `check-runs?check_name=gate` per sha.
+    - `merge_train.py` classify and batch: 21, about 3.7%. Everything else is 5 or fewer per
+      caller.
+  - About 300 of the 563 calls (roughly 50%) have no local `gh` process. They are pagination
+    pages, calls the sampler missed, or other holders of the token. Only the log can split these.
+
+Cost:
+- **The fix is two small edits:**
+  - `gh_calls.py --top` refuses with rc 3 and a line naming the first `gh` on PATH and whether it
+    is the shim, when no call is logged since `--since`. Today it prints `(none)`.
+  - The tracked `tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh` prepends the seat bin dir to the PATH of its
+    children (`orchestrator_tick.py`, `cloud_relay.sh`). It prints one flag line each pass in
+    which `command -v gh` is not the shim.
+- **Benefit.** It names the 50% of the bucket nobody can attribute today. Every cut the owner's
+  order asks for depends on that, and the drain has now recurred, so the 20% bar is met.
+
+Binding: two drains (11-08, 11-11) could not be attributed because a dismissed half left the tick
+loop off the shim. The instrument printed a clean zero both times.
+
+Rule per instance:
+- **Now, an operational step for the orchestrator, no code.**
+  - Run `seat_venv.sh --install-shims ~/.local/state/hpo/bin`. The train and beatd log at once,
+    since they already carry that dir on PATH.
+  - Restart the tick loop with that dir first on PATH. One hour later, `gh_calls.py --top` names
+    the remaining spender, and the cut is ruled on that log.
+- **The 11-11 instance under the carry.** `gh_calls.py --top --since 2026-11-11T06:24:00Z` would
+  have printed `gh_calls: UNATTRIBUTED: no call logged since ...; gh on PATH is
+  /opt/homebrew/bin/gh (not the shim)` and rc 3, instead of a clean zero.
+- **Self-test.**
+  - An empty log with a non-shim `gh` on PATH gives rc 3 and the line.
+  - Null control: one logged call gives rc 0 with today's tables.
+  - The tick loop's child PATH starts with the seat bin dir.
+  - A mutant that drops the prepend fails the PATH check.
+
+## P589: EVIDENCE-CARRY-WORD-NOT-MARKER
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, re-pointed, as a carry on R10-CARRY-AUDIT-P5 (stage not-started, severity
+medium; it owns `tools/audit/carry_audit.py`, and P587 also lands there). Both proposed fixes are
+REJECTED:
+- **(a), a prompt line.** The reviewer prompt already says that an Evidence item carrying `Carry:`
+  is a finding (`cloud_dispatch.py:291-296`). All three instances below happened under that text.
+- **(b), ignoring `## Evidence`.** It would undo P308/P314. It would also drop a routed finding
+  that a reviewer files under Evidence.
+
+Source: the proposal queue, s14-12, 2026-11-11 (line 268: "push-verdict refused a carry-only merge
+verdict because an '## Evidence' bullet began 'Carry: review_carry.py ... prints CARRY' ... PR
+3425").
+
+Instances:
+- **The 3425 instance.** The verdict ref is `probe/rev-3425-a7ac54c9`, commit `f051f4562d`, and
+  `verdict.md:7` reads ``- Carry: `review_carry.py c6becb31 c93903f0` prints CARRY.``
+  `tick.txt.relay.log:25` records "bus: REFUSE: push-verdict: 1 finding item(s) with no valid
+  Carry: ... UNROUTED review push-verdict item b6e4992b (## Evidence) [carry]".
+- **The whole class.** `grep 'UNROUTED review.*(## Evidence)'` over `tick-loop.log` (since
+  2026-10-24), `tick.txt.relay.log` and `cloud-relay.log` gives 8 lines. They are 3 distinct
+  items, and every one has the reason `[carry]`:
+  - item b6e4992b (PR 3425): "Carry: `review_carry.py ...";
+  - item 2c51d159: "Contradiction grep (own group, own-group, Carry: across
+    dev/governance ...)";
+  - item 8e3e097e: "The deleted closing line of fix-review.md ... states it as a Carry: marker".
+  In each, `Carry:` is a word the text mentions, not a destination marker. Each refusal sends the
+  verdict back for a second reviewer turn.
+- **The marker regex.** It is `CARRY = (?<![\w-])Carry:` (`carry_audit.py:169`), and it matches
+  any mention. Destination tokens have fixed shapes: `GROUP_TOK` (`carry_audit.py:176`),
+  `ISSUE_TOK` (line 177), `O<n>` and `dismissed:`.
+
+Cost:
+- About 6 lines in `carry_audit.py`, plus three self-test checks. No new file.
+- The group's severity is medium, so the machinery bar does not apply.
+- The benefit is 3 of 3 measured Evidence `[carry]` refusals removed, each one reviewer turn.
+
+Binding: a word mentioned in evidence costs a full review turn. In every section, a destination
+shape separates a marker from a mention without reading meaning.
+
+Rule per instance:
+- **The rule.** In a structural section (`## Evidence`, and a merge verdict's sections other than
+  findings), a `Carry:` counts as a marker only when its next token matches a destination shape:
+  `GROUP_TOK`, `ISSUE_TOK`, `O<n>` or `dismissed:`, with trailing punctuation stripped.
+  - A findings section keeps today's rule, so an off-shape `Carry:` there is still refused as
+    UNROUTED.
+  - An on-shape but unknown group is still refused as a bad destination, so a mistyped group
+    name is still caught.
+- **Run against the instances** (`CARRY.search` plus the shape test, run at main `a7628041dc`):
+  - The three mentions are not markers: the next tokens are `` `review_carry.py ``, `across` and
+    `marker`.
+  - The null controls are markers: `Carry: R10-CARRY-AUDIT-P5`, `Carry: #3425` and
+    `Carry: dismissed: dup`.
+- **Self-test.** The three mention shapes under `## Evidence` route nothing. A
+  `Carry: R10-NO-SUCH` under Evidence is still refused. A mutant that drops the shape test refuses
+  the first shape again.
