+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 173 (P590)
+
+This batch rules queue line 269 (the orchestrator's merge-train intake), 2026-11-11.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `e67b79c9fc`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The merge train's log, `~/.local/state/hpo/merge_train/train.log`, lines 19707-19850 (batch
+  `20261111-002834-b4`).
+- The jobs of code run 42969771406 at 141f8af1, read once from the Actions API (41 jobs).
+
+## P590: TRAIN-DEFER-WAIT-UNDER-RUN and POLICY-REFUSAL-REVIEW-MISREAD
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, re-pointed, as a carry on R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER (stage not-started, size M).
+That group owns the seam: its brief has every reader of the gate conclusion, `merge_train`'s
+`policy_refusal` first, treat a deferral red as provisional, and it holds the moved
+R10-HOTFIX-TRAIN-DEFER-WAIT carries. R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE, which owns `merge_train.py`, is
+`carries-open` since PR 3424 merged at 07:47:51Z. It is therefore not `carry_receivable`, and the
+drain refused the first queue line (4391) on that ground. The proposal's remedy "count the wait from the code run's START" is rejected:
+the run started before the wait did, so counting from its start makes the wait shorter.
+
+Source: the orchestrator's queue line 269, 2026-11-11. It reports that #3398 was skipped as
+`ci red TIMEOUT` although its code run concluded success minutes later, and that the train first
+logged "the missing requirement is a review" while two approvals stood at that head.
+
+### Defect 1: the deferral wait is bounded by `polls`, and a legitimate code run outlasts it
+
+- **What happened.** `wait_ci` (`merge_train.py:1905`) loops `for k in range(1, self.polls + 1)`
+  (`:1934`), with `polls: int = 24` (`:1512`), and returns `["TIMEOUT"]` (`:2000`). The log shows
+  the deferral read at 141f8af1 ("gate red ... is a deferral while ci.yml run(s) [42969771406]
+  are unfinished"), then beats at t+244 s through poll 24 at t+5589 s, then
+  `#3398 141f8af1 ci red=['TIMEOUT']` and `SKIP #3398`. The beats are about 243 s apart, not
+  305 s.
+- **The run.** Code run 42969771406 was created at 06:03:35Z and completed `success` at
+  07:41:18Z, 5863 s in all. The wait ran out after about 5589 + 243 s. Its critical path:
+  - `prelude` queued 305 s, ran 36 s;
+  - `tests / mutation` queued 74 s and **ran 5282 s**;
+  - `pr-contract`, `gate` and `sweep-self` took about 160 s together.
+- **The proposal's question: job-cap queueing against the wait budget.** The queue time on the
+  critical path was about 385 s, or 6.6% of the run. Queue time over all 41 jobs was 3853 s, but
+  it was spread over jobs running in parallel. So the job cap did not cause the miss. The cause
+  is that a fixed 24-poll budget (about 97 min) is shorter than a healthy code run. One
+  mutation job ran 88 min, and `tests.yml` sets job ceilings of 90, 160 and 350 minutes.
+- **What the miss cost.** The skip is per verdict. The log reads "ALREADY #3398: skipped by this
+  train at this same verdict 141f8af1b1a5; a new verdict head re-admits it". An outside PR,
+  which ranks first in the queue, lost its batch.
+- **Frequency.** The train log holds 6 `ci red=['TIMEOUT']` lines (#2872, #3006, #3304, #3358,
+  #3355, #3398). The last three came within two days.
+- **The fix.**
+  - While the deferral is read and the sibling ci.yml run at this head reports `in_progress` (it
+    has started), bound the wait by that run's own deadline: its `run_started_at` plus a ceiling,
+    such as the longest `timeout-minutes` among the jobs still running, or one named constant.
+    Do not bound it by `polls`.
+  - A run still `queued`, or past its deadline, keeps the `polls` bound and ends as TIMEOUT. The
+    self-test check "defer-wait bound: a code run that never finishes ends in TIMEOUT within
+    `polls`, never merges" (`:6695`) is kept, with its fake clock run past the new deadline. The
+    R10-HOTFIX-TRAIN-DEFER-WAIT bound is never removed, only aimed at the run's own clock.
+  - The cost is that the record beat holds longer behind such a wait (`TRAIN HOLD ... the record
+    beat waits` was logged 24 times here). That is bounded by the same deadline.
+
+### Defect 2: `policy_refusal` names a review when the deferral is the block
+
+- **The code.** `policy_refusal` (`merge_train.py:2792`) collapses `statusCheckRollup` into
+  `last[name]` (`:2813`). The last same-named entry wins. Here, a `CI review` run's `gate` is
+  success, and it hides the edit run's deferral `gate`. With nothing red or pending, `BLOCKED`
+  becomes "every required context is green, so the missing requirement is a review" (`:2829`).
+  That holds even under `reviewDecision APPROVED`.
+- **Measured over the whole train log.**
+  - 66 lines carry that inference, and all 66 say `reviewDecision APPROVED`.
+  - In 8 of the 66 (12.1%), the train's own deferral read ("is a deferral") follows within 6
+    lines.
+  - **Null control:** 1.4% of all log lines are followed by a deferral read within 6 lines. Of
+    the 9 park lines with any other reason, none is.
+  - So the inference over-fires where the deferral is the block. It does not account for all 66:
+    the ruleset's last-push approval is a real cause, as the docstring says.
+- **The fix.**
+  - Before naming a review, read the head's same-named required contexts, not the collapsed
+    `last`. Where any of them is a deferral-shaped red, or its sibling ci.yml run is unfinished,
+    return `wait` with the deferral reason. Use the predicate `wait_ci` already uses at `:1951`.
+  - Under `reviewDecision APPROVED`, word the remaining case as a last-push approval at the moved
+    head, never as "a review".
+  - The self-test seeds a rollup that holds both a success `gate` (review run) and a failure
+    `gate` (edit-run deferral) at one head. It asserts `wait` and no review wording.
+
+### What it costs and what it saves
+
+- **Cost:** one carry in a not-started group that already owns the deferral seam. It is two bounded edits plus two self-test cases in
+  one file, about 1-2 fixer hours.
+- **Benefit:** 3 TIMEOUT skips in two days, each losing a batch of hours. The latest one was an
+  outside PR, which the queue ranks first. The 8 misread parks also mislead a seat into chasing an
+  approval that already stands.
+- The benefit clears the 20% bar. It is accepted as a carry, not as a permanent new mechanism.
+
+### Operational, not part of the carry
+
+#3398 stays out of this train until a new verdict head re-admits it. That re-add is the
+orchestrator's call.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 174 (P591)
+
+This batch rules queue line 270 (the orchestrator's shim intake), 2026-11-11.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `e67b79c9fc`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The installed shim `~/.local/state/hpo/bin/gh` (reinstalled 07:50Z), the merge train's log,
+  `$HPO_STATE_DIR/gh-calls.log`, and `ps`.
+
+## P591: SHIM-COMMENT-GUARD-ONE-CHECKOUT
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, re-pointed, as a PART 2 ITEM carry on R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE (stage in-progress).
+That group owns `tools/audit/seat/shims/`, which includes `seat-gh`, the shim's source. Neither of
+the proposal's alternatives is taken as written:
+- A blob equal to origin/main's refuses every checkout that lags main by one commit to
+  `gh_comment.py`.
+- A registered-checkout list is one more file to keep current.
+- Refusing the install fixes nothing for checkouts that already exist.
+
+Source: the orchestrator's queue line 270, 2026-11-11.
+
+Instances, measured:
+- **The defect.** `seat_venv.sh --install-shims` writes one tree's path into the shim's `gcpy=`
+  line (`tools/audit/seat/seat_venv.sh:301-305`). The shim lets a record-issue comment write
+  through only when the caller's script real path equals `gcpy`. The installed copy now reads
+  `gcpy=.../s14/tools-wt-45adb0c3/tools/pr/gh_comment.py`.
+- **Live checkouts running seat tools,** counted from `ps` argv:
+  - `tickloop-wt`: 7 processes (`orchestrator_tick.py` and the tick loop's posters);
+  - `beat-wt-a7628041`: 4 (`beatd.py`);
+  - `tools-wt-45adb0c3`: 1 (the merge train, by cwd).
+  Whichever checkout installed last is the only one whose tracker posts pass.
+- **A refusal that happened.** The train log, line 19861: `#3424 OWED record: the #3394 comment
+  was refused (1: gh shim: a comment write on a record issue ...)`. That was under the
+  earlier install.
+- **A refusal waiting to happen.** In `gh-calls.log`, `tickloop-wt/tools/pr/gh_comment.py` runs at
+  07:52-07:53Z, after the 07:50Z reinstall baked the train's checkout. Its next tracker write is
+  refused. Had the guard accepted any checkout, `gcpy` would not name a single tree.
+
+The fix, in `shims/seat-gh` and its self-test:
+- Accept a caller whose script real path is `<root>/tools/pr/gh_comment.py`, where `<root>` is a
+  checkout of this repository (it holds `tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh`) and
+  `git -C <root> diff --quiet HEAD -- tools/pr/gh_comment.py` holds (committed, unmodified).
+- A committed `gh_comment.py` carries `mandate_guard`, which is the reason the guard exists.
+- The baked `gcpy` stays as the fast path. The guard stays deny-by-default for every other caller.
+- The `ps` spoof residual is unchanged and still accepted by design.
+- Self-test:
+  - a second checkout's clean `gh_comment.py` passes;
+  - the same file with a local edit is refused;
+  - a `gh_comment.py` outside any checkout is refused.
+
+What it costs and what it saves:
+- **Cost:** about 15 shim lines and 3 self-test cases, in a group that is already open on this file.
+- **Benefit:** every tracker record post from 2 of the 3 live checkouts is refused after each
+  install, and each refusal is an OWED record the orchestrator hand-repairs.
+- It clears the 20% bar as a carry. No new mechanism is added.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 175 (P592)
+
+This batch rules queue line 271 (the orchestrator's dispatch intake), 2026-11-11.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `45a8b828a4`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/design-verdict/*'` and the `verdict.md` history of each ref.
+
+## P592: DESIGN-REVIEW-ROUND-CONTEXT
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, narrowed, as a carry on R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE (stage in-progress). That
+group owns `tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py`. Parts p1, p3 and p4 are dispatched already, so
+this carry rides the group's next part.
+
+Source: the orchestrator's queue line 271, 2026-11-11 (R10-ADVISOR-STEADY-START round 3, with
+the round context pasted into the fire message by hand).
+
+Measured:
+- `cloud_dispatch.py --group` refuses `--brief`, because "the roster gives the brief"
+  (`GROUP_FLAGS`, `:1305`).
+- The design-reviewer prompt (`:340-353`) names only the design tip from `design_tip`
+  (`:524`). It carries no previous verdict and no round number. `reviewed_head` is a
+  reviewer-only argument (`:388`).
+- **How often a later round happens.** 27 `design-verdict/*` refs hold 51 verdicts. 25 of the 51
+  are later rounds: a ref's second or later `verdict.md` commit. Each one needed the context
+  pasted by hand, or the reviewer went without it.
+  - Had later rounds been rare, the count would read near 0 of 51.
+  - The maximum is 4 verdicts on one ref (r10-combi-tank, R10-ORCH-BEATD). That is the
+    three-note limit in `design-review.md`. A reviewer who cannot see the previous verdicts
+    cannot apply that limit.
+
+The fix, narrowed to what the refs already hold:
+- When `design-verdict/<group>` exists, the design-reviewer render states:
+  - the round number (that ref's `verdict.md` commit count plus 1);
+  - the last verdict's first line and its commit sha, which the reviewer reads with
+    `git show <sha>:verdict.md`;
+  - the range `git diff <previous design sha>..<design tip>`, where the previous design sha is
+    the one the last verdict line names.
+- A first round, with no ref, renders none of this. That is the null control the self-test pins.
+- **The owner's non-acceptance is not rendered from the fire message, and no new flag is
+  added.** Like any routed decision, it goes into the group's brief through the roster's
+  existing `edit-brief` op. `group_brief` already renders the brief, and `GROUP_FLAGS` keeps its
+  refusal of `--brief`.
+
+What it costs and what it saves:
+- **Cost:** about 25 lines in `cloud_dispatch.py`, using git reads it already makes for
+  `design_approved`, plus two self-test checks.
+- **Benefit:** 25 of 51 design reviews to date were later rounds. Each one is a hand-paste the
+  orchestrator owes, or a review blind to the verdict it follows.
+- It clears the 20% bar as a carry.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 176 (P593)
+
+This batch rules queue line 272 (the orchestrator's intake), 2026-11-11.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `f24d107bd7`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster branch `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `988e5cf6ba`, and its history for
+  R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE's `carry` list.
+- The `handoff-wip/<topic>` and `handoff-wip/<topic>-body` refs of the three topics, their
+  `BLOCKED.md` files, the relay's `cloud-fold.out`, and `dispatch/fixer-r10-review-dispatch-residue-p3`'s
+  `PROMPT.md`.
+
+## P593: BRIEF-CARRIES-PART-SCOPE
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, re-scoped, as a carry on R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE (stage in-progress). That
+group owns `tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py`, and its own parts hit the defect.
+
+Source: the orchestrator's queue line 272, 2026-11-11. Three fixer handoffs left a refused body on
+`handoff-wip/<topic>-body` and no `handoff-body/<topic>`.
+
+Measured: the refusal kind of each stranded body. `body_push.sh` prints `body_push: REFUSED <KIND>`
+to stderr only, and the kept commit says only "refused body: <topic>". So the kind comes from each
+fixer's `BLOCKED.md` or, where there is none, from the diff between the refused body and the body
+that later passed.
+- **r10-review-dispatch-residue-p1** (`819f39ac5b`, 07:22Z). Its `BLOCKED.md` names REVIEW-PACKET:
+  `brief-carries: carry 1 ... carry 24 is not named in the body`. The part's brief assigns it Carries
+  14 and 22 by their 0-based roster index. The check demands every carry of the whole group, numbered
+  from 1.
+- **r10-dependabot-3414-compat-p2** (`ac966c9e96`, 07:51Z). There is no `BLOCKED.md`. The body that
+  passed (`handoff-body`, `767634fbd9`) differs from the refused one only by the added lines
+  `Carry 1 ...` and `Carry 2 (the same text, second roster index) ...`. That is the same
+  `brief-carries` refusal. The roster holds the carry twice, and the fixer had to answer the
+  duplicate.
+- **r10-review-dispatch-residue-p3** (`5a2a3bb4a2` and `587a30e2c0`, 08:05-08:07Z). Its `BLOCKED.md`
+  names CARRY-LANDED. That missing carry is the fixer's own item `review-packet-brief-carries:
+  contradiction`, which reports that the packet refused this part's body for 18 group carries the
+  part's brief says to answer none of. The relay's carry-fold arm folded it and re-ran `body_push.sh`,
+  which refused again (`cloud-fold.out`): `REFUSE brief-carries: carry 25 is not named in the body`.
+  - **Carry 25 is this seat's P592**, appended at `4cc00eec0f`, 08:06:52Z. The group held 24 carries
+    at `315a274656` (08:06:03Z), 23 when p3 was dispatched (its PROMPT says "The group's 23 carries"),
+    and 25 at `4cc00eec0f`.
+  - Had the count been read at dispatch, the re-run would have printed no carry-25 line.
+
+One cause, three faces. `review_packet.py handoff` (`:720-736`) reads the group's carry count at the
+roster ref's tip (`fetch_roster_ref`) and `unnamed_carries` (`:547`) demands `Carry 1..n`. So:
+1. **Scope.** A split part must name every carry of the group, though its dispatch brief assigns it
+   a subset (p1, and p3's contradiction item).
+2. **Base.** The part brief numbers carries 0-based (`Carries 2, 3, 8, 9, 13 (0-based roster
+   indexes`), and the check numbers them 1-based. A part that answers "Carry 2" as its brief names it
+   satisfies a different index.
+3. **Time.** A carry that triage, a fold or the roster appends after dispatch refuses every in-flight
+   part at its handoff (p3, carry 25). Such a carry rides the group's next part, and the P592 carry
+   says so itself.
+
+Not the cause: the CARRY-LANDED arm. It worked for p3, and the fold landed the contradiction item.
+The p2 refusal was correct on its face (it had not named its two carries), and only the duplicate
+roster index was noise.
+
+The fix, in `review_packet.py`'s handoff only:
+- When `dispatch/fixer-<topic>` exists on origin, count carries at the roster commit that was the
+  tip at that dispatch commit's time. Demand only the indexes its `PROMPT.md` line `This part:
+  Carries <list> (0-based roster indexes` assigns, spelled as the prompt spells them.
+- With no dispatch ref (a local fixer) or no part line, keep today's whole-group count at the tip.
+  That is the null control.
+- The refusal names the base it reads ("carry 13 (0-based, this part's brief)"), so that a fixer can
+  repair it without a continuation.
+
+Self-test:
+- A part prompt assigning {2, 3} with the group at 5 carries passes a body naming Carry 2 and
+  Carry 3.
+- The same body is refused when Carry 3 is missing.
+- A carry appended after the dispatch time is not demanded.
+- Null control: with no dispatch ref, all 5 are demanded, as today.
+
+What it costs and what it saves:
+- **Cost:** about 40 lines in `review_packet.py` (one `git ls-remote`, one `git show` of
+  `PROMPT.md`, and one `rev-list -1 --before` on the roster ref), plus four self-test checks.
+- **Benefit:** 3 stranded handoffs in one day. Each cost a continuation fixer or a relay fold-and-retry
+  pass, plus orchestrator attention. Three parts of this group (p2, p5, p6) are still to be
+  dispatched, and each would meet the same check.
+- It clears the 20% bar as a carry.
+
+**Ordering:** this carry and P592 both ride the group's next dispatched part. That part should build
+this one first, because every part after it is then immune.
+
+**Immediate repair, not this ruling's to perform:** p3's kept body needs a `Carry 25:` line
+(P592, not this part's, rides the next part), and a `Carry 26:` line once this carry lands. The
+orchestrator or relay re-runs `body_push.sh`. Appending this carry raises the group to 26 at the tip.
+p1 and p4 already hold `handoff-body` refs and are not re-checked.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 177 (P594-P596)
+
+This batch rules queue lines 273-275 (the orchestrator's intake) and the P588 follow-up hour of the
+gh logging shim, 2026-11-11.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster branch at `988e5cf6ba` or later.
+- The Actions API for #3446's head `4cc5d8b962`, and for `gate-sweep.yml`'s runs.
+- `gh-calls.log` over 07:40-08:41Z, and `gh api rate_limit` at 08:44Z.
+
+## P594: GATE-SWEEP-QUEUE-WAIT
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, narrowed, as a carry on R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER (stage not-started, no
+`handoff`/`handoff-wip`/`dispatch` ref in flight). That group owns every reader of the gate
+conclusion in `merge_train.py`.
+
+Source: queue lines 273 and 274. The train skipped #3446 as "red at its head: gate", and
+`classify` still read RED at 08:40Z.
+
+Measured at #3446's head:
+- Gate check runs: two edit-run suites failed, at 07:51 and 07:54Z. The deferring code run's gate
+  was re-run by hand at 08:38Z. The review run's gate succeeded at 08:31:14Z.
+- `latest_runs` (`:400`) keeps the latest gate of each suite and lets the worst stand. That is by
+  design (A5: an older suite's red is never hidden behind a newer green). The deferred reds are
+  meant to be re-judged by `gate-sweep.yml`.
+- The sweep fired on time: run 42987689816 was created at 08:31:17Z, 3 s after the green gate.
+  Its `sweep` job did not **start** until 08:41:55Z, 10 min 38 s later. That is the account's
+  runner queue under the concurrency cap.
+- The train waits for that re-run for `SWEEP_SETTLE_POLLS = 1` poll (`:584`, 240 s).
+  `SWEEP_SETTLE_SECONDS` (`:818`) was set from one measured 62 s start (`:816-817`).
+- Had the sweep never fired, no gate-sweep run would exist after 08:31:14Z. One does, and it is
+  queued.
+
+So the defect is not that `classify` misreads a deferral. The settle window assumes a sweep starts
+within one poll, and under a queued runner it does not. The addendum's proposal (line 274) is
+narrowed away: reading a deferral-only red as superseded would need each red gate's log text, and
+it would weaken A5, which the sweep already serves.
+
+The fix: while the only red is GATE and a `gate-sweep.yml` run created at or after the newest
+green gate suite's `completed_at` is `queued` or `in_progress`, the red is a wait. The read is
+one `actions/workflows/gate-sweep.yml/runs?created=>=<t>` listing per poll. `wait_ci`'s polls
+still bound it (TIMEOUT). With no such run, the red stands after the one settle poll, as today.
+The same rule goes in `classify_at`'s one-read path (`sweep_settling`, `:566`).
+
+Self-test:
+- A queued sweep created after the green keeps the red a wait.
+- A completed sweep with the red unchanged reads RED.
+- Null control: no sweep run reads RED after the settle poll, as today.
+
+What it costs and what it saves:
+- **Cost:** about 25 lines and three checks.
+- **Benefit:** the orchestrator counts this as the third gate-deferral skip this session (#3398,
+  #3445, #3446). Each skip cost a hand re-run or a `--front` re-add.
+- It clears the 20% bar as a carry.
+
+## P595: A5-ROLLUP-PAGES
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, as a carry on R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER. `platform_gate` is a reader of the gate
+conclusion (A5 item 3), in `merge_train.py`.
+
+Source: queue line 275. The train skipped #3355 with "more than 100 contexts: not read whole".
+
+Measured:
+- #3355's head `dee7a1fa45` carries 114 rollup contexts (`statusCheckRollup.contexts.totalCount`).
+- `ROLLUP_Q` reads `contexts(first:100)` (`:460`), and `platform_gate` returns `unread` on
+  `hasNextPage` (`:480`). The train refuses any disagreement, so a head that collects re-runs past
+  100 contexts can never merge by the train. The only remedy is a fresh head.
+
+The fix: page the rollup with `after:` while `hasNextPage` (bounded, say 5 pages), and judge the
+union. A short page is still `unread`.
+
+Self-test:
+- A two-page rollup whose required gate is on page 2 reads green.
+- Null control: a single page reads as today.
+
+What it costs and what it saves:
+- **Cost:** about 15 lines and two checks. One extra GraphQL call happens only at heads with more
+  than 100 contexts.
+- **Benefit:** one observed instance, and its remedy (remerge main) costs a full CI cycle.
+- It clears the bar as a carry, because the refusal is permanent at that head.
+
+The slip in the same line, the shim rebound to another checkout's `gh_comment.py`, is a second
+instance of P591. P591 sits on R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE, which is carries-open with part p2 in flight.
+The instance is recorded on P596's new group below, not on that group.
+
+## P596: TICK-CONDITIONAL-READS
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, as a NEW group R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE-P3. It is a not-started sibling, by the
+orchestrator's 2026-11-11 rule against landing carries on a group with a part in flight.
+- R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE owns the gh-read seam. It is carries-open, and
+  `handoff-wip/r10-gh-read-residue-p2` is in flight.
+- R10-TICK-RESIDUE owns `orchestrator_tick.py`, and its PR #3425 is open.
+- The new group runs after both.
+
+Source: the P588 follow-up. The shim has been live since 07:39:27Z.
+
+Measured over 07:40-08:41Z with `gh_calls.py --top --since 2026-11-11T07:40:00Z`: 1876 logged
+gh invocations.
+- **orchestrator_tick:** 798 (43%), at about 6 passes an hour. Its REST reads are:
+  - `issues/{n}/comments?per_page=100` (`:709`): 218 an hour. Every open PR is re-slurped every
+    pass.
+  - `commits/{sha}/check-runs?per_page=100` (`:378`): 205 an hour over 44 distinct shas, 27 of
+    which were read 5 or more times.
+  - `pr view` (152) and `api graphql` (76) are in the GraphQL bucket.
+- **worktree_gc.sh:** 283, three runs at 07:48, 07:58 and 08:08Z, each one `gh pr list` per branch
+  worktree. `gh pr list` is GraphQL, not core.
+- **merge_train:** 193 (`actions/runs` 72, `rulesets` 38).
+
+The core bucket is what binds. `rate_limit` at 08:44:09Z read core used=1390 since 08:25:02Z, about
+4390 an hour against a 5000 cap. That is above the 07:25Z baseline (about 3380 an hour). GraphQL used
+130 in the same window, about 410 an hour against 5000. So worktree_gc and `pr view` are not worth
+cutting.
+
+The cut is conditional GETs on the tick's two per-PR REST reads.
+- **304s are measured free.** One ETag-conditional `issues/3446/comments` read returned
+  `HTTP/2.0 304 Not Modified`, with `gh` exiting rc=1. Two trials of 5 conditional reads moved core
+  `used` by 0 and 3. The second trial's 3 matches concurrent callers. In the same trials, 5 plain
+  reads moved it by 6 and 5.
+  - Had a 304 cost a call, the conditional deltas would have read 5 or more.
+- The fix: one helper on `TickRun.gh`. For a single-page GET it stores the ETag and body under
+  `$HPO_STATE_DIR/gh-etag/`. It sends `If-None-Match` and reads `gh api -i`'s status line. A 304
+  serves the stored body. A 200 replaces it. Any other failure is `UNREADABLE`, as today.
+  - The comment slurp drops `--paginate --slurp` for a first page under 100 comments, and falls
+    back to the full read when the page is full.
+  - The `#201`/`#3394` since-cursor reads are untouched.
+- **Removed:**
+  - At most 423 - 76 = 347 core calls an hour, if only the first read of each sha (44) and PR (32)
+    in the hour cost anything.
+  - At least about 210 an hour, if every PR's comments and every sha's runs changed on every
+    second pass.
+  - That is 5-8% of the measured core rate, or about 35-55% of the 610 an hour of headroom left
+    under the cap.
+- The self-test pins three cases:
+  - a 304 serves the stored body with no second read;
+  - a 200 replaces it;
+  - null control: with no ETag stored, the plain read is made.
+
+**Folded into the same group** (the gh-read seam's not-started part):
+- **The shim's caller field.** The shim keeps the first 80 characters of argv (`seat-gh:7`). An
+  absolute path therefore loses its script name: the hour logs 798 calls as
+  `.../tools/audit/seat/orch` and 100 as `.../beat-wt-a7628041/tools/audit/seat`. The fix: log the
+  script's basename first, then the cut path.
+- **P591's second instance** (queue line 275): the shim was rebound to `tools-wt-45adb0c3` while the
+  train ran from `tools-wt-63bcdcaa`, and #3398's record comment was refused. Build P591's
+  multi-checkout fix here if R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE-p2 does not.
+
+**Still dark to the shim:**
+- Core used 1390 in 08:25-08:44Z against 458 logged invocations, of which part are GraphQL. The
+  shim logs one line per invocation, so `--paginate` pages are uncounted. Even so, at least about
+  two thirds of core calls are not attributable.
+- Every local long-runner checked is covered:
+  - merge_train (pid 34433) and beatd (63651) have `~/.local/state/hpo/bin` on PATH;
+  - tick_loop's children log as `orch`;
+  - this Claude session's `gh` is the shim;
+  - wake.sh and the dispatch seat's watch.sh call no `gh` (wake.sh uses `git ls-remote`).
+- The dark share is therefore cloud seats on the shared token, plus paginated pages. Measuring them
+  needs a per-request count (`X-RateLimit-Used` read by the shim) or a cloud-side shim. That is a
+  separate proposal, not ruled here.
+
+What it costs and what it saves:
+- **Cost:** about 50 lines in `orchestrator_tick.py` and 5 in `seat-gh`, plus four checks.
+- **Benefit:** 5-8% of the core bucket at 88% of its cap. It is the largest attributable REST cut,
+  and the caller field makes the next attribution exact.
+- It clears the 20% bar on headroom rather than on the total.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 178 (P597)
+
+This batch rules queue line 276 (the orchestrator's intake), 2026-11-11.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster branch at `f4d478511d` or later.
+- The relay logs under the state directory: `cloud-relay.daemon.log` and `tick-loop.log`.
+  Both are local, so no API was used.
+
+## P597: TRAIN-SKIP-RELEASES-WORKTREE
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, widened from recarry-conflict skips to every SKIP phase, as the new not-started
+group R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2 (S, after R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE).
+
+Why a new group:
+- The seam's owner, R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE, is carries-open. Its part #3424 merged at 07:47:51Z.
+  `roster_lib.carry_receivable` refuses a carries-open destination (R10-CARRY-SINK-BARRIER), and
+  `queue_carry.py` refused it.
+- Two receivable groups list `merge_train.py`, and neither owns this seam:
+  - R10-SEAT-SCRIPT-OUTPUT covers output calls only.
+  - R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER is a class barrier over gate-conclusion readers, and it carries a
+    policy file.
+- Neither of the two has a `handoff/`, `handoff-wip/` or `dispatch/` ref in flight.
+
+Source: queue line 276. The train skipped #3404 on a recarry conflict, but kept
+`merge_train/wt/3404` on the PR branch until the train closed. The relay's `update_pr` for the
+conflict-repair handoff answered BUSY on every pass for more than 25 min. The orchestrator
+detached the worktree by hand.
+
+Measured in the code:
+- The recarry makes `state/wt/<pr>` with `git worktree add -B <branch>` and appends it to
+  `made_wts` (`:2525`).
+- `release_worktrees` (`:2895`) removes `made_wts`, but only before the run's closing line.
+- `skip` (`:3681`) logs the line, records the row and calls `seen_mark`. It never touches the
+  entry's worktree.
+- `update_pr.sh` (lines 14-16) exits 75, BUSY, while the branch is checked out in a worktree that
+  is not its own run's.
+- So a skipped entry's branch stays held for the rest of the train. A batch that holds for a
+  rejoin can run for an hour or more.
+
+Instances:
+- `grep -h "BUSY.*merge_train/wt/" cloud-relay.daemon.log` gives 22 lines: wt/3297 5,
+  wt/3350 13, wt/3361 4.
+- The same grep on `tick-loop.log` gives 18 lines: wt/3297 2, wt/3350 4, wt/3355 3, wt/3361 1,
+  wt/3398 6, wt/3404 2.
+- So there are 40 BUSY relay passes against a train worktree, across 6 pull requests.
+- `grep -rh "SKIP #<pr> "` finds a SKIP line for each of the 6, at more than one phase:
+  - 3297: recarry and ci.
+  - 3350: carry and ci.
+  - 3355: ci.
+  - 3361: carry and ci.
+  - 3398: recarry and ci.
+  - 3404: recarry, from the orchestrator's line.
+- The fix must therefore release at every SKIP, not only at a recarry conflict.
+- Across all logs, 23 distinct pull requests hit a recarry-conflict SKIP ("main does not merge
+  without a resolution").
+- The relay pass interval defaults to 120 s (`cloud_relay.sh:164`). So 40 passes is a lower bound
+  of about 80 min of repair handoffs waiting, plus the hand detach each time.
+
+The fix:
+- `skip(pr, ...)` releases that entry's worktree at the SKIP line, if this run made it. The
+  release takes it out of `made_wts`, so the closing release does not repeat it.
+- A conflicted or dirty tree first gets `git merge --abort` when a merge is in progress.
+- Then `git worktree remove` runs, never forced. If the remove fails, the fallback is
+  `git -C <wt> checkout -q --detach`.
+- It logs `released <wt> at SKIP` or `NOT released ...`, the same as `release_worktrees`.
+- A queue entry's own `worktree` is never touched (`release_worktrees`'s rule).
+- A rejoin of a skipped entry re-makes the worktree, because the recarry path already makes it when
+  absent (`:2513`).
+
+Self-test:
+- A SKIP at the recarry phase leaves `wt/<pr>` gone, or detached, before the next entry's first
+  line.
+- A SKIP at the ci phase does the same.
+- A worktree that holds unpushed commits stays. The skip logs `NOT released`.
+- Null control: a non-skipped entry's worktree is still released only at close, as today.
+
+Cost:
+- About 20 lines in `merge_train.py` and four checks.
+- `merge_train.py` has no row in `tests/structure_budgets.json` at `cbd23f1c8b`.
+
+Binding:
+- This removes a recurring slip class: 6 pull requests and 40 BUSY passes, each followed by a hand
+  detach.
+- The group's severity is `medium`, so the machinery bar does not apply.
+- No ratchet exemption is claimed.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 179 (P598)
+
+This batch rules queue line 277 (the orchestrator's intake), 2026-11-11.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster branch at `2ff0ab30e0` or later.
+- The installed shim `$HOME/.local/state/hpo/bin/gh`, whose flag tables match main's
+  `tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh:240-241`.
+- `$HOME/.local/state/hpo/gh-calls.log`.
+- Four reads of job `130415790006`, made through the shim and around it.
+
+## P598: SHIM-ESCAPES-FLAG
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, narrowed from "add the log paths to the read arm" to the flag table, as the new
+hotfix group R10-HOTFIX-SHIM-ESCAPES (S, severity high, no `after`).
+
+Why a hotfix group:
+- The defect degrades the live merge train now, so it is not left queued behind
+  R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE-P3. That group runs after R10-TICK-RESIDUE (#3425 open) and
+  R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE (p2 in flight).
+
+Source: queue line 277. After the shim was reinstalled at 08:42Z, a haiku's job-log read was
+refused with the record-issue comment-write message. The orchestrator suspected that the read arm
+did not know the path.
+
+The path premise is refuted. These plain GET forms all reached GitHub through the shim and
+answered `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`, not a shim refusal:
+- `repos/<o>/<r>/actions/jobs/1/logs`, plain.
+- The same with `-X GET`.
+- The same with `-H Accept:...`.
+- The same with a leading `/`.
+- The same with `-i`.
+- `repos/<o>/<r>/actions/runs/1/logs` with `--method GET`.
+
+`api_gate` (`seat-gh:275-277`) returns 0 for any GET with no write flag, whatever the path.
+
+The measured cause:
+1. The haiku made three plain reads of `actions/jobs/130415790006/logs` at 09:11:20Z, 09:11:36Z
+   and 09:11:44Z (`gh-calls.log`).
+2. Replayed through the shim, the plain read gives rc=1 and 0 bytes. The stderr is gh 2.98.0's own
+   refusal: "the response contains terminal escape sequences; pass --allow-escape-sequences".
+3. The same read with `--allow-escape-sequences` is refused by the shim: "gh shim: a comment write
+   on a record issue (#201, #3394) ... refused".
+4. The reason is that `--allow-escape-sequences` is in neither `API_VAL` nor `API_BOOL`
+   (`seat-gh:240-241`, unchanged since `1d4ed28e4f`, 2026-11-05). So the unknown-flag arm
+   (`seat-gh:268-270`) returns 1, and `gate` prints the one refusal message it has.
+
+Impact, measured:
+- `merge_train.job_log` (`merge_train.py:648`) is the tree's only Actions job-log reader. It always
+  passes `ESCAPES_FLAG` (`:645`, added by `5c1bc399dd`, 2026-11-06). It falls back to a flagless
+  read only on gh's "unknown flag", which is not the shim's text.
+- `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py job-log 130415790006 tvofi/heatpump_optimizer` with
+  the shim on PATH gives rc=1 and 0 bytes.
+- The same command with the real gh first on PATH gives 1,093,937 bytes.
+- `job_log`'s callers:
+  - `failure_logs.sh`, which reads through `merge_train.py job-log` (`failure_logs.sh:42`).
+  - `gate_raise_only` (`:675`).
+  - The failed-script culprit read (`:3370`).
+  - The infra rerun (`:3633`).
+- On a None these callers read a raise-only gate red as a plain red, name no culprit and fire no
+  infra rerun. None of them refuses or warns.
+- The live train, `merge_train.py batch`, pid 90809, has `venv-ci/bin` and then
+  `$HOME/.local/state/hpo/bin` on its PATH. `venv-ci/bin` has no `gh`. So the train resolves `gh`
+  to the shim.
+- Every shim-era read through `job_log` fails, which is 100% of them.
+
+The fix, in `tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh`:
+1. Add `--allow-escape-sequences` to `API_BOOL`. It is output-only, with no request body and no
+   method.
+2. When `api_gate` refuses an unknown flag, the shim names that flag ("gh shim: unknown gh api
+   flag <x>; refused"), instead of the record-issue comment-write message. A tracker-comment write
+   keeps its own message.
+   - Why this part: the wrong message sent a seat and the orchestrator after a path cause that does
+     not exist.
+
+Self-test, in the shim's existing self-test home (`gh_calls.py`):
+- `gh api --allow-escape-sequences repos/o/r/actions/jobs/7/logs` passes the gate.
+- `gh api --allow-escape-sequences -f body=x repos/o/r/issues/201/comments` is still refused, with
+  the comment-write message.
+- An unknown flag (`--bogus`) is refused with the unknown-flag message.
+- Mutation: dropping the flag from `API_BOOL` fails the first case.
+- Null control: a plain GET of a non-tracker path passes, as today.
+
+Cost:
+- About 3 changed lines in `seat-gh` and 3 self-test cases.
+- Neither file has a row in `tests/structure_budgets.json` at `cbd23f1c8b`.
+- Interim workaround, the orchestrator's call: put the real gh's directory ahead of
+  `$HOME/.local/state/hpo/bin` for the train, or read logs by the real gh's absolute path.
+
+Binding: this is a defect fix on a non-production instrument, at severity high. It restores 100%
+of the tree's job-log reads under the shim, against 0% today. The machinery bar does not apply.
+No ratchet exemption is claimed.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 180 (P599)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` line 278. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` (`48ee8ce3a6`), fetched at 09:28Z.
+- The verdict bus: `origin/verdict/*`, fetched at 09:25Z. The handoff bodies are `origin/handoff-body/*`.
+- `tools/audit/seat/review_strength.py --by class --window d1=2026-11-10T09:00:00Z..2026-11-11T09:30:00Z`.
+- Batch 163 (P577), which measured the same class on five heads at 05:01Z.
+- No GitHub API calls.
+
+## P599: MUTATION-VACUOUS-DIFF-PASS-REFUSE
+
+Verdict: REJECT both arms:
+- (b) a refusing diff-mutant step in `body_push.sh`;
+- the expected saving of "one review round on ~35% of fix PRs".
+
+Arm (a) is answered by measurement below. It needs no change.
+
+The proposed step refuses on the generator's survivors. That generator reaches 2 or 3 of the 17
+sites reviewers named in 24 h. It would have prevented the block on 1 of the 7 blocked PRs. On a
+head where it catches anything, it raises about 23 survivors per real site. This repeats P577's
+REJECT and adds two more heads, neither of which the generator can reach. The class keeps its
+root cause `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-MUTATION-VACUOUS.md`, and no new seat is owed.
+
+Source: queue line 278, 2026-11-11T09:19:12Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+### Before: what the bus says (24 h, d1 window)
+
+- **All reviewed PRs.** 33 reviewed PRs, real-catch incidence 8/33, first-pass yield 10/22 (0.45).
+- **Blocks by class.**
+  - `mutation-vacuous`: 8 verdicts on 6 PRs, first pass 0/5.
+  - `mutation-survivors`: 2 verdicts on 1 PR.
+- **Distinct blocked heads in the class:**
+  - 3419 (`245ddf7876`);
+  - 3423 (two heads);
+  - 3425;
+  - 3427;
+  - 3428 (two heads);
+  - 3431 (two heads);
+  - 3448 (`185699076f`).
+- **Totals.** That is 7 PRs and 10 head-blocks. Across them the reviewers name 17 sites.
+- **PR 3442.** It has no verdict ref on the bus, so it is not counted.
+- **Share of PRs.** 7 of the 33 reviewed PRs (21%) were blocked in the class. That is the ceiling on
+  the proposal's "~35%".
+
+### Arm (a): did the last 20 fixer handoffs run the diff pass?
+
+The count covers the newest 20 `handoff-body/r10-*` refs, from tick-residue to process-slim-p2.
+Each BODY.md was grepped:
+- **2/20 (10%) ran `mutant_run.py --diff`.**
+  - plan-page-residue ran it.
+  - suite-env-residue also ran it. It reports "lists no mutant", because the diff touched only
+    `tests/` and one shell script.
+- **7/20 ran hand-built `--spec` mutants.** These were:
+  - arbiter-off-restore;
+  - dependabot-3414-compat-p2;
+  - review-dispatch-residue-p1;
+  - worktree-gc-live;
+  - outside-diag-redact-location;
+  - outside-dhw-charge-settle;
+  - suite-env-residue.
+- **11/20 carry no mutant evidence.**
+- **`MUTANT_CMD` is set in 0/20.** process-slim-p2 only mentions it.
+
+The low usage is real. The question the ruling turns on is different: would the pass have caught
+what the reviewers caught?
+
+### What the generator can reach (mutant_run.py, measured in P577)
+
+The generator only reaches some lines:
+- it mutates added `*.py` lines only;
+- it skips lines under `tests/` and `dev/`;
+- it applies statement-level operators only.
+
+Site by site:
+- **3419.** One of its 2 sites is caught, and only uncapped (at positions 50 and 51 of 51). The other
+  site is YAML.
+- **3425, 3427, 3428, 3431.** These are measured in P577. Together with 3419 they give 2/11 sites at
+  cap 40 and 3/11 uncapped. 3431's site is in `tests/harness.py`, which the generator skips.
+- **3423 (new): 0 of 2+ sites.** Both are on an awk line inside a shell script, and the generator
+  does not read shell.
+- **3448 (new): 0 of 4 sites.** The diff is `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh` alone, which is shell.
+- **Total.** 2-3 of 17 sites (12-18%). The step would have prevented the block on 1 of 7 PRs (3419,
+  uncapped only). That saves 1 review round in 24 h, against 33 reviewed PRs, which is 3%. The
+  proposal expects 35%.
+
+### Standing cost of a refusing step
+
+- **Time.** At the default cap of 40, the step costs 40 × the self-test time per handoff. For the
+  measured 1-4 s self-tests that is 40-160 s. A `features_block.py` command costs more. P577's
+  uncapped run of one head took 31 s.
+- **Noise.** P577 found 47 survivors on the 2 heads that caught anything, against 3 real sites.
+  Precision is about 6%.
+- **Triage burden.** A refusal would make every survivor a triage record before the handoff. That
+  is about 23 records per head on such heads, which is a token cost larger than the one review
+  round it saves 3% of the time.
+
+### Bar
+
+- None of the four >20% axes is met.
+- Review rounds saved: 3%.
+- Right-first-time: +1/22 first-pass reviews, about 4.5 points.
+- The step does not remove the slip class, because 14-15 of the 17 sites are outside its reach.
+
+The reach is the binding number. 9 of the 17 sites are shell, YAML or `tests/`, and the generator
+reads none of them. Making the pass refuse cannot change that.
+
+### Expected after, if adopted
+
+The class incidence would go from 7/33 PRs to 6/33. The first-pass yield would go from 0.45 to
+about 0.50, still under the 0.6 alert.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 181 (P600)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` line 279. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster`, read at 09:55Z.
+- The live board `$HPO_STATE_DIR/tick.txt`, measured from main at 2026-11-11T09:45:32Z, and a copy
+  of `owed-unactioned.json`. Every `owed_unactioned.py` run here used `--no-write`.
+- No GitHub API calls beyond one `gh pr list` for #3425's state.
+
+## P600: OWED-CAP-BLINDS-UNACTIONED
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT. The ruling has two arms. It opens the not-started group R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P2 with
+`after: [R10-TICK-RESIDUE]`.
+
+Source: queue line 279, 2026-11-11T09:49:37Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+### Measured
+
+**The cap line is unreadable.** The current board's cap line is
+`-> OWED handoffs capped at 20 of 46; ...`.
+- `orchestrator_tick.py:2427` prints that line, flagged, so it matches `owed_unactioned.FAMILY` (`:56`).
+- `key_of` has no pattern for it, so it reaches `raise Unreadable` (`:120`).
+- On the live board, `owed_unactioned.py --tick tick.txt --state <copy> --no-write` exits **rc 2**
+  `UNREADABLE`.
+- That one line blinds all 85 keys on the board.
+
+**Null control.** The same board with only the cap line removed (`grep -v '^-> OWED handoffs capped
+at'`) exits **rc 1**. It reads 85 keys and reports 2 UNACTIONED:
+- `audit-r10-roster`, 37 sweeps, 110.7 h;
+- `r10-process-slim`, a handoff stranded for 47.2 h, `repair=update`.
+
+Both have been standing unflagged while the check was blind.
+
+**Held triage refs crowd the cap.** The 20 `OWED handoff:` lines printed under the cap
+(`CAP_ORPHANS = 20`, `:182`) are dominated by triage refs:
+- 14 of the 20 (70%) are `triage-s14-batch*` refs. By ruling these open no PR until the stamp sweep.
+- Only 6 are fixer or record work.
+- 26 more orphans are hidden "next pass". That pass never comes while the held refs stay.
+
+### Bar
+
+- **(a) It removes a recurring slip class.** This is the owed-but-unactioned detector itself. It
+  has been dead on every sweep since at least 08:21Z, which is more than 1.5 h at the beat cadence.
+  On the blinded board it hides 2 real items, one of them 110 h old.
+- **(b) It is a >20% improvement on the owed-work signal.** 70% of the capped OWED-handoff slots go
+  to refs that are owed nothing until the stamp sweep. Listing them last returns those 14 of 20
+  slots to actionable lines.
+- **Cost.** A one-pattern change in `key_of` and a sort key in `orphans()`. The runtime cost is
+  under 1 ms per sweep.
+
+### Carry (for R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P2)
+
+R10-TICK-RESIDUE owns both files and is carry_receivable. Its PR #3425 holds a `merge` verdict at
+`c93903f075` (09:34Z) and is heading to the train. A carry there would re-open a merge-ready PR, so
+this ruling opens a not-started sibling that runs after it instead.
+
+1. **`tools/audit/seat/owed_unactioned.py`, `key_of`.** Read the tick's level line
+   `OWED handoffs capped at <n> of <m>` as a non-obligation and skip it. The individual
+   `OWED handoff:` lines carry the obligations. Do not raise on it.
+   - The self-test gains that board line: before the fix it gives rc 2 UNREADABLE, after it a
+     computed result.
+   - Mutation proof: deleting the new pattern returns rc 2.
+2. **`tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py`, `orphans()`.**
+   - Order `stranded` so that held triage and record batch handoffs come after every other topic
+     before the `[:CAP_ORPHANS]` slice. Held batches are topics `triage-*` and the record batches
+     the stamp sweep opens.
+   - Keep them listed: never exclude them, because `bus.sh orphans --exclude-topic` would hide them
+     for good.
+   - Print the held count in the cap line.
+   - Self-test: a 25-line `stranded` holding 14 held refs prints all 11 others within the cap.
+
+### Local workaround, until the group merges (verified)
+
+Run the unactioned check on the board with the one cap line filtered out:
+`grep -v '^-> OWED handoffs capped at' tick.txt > tick-nocap.txt`, then
+`owed_unactioned.py --tick tick-nocap.txt --state owed-unactioned.json`.
+
+Measured with `--no-write`: rc 1, 85 keys, 2 UNACTIONED.
+
+The two other forms do not work:
+- **An acks-file form.** `key_of` raises before any ack is read.
+- **`cloud_relay.sh dispose` on the held refs.** It writes the relay ledger's `dispositions.tsv`.
+  `bus.sh orphans` never reads that ledger, so the refs stay stranded and still fill the cap.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 182 (P601)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` line 280. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster`, read at 10:20Z.
+- `$HPO_STATE_DIR/cloud-relay.log`: its `POSTED <utc> <pr> <head>` lines.
+- The committer times of the `origin/probe/rev-*` refs.
+- No GitHub API calls.
+
+## P601: RELAY-ARMS-BEFORE-HANDOFF-ARM
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, narrowed:
+- arm 1 is accepted: the relay and confirm arms run first;
+- arm 2 is rejected: detached per-branch updates.
+
+The ruling opens the not-started group R10-RELAY-ARM-ORDER.
+
+Source: queue line 280, 2026-11-11T10:08:41Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+### Measured
+
+**The order.** `pass()` (`cloud_relay.sh:860`) runs, serially:
+`handoff_arm; carry_fold_arm; probe_arm; confirm_arm; stuck_arm; noreturn_arm`.
+
+`handoff_arm` (`:572`) runs `update_pr.sh`, which runs a full prepr, inline. Every `probe/rev-*`
+verdict returned in the meantime waits for it.
+
+**Verdict-to-post latency, 24 h from 2026-11-10T10:00Z.** Each `POSTED` line is matched to the
+latest `probe/rev-<pr>-*` commit at or before it. That gives n = 45:
+- median 6.8 min;
+- p75 18.1 min;
+- p90 51.6 min;
+- max 112.7 min.
+
+16 posts waited more than 10 min, 11 more than 20 min, for 715 PR-minutes in total. The tail is the
+proposal's class: 3449 waited 55 min and 3423 73 min, both posted at 10:09Z after the #3442 update.
+
+**Confound.** The latency also holds confirm retries and refusals. For example, 3438's 113 min
+includes a re-review. So the shares below are upper bounds.
+
+**The coupling.** `confirm_arm` (`:433`) reads the open-PR list `handoff_arm` writes (`:588`, P332).
+When that file is absent, it already lists the open PRs itself (`:434-436`). So the arms can be
+reordered without losing confirm's open-PR filter.
+
+### Bar
+
+- **Benefit.** With the relay first, a returned verdict waits at most one pass interval plus the
+  relay's own seconds, not an update queue. The 11 posts over 20 min carry about 510 of the 715
+  PR-minutes. Capping them near one tick removes up to about 55-65% of verdict-wait minutes.
+- **Why that counts on the bar.** Verdict wait is on the critical path of every PR between its
+  review and its repair or merge. A cut of more than 20% therefore counts on the
+  programme-completion axis. Reviewer idle time falls with it.
+- **Cost.** One pass-order change plus hoisting the one open-PR listing, so that both arms share
+  it. No extra API calls, and zero extra seconds per pass.
+
+### Narrowed
+
+Arm 2, detached updates under a per-branch lock, is REJECTED:
+- it is not needed for the latency once arm 1 lands;
+- it would run several full preprs at once on the local box;
+- `update_pr.sh` already answers BUSY on a held worktree, 83 times in this log, so the lock already
+  exists and a detached runner adds a second concurrency surface for no measured gain.
+
+### Card (R10-RELAY-ARM-ORDER)
+
+1. **`tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh` `pass()` (`:860`).**
+   - List the open PRs once at the head of the pass, into the file `confirm_arm` already reads.
+   - Then run `probe_arm`, then `confirm_arm` (under `--confirm`), then `handoff_arm`,
+     `carry_fold_arm`, `stuck_arm` and `noreturn_arm`.
+   - `handoff_arm` reuses that listing instead of making its own call.
+   - **Self-test.** With a stub `handoff_arm` that sleeps or records its order, a probe ref returned
+     before the pass is POSTED before `handoff_arm` starts.
+   - **Mutation proof.** Restoring the old order fails that check.
+   - **Null control.** A pass with no probe ref posts nothing and still runs the handoff arm once.
+   - The existing `pass` self-tests at `:1033-1035` stay green.
+
+Destination: every group that lists `cloud_relay.sh` is done or absorbed, except
+R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE, which the brief excludes. So this is a new S group. Its overlap with
+R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE is on a distinct seam, the arm order in `pass()`.
+
+### Local workaround, in force
+
+Run `cloud_relay.sh --watch --once --confirm` beside the pass. This is the orchestrator's own
+workaround and is unchanged.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 183 (P602-P605)
+
+This batch rules `s7/triage-queue-s7.txt` lines 281 to 284. The bar and the denominators are
+batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster`, read at 10:50Z.
+- `$HPO_STATE_DIR/open-driver/open-driver.log`.
+- No GitHub API calls. The CodeQL job durations are the orchestrator's, quoted in line 281.
+- Nothing was run to measure line 283. It was read statically, on the orchestrator's instruction.
+
+## P602: CODEQL-PYTHON-CRITICAL-PATH
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, narrowed to arm (c): a pulse line that names the one unfinished job against its
+baseline. It goes as a carry on R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P2, which is not-started and carry_receivable.
+
+Arms (a) and (b) are not triage's to accept, and are routed to the owner:
+- (a) paths-ignore on the python leg;
+- (b) making `Analyze (python)` non-gating for the PR gate.
+
+Source: queue line 281, 2026-11-11T10:31:01Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+### Measured
+
+- **Job durations.** `codeql / Analyze (python)`: 2173-3623 s over six jobs today. The sibling
+  legs: 48-104 s.
+- **Cause, already measured in the tree.** `.github/workflows/codeql.yml:113-126` records it as the
+  single-threaded extraction of `tests/features.py`, plus a query evaluation that grows with it. The
+  python cap is 75 min (`:128-134`). The file says: "The structural cure (splitting
+  tests/features.py) is an owner ruling, not this cap".
+- **Python bytes on main.** 26.1 MB in total:
+  - `tests/`: 9.2 MB, of which `tests/features.py` alone is 3.6 MB;
+  - `tools/`: 5.3 MB;
+  - `custom_components/`: 3.2 MB.
+- **Arm (a).** paths-ignore of `tests/`, or of `tests/` plus `dev/`, narrows the security finding
+  set. The workflow's own rule (`:41`) is that its one paths-ignore entry "narrows no finding set".
+  The query suite is `security-extended` (`:198`).
+- **Arm (b).** Non-gating on PRs changes a required context of the `main` ruleset.
+
+So both (a) and (b) are owner decisions, and so is the features.py split. Triage cannot accept them.
+For the owner, the expected effect of either is PR CI wall time falling from 36-60 min to the
+next-longest job.
+
+### Arm (c): the slip it removes
+
+- **The slip.** Two near-complete python jobs were cancelled at 10:29Z, misread as hung. Each was
+  about 36-60 min of critical-path wall time, and the relaunch restarts the clock. That is about
+  70-120 min of critical-path CI lost in one misread.
+- **The line.** When exactly one job of the waited run is unfinished, the pulse prints its name,
+  elapsed time and baseline: the p50 and max of the last 6 completed jobs of the same name, read
+  from the same check-runs listing. For example:
+  `CI waits on 1 job: codeql / Analyze (python) 41m of p50 47m / max 60m (normal)`.
+- **Cost.** One line per pass, from data the wait already lists. No extra API calls.
+
+## P603: OPENER-STALE-LEVEL-TIP
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT. It goes as a carry on R10-RELAY-ARM-ORDER, which is not-started and
+carry_receivable. That group is the same incident's group: the relay pass length starves its
+consumers.
+
+Source: queue line 282, 2026-11-11T10:31:33Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+### Measured
+
+- **What the log shows.** `open-driver.log` holds 18 `SKIP ... moved` lines, all on two topics:
+  - r10-outside-disinfection-setpoint, 9 lines. This is the top-priority outside PR.
+  - r10-process-slim-p2, 9 lines.
+
+  Each pass skipped the topic because the board's sha was not origin's live handoff tip.
+- **Why it never cleared.** `open_driver.py:278-279` skips on `moved`, and the board is rewritten
+  only once per relay pass.
+- **Why P601 does not fix it.** P601's reorder writes the level seconds after the relay arms. It
+  still writes it once per pass, and a pass still holds one full prepr per update. So it would not
+  have stopped this 45-min starvation.
+
+### Card (carry 2 on R10-RELAY-ARM-ORDER)
+
+**`tools/audit/seat/open_driver.py`.** On `moved`, re-run the candidate checks at the live tip in
+`tips` instead of skipping:
+- `no-body`, `seen`, `landed` and `fix-branch` are each already computed from live refs;
+- open_pr.sh's own refusals cover the rest.
+
+Keep `SKIP moved` only when the live tip is absent.
+
+- **Self-test.** A board line at sha A, with origin's tip at B and B clean, opens at B.
+- **Mutation proof.** Restoring the skip fails that check.
+- **Null control.** A line whose handoff ref is gone still prints `SKIP moved`.
+
+**File overlap.** R10-SEAT-IDENTITY-P5 also lists `open_driver.py`. The seam is distinct: the
+candidate's tip, not identity. The overlap is admitted.
+
+## P604: SELFTEST-FORK-EXHAUSTION
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT arm (a), narrowed: a process cap in the tracked mutant driver
+`tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py`. It opens the new S group R10-MUTANT-RUN-FORKCAP; no receivable
+group lists `mutant_run.py`.
+
+REJECTED:
+- arm (b), a re-entry guard in `cloud_relay.sh`'s self-test;
+- a separate root-cause seat.
+
+Source: queue line 283, 2026-11-11T10:37:31Z, orchestrator s14, and its follow-up relay naming the launcher.
+
+### Measured, by reading only
+
+- **What happened.** A chain of `cloud_relay.sh --self-test` runs nested about 680-700 deep in one
+  process group. It exhausted the per-user limit (`ulimit -u` 1333) for about 4 min and stopped every
+  local seat. It was launched by an out-of-tree prototype that ran a reverted hunk of the #3448 head.
+  The prototype killed only its direct child.
+- **The tracked driver groups and kills correctly, but has no cap.** `mutant_run.run_cmd` (`:86-99`)
+  already starts the command in a new session (`start_new_session=True`). On timeout it SIGKILLs the
+  whole group (`_killpg`, `:102-104`).
+
+  The timeout defaults to 600 s (`:347`), and nothing caps the process count. The chain filled the
+  1333 slots in under 4 min. So under the tracked driver the same mutant would still have exhausted
+  the host, and held it until the 600 s timeout fired. The group kill bounds how long the outage
+  lasts, not whether it happens.
+- **pr_bounded.** `pr_bounded` (`pr_args.sh:296-343`) bounds wall time and setsids each entry. It
+  runs unmutated code, whose re-entry is guarded by PR_BOUND (`cloud_relay.sh:1862`). It is not the
+  exposure, so no card is put on it.
+- **Why arm (b) fails.** A re-entry guard inside the self-test is itself mutable code. A mutant that
+  deletes or reverts it reproduces the chain, and that is this incident's shape, since a reverted
+  hunk made the self-test re-enter. Only the driver, which runs outside the mutated tree, can bound
+  every mutant.
+- **Why no root-cause seat.** The launcher is identified. The cause is named: an unbounded fork
+  under a mutant with no process cap. The countermeasure is this card. A root-cause seat would add
+  nothing that the card does not owe.
+
+### Bar
+
+- It removes a slip class that, in one instance, stopped every local seat and the wake loop.
+- Exposure grows with every mutant run. P599 and the mutation-vacuous investigation are driving more
+  mutant runs over self-tests.
+- Cost: a cap check at launch and per poll. No new dependency.
+
+### Card (R10-MUTANT-RUN-FORKCAP)
+
+**`tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py` `run_cmd`.** Bound the command's process tree. Either of these
+works:
+- poll the command's session every 0.5 s and `_killpg` it past 256 processes;
+- or set an RLIMIT_NPROC soft limit at the user's current count plus 256 in the child.
+
+Report it as a distinct outcome, `FORKCAP`, never as `KILLED`. A cap stop says nothing about
+whether the test pins the mutant; counted as a kill, it would hide a survivor.
+
+- **Self-test.** A command that forks a chain without end is stopped within seconds, reported as
+  FORKCAP, and leaves no process of its session behind. The user's process count returns to its
+  starting level.
+- **Mutation proof.** Removing the cap fails that check. Run it under a test-only low cap, for
+  example 32, so the proof never approaches the host limit.
+- **Null control.** A command that forks a bounded 10 is unaffected.
+
+The finding goes into the mutation-vacuous report: an out-of-tree mutant prototype must run through
+`mutant_run.py`, never its own Popen.
+
+## P605: CARRY-LANDED-OWN-GROUP
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT. It goes as a carry on R10-CARRY-AUDIT-P5, which is not-started and
+carry_receivable, after R10-BODY-CONTRACT. That group owns the carry-audit seam of a part-N body.
+
+Source: queue line 284, 2026-11-11T10:38:57Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+### Measured
+
+- **What bus.sh passes.** `bus.sh carry_landed` (`:228-237`) runs
+  `carry_audit.py landed --body <b> --pr "#N"`, with no `--topic`. The `landed` subcommand accepts
+  `--topic` (`carry_audit.py:962-966`).
+- **Why the own group is lost.** `own_group` (`:602-610`) falls back to a topic token only for a
+  source that is not `#`-prefixed. When the roster's `pr_group` does not name the PR, the own group is
+  None. Then the own-carry status exemption (`:643`, `mut:ownstatus`) never applies, and a part-N
+  body's "not built in this part ... Carry: <own group>" lines are refused CARRY-MISSING.
+- **Cost of the instance.** #3448: 23 lines, one refused reviewer dispatch, one body-repair seat,
+  about 15 min.
+- **Exposure.** 6 live part-N groups (`-P<n>`), 1 in-progress and 5 not-started.
+- **Check behaves correctly.** `check` already resolves the group from `--branch` (`:995`).
+
+### Bar
+
+- It removes a recurring slip class that refuses the dispatch of every later-part body carrying an
+  own-group status line.
+- Saving: about 15 min and one repair seat per hit, about 90 seat-min over the 6 live part-N groups.
+- Cost: one argument in bus.sh. The PR's head ref is already in the `gh api pulls/N` response that
+  carry_landed reads.
+
+### Card (carry on R10-CARRY-AUDIT-P5)
+
+**`tools/audit/seat/bus.sh` `carry_landed`.** Read `.head.ref` in the same `gh api` call, map it to
+the topic with `topic_grammar.py pr-topic`, and pass `--topic <topic>` to `carry_audit.py landed`.
+
+- **Self-test.** A part-N body with "Carry K: not built in this part ... Carry: <own group>",
+  under a stub PR whose head ref is the group's fix branch, passes carry_landed (rc 0).
+- **Mutation proof.** Dropping `--topic` returns rc 1, CARRY-MISSING.
+- **Null control.** The same line naming another group is still refused.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 184 (P606)
+
+This batch records the orchestrator's ruling on the part of P602 (batch 183, queue line 281) that
+was routed to the owner. The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster`, read at 11:05Z.
+- The orchestrator's relay, 2026-11-11, after batch 183.
+
+## P606: CODEQL-PR-PATHS
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, as the new S group R10-CODEQL-PR-PATHS: sonnet fixer, opus reviewer, serial on the
+train.
+
+**Authority.** This verdict is the orchestrator's ruling under mandate 6715477401 (scope `all`). It
+was not given by tvofi in person. Triage records it and adds what the tree says. It is not a triage
+judgement of the owner-routed arms.
+
+### The ruling, as relayed
+
+- **Pull-request runs.** These analyse Python with `tests/` and `dev/` path-ignored, on the PR leg
+  only.
+- **The push-to-main run.** It keeps the full path set. No finding class is dropped from main. A
+  finding is only moved from before the merge to main's own run.
+- **Missed findings.** A finding that main's full run raises and the PR leg missed is a main red,
+  handled like any other.
+- **The required context.** `codeql / Analyze (python)` stays required on PRs, under the same name.
+  The non-gating-leg arm is DECLINED.
+- **Acceptance.** The PR python Analyze job must run in under 15 min. The body states before and
+  after job seconds from `tools/audit/seat/ci_critpath.py` over at least 5 runs each.
+
+### What the tree adds (for the fixer)
+
+- **There is no scheduled run.** `codeql.yml` is a `workflow_call` callee of ci.yml alone
+  (`:63-70`, `:86-94`); "the schedule is gone". The full path set therefore survives on main's
+  push runs only.
+- **How the leg learns the event.** The leg cannot see the event itself, because ci.yml's `codeql`
+  job calls it. ci.yml must pass the event, or a paths input, through `workflow_call`.
+- **The existing paths-ignore is pinned.** The one entry today is `.claude/workflows/*.js`
+  (`codeql.yml:199-202`), and `tests/entities.py` pins it (`:19999`, `:21919-21929`). The pins move
+  in the same PR.
+- **Comparison risk.** GitHub compares a PR's analysis against the base branch's analysis in the
+  same category. Alerts in the ignored paths may then read as "fixed" on every PR. The fixer
+  measures this on one PR before handoff. If they do read as fixed, the PR leg gets its own category,
+  so the comparison is not polluted.
+- **Overlap.** R10-HOTFIX-RESTORE-BASE-SKEW (in-progress) also lists `ci.yml` and `codeql.yml`.
+  The seam is distinct: the PR leg's paths. The overlap is admitted, and the train's serial
+  workflow rule orders them.
+
+### Bar
+
+- **Before.** The PR python Analyze job takes 2173-3623 s. The sibling legs take 48-104 s. The job
+  is on the critical path of every code PR and of the train's admission wait.
+- **Target.** Under 900 s.
+- **Expected cut.** At least 58% of that job's duration, and up to 75%.
+- **Owner's axis.** CI time, well over 20%.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 185 (P607)
+
+The bar and the denominators are batch 141's. This proposal is a root-cause countermeasure, so
+`proposal-triage.md` judges it on whether benefit clearly outweighs cost, not on the 10%/20%
+machinery thresholds. The 20% bar is still reported, because the proposal asks.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` `9c8603012a`, read at 10:56Z.
+- The mutation-vacuous investigation's evidence directory (`rca-mutvac`, out of tree): `verdicts.tsv`,
+  `heads.tsv`, `sites.tsv`, `verdicts/`, `batch*.log`.
+
+## P607: MUTVAC-REVERT-ARM
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, narrowed. The narrowed part is a statement-deletion operator, `STMT_DEL`, in the
+existing driver's diff mode (`tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff`), report-only. It goes as a
+carry on R10-MUTANT-RUN-FORKCAP, which is not-started, has no dispatch ref, and owns the same file.
+
+REJECTED:
+- a separate revert arm, or a second tool. Its copy-tree, process-group kill and fork cap would be
+  a second copy of the driver's. The out-of-tree prototype that did this without a group kill is
+  the P604 incident.
+- running the reviewer's existing diff arm unchanged as the fixer's pre-handoff step, as the only
+  countermeasure. It reaches 7 of 23 reviewer sites (see below).
+
+ROUTED TO THE ORCHESTRATOR (policy, owner-class): the `fixer.md` step 2 change that would make a
+pre-handoff run mandatory. Triage's data for that ruling is under "Bar".
+
+Source: queue line 285, 2026-11-11T10:49:37Z, orchestrator s14, from the Fable mutation-vacuous
+investigation.
+
+Instances:
+- **Window figures, recomputed.** Command: first row per PR in `verdicts.tsv` from
+  2026-11-04T10:49Z, then count verdict `merge` and a mutation-class cause.
+  - Result: 207 first verdicts, 85 first-pass (0.411), 29 mutation-class.
+  - The investigation reports 208, 85 and 31. The two differ only on the window edge.
+  - If the claim were false, the first-pass rate would differ by more than a point, or the
+    mutation class would be under 10.
+- **How the reviewer found each site.** Command: tally the `found` column of `sites.tsv`.
+  - Result: 43 blocked rows, 113 sites.
+  - 89 sites came from hand mutants, 14 from CI's mutation lane, 2 from `mutant_run.py`, and 8
+    from other routes.
+  - The body's own mutants reproduce as killed on 33 of 43 rows (`K`).
+  - Kinds: 98 sites are Python (`prod` 21, `tpy` 69, `tests` 8). The rest are sh 15, js 3 and
+    yml 3.
+  - Pattern tags: L 22, W 14, A 14, F 2, CI 1.
+- **Reach of the existing diff arm on the sites reviewers named.**
+  - Command: `s14-15/cover.py`. For every `*.py:N` that a blocked verdict names, it checks
+    whether the line is added in `base...head` (`heads.tsv` columns 3 and 4). It then checks
+    whether `mutant_run.mutate_line` (`:245-271`) yields an operator for that line.
+  - Result: 23 distinct resolvable sites over 14 blocked heads. 16 sites are added lines and 7
+    are not; the reviewer mutated an unchanged caller or context line.
+  - Of the 16 added sites, the 5 existing operators reach **7 of 23** (30%): GUARD_OFF 5,
+    RETURN_DEL 1, CALL_DEL 1. 9 added sites have no operator, because they are assignments,
+    expression statements and continuation lines.
+  - If the claim "the reviewer's own diff arm is enough" were true, this would read about 20 of
+    23.
+- **Reach of statement deletion.**
+  - Command: `s14-15/lr.py`. It replaces each added site's line with `pass` at its indent and
+    compiles the file at the blocked head.
+  - Result: 7 of the 9 operator-less sites compile, or would compile once a deleted
+    continuation statement is taken whole (5 of these compile as a single line; the
+    continuation ones are `coordinator.py:6032`, `orchestrator_tick.py:758` and
+    `survivor_list.py:77`).
+  - The union with the existing operators reaches about **14 to 16 of 23** (61-70%). The
+    prototype's revert unit reached 13 of 23.
+  - The 7 sites on lines that are not added stay out of reach of any diff-scoped arm.
+- **The prototype's claim was spot-checked on #3425.** `batch*.log`, `orchestrator_tick.py`:
+  SURVIVED=2 at the blocked head (r1), and the named site is killed at the merged head
+  (SURVIVED=1, a different unit).
+
+Cost:
+- **The change.** It is one operator in one file, `mutant_run.py`, of about 30-50 lines with its
+  self-test arm. There is no new file, CI check, hot file or dependency.
+- **Budgets.** `mutant_run.py` is not in `tests/structure_budgets.json`.
+- **Runtime.** The investigation measured 2-136 s per file where the self-test is under 16 s.
+  The operator adds at most one mutant per added simple statement.
+- **The limit.** Serial runs are infeasible for `cloud_relay.sh`, `bus.sh`, `prepr.sh` and
+  `roster_edit.py`. That is why this card rides on FORKCAP's process cap and keeps
+  `--max-mutants` and `--report-only`.
+
+Binding:
+- **Bar.** The class ceiling is +19% to +36% relative to first-pass. The revert unit's estimate is
+  0.409 to about 0.436 (+6.7%, range +3% to +17%). Scaled to 14-16 of 23 sites, it is about
+  +7% to +9%. That is **below the 20% bar** for a permanent mandatory step.
+- **What carries the ACCEPT.** The narrowed part is a root-cause countermeasure with a small,
+  one-file, opt-in cost.
+  - Reviewers already drive `mutant_run.py --diff`, and `survivor_list.py` reads its
+    `SURVIVED` lines (#3262: four blocks in one class). So the operator first replaces hand
+    mutants on the W and L patterns, at no standing cost.
+  - At 207 first verdicts a week, +7% means about 6 first-pass merges, so about 6 fewer
+    repair-and-re-review rounds a week. The cost is CPU seconds on an opt-in run.
+- **Why the mandatory step is not ruled here.** It is policy, and its own gain (under 20%) is
+  unproven.
+  - Triage's recommendation is to DEFER it until this operator lands. Then re-run the card's
+    acceptance harness and the next 10 mutation-vacuous blocks against STMT_DEL output.
+  - If the operator's survivors cover 12 or more of the reviewer-named sites in those 10 blocks,
+    a mandatory report-only run in step 2 is the stronger form, for files whose self-test is
+    under 16 s.
+
+### Card (carry on R10-MUTANT-RUN-FORKCAP)
+
+**`tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py` `mutate_line` / `diff_mutants` (`:245-297`), and the operator
+list in the module docstring (`:25-45`).**
+
+- **The operator.** Add `STMT_DEL`, from the `ast` of the file at the diff's head end. For each
+  simple statement whose line span intersects the added lines:
+  - Replace the whole span with `pass` at the statement's indent. Skip compound headers
+    (`if`/`for`/`while`/`with`/`try`/`def`/`class`, which `GUARD_OFF` already covers), docstrings,
+    `import`s, `print` and `_LOGGER` calls.
+  - Keep the existing compile check and dedupe: a statement that `CALL_DEL` or `RETURN_DEL`
+    already turns into `pass` is not a second mutant.
+- **Output.** `SURVIVED <file>:<first line> STMT_DEL  pass`, which `survivor_list.py` already
+  keys on `file:line`.
+- **Acceptance (the finder's harness).** These 23 sites (block, head, base, site) are re-run with
+  `--list`.
+  - **What must pass.** The listed mutants must reach 14 or more (today 7). The five sites below
+    marked + must each gain a STMT_DEL mutant.
+  - **Null control.** A diff that adds only a comment or a docstring lists zero STMT_DEL mutants.
+  - **Mutation proof.** Removing the operator's dispatch line drops the count back to 7.
+- **Self-test.**
+  - A fixture adds a bare assignment that no check reads: it is reported as SURVIVED STMT_DEL.
+  - The same assignment pinned by the check is reported as KILLED.
+  - A three-line continuation statement yields exactly one mutant.
+
+Sites (head..base short ids from `heads.tsv`; `+` = needs STMT_DEL, `=` = already reached):
+- 3184-r1 `freq_control.py:228` =; 3193-r1 `coordinator.py:2235` =, `:6032` + (continuation)
+- 3231-r1 `inputs.py:467` +, `inputs.py:478` =, `config_flow.py:1667` (list element; a deletion,
+  not `pass`)
+- 3232-r3 `coordinator.py:1957` +; 3241-r1 `orchestrator_tick.py:758` (continuation)
+- 3260-r1 `carry_audit.py:927` =, `:929` +, `:956` =; 3264-r1 `replan.py:2041`
+- 3297-r1 `coordinator.py:4575` +, `:5400` =; 3341-r1 `survivor_list.py:77` (continuation)
+- 3425-r1 `orchestrator_tick.py:1220` =
+- Not-added (out of reach, listed so the count is honest): 3184 `tests/features.py:24969`,
+  3193 `coordinator.py:11057`, 3231 `config_flow.py:1590`, 3262-r6 `beat_jobs.py:392`,
+  3405 `config_flow.py:1562`, 3428-r3 `plan_page.py:212`, `replan.py:3290`.
+
+**Size.** FORKCAP was S. With this carry it is an S/M edge in one file; the fixer stays sonnet. It
+runs after the fork cap inside the same PR, because a statement deletion that removes a re-entry
+guard is exactly the P604 shape.
+
+### Owner-class answer (recorded after the ruling)
+
+The orchestrator ruled on the routed `fixer.md` step 2 arm under mandate 6715477401 (scope `all`),
+2026-11-11. This is not tvofi in person.
+
+- **DEFERRED, as triage recommended.** There is no policy pull request now.
+- **Re-open trigger.** It returns as a triage-queue line once two things hold:
+  - STMT_DEL has merged;
+  - 10 further `mutation-vacuous` blocks exist after that merge to measure against.
+- **Threshold.** STMT_DEL survivors must cover 12 or more reviewer-named sites in those 10
+  blocks. If they do, the stronger form is a mandatory report-only run in step 2, for files whose
+  self-test is under 16 s.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 186 (P608)
+
+The bar and the denominators are batch 141's.
+
+Sources:
+- origin/main `cbd23f1c8b`. Every line number below is at that commit.
+- The roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster`, read at 11:10Z.
+- The live train log (`merge_train` state directory, `train.log`).
+- GitHub, read at 11:10Z:
+  - `gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup,mergeStateStatus` for #3445, #3405 and #3398;
+  - ruleset 23698884 (`main-protect-checks`).
+
+## P608: TRAIN-POLICY-REASON-STALE-CONTEXT
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, narrowed to the misread that both queue lines share. The narrowed arm makes
+`policy_refusal` read each required context's newest rollup entry, not the last one listed. It goes
+as a carry on R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2, which is not-started, has no `*train-residue-p2*` ref, and owns
+`merge_train.py`.
+
+REJECTED:
+- **(b), undraft on every route.** The draft flag is not the cause:
+  - #3398 was undrafted (`UNDRAFT #3398 141f8af1b1a5` in `train.log`), and it was still refused
+    with the same text.
+  - #3445 is still BLOCKED after `gh pr ready`.
+- **Reading `isDraft` in the reason.** A draft reports `mergeStateStatus` DRAFT, not the BLOCKED
+  that all three instances logged.
+- **(a) as worded, a CodeQL re-run as the blocker.** `codeql / Analyze (python)` is not a required
+  context: the ruleset's required list is `["gate"]`, strict false. The newest-entry rule below
+  still covers a re-run of any required context in progress over an older success.
+
+Source: queue lines 286 and 287, 2026-11-11T10:54:06Z and 10:54:22Z, orchestrator s14.
+
+Instances:
+- **The reason text in all three instances.** Command:
+  `grep -E '#(3445|3405|3398)' train.log | grep 'policy refusal'`.
+  - Result: all three read `mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, reviewDecision APPROVED: every required
+    context is green, so the missing requirement is a review at <head>`.
+  - If draft were the cause, the state would read DRAFT, or #3398 would carry no UNDRAFT line.
+- **The cause, at #3445's head `7fb8680c85`.** Command:
+  `gh pr view 3445 --json statusCheckRollup`, the `gate` entries in list order.
+
+  | index | conclusion | completed |
+  |---|---|---|
+  | 88 | FAILURE | 09:29:08Z |
+  | 89 | FAILURE | 09:24:57Z |
+  | 90 | FAILURE | 09:22:49Z |
+  | 91 | FAILURE | 09:29:14Z (the newest) |
+  | 92 | SUCCESS | 09:23:45Z |
+
+  - The newest `gate` is red, so GitHub blocks the merge.
+  - `policy_refusal` (`:2792-2834`) builds `last[name] = conclusion` in list order. It keeps entry
+    92, the older SUCCESS. It then reads every required context as green and blames a review.
+  - If the claim were false, the last-listed `gate` entry would also be the newest, or would be
+    red.
+- **The train attempted #3445 unproved.** `#3445 D: a batch of one merges at its verdicted head,
+  unproved`. Under `--overlap`, main itself was red on `gate` right before. So nothing upstream of
+  the attempt read the PR's own red `gate`, and the policy read was the only diagnosis.
+- **#3405 and #3398.** Both are merged, and their rollups now show only SUCCESS `gate` entries. The
+  refusal-time state cannot be re-read, so they are counted as the same text, not as the same
+  proven cause.
+- **What each instance cost.** A wrong park reason led to a re-add, a batch, and an orchestrator
+  diagnosis (lines 286 and 287 themselves). The correct reason, "gate red at 7fb8680c", sends the
+  orchestrator straight to a re-run.
+
+Cost:
+- About 10-15 lines in one method of `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`, and one self-test fixture.
+- No new file, check or API call: the same `gh pr view` read.
+- `merge_train.py` is not in `tests/structure_budgets.json`.
+
+Binding: this repairs a misdiagnosis in existing machinery, not new machinery. The benefit clearly
+outweighs the cost: three instances in one session, each a lost batch slot plus a manual
+diagnosis, against a one-method change.
+
+### Card (carry on R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2)
+
+**`tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` `policy_refusal` (`:2792-2834`).**
+
+- **The newest-entry rule.** Reduce `statusCheckRollup` to one entry per context name, chosen by
+  newest `completedAt`, else `startedAt`. Any entry still QUEUED, IN_PROGRESS or PENDING makes the
+  context pending, so the method returns `wait`. Never use list order.
+- **Context names.** Keep the existing name/context key, and key the duplicates the same way.
+- **The reason text.**
+  - A newest-red required context is reported as `required context(s) red at <h>: gate`.
+  - A context that is only an older success under a newer failure must never read as "green".
+
+**Self-test fixture.** It is the five #3445 `gate` entries above, frozen.
+- **In list order:** the method returns red `gate`, with wait false and approval false.
+- **Reversed:** the result is the same.
+- **[SUCCESS 09:00, IN_PROGRESS started 10:29]:** the method waits.
+- **Null control:** five SUCCESS entries in any order still reach the review branch, as today.
+- **Mutation proof:** restoring the last-listed-wins dict fails the list-order case.
