+## P714: outside-contributor fixer and review cycle (the mechanism)
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the owner ruling above, first and second sentences. Destination: a new group,
+R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE, size L, lane IN, source outside, design first under decision 0014.
+Today a fork pull request is rebuilt by our fixer as an hpo-author pull request: pr-contract
+refuses any other author (0011), verdicts post only through bus.sh confirm as hpo-approver (0013),
+and tools/pr/app_approve.sh takes a verdict only from an allowlisted account. Wanted: an
+allowlisted contributor's fork pull request is admitted unchanged when every required check and the
+body contract pass at its head and a valid "Fix review: merge <head>" verdict exists for that head,
+which the contributor's own reviewer seat may produce; merge of main, code-owner approval, the
+train and the record stay ours. The brief lists what the design must decide. No after-edges; it
+shares tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py with R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER (critical path) and must not
+take it ahead of that group. Severity medium. Figure against 20%: not applicable (owner ruling).
+
+## P715: the fold rule for outside work, rest of round 10
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the owner ruling above, third and fourth sentences. Rule: for the rest of round 10 a
+non-critical outside request is planned into round 10 only if it does not move the programme
+closure ETA; if it does, it is planned for round 11. A critical one (a defect a user is hitting
+now) is exempt. Applied against plan-live.json generated 2026-11-12T07:27Z (closure
+2026-11-15T05:43Z); a group finishing after about 2026-11-14T12:00Z moves closure. Planned
+finishes: SUPPLY-MIN-RUN-PAUSE 11-13T22:29, LEARNER-ROBUSTNESS-P2 11-13T21:51, START-COUNTER-EDGES
+and MODE-BEFORE-SUPPLY-ON 11-14T04:49, RESTART-LEARNING-PR-B 11-14T05:53, PLANNER-PRICE
+11-14T06:02, DHW-START-HYSTERESIS 11-14T11:04 (round 10); DISINFECTION-STEP-NOTICE 11-14T18:23,
+LEARNER-ROBUSTNESS-P3 11-15T00:23, OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE unplanned, L with design (round 11).
+None sits on an after-edge path into R10-ROUND-PLAYBOOK-FINAL or closeout; none but P714's group
+shares a file with a critical-path group. Stage changes are the orchestrator's to order.
+A round-11 group is recorded as P709 did: an append-carry on R10-ROUND-PLAYBOOK-FINAL adding the
+item to dev/audit/README.md's round-11 opening plan carries, then set-stage <group> deferred.
+
+## P716: closure and the catalog pull request by 2026-11-15 outrank outside work
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the owner ruling above, last sentence. Programme closure and R10-CATALOG-PR are critical
+and must be ready by 2026-11-15; they outrank every non-critical outside group. R10-CATALOG-PR's
+after-edges (USER-DOCS-VERIFY, ARCH-DOCS, ROUND-PLAYBOOK-FINAL, CLOSEOUT-CLEANUP, CLOSEOUT-PREP,
+ARCH-DOCS-DELTA) hold every closeout predecessor; no edge is missing, so no roster op. The plan
+puts it post-closure (start 11-15T07:43Z, finish 11-16T07:27Z), past the date: the orchestrator's.
+
+## P717: R10-HOTFIX-REPLAY-CLASS-CUT discharged by #3477
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Its one carry (0-based 0; #3477 body "Carry 1"), the RCA countermeasure, is built at merge

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 239
+
+Source: owner rulings (tvofi, 2026-11-12 about 07:50Z, 08:00Z and 08:10Z), recorded, not weighed
+(P718, P719). Ruling recorded by triage s14-64.
+
+Owner rulings, verbatim:
+- ~07:50Z: "The "may not move the programme closure later" ruling should also apply to groups that
+  are self-fed from the ongoing round 10"
+- ~08:00Z: "Good. It should also apply to any new such self fed groups"
+- ~08:10Z: "The contributur cycle mechanism should be built in full, asap"
+
+## P718: the closure rule extends to self-fed groups, existing and new
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the 07:50Z and 08:00Z rulings above, extending batch 238 P715 (outside work) to work round
+10 feeds itself: residue parts, HOTFIX groups not fixing a red main, FLY and SEAT groups, and
+instruments grown by triage ACCEPTs, both those already on the roster and any appended from now on.
+Rule for the rest of round 10: such a group stays in round 10 only if the critical path or closeout
+needs it, or it is small and finishes without moving the programme closure (plan-live finish at or
+before about 2026-11-14T12:00Z); otherwise it is planned for round 11. Standing rule for this seat:
+every ACCEPT that would append a group or a carry gets that closure test at ruling time, and the
+entry says which; a round-11 outcome is recorded the P709 way (append-carry on
+R10-ROUND-PLAYBOOK-FINAL citing the ACCEPT, and a new group at stage deferred). Existing groups:
+the stage changes are the orchestrator's to order, from the self-fed table measured by s14-63; this
+entry queues no roster op. Exempt: R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE (P719). Closure and R10-CATALOG-PR
+by 2026-11-15 still outrank all non-critical work (P716). Severity high (closure date). Figure
+against 20%: not applicable (owner ruling).
+
+## P719: R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE is round 10, in full, top priority above the cap
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the 08:10Z ruling above. The group (appended by P714, source outside) is round 10 by owner
+order: its design and every build part run in round 10, no part deferred, exempt from P715 and
+P718; it is dispatched at top priority above the open-PR cap. This supersedes the earlier note that
+the build's round is decided at design approval. Plan check, one read of origin/main: replan.py
+dispatch_tier returns TIER_TOP for roster_lib.is_outside (source "outside", set at 4721), and
+roster_lib.dispatch_rank returns RANK_TOP for it, so the tier needs nothing more. The plan's own
+cap exemption (scheduler pick with cap_exempt) keys on the computed critical path only; this group
+has no after-edges and is not on it, so the plan models it as a top-tier peer of the critical path
+inside the slot count, not above it. No roster field expresses "above the cap"; the cap that binds
+dispatch is the orchestrator's open-PR cap, so above-the-cap is the orchestrator's dispatch act,
+and no roster op is queued. The group's L size plus design is unmovable slot load in the date
+analysis. Severity high (owner order). Figure against 20%: not applicable (owner ruling).

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 245
+
+Source: orchestrator order of 2026-11-12 to triage seat s14-72 (three proposals). Standing owner
+rulings applied: the closure test on every ACCEPT (P718); R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE and outside
+work first (P719); owner-approved study decisions built now when they do not move closure (P734).
+
+## P739: open_pr.sh re-renders a body's figure blocks at the head it pushes
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Source: seat s14-69's defect note and local patch (s14-69/NOTE.md and
+s14-69/open_pr-figure-refresh.diff, uncommitted, against origin/main).
+Instances: `tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh` writes the PR body once from handoff-body/<topic>:BODY.md
+and never runs `tools/pr/figure_block.py refresh`. A figure block names the head it was rendered
+at, so pr-body lint refuses p1 after a main merge and always refuses p2, whose row commit moves the
+head. Seen on R10-OUTSIDE-DISINFECTION-SETPOINT part 2: the opener was refused twice and PR #3495
+was opened and auto-closed after its p2 refusal (s14-69/NOTE.md). `open_pr.sh --self-test` runs
+only delivery_row.sh's and pr_args.sh's self-tests, so no case covers the p1/p2 body path: it
+passed before and after the patch (s14-69/NOTE.md).
+Cost: one S fixer part, about 25 changed lines in open_pr.sh (s14-69 diff: 2 hunks, 7 added
+lines) plus a self-test case. A body with a figure block then runs the full prepr at p2 instead of
+the row-only skip (the refreshed body differs past the `## Head` note); a body without a block
+keeps the skip. No capped file named; the fixer reports structure.py and `--budgets` rows.
+Binding: an outside product group's PR cannot open while its body carries a figure block; outside
+work outranks all else (P719).
+Destination: new group R10-HOTFIX-OPENPR-FIGURE-REFRESH, class hotfix, kind instrument, size S,
+severity high, sonnet fixer, opus reviewer, files tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh, after none. Overlap
+on open_pr.sh with R10-SEAT-SCRIPT-OUTPUT (in-progress, PR #3490) is admitted by seam: this group
+touches only the p1/p2 body-render points. Build: (1) refresh before p1 when the merged head
+differs from the code head, refusing with nothing pushed on failure; (2) refresh before p2 at the
+row head, always, closing the PR with the reason on failure; (3) a self-test case with a figure
+block in the body. Null control (s14-69/NOTE.md): a figure-block body opens with p1, p2 and the row;
+the mutant without the p2 refresh is refused at p2 with "figure-block scope-line names another
+head"; a body with no block still prints `ROW-ONLY: prepr SKIPPED`. (4) the rerun hazard the same
+open hit: a closed-after-p2 open leaves branch fix/<topic>-pr and a detached worktree that make
+the next `git worktree add -b` fail; the re-run removes or reuses them. Keeping row-only for a
+figure-block-only re-render is optional, not owed.
+Closure: needed by an outside group's opener (DISINFECTION-SETPOINT part 2), so it is on the
+outside path and enters round 10; size S on a non-binding lane. Not measured by replan; main runs
+the replan on dispatch if it wants a number. Machinery bar: severity high skips the 10% keep bar.
+Figure against 20%: not applicable (defect repair).

-## The shape at programme end
-
-The page above describes `main`. The round-10 roster still holds groups that
-change the shape of the code, and each change below is marked with the group
-that lands it, so R10-ARCH-DOCS can resolve every line once its group is done.
-No group in the roster adds a module, so the module map above is already the
-module set at programme end.
-
-- **One owner of the thermal parameters**, copied on write, so a service call cannot publish a torn or unclamped set across its await, and the coordinator context is written once [target: R10-PARAMS-OWNER]
-- **The live state published whole**: the thermal state, the away state and the event callbacks publish a copy, and each collaborator owns its own fields [target: R10-LIVESTATE]
-- **One owner per duplicated shape**: a power reader in `inputs` that refuses a non-finite or out-of-range reading, one hour-clock owner and one finite-float owner [target: R10-ARCH-SHAPES]
-- **Payload mixins on the entity base**: the finite scrub, the value and path mixins and the zone set-point attributes, shared by the sensors that each carried their own guard [target: R10-SENSOR-PAYLOAD]
-- **A delivered-heat meter input**: measured COP from heat over electric energy, split into hot water and space by the pump's mode [target: R10-HEAT-METER]
-- **An honest COP state**: "not measurable here" where no meter makes COP observable [target: R10-COP-GATE]
-- **One rule for scores**: no evidence is a dash with a reason, never zero, and one view model behind the scores, Savings, Advisor and Health [target: R10-SCORES]
-- **Learner progress in the payload**: phase, progress and what each learner waits for [target: R10-LEARNER-ETA]
-- **One options page template** driven by the field registry [target: R10-CONFIGFLOW-PAGES]
+## One owner per concern
+
+Each bullet names the module that owns one rule, and what the rule is.
+
+- **The thermal parameters have one writer.** `_publish_params` in `coordinator.py` builds a new parameter set, which re-runs the divisor floor, and rebinds the coordinator context and the live model to it. A solve or a learner in the middle of an await keeps the set it read. The coordinator context is a frozen dataclass, replaced whole.
+- **A long computation works on a snapshot of the live state.** In `coordinator.py` a solve takes its own deep copy of the configuration, the parameters and the thermal state, and the away recovery job and the diagnosis each take a copy of the thermal state.
+- **One owner per duplicated shape.** `inputs.py` owns the power conversion: `normalize_power_kw` converts by the entity's declared unit and refuses an unknown one, and `state_power_kw` refuses a reading that is not finite before or after conversion. `finite_float` in `const.py` gives a value as a finite float, or a default. Two functions own what the end of the day reads as: `quiet_windows.wall_clock` folds it to 00:00, and `dhw_schedule.format_clock` keeps a window label's 24:00.
+- **One payload read on the entity base.** `entity.py` owns the finite scrub, the payload-number rule and the zone set-point attributes. A mixin in `sensor.py` reads the number at one path of the payload.
+- **A delivered-heat counter.** `heat_energy.py` owns the span a delivered-heat kWh counter measured, the time the pump spent in each duty, and the one rule that splits an interval between space heating and hot water: the observed shares, else the plan's split. It imports nothing from Home Assistant; the coordinator reads the entities and calls in.
+- **An honest COP state.** `accuracy.cop_observability` owns the state: no electric meter, then an electric meter with no measured heat, which reads "not measurable", then estimated inputs or a heat meter.
+- **One rule for scores.** `compose_scores` in `coordinator.py` puts the grades on one scale; no evidence is no grade with one reason code, never zero. The insight payload takes the restart advice once and hands the same advice to the scores, and `house_loss_converged` is the convergence rule that both the envelope grade and the learning view's "learned" flag read.
+- **Learner progress in the payload.** `learner_progress.py` gives each thermal learner's phase, its progress and what it waits for.
+- **One options page template.** `config_flow.py` builds the options pages that edit stored fields from one field registry. The setup overview, the factory reset, quick setup and the pre-fill preview build their own forms.
 
 ## Where to start reading

With that sensor the efficiency health watch also judges the pump at a common water temperature, so a hotter supply is not reported as a failing compressor, and it skips any interval where the sensor has no fresh reading — **so while that sensor is dead the watch does not judge space heating at all**. Readings judged this way keep their own baseline, so switching the option or the sensor on or off starts that baseline afresh rather than comparing unlike numbers. **The learned offset is capped at 15 °C**, so on a plant whose supply runs well above the modelled curve only part of the extra work is priced. The lift is only charged above a 35 °C supply. Refused together with a throttling valve, whose tank temperature already sets the price. |

@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+# R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING, part A: observe, estimate, persist, publish
+
+Revision 1, answering `Design review: revise edf2ceb333956fa6797d6bb30d7c5b72f440123e`. Base: origin/main d08ed31049cd3636cde4d2fdeb3bd7cd4b3c842a. Every line cited below is at the predecessor's head 068074f0f2c2dfdb57fc1821ed39f3510bc913ed (pull request 3405, R10-WATER-SETPOINT-FEEDBACK), which this group builds after. The finding, install description and reasoning are Bankaifan's, pull request 3420, with thanks; their note is this ref's parent commit edf2ceb333 and stays unchanged on 3420. No finder harness: outside report, owner-routed.
+
+## Finding (Bankaifan, 2026-11-10, alpha innotec LWDV 91-1/3, Luxtronik 2.1, select transport, 15 min steps)
+
+| Mode write | Direction | Source leg | Return at write / set-point | Compressor | Off time |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 14:02:53 | hot water to space | 17 min | 44.2 / 32.0 °C | stopped after 19 s | 8.2 min |
+| 14:18:53 | hot water to space | 3 min | 43.6 / 32.0 °C | stopped after 12 s | censored: HPO wrote the mode before the restart |
+| 15:00:01 | hot water to space | 29 min | 51.0 / 32.0 °C | stopped after 12 s | 8.5 min |
+| 03:32:32, 13:45:53, 14:15:53 | space to hot water | n/a | n/a | ran on | n/a |
+| 13:29:53 | hot water to space, 14 s leg | 14 s | return not heated | ran on | n/a |
+
+`cycling_penalty_batch` (`optimizer.py:1546`) prices the swing of the combined series (`optimizer.py:4707`), so this switch costs nothing in the plan, and nothing observes it.
+
+## Scope (revise point 6)
+
+The reviewer's split is adopted. This group is **A only**: the learner exists, records, estimates, persists and publishes; **nothing reads the estimate to change a plan or a write**. B (arbiter order latch and minimum share), C (planner price), D (start counter fed from edges) and E (mode write ahead of the supply switch-on) are the orchestrator's to place; B waits on the owner's product call the verdict routed.
+
+## Owning seam (points 1, 2, 3)
+
+**Owner of episodes, estimate and store: a new module, duty_switch.py, beside `wear.py`.** It holds a pure learner (no Home Assistant import, like `wear.py`), its own `QuarantiningStore` keyed per config entry (one entry is one pump) on the pattern of `dhw_learning.py:111`, and its per-entry registry on the pattern of `_STATES` (`pump_arbiter.py:374`). `ArbiterState` gains no field and `_persist` (`pump_arbiter.py:1699`) keeps saving only `written`.
+
+**Owner of "the compressor runs" and its edges: `wear.py`**, which already owns the start counter. It gains a pure classifier and a debounced edge tracker. Signal order: the frequency from `freq_control.resolve_reading` (the existing owner of the Hz reading, used at `coordinator.py:10729`) above a named floor where one is configured and numeric; else metered power at or above `on_threshold_kw` (`thermal_model.py:1785`), the one threshold both existing readers already share; else no signal. Readers in this group: the new learner only. **Stays, start counter** (`coordinator.py:10446`, fed from `_record_accuracy` at `coordinator.py:9976`): moving it changes the counted starts that feed `_effective_cycling_cost` (`coordinator.py:10432`), a behaviour change this group's finding only reports; it is part D. **Stays, 3405's loop** (`_ran_kw`, `pump_arbiter.py:1204`, read at `:922` and `:1423`): it controls on the size of the draw error, so it needs kW and its own sample period, not an edge; it keeps the shared threshold.
+
+**Owner of the listener: duty_switch.py.** It registers on the frequency sensor, else the power entity, and keeps its unsubscribe in its own registry. The arbiter attaches it from `_listen` (`pump_arbiter.py:1667`) and detaches it in `release_listeners` (`pump_arbiter.py:1661`). **`coordinator.py` gains zero lines and zero attributes**; `coordinator_attrs` and `coordinator_private_reach` do not move. The new module never imports `pump_arbiter.py` (`import_cycle_modules` is at zero): the arbiter hands it a reader callable at attach.
+
+## Shape
+
+```
+listener event --> reader() --> wear classifier --> edge tracker --(edge: when, running)--> learner
+_write, slot "mode" landed (pump_arbiter.py:1332) --(when, old option, new option, context)--> learner
+_arbitrate, each pass (pump_arbiter.py:1466) --(when, context)--> learner: void checks, close window, save if changed
+sensor.py:2776 extra_state_attributes <-- learner summary (counts, durations)
+```
+
+Calls the arbiter makes, all into duty_switch.py: attach(hass, entry id, entities, reader), detach, note-mode-write, note-pass. Read API for B and C, unused in A: per direction, usable (bool), stop probability, median off seconds.
+
+Context (built by one arbiter helper from `ArbiterInputs`, `pump_arbiter.py:346`): supply on (`_pump_off`, `:1639`), defrosting, disinfecting, boost held, immersion active, inlet temperature (`_flow_inlet_c`, `:714`) and written space set-point, source-leg age (`dhw_since`, `:329`, or the mode record's age), target duty has demand (room under `_planned_room`, `:575`; tank under its set-point), plan keeps the target duty on, origin (share, lease, other).
+
+**Episode.** Opens on a landed mode write between the two single duties while the tracker says running, and counts only if the circuit was heated (inlet minus set-point at least 2 K; with no inlet entity, source leg at least 1 min), the target has demand and the plan stays on. Within 3 min: **stopped** on a stop edge, **kept** at expiry, **void** on supply off, any other write (a re-send by `hold`, `:1275`, included), defrost, boost, disinfection, immersion, a set-point below the open-loop base (3405's loop), or loss of signal. Off time runs to the next start edge, censored by any HPO write in between. One open episode at most.
+
+**Edge tracker.** An event whose class equals the settled class returns after one parse and compare. A changed class is confirmed after a named debounce, by the next event or by the arbiter's pass; the edge carries the first changed event's time. This replaces a time-spacing throttle (`power_guard.py:82`) deliberately: that throttle can drop the final event to zero, after which no event arrives and the stop is never seen. The listener never calls `apply` (`pump_arbiter.py:1449`).
+
+**Estimate and its invariant (point 8).** Per direction, decayed counts k (stopped) and n (stopped plus kept), half-life 14 days. Decay scales both alike, so **p = k / n never moves with age; only n falls.** Usable switches **on** at n >= 5, evidence spanning two days, p >= 0.5; once on it stays on until n < 2.5 or p < 0.3. The latch is stored. One episode lifts n by at most 1, so a direction that fell under 2.5 cannot cross 5 on one episode: no toggle at the threshold. When B or C avoid a direction, n halves every 14 days, usable drops, the default runs and at least two fresh episodes re-test it: that bounded re-test is the relearn path, and its cost is those starts. Off time: median of a capped list (32, oldest dropped).
+
+**Store.** Version 1: per direction k, n, last-decay instant, first and last episode day, latch, off-time list, void and censored counts. `from_dict` validates shape and bounds and returns an empty learner otherwise, as `wear.py:101` does. Loaded on the first pass; reports before load are dropped.
+
+**Published** on the compressor-starts sensor's attributes, read from the learner in `sensor.py:2776`, never through the coordinator payload (`coordinator.py:10707`), which the goldens snapshot: per direction k, n, stopped, kept, void, censored, median off seconds, span days. Counts and durations only.
+
+## Planner price (point 4): part C, not built here
+
+Direction for C's own design round, not a commitment: the price belongs in the objective closure of `_solve_objectives` (`optimizer.py:4622`) beside `cycling(combined)`, because `_solve_space` (`:4230`) and `_co_optimize` (`:3200`) both score with it and both hold the hot-water and space series separately; the duty sequence comes from the rule `step_duty` (`pump_arbiter.py:466`) already uses; the off time enters as lost headroom at `optimizer.py:4246`; `OptimizationConfig` (`:2027`) gains the two learned values next to `cycling_cost` (`:2070`). An indicator of a duty change is not smooth, which is why C needs its round.
+
+## Alternatives
+
+- **Record on `ArbiterState`, saved by `_persist`** (the contributor's): the pump-duty store holds only the ownership record that `_load` (`:1710`) and `_writable` (`:1731`) filter; a second meaning there puts learned state in the arbiter.
+- **Learner as a coordinator attribute**, like the hot-water learner (`coordinator.py:3731`): costs `coordinator_attrs`, which only moves down, and a line in the load list.
+- **No listener, sample per arbiter pass**: it would see an 8 min stop, but a void cause and a stop inside one tick lose their order, so the void rule cannot be applied; and D needs edges.
+- **Classifier in the new module**: D's reader, the start counter, would then import the switch learner for a signal `wear.py` already owns.
+
+## Sibling sites (point 7)
+
+`git grep -n -E "select_option|await _command\(" -- 'custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py'` prints the only mode write (`pump_arbiter.py:1324`, through `_write`) and its two callers (`:1486`, `:1658`). Observing at `_write` covers every origin:
+
+| Path into space | Site | In A |
+|---|---|---|
+| split inside a "both" step, hot water first | `_share`, `:1494`, `:1513` | covered, origin share |
+| step change, re-solve, away return (arrives as a plan) | `_planned_duty`, `:1129`, `:1151` | covered, origin other |
+| lease cap | `_leased`, `:1217` | covered, origin lease |
+| re-send | `hold`, `:1275` | same option: opens nothing, voids an open episode |
+| boost end | `_without_block`, `:1162`; `:1477` | void while held, covered after |
+| disinfection | `:1094`, `:1502` | void while disinfecting; "both" to space is not a single-duty switch |
+| supply tick, supply off | `supply_tick`, `:1607`; `:1483` | writes no mode; voids |
+| unload | `release`, `:1651` | detach first, no episode |
+| set-point gate transport | `desired`, `:1083` | out of scope: no single-duty mode write exists there |
+
+## Evidence, by file (point 5)
+
+All in `tests/features.py`, failing today because the module and the two `wear.py` symbols do not exist:
+
+1. Observer replay of the table: three stopped, three kept, the 14 s row counts nothing, row 2 counts as stopped with no off sample; each void cause in turn turns a stopped episode void.
+2. Edge tracker: `unavailable`, `unknown`, non-numeric give no signal and void; a one-frame zero is no edge; a final zero with no later event is confirmed by the pass.
+3. Gates: below 5, or within two days, not usable; on at the thresholds; the 2.5 and 0.3 off conditions; decay leaves p unchanged; one episode after switch-off does not switch on.
+4. Restart: dict round trip keeps counts and latch; a malformed or out-of-bounds payload loads empty; the off list never exceeds its cap.
+5. **Null control, no stops**: an install whose every switch is kept, and
+6. **null control, flat prices**: scenario `tests/golden/flat_prices.json`; in both, the plan, the split order and every written command are byte-identical between an empty learner and one saturated at p = 1. This is the stronger control and it holds by construction in A.
+7. Attributes carry only the listed keys, all numeric.
+
+**No golden moves; neither claim file is touched.** A moving golden is a defect in the build. The new file goes into a measured closure in `tests/closures.json`. Mutation targets: the count conditions, each void rule, the four latch comparisons, the debounce comparison, and the report line in `_write`. Field check on the contributor's install after B or C; not an acceptance test of A.
+
+## Hot files, position, carries
+
+After R10-WATER-SETPOINT-FEEDBACK. Hot: `pump_arbiter.py`, `wear.py`, `sensor.py`, `tests/features.py`, `tests/closures.json`, plus the new module. Not touched: `coordinator.py`, `optimizer.py`, `dhw_planner.py`, `const.py` (constants live in the new module; `const_modules_over_50` does not move).
+
+## Notes for the fixer
+
+- No signal is never "stopped"; it voids. Carry: R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING (item n1)
+- Class-equality early return and debounce, not a time-spacing throttle; never trigger a pass. Carry: R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING (item n2)
+- Off list capped at 32; counts are two floats per direction. Carry: R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING (item n3)
+- `QuarantiningStore` (`store.py:673`) scrubs poisoned leaves to a default and does not reject, so the learner's own `from_dict` must return empty on any invalid shape. Carry: R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING (item n4)
+- 3405's loop is on the void list by name. Carry: R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING (item n5)
+- 2 K, 1 min, 3 min, 14 days, 5, 2.5, 0.5, 0.3 are named constants from one day on one install, not measured thresholds. Carry: R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING (item n6)
+- Re-read every `pump_arbiter.py` anchor after 3405 merges. Carry: R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING (item n7)
+- The reviewer's `optimizer.py` lines were at another tree; here they are `:4707` and `:4246`. Carry: dismissed: corrected in this note (item n8)
+- The frequency floor: check what the sensor reports when stopped before fixing the constant. Carry: R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING (item n9)
+
+Seat tokens: subagents 75890, 49789 and 41294; the harness reports no figure for the main loop.
+
+## Part A as built: where the code departs from this note
+
+The text above is the approved design, unchanged. Part A (`duty_switch.py`) departs from it in the points below; parts B and C build on the code, so where the two disagree this section is the one to read.
+
+- **No read API.** "Read API for B and C, unused in A" was not built: an unused module-level function is refused by `tests/structure.py`'s `dead_top_level_symbols`. `Direction.usable`, `Direction.p` and `Direction.median_off_s` hold the three values; the part that first reads them adds the module-level reader together with its first caller. Control: a reader added with no caller turns that metric red.
+- **Stored record.** Version 1 stores, per direction, `k` and `kept_w` (the kept episodes' weight; n is their sum), the decay stamp, first and last day, the latch, the off list and the four integer tallies `stopped`, `kept`, `void`, `censored`. With k and n stored, `tests/finite_boundary.py`'s in-domain probe produced k over n. n has no ceiling but the load bound.
+- **Publication is conditional.** A direction publishes its attributes only once it holds a stopped, kept or void episode, and the median only once an off time exists: five `coord_*` goldens snapshot the starts sensor's attributes. A reader of those keys treats an absent key as no observation, never as zero. Control: with the condition removed (the body's mutant `publish_only_observed`) the section's attribute check fails.
+- **The feedback-loop void is wider.** An episode voids on any target the loop moved off the open-loop one (`FeedbackRun.sent_c` set), raised as well as lowered; it costs evidence only.
+- **Origin** (share, lease, other) is not in `SwitchContext`: nothing in A reads it.
+- **Source-leg age** is the age of the mode record the write replaced, not `dhw_since`, which `_leased` has reset by the pass that leaves hot water.
+- **The heated gate's space set-point** is the command's, written right after the mode, not the written record, which at that instant is still the hot-water leg's.
+- **The heated gate is decided per set-point unit.** The inlet is compared with the command's space set-point only where that set-point is a water temperature (`space_setpoint_unit` flow or return). On the default indoor unit it is the planned room temperature, which a running pump's return is always over, so there the gate is the source leg's age, as it is with no inlet reading. Control: the section's "an indoor set-point, a return 9 K over the room's, and a 30 s leg" row opens nothing, and the same return with a 60 s leg books.
+- **The span ages with the evidence.** Once a direction's decayed n is under `SPAN_FLOOR_N` (0.5, one episode a half-life old; a named constant, not a measurement) its first and last day are forgotten, so "spanning two days" is judged on evidence that still weighs. Without it the first day never moved and one year-old episode made six stops on a single day usable. A reader of `span_days` treats 0 beside non-zero tallies as "nothing recent", not as "never observed".
+- **The pass does not judge a lost signal.** `DutySwitchLearner.note_pass` takes no "signal known" argument: with an episode open the settled class is unknown only after a confirmed edge to unknown, which `edge` has already voided, and `detach` clears both, so no install could exercise it.
+- **Factory reset keeps the store** (`_FR_STORES` in `tests/features.py`), where every other learned estimate is voided. The owner rules on this before any part reads the estimate.
+- **The supply minimum-run hold** of pull request 3420 is removed and built nowhere.
+
+## Part B, first pull request: the carries part A left to its first reader
+
+Part B's own rule (the arbiter's split order) is a later pull request of the same group; this one settles what part A's review left to "the part that first reads" and changes no plan and no write.
+
+- **`N_ON` is a decayed weight, not a count of episodes** (part A's body item ef5d3875). Each booking ages the earlier ones first, so five stops ten hours apart weigh under five and a sixth latches; the approved note's "n >= 5" already reads that way, and the code is unchanged. Pinned by the section's check "N_ON is a weight"; control, the check where a stop taking an undecayed n from 4 to 5 switches a direction on.
+- **The publication moves with observations, not with age** (item c7d068a1). The starts sensor publishes `p` to two places, which decay does not move, and `n` as the whole episodes still weighing, rounded down; `k` is no longer published, being `p` times `n`. Age alone now moves only `n`, one step per whole episode lost. Pinned by the section's check "age alone moves no published attribute within a day"; its null control is the decayed weight read to two places, the old resolution, which moves within the same reads.
+- **Still owed by part B's later pull request**, which first reads the estimate: the module-level reader added with its first caller (item 1b22f416); the owner's ruling on factory reset keeping this store, before that reader merges (item 3c666f5b); a reader taking an absent key as no observation and `span_days` 0 beside non-zero tallies as "nothing recent" (item 90bc5153); evidence accruing at different rates per set-point unit (item d088605d); and the ceiling on `n` the group's ruling sets, which also bounds how often the published `n` can step.

+A change of the away indicator, the away switch or the holiday calendar
+replans at once, not at the next optimization interval.
+
+**Away and the mold guard.** With *Keep cold surfaces below mold humidity* on,
+the room is never planned below the mold-safe temperature, and that floor
+outranks the away setback by design: protecting the coldest surface comes
+before saving. The mold-safe temperature rises with indoor humidity and falls
+with outdoor temperature. The floor the plan holds is that temperature capped
+at your comfort target: the guard never heats past the target, because drying
+a house further is a dehumidifier's job. In a humid house in cold weather the
+floor can therefore sit at or near the target itself. On one recorded install,
+at 52–53 % indoor humidity and 1 to 5 °C outdoors, the mold-safe temperature
+worked out at 19.2 to 20.9 °C; with a 19.5 °C comfort target the floor in force
+was 19.2 to 19.5 °C, and the plan heats to it while you are away. The setback
+to *Temperature while away* then saves little or no space-heating energy for as
+long as the guard holds the floor above it. Hot water still drops to its away
+minimum. The setback saves again once the house is dry enough, or mild
+enough, that the mold-safe temperature falls below the away temperature; the
+**Mold Floor Breach** sensor's `floor_c` attribute shows the floor in force.

 ### COP, and the tracking-error gate
 
 With a power meter, COP becomes observable instead of derived from a nameplate
 figure and a temperature curve. The learned `cop_scale` multiplies the nameplate
 curve, bounded to [0.5, 1.6] so a mis-scaled power entity cannot destroy the
-model. A sample only counts if the pump is genuinely running (below a third of
-nameplate the reading is mostly auxiliaries), and samples are skipped while the
-immersion element is drawing, because a resistive kW is a different appliance on
-the same meter.
+model. A sample only counts if the pump is genuinely running: the draw and the
+plan's ask must both reach 80 % of the configured minimum power (with no minimum
+configured, 30 % of the maximum), and never less than 0.2 kW, because below that
+the reading is mostly auxiliaries. Samples are skipped while the immersion
+element is drawing, because a resistive kW is a different appliance on the same
+meter.
+
+**Measured COP, and the model's COP.** A COP is *measured* only where both sides
+are meters: a heat energy meter or a thermal power meter for the heat, and a
+power or energy meter for the electricity, neither of them the pump's own
+estimate (the *meter or estimate* settings on the metering page), and, for an
+interval that heated hot water, a heat reading declared to see the hot-water
+circuit. Only a measured COP is recorded and graded. Every other install still
+trains `cop_scale`, from the vendor's estimate or from the commanded-versus-
+measured power ratio below, but its efficiency is the model's own, and the
+Health page says so: *COP cannot be measured on this install*, with what it
+lacks.
+
+**Efficiency at part load.** *Heat pump COP loss at max power* (default 0, off)
+lowers the COP linearly from the minimum to the maximum power, to one minus the
+setting at max power, because larger heat flows need larger temperature
+differences across the heat exchangers. The plan then prices each step at its own
+draw, so a kWh of heat bought at high power costs more than one bought near
+the minimum. A value
+at or above *band / (band + max power)*, band being max minus min power, would
+make more power buy less heat; the setting is then ignored and treated as 0.

+not writing compressor power itself (a compressor frequency entity with its
+control set to Control skips the probe, since the plan already sets the draw
+directly). On the same
+kind of night (between 23:00 and 05:00, outdoor between −5 and 10 °C, a price
+among the cheapest 30 % of the horizon) it asks for full power, which writes the
+*Heating flow ceiling*, for the longest step of at most two hours that keeps the room inside
+the comfort bound, and records the metered draw. It needs room for at least two
+metering intervals, or it aborts. Twelve recorded intervals make a learned
+maximum, their median. Where that median is more than 15 % below the configured
+**Heat pump max power**, the plan is solved with the learned figure, because
+the pump cannot draw what the setting says; it never raises the configured
+maximum. A learned maximum lapses 45 days after its newest sample, and two
+ordinary intervals at the top set-point that draw more than 15 % above it
+clear it, so it is measured again. A probe runs
+at most every 7 days until a maximum is learned and every 30 days after. The
+**Learning Model Status** sensor publishes the maximum in use and where it came
+from (`pump_max_power`, `pump_max_power_source`, `pump_max_power_reason`), and
+the last experiment's kind, phase and result in `system_identification_outcome`.
+
 The fit regresses the room's rate of change on `(T_room − T_out)`, applied power
 and a **constant**, over both the step and relaxation phases: relaxation carries
 the cleanest information about the loss coefficient (no input to confound it),

 Optional price tiles also re-price the plan under the comfort schedule one degree
 lower, one higher, and power capped at 75%. One tile is refreshed per scheduled
 solve, in rotation, so a refresh costs one extra solve for a degree tile and up to three for the power-cap tile.
+The power-cap tile is refreshed at most every six hours, the first time six hours after a start:
+between refreshes its turn in the rotation solves nothing, and the tile keeps the figure and the
+time of its last refresh.

 baseline's difference), not the plan's spend from the house as it stands, which
 includes a one-off coast or heat-up. The cap tile, and the fuse advisor's bill

-<section class="band" id="features" aria-labelledby="features-h">
-  <div class="sec-head"><span class="eyebrow">What it does</span><h2 id="features-h">A plan, a model of your house, and the reasons behind both</h2></div>
-  <div class="features">
-    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M3 17h4v-5h4v7h4V8h6"/></svg></span>
-      <h3 data-feature>Plans ahead instead of reacting.</h3>
-      <p>A 24-hour model-predictive plan is re-solved on every interval against the full forecast trajectory, not against the weather right now. Space heating and hot water share one compressor, so they are planned against each other rather than one after the other.</p></article>
-    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M3 11l9-7 9 7v9H3z"/><path d="M9 20v-6h6v6"/></svg></span>
-      <h3 data-feature>Learns your house.</h3>
-      <p>The heat-loss scale, tank cooling rates, the COP curve and its defrost derate, the solar aperture, internal gains, how the loss splits between floors, your hot-water draw statistics, your revealed comfort preference, and a cool-only heat-curve correction are all estimated from your own house. Every learner is snapshotted weekly (the last eight are kept), and a drift watchdog can roll them back to the last healthy snapshot.</p></article>
-    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M13 2L4 14h7l-1 8 9-12h-7z"/></svg></span>
-      <h3 data-feature>Knows what your electricity actually costs.</h3>
-      <p>Tibber spot prices, time-of-use grid transfer fees, the monthly capacity (effekt) tariff and its billing clock, PV self-consumption priced at what consuming actually costs you, and a learned diurnal price prior for the part of the horizon that has not been published yet. A live peak guard and a main-fuse headroom advisor act inside the metering window the plan never saw, and a contract comparison settles the month three ways so you can see what your tariff choice is worth.</p></article>
-    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 4v6a4 4 0 0 0 4 4h8a4 4 0 0 1 4 4v2"/><circle cx="4" cy="4" r="1.5"/><circle cx="20" cy="20" r="1.5"/></svg></span>
-      <h3 data-feature>Handles real plumbing.</h3>
-      <p>A mixing valve is what lets a buffer tank store anything, so it is modelled explicitly. A wood furnace tank is a store of its own, drawn wood-first while it is usable, with an optional hot-water inlet coil. Your hydronic layout is picked from a catalog of drawn arrangements rather than described in prose, and circulation pumps — the hot-water loop and the space pump — are scheduled instead of left running.</p></article>
-    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 3s6 6.5 6 11a6 6 0 0 1-12 0c0-4.5 6-11 6-11z"/></svg></span>
-      <h3 data-feature>Hot water that fits your household.</h3>
-      <p>Hot water is guaranteed inside demand time frames rather than kept permanently hot, which is where most of the saving comes from. <span>Draw statistics are learned per window, with a heavy-day (90th percentile) target so the second shower is not the one that runs cold.</span></p></article>
-    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 19V5M4 19h16"/><path d="M8 15l3-4 3 2 5-6"/></svg></span>
-      <h3 data-feature>Shows its work.</h3>
-      <p>The plan is published as sentences grouped by reason, and graded 0–100 across envelope, machine and operation. Energy and cost accumulate into the Energy dashboard split by hot water versus space heating.</p></article>

+<section class="band" id="features" aria-labelledby="features-h">
+  <div class="sec-head rv"><span class="eyebrow">What it does</span><h2 id="features-h">A plan, a model of your house, and the reasons behind both</h2></div>
+  <div class="features rv">
+    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M3 17h4v-5h4v7h4V8h6"/></svg></span>
+      <h3 data-feature>Plans ahead instead of reacting.</h3>
+      <p>A 24-hour model-predictive plan is re-solved on every interval against the full forecast trajectory, not against the weather right now. Space heating and hot water share one compressor, so they are planned against each other rather than one after the other.</p></article>
+    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M3 11l9-7 9 7v9H3z"/><path d="M9 20v-6h6v6"/></svg></span>
+      <h3 data-feature>Learns your house.</h3>
+      <p>The heat-loss scale, tank cooling rates, the COP curve and its defrost derate, the solar aperture, internal gains, how the loss splits between floors, your hot-water draw statistics, your revealed comfort preference, and a cool-only heat-curve correction are all estimated from your own house. Every learner is snapshotted weekly (the last eight are kept), and a drift watchdog can roll them back to the last healthy snapshot.</p></article>
+    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M13 2L4 14h7l-1 8 9-12h-7z"/></svg></span>
+      <h3 data-feature>Knows what your electricity actually costs.</h3>
+      <p>Tibber spot prices, time-of-use grid transfer fees, the monthly capacity (effekt) tariff and its billing clock, PV self-consumption priced at what consuming actually costs you, and a learned diurnal price prior for the part of the horizon that has not been published yet. A live peak guard and a main-fuse headroom advisor act inside the metering window the plan never saw, and a contract comparison settles the month three ways so you can see what your tariff choice is worth.</p></article>
+    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 4v6a4 4 0 0 0 4 4h8a4 4 0 0 1 4 4v2"/><circle cx="4" cy="4" r="1.5"/><circle cx="20" cy="20" r="1.5"/></svg></span>
+      <h3 data-feature>Handles real plumbing.</h3>
+      <p>A mixing valve is what lets a buffer tank store anything, so it is modelled explicitly. A wood furnace tank is a store of its own, drawn wood-first while it is usable, with an optional hot-water inlet coil. Your hydronic layout is picked from a catalog of drawn arrangements rather than described in prose, and circulation pumps — the hot-water loop and the space pump — are scheduled instead of left running.</p></article>
+    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 3s6 6.5 6 11a6 6 0 0 1-12 0c0-4.5 6-11 6-11z"/></svg></span>
+      <h3 data-feature>Hot water that fits your household.</h3>
+      <p>Hot water is guaranteed inside demand time frames rather than kept permanently hot, which is where most of the saving comes from. <span>Draw statistics are learned per window, with a heavy-day (90th percentile) target so the second shower is not the one that runs cold.</span></p></article>
+    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 19V5M4 19h16"/><path d="M8 15l3-4 3 2 5-6"/></svg></span>
+      <h3 data-feature>Shows its work.</h3>
+      <p>The plan is published as sentences grouped by reason, and graded 0–100 across envelope, machine and operation. Energy and cost accumulate into the Energy dashboard split by hot water versus space heating.</p></article>
+    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="3" y="6" width="18" height="12" rx="3"/><path d="M8 12h8"/><path d="M12 9v6"/></svg></span>
+      <h3 data-feature>You stay in charge.</h3>
+      <p>The card's editor pins exact run slots for up to 20 hours and the optimizer plans around them; a what-if simulator prices a comfort change before you commit to it; a climate entity and a switch give you the ordinary Home Assistant controls. <span>Compressor frequency control is deliberately two-stage: it observes and advises until you explicitly turn writing on.</span></p></article>
+    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 3l8 3v6c0 5-3.5 8-8 9-4.5-1-8-4-8-9V6z"/></svg></span>
+      <h3 data-feature>Stays out of trouble.</h3>
+      <p>A staleness watchdog treats a sensor that stopped updating as missing and pauses learning rather than training on a flatline. <span>Away and holiday mode sets back deeply and buys the recovery heat in the cheapest hours before you get home.</span></p></article>
+    <article class="feat" data-src="README.md#what-it-does"><span class="ic" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3a14 14 0 0 1 0 18M12 3a14 14 0 0 0 0 18"/></svg></span>
+      <h3 data-feature>Fits your Home Assistant.</h3>
+      <p>Entity names are translated (English, Swedish and German) and follow your Home Assistant language, without touching entity ids or history. Monetary units follow your instance currency.</p></article>
+  </div>
+</section>
+

+    snap = _dhw_snap(**booking)
+    return replace(snap, params=replace(
+        snap.params, dhw_enabled=True, dhw_combi_tank_enabled=True, combi_potable_volume_l=2.0,
+        dhw_combi_legionella_force=force, mixing_valve_mode="manual", buffer_tank_volume=300.0,
+    ))
+
+
+def _written(snap, duty):
+    return arb.desired(_Coord(snap), snap, duty, NOW).dhw_setpoint
+
+
+#: Every row of ``desired`` and every way a step books a cycle: the grid the
+#: null controls drive, so a row that bypasses the cycle's answer is in it.
+_DUTIES = (None, "idle", "space", "dhw", "both")
+_BOOKINGS = ({}, {"action": {"dhw_reason": "legionella"}}, {"disinfecting": True},
+             {"action": {"dhw_reason": "legionella"}, "disinfecting": True})
+
+
+def _fix_value(snap, *, arbiter=True):
+    """The hot-water repair once the arbiter wrote this step's answer (none
+    with ``arbiter`` false), the pump reading the snapshot's value: ``None``
+    when it stands down, else the value its Fix writes."""
+    coord = _Coord(snap)
+    own = arb.desired(coord, snap, "dhw", NOW).dhw_setpoint
+    if arbiter and own is not None:
+        arb.state_for(coord).written["dhw_setpoint"] = (own, NOW)
+    hass = snap.hass
+    setpoint_check._dhw(hass, snap.config, snap.params, lambda pump: arb.dhw_gated(coord, pump))
+    raised = [i for i in getattr(hass, "issues", []) if i[1] == setpoint_check.ISSUE_DHW]
+    return raised[0][2]["data"]["value"] if raised else None
+
+
+def _step(step):
+    """The hot-water entity's attributes, 30 to 80 degC, on ``step``."""
+    return {"min": 30, "max": 80, "step": step}
+
+
+#: The census of ``_dhw_write``'s cycle rounding paths: every step size an
+#: entity states here, and everyday/disinfection pairs below, at and above
+#: each other, on and off each step, up to the 70 degC cap.
+_GRID_STEPS = (0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5)
+_GRID_TEMPS = (50.0, 55.0, 57.0, 58.0, 60.0, 60.2, 60.3, 60.4, 60.7, 62.0, 69.6, 70.0, 72.0)
+
+
+def _cycle_grid_over_hard_max():
+    """Every (step, everyday, disinfection) whose cycle write exceeds the hard
+    maximum the same parameters state, or is no write at all; asserts the
+    grid holds all three orderings first, so a narrowed grid refuses."""
+    pairs = [(e, d) for e in _GRID_TEMPS[:-1] for d in _GRID_TEMPS]
+    assert {(d > e) - (d < e) for e, d in pairs} == {-1, 0, 1}
+    bad = []
+    for step in _GRID_STEPS:
+        for e, d in pairs:
+            snap = _dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, configured=e, disinfection=d, attrs=_step(step))
+            w = _written(snap, "dhw")
+            if w is None or w > snap.params.dhw_hard_max_temp + 1e-9:
+                bad.append((step, e, d, w, snap.params.dhw_hard_max_temp))
+    return bad
+
+
+#: The no-cycle arms of the census: the cycle enabled and not running (no
+#: booking, the switch not held), and the cycle disabled (switch held).
+_NOCYCLE_ARMS = {"idle": dict(cycle=True), "disabled": dict(cycle=False, disinfecting=True)}
+
+
+def _nocycle_grid_over_limit(arm):
+    """Every (step, everyday, disinfection) whose no-cycle write in ``arm``
+    exceeds the charge limit (``dhw_max_temp``) the same parameters state, or
+    is no write at all. Asserts its preconditions first: every row is one no
+    cycle runs on, and every step size but the finest holds an off-step
+    everyday set-point, so a narrowed grid refuses."""
+    kw = _NOCYCLE_ARMS[arm]
+    pairs = [(e, d) for e in _GRID_TEMPS[:-1] for d in _GRID_TEMPS]
+    assert all(any(abs(e / s - round(e / s)) > 1e-9 for e in _GRID_TEMPS[:-1]) for s in _GRID_STEPS[1:])
+    bad = []
+    for step in _GRID_STEPS:
+        for e, d in pairs:
+            snap = _dhw_snap(configured=e, disinfection=d, attrs=_step(step), **kw)
+            assert (snap.params.dhw_cycle_temp is None) == (arm == "disabled") and not snap.action
+            assert snap.params.dhw_cycle_temp is None or not snap.disinfecting
+            w = _written(snap, "dhw")
+            if w is None or w > snap.params.dhw_max_temp + 1e-9:
+                bad.append((step, e, d, w, snap.params.dhw_max_temp))
+    return bad
+
+
+def _repair_grid_over_hard_max():
+    """Every (step, everyday, disinfection) whose repair Fix, on an install the
+    arbiter does not write and a pump reading of 30, exceeds the tank's hard
+    maximum the repair's own parameters state."""
+    bad = []
+    for step in _GRID_STEPS:
+        for e in _GRID_TEMPS[:-1]:
+            for d in _GRID_TEMPS:
+                snap = _dhw_snap(configured=e, disinfection=d, attrs=_step(step), reading=30.0)
+                fix = _fix_value(snap, arbiter=False)
+                if fix is None or fix > snap.params.dhw_hard_max_temp + 1e-9:
+                    bad.append((step, e, d, fix, snap.params.dhw_hard_max_temp))
+    return bad
+
+
+def disinfection_checks() -> None:
+    """A disinfection cycle holds its own temperature, not the everyday set-point."""
+    written = _written
+    check(
+        "a commanded or held disinfection cycle writes its temperature, not the configured set-point",
+        lambda: written(_dhw_snap(action={"dhw_reason": "legionella"}), "dhw") == 60.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True), "both") == 60.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(), "dhw") == 55.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "a configured set-point above the disinfection temperature is never lowered to it",
+        lambda: written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, configured=62.0), "dhw") == 62.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "every row a cycle step can take writes the cycle's temperature, the idle and baseline rows too",
+        lambda: all(written(_dhw_snap(action={"dhw_reason": "legionella"}), d) == 60.0
+                    for d in (None, "idle", "dhw", "both")),
+    )
+    check(
+        "the cycle's temperature is the thermal parameters' own answer, not a copy",
+        lambda: written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, disinfection=58.0), "dhw")
+        == ThermalParameters(dhw_setpoint=55.0, dhw_legionella_temp=58.0).dhw_cycle_temp == 58.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "a cycle never lowers the tank: an everyday set-point above the disinfection temperature is the cycle's and the ceiling's",
+        lambda: ThermalParameters(dhw_setpoint=62.0, dhw_legionella_temp=60.0).dhw_cycle_temp == 62.0
+        and ThermalParameters(dhw_setpoint=62.0, dhw_legionella_temp=60.0).dhw_hard_max_temp == 62.0
+        and ThermalParameters(dhw_setpoint=62.0, dhw_legionella_enabled=False).dhw_cycle_temp is None,
+    )
+    check(
+        "an off-step disinfection temperature above the everyday set-point is written on the step at or "
+        "below it, never above the tank's hard maximum",
+        lambda: written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, disinfection=60.3), "dhw") == 60.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, disinfection=60.3, attrs=_step(5)), "dhw") == 60.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, disinfection=62.0, attrs=_step(5)), "dhw") == 60.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, disinfection=60.7, attrs=_step(0.5)), "dhw") == 60.5
+        and written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, disinfection=60.0, attrs=_step(5)), "dhw") == 60.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "a cycle whose temperature is an off-step everyday set-point (the disinfection temperature at or "
+        "below it) writes the step at or below it, as 49a45dd8 and the same install's everyday step do",
+        lambda: all(written(_dhw_snap(**b, configured=60.4, disinfection=60.2), "dhw") == 60.0
+                    for b in _BOOKINGS)
+        and all(written(_dhw_snap(**b, configured=57.0, disinfection=50.0, attrs=_step(5)), "dhw") == 55.0
+                for b in _BOOKINGS)
+        and written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, configured=57.0, disinfection=57.0, attrs=_step(5)), "dhw") == 55.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(cycle=False, disinfecting=True, configured=57.0, disinfection=50.0,
+                              attrs=_step(5)), "dhw") == 55.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "an everyday set-point the nearest step rounds up is held below it on a cycle: the tank's hard "
+        "maximum is the everyday set-point there (the everyday step's own nearest write is main's)",
+        lambda: written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, configured=58.0, disinfection=50.0, attrs=_step(5)), "dhw") == 55.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(configured=58.0, disinfection=50.0, attrs=_step(5)), "dhw") == 55.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "no no-cycle write exceeds the charge limit (dhw_max_temp), the cycle enabled and not running "
+        "or disabled, over every step size and everyday set-point on and off the step",
+        lambda: _nocycle_grid_over_limit("idle") == [] and _nocycle_grid_over_limit("disabled") == [],
+    )
+    check(
+        "an off-step everyday set-point is written on the step at or below it, never rounded up "
+        "(everyday 58, step 5: 55, not 60; everyday 60.7, step 1: 60), the cycle idle or disabled",
+        lambda: all(written(_dhw_snap(configured=58.0, attrs=_step(5), **kw), d) == 55.0
+                    and written(_dhw_snap(configured=60.7, attrs=_step(1), **kw), d) == 60.0
+                    and written(_dhw_snap(configured=60.3, attrs=_step(0.5), **kw), d) == 60.0
+                    for kw in _NOCYCLE_ARMS.values() for d in (None, "idle", "dhw", "both")),
+    )
+    check(
+        "a charge limit below the entity's minimum writes the entity's minimum, never a value it refuses",
+        lambda: written(_dhw_snap(configured=25.0, cycle=False), "dhw") == 30.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(configured=25.4, cycle=False, attrs={"min": 30.5, "max": 65, "step": 0.5}), "dhw") == 30.5
+        and written(_dhw_snap(configured=25.0, cycle=False, attrs={"min": 30.4, "max": 65, "step": 1}), "dhw") == 31.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(configured=30.6, cycle=False, attrs={"min": 30.4, "max": 65, "step": 1}), "dhw") == 31.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(configured=72.0, cycle=False, attrs={"min": 70, "max": 80, "step": 1}), "dhw") == 70.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(configured=58.0, cycle=False, attrs={"max": 65, "step": 5}), "dhw") == 55.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "the hot-water repair's Fix never exceeds the tank's hard maximum it is judged against, over every "
+        "step size and pair, and an off-step floor's repair stands down at the step below it",
+        lambda: _repair_grid_over_hard_max() == []
+        and _fix_value(_dhw_snap(disinfection=60.3, reading=60.0), arbiter=False) is None
+        and _fix_value(_dhw_snap(disinfection=60.3, reading=59.0), arbiter=False) == 60.0
+        and _fix_value(_dhw_snap(disinfection=60.3, reading=60.0 - setpoint_check.MIXING_VALVE_WRITE_EPSILON),
+                       arbiter=False) is None
+        and _fix_value(_dhw_snap(disinfection=72.0, reading=69.0, attrs=_step(1)), arbiter=False) == 70.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "a disinfection temperature above 70 degC is written at the tank's 70 degC hard maximum",
+        lambda: written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, disinfection=72.0,
+                                  attrs={"min": 30, "max": 80, "step": 1}), "dhw") == 70.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "no cycle write exceeds the tank's hard maximum, over every step size and the disinfection "
+        "temperature below, at and above the everyday set-point, on and off the step",
+        lambda: _cycle_grid_over_hard_max() == [],
+    )
+    check(
+        "a disinfection temperature above the entity's range stays bounded at its maximum",
+        lambda: written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True, attrs={"min": 30, "max": 58, "step": 1}), "dhw") == 58.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "the space-only gate stays a gate on a booked step, but a held cycle turns it into Heating + DHW",
+        lambda: written(_dhw_snap(action={"dhw_reason": "legionella"}), "space") == 30.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(), "space") == 30.0
+        and written(_dhw_snap(disinfecting=True), "space") == 60.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "null control: a disabled cycle writes the everyday set-point on every row and booking",
+        lambda: all(written(_dhw_snap(cycle=False, **b), d) == (30.0 if d == "space" and not b.get("disinfecting") else 55.0)
+                    for d in _DUTIES for b in _BOOKINGS),
+    )
+    check(
+        "a combi store at or under the potable limit runs no cycle: a booked or held step writes the "
+        "everyday set-point, unless the cycle is forced (#3398's predicate, read through the cycle's owner)",
+        lambda: not _combi_snap(False).params.legionella_cycle_active
+        and _combi_snap(True).params.legionella_cycle_active
+        and all(written(_combi_snap(False, **b), "dhw") == 55.0 and written(_combi_snap(True, **b), "dhw") == 60.0
+                for b in _BOOKINGS[1:]),
+    )
+    check(
+        "null control: an everyday set-point at or above the disinfection temperature is written as is",
+        lambda: all(written(_dhw_snap(configured=c, **b), d) == (30.0 if d == "space" and not b.get("disinfecting") else c)
+                    for c in (60.0, 62.0) for d in _DUTIES for b in _BOOKINGS),
+    )
+    check(
+        "null control: no hot-water set-point entity is no hot-water write on any row",
+        lambda: all(written(_dhw_snap(entity=None, **b), d) is None for d in _DUTIES for b in _BOOKINGS),
+    )
+    check(
+        "the arbiter's own everyday write raises no disinfection-floor repair: it writes the cycle itself",
+        lambda: _fix_value(_dhw_snap()) is None,
+    )
+    check(
+        "a person's value beside the arbiter's write still raises the repair, its Fix on the floor",
+        lambda: _fix_value(_dhw_snap(reading=50.0)) == 60.0,
+    )
+    check(
+        "null control: with no arbiter write the pump's own set-point must still permit the cycle",
+        lambda: _fix_value(_dhw_snap(entity=None)) is None
+        and _fix_value(_dhw_snap(), arbiter=False) == 60.0
+        and _fix_value(_dhw_snap(reading=60.0), arbiter=False) is None,
+    )
+    check(
+        "null control: a disabled cycle and an everyday set-point at the disinfection temperature raise nothing",
+        lambda: _fix_value(_dhw_snap(cycle=False)) is None
+        and _fix_value(_dhw_snap(configured=60.0, reading=60.0)) is None,
+    )
+
+
+def _hyst_snap(hysteresis=None, *, action=None, space=None, disinfecting=False, reading=55.0):
+    """``_dhw_snap`` (real parameters, a 0.1 step number) over a state with the pump's hysteresis."""
+    snap = _dhw_snap(action=action, disinfecting=disinfecting, reading=reading,
+                     attrs={"min": 30, "max": 75, "step": 0.1})
+    return replace(snap, state=SimpleNamespace(
+        room_temperature=21.0, outdoor_temperature=5.0, dhw_temperature=52.0,
+        dhw_start_hysteresis_k=hysteresis, space_start_hysteresis_k=space,
+    ))
+
+
+def _start_state(hysteresis, attrs=None):
+    """A ``ThermalState`` with the pump's hot-water hysteresis and, with ``attrs``, the grid of a
+    set-point number carrying them, read as the coordinator's input read reads it."""
+    from heatpump_optimizer import inputs as inputs_mod
+    from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import ThermalState
+
+    state = ThermalState()
+    hass = FakeHass({"sensor.h": FakeState("" if hysteresis is None else str(hysteresis), unit="K"),
+                     "number.dhw": FakeState("55", attributes=attrs or {})})
+    inputs_mod.read_start_hysteresis(state, hass, {
+        "dhw_hysteresis_entity": "sensor.h", "dhw_setpoint_entity": "number.dhw" if attrs else None})
+    return state
+
+
+def hysteresis_checks() -> None:
+    """The pump's own start hysteresis: read, planned, written and logged."""
+    import ast
+    import pathlib
+
+    import numpy as np
+
+    from heatpump_optimizer import dhw_planner as planner
+    from heatpump_optimizer import inputs as inputs_mod
+    from heatpump_optimizer import thermal_model as tm
+
+    # 1. The reading is a temperature difference.
+    hass = FakeHass({
+        "sensor.k2": FakeState("2", unit="K"), "sensor.f9": FakeState("9", unit="\u00b0F"),
+        "sensor.c3": FakeState("3", unit="\u00b0C"), "sensor.nu": FakeState("4"),
+        "sensor.k20": FakeState("20", unit="K"), "sensor.k0": FakeState("0", unit="K"),
+        "sensor.big": FakeState("25"), "sensor.neg": FakeState("-1"),
+        "sensor.na": FakeState("unavailable"), "sensor.pct": FakeState("2", unit="%"),
+    })
+    read = lambda e: inputs_mod.read_temperature_delta_k(hass, e)  # noqa: E731
+    check("a hysteresis in K reads as it stands", lambda: read("sensor.k2") == 2.0)
+    check("a hysteresis in degF is scaled by 5/9, not offset", lambda: abs(read("sensor.f9") - 5.0) < 1e-9)
+    check("a hysteresis in degC reads as it stands", lambda: read("sensor.c3") == 3.0)
+    check("a hysteresis with no unit is taken as K", lambda: read("sensor.nu") == 4.0)
+    check("the bounds of the hysteresis range, 20 K and 0 K, are readings",
+          lambda: read("sensor.k20") == 20.0 and read("sensor.k0") == 0.0
+          and inputs_mod.TEMPERATURE_DELTA_MAX_K == 20.0)
+    check("a hysteresis outside 0 to 20 K, unavailable, in a non-temperature unit, unset or unknown is no reading",
+          lambda: read("sensor.big") is None and read("sensor.neg") is None
+          and read("sensor.na") is None and read("sensor.pct") is None
+          and read(None) is None and read("sensor.nowhere") is None)
+
+    # 2. One lift.
+    lift = tm.start_flow_min_lift_k
+    half = {"flow_min_lift_k": 0.5}
+    check("a heating hysteresis above the configured lift is the lift",
+          lambda: lift(half, 2.0) == 2.0 and lift({}, 7.0) == 7.0)
+    check("a heating hysteresis at or below the configured lift, or none, leaves the configured lift",
+          lambda: lift(half, None) == 0.5 and lift(half, 0.3) == 0.5 and lift(half, 0.0) == 0.5
+          and lift({}, None) == tm.FLOW_MIN_LIFT_K)
+    check("null control: no hysteresis gives configured_flow_min_lift_k exactly",
+          lambda: all(lift(c, None) == tm.configured_flow_min_lift_k(c)
+                      for c in ({}, half, {"flow_min_lift_k": 0.0}, {"flow_min_lift_k": "x"}, None)))
+
+    # 3. The start temperature.
+    below = tm.dhw_start_below_c
+    check("the start temperature is the target less the hysteresis",
+          lambda: below(55, 4) == 51.0)
+    check("no target, or a hysteresis that is missing, zero or negative, is no start temperature",
+          lambda: below(55, None) is None and below(55, 0) is None and below(55, -1) is None
+          and below(None, 4) is None)
+
+    check("a hysteresis under one kelvin is still a start condition",
+          lambda: tm.dhw_start_below_c(55.0, 0.5) == 54.5)
+
+    # 4. The step targets, on real parameters.
+    cyc = ThermalParameters(dhw_setpoint=55.0, dhw_legionella_temp=60.0, dhw_legionella_enabled=True)
+    nocyc = ThermalParameters(dhw_setpoint=55.0, dhw_legionella_temp=60.0, dhw_legionella_enabled=False)
+    check("precondition: the cycle is 60 over a 55 set-point, and absent where disabled",
+          lambda: cyc.dhw_cycle_temp == 60.0 and nocyc.dhw_cycle_temp is None)
+    check("the step target is the everyday set-point, or the cycle's on a cycle step",
+          lambda: tm.dhw_step_target_c(cyc, False) == 55.0 and tm.dhw_step_target_c(cyc, True) == 60.0)
+    check("null control: with no cycle active a cycle step holds the everyday set-point",
+          lambda: tm.dhw_step_target_c(nocyc, True) == 55.0)
+    check("each step's start temperature is its own target less the hysteresis, the cycle step the cycle's",
+          lambda: list(planner.dhw_start_temps(cyc, _start_state(4.0), 6, 3)) == [51, 51, 51, 56, 51, 51]
+          and list(planner.dhw_start_temps(cyc, _start_state(4.0), 6, None)) == [51.0] * 6)
+    check("a cycle on the first step is judged against its own target; one past the horizon moves no step",
+          lambda: list(planner.dhw_start_temps(cyc, _start_state(4.0), 3, 0)) == [56, 51, 51]
+          and list(planner.dhw_start_temps(cyc, _start_state(4.0), 3, 3)) == [51, 51, 51]
+          and list(planner.dhw_start_temps(cyc, _start_state(4.0), 3, 2)) == [51, 51, 56])
+    check("with no or zero hysteresis no step has a start temperature",
+          lambda: planner.dhw_start_temps(cyc, _start_state(None), 6, 3) is None
+          and planner.dhw_start_temps(cyc, _start_state(0.0), 6, 3) is None
+          and planner.dhw_start_temps(cyc, _start_state(0.0, _step(5)), 6, 3) is None)
+
+    # 5. One owner of the target: what the arbiter writes.
+    check("the arbiter writes dhw_step_target_c: the everyday set-point with no cycle booked",
+          lambda: arb._dhw_write(_hyst_snap(4.0)) == tm.dhw_step_target_c(cyc, False))
+    check("the arbiter writes dhw_step_target_c: the cycle's temperature on a booked legionella step",
+          lambda: arb._dhw_write(_hyst_snap(4.0, action={"dhw_reason": "legionella"}))
+          == tm.dhw_step_target_c(cyc, True) == 60.0)
+
+    # 5b. One owner, read by the write: the two values, the two bounds and the entity's step.
+    hot = ThermalParameters(dhw_setpoint=72.0, dhw_legionella_temp=60.0, dhw_legionella_enabled=False)
+    hot_cycle = ThermalParameters(dhw_setpoint=55.0, dhw_legionella_temp=72.0, dhw_legionella_enabled=True)
+    check("the everyday step target never exceeds the charge limit (dhw_max_temp, 70 over a 72 set-point)",
+          lambda: hot.dhw_max_temp == 70.0 and tm.dhw_step_target_c(hot, False) == 70.0)
+    check("the cycle's step target never exceeds the tank's hard maximum (70 over a 72 disinfection temperature)",
+          lambda: hot_cycle.dhw_hard_max_temp == 70.0 and hot_cycle.dhw_cycle_temp == 72.0
+          and tm.dhw_step_target_c(hot_cycle, True) == 70.0)
+
+    def owner_gaps():
+        # Every write the arbiter makes against the owner handed the same entity's grid.
+        gaps = []
+        for step in (0.1, 0.5, 1, 5):
+            for configured in (55.0, 57.0, 58.0, 60.4, 72.0):
+                for disinfection in (50.0, 60.0, 60.3, 72.0):
+                    for cycle in (True, False):
+                        for booking in _BOOKINGS:
+                            snap = _dhw_snap(configured=configured, disinfection=disinfection, cycle=cycle,
+                                             attrs=_step(step), **booking)
+                            grid = inputs_mod.setpoint_grid(snap.hass, "number.dhw")
+                            on_cycle = bool(booking.get("disinfecting")) or bool(booking.get("action"))

+def _solve_winter_mild(hysteresis, dhw_pins=None, setpoint_c=None, attrs=None):
+    """The 24 h solve of ``dev/audit/harnesses/r10_dhw_start_hysteresis.py`` (winter_typical, winter_mild, 53 degC)."""
+    import numpy as np
+    from profiles import house, prices, solve_inputs, weather
+    from heatpump_optimizer.optimizer import HeatPumpOptimizer, OptimizationConfig
+    from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import ThermalModel, ThermalState
+
+    begin = datetime(2026, 1, 15, 0, 0)
+    cfg = house()
+    params = ThermalParameters.from_config(cfg)
+    params.dhw_enabled = True
+    if setpoint_c is not None:
+        params.dhw_setpoint = setpoint_c
+    opt = HeatPumpOptimizer(ThermalModel(params), OptimizationConfig(
+        horizon_hours=24, time_step_minutes=15, target_temp=cfg["target_temperature"],
+        min_temp=cfg["min_temperature"], max_temp=cfg["max_temperature"]))
+    outdoor, wind, rain, sun = weather("winter_mild", begin)
+    state = ThermalState(
+        room_temperature=21.0, slab_temperature=22.0, outdoor_temperature=float(outdoor[0]),

+        lower_floor_temperature=21.0, buffer_tank_temperature=40.0)
+    state.dhw_start_hysteresis_k = hysteresis
+    if attrs:
+        state.dhw_setpoint_grid = _start_state(hysteresis, attrs).dhw_setpoint_grid
+    result = opt.optimize(inputs=solve_inputs(
+        initial_state=state, prices=np.asarray(prices("winter_typical", begin), dtype=float),
+        outdoor_temps=outdoor, wind_speeds=wind, precipitation=rain, solar_radiation=sun,
+        start_time=begin, dhw_pins=dhw_pins))
+    return (np.asarray(result.dhw_power_schedule, dtype=float),

+# Press surfaces, driven only by dev/audit/harnesses/boost_press_tail_walk.py
+# (not the gate): ``press:<minutes>:<count>`` presses the space overlay
+# through the channel switch at each window start, held ``minutes`` and then
+# cancelled (a press of the whole window expires instead), ``count`` presses
+# one cycle apart; ``freeze:<minutes>:<count>`` runs the same presses with the
+# true house driven by the plan throughout, so the freeze has no boost heat
+# behind it.
+def press_windows(surface: str, day_index: int) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
+    """The ``(start, end)`` local hours a ``press:`` surface boosts on this day."""
+    _kind, minutes, count = surface.split(":")

+    return [
+        (s + k * DT_MIN / 60.0, s + k * DT_MIN / 60.0 + int(minutes) / 60.0)
+        for s in BOOST_STARTS for k in range(int(count))
+    ]

+// an ad blocker's generic element-hiding rules target. EasyList's

+// is a deny set of ad-list-prone stems, not a copy of any list: a name that

+  // near misses (a stem glued to a letter, or a word that merely contains
