@@ -14,6 +14,9 @@ written (tvofi's D2). Four arms, each counted separately:
               tracked file, and every retired target lands in one category:
               a glob that matches nothing is a check that measures nothing
 
+plus a fifth, uncounted check (`gitignore_config`): the .gitignore `config/`
+rule stays root-anchored. Its findings fail the exit code in every mode.
+
     python3 tests/layout.py               # report on this tree, then --self-test
     python3 tests/layout.py --report      # per-arm counts; exit 0 whatever they are
     python3 tests/layout.py --enforce     # exit 1 on any finding (R9-RO-9 flips to this)
@@ -488,6 +491,37 @@ def stale(root: Path, manifest: dict) -> list[str]:
     return [f"{k[1:]}: {o} | {line.strip()[:120]}" for k, t in text.items() if t for o, line in stale_lines(t, now)]
 
 
+def ignored(root: Path, path: str) -> bool:
+    return subprocess.run(["git", "check-ignore", "-q", "--no-index", path],
+                          cwd=root, capture_output=True).returncode == 0
+
+
+def gitignore_config(root: Path) -> list[str]:
+    """The .gitignore `config/` rule is root-anchored: an unanchored one hides
+    dev/audit/config/ and dev/governance/config/ from `git add`, and a handoff
+    silently omits the file. The root-level HA runtime directory stays ignored."""
+    out = [] if ignored(root, "config/x") else ["root-level config/x is no longer ignored"]
+    return out + [f"{n} is ignored by .gitignore" for n in ("dev/audit/config/x", "dev/governance/config/x")
+                  if ignored(root, n)]
+
+
+def gitignore_self_test() -> int:
+    """Null control: an unanchored `config/` rule must be flagged, an anchored one not."""
+    from throwaway_git import throwaway_git_init
+    failed = 0
+    for rule, want in (("config/", 2), ("/config/", 0)):
+        tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="hpo-layout-ignore-"))
+        try:
+            throwaway_git_init(tmp, "-q")
+            (tmp / ".gitignore").write_text(rule + "\n")
+            got = len(gitignore_config(tmp))
+        finally:
+            shutil.rmtree(tmp)
+        failed += got != want
+        print(f"  {'ok  ' if got == want else 'FAIL'} gitignore self-test: rule {rule!r}: {got} finding(s), want {want}")
+    return failed
+
+

     """A two-commit repo per case on a stub manifest: the base, then the
     change staged, each case naming how many findings of which kind it owes."""

+        ign = gitignore_config(ROOT)

+        rc = rc or (1 if ign else 0)
     if a.guard or run_all:

@@ -814,7 +851,7 @@ def main() -> int:

+def _fresh_repo(w: Path, label: str, prog: Path, main_adds: dict, local: bool = False,
+                dirty: bool = False):
+    """A checkout holding `prog` at tools/audit/seat/beatd.py on branch main at C1,
+    with origin/main at C2 = C1 + main_adds. Returns (repo, env, g, c1, c2)."""

+def _binders(source: str, start: str) -> dict[str, list[ast.stmt]]:
+    """Each name's top-level binding statements between the header and the block, in order."""
+    lo = source[: source.index('R = Results("Feature modules")')].count("\n") + 1
+    hi = source[: source.index(start)].count("\n") + 1
+    out: dict[str, list[ast.stmt]] = {}

+#: One page of a paged list, GitHub's maximum, and the walk's bound: past
+#: MAX_PAGES full pages the read refuses rather than return a truncated list.
+PER_PAGE = 100
+MAX_PAGES = 100
+
+
+def read_pages(read, path: str, key: str = "", per_page: int = PER_PAGE, max_pages: int = MAX_PAGES):
+    """Every item of the paged list at <path> -> (code, items, why); items is
+    None and why the failure on a failed, unparseable or unbounded walk.
+
+    Page by explicit `page=N`, never `gh api --paginate`: that follows the Link
+    header, which names `repositories/<id>/...`, and a cloud seat's proxy
+    answers that URL 403 (S14-CLOUD-CLASSIFY-PAGINATE: `merge_train.py
+    classify` exited 2 on it). A short page ends the walk. `read` is the
+    caller's runner -- `merge_train`'s carries this file's retry rule -- and
+    <key> names the list in an object page (`check_runs`), "" an array page."""
+    sep = "&" if "?" in path else "?"
+    items: list = []
+    for n in range(1, max_pages + 1):
+        code, out = read(["gh", "api", f"{path}{sep}per_page={per_page}&page={n}",
+                          "--jq", f".{key}[]" if key else ".[]"])
+        if code:
+            return code, None, out
+        try:
+            page = [json.loads(x) for x in out.splitlines() if x.strip()]
+        except ValueError:
+            return 1, None, f"page {n} of {path} is not JSON: {one_line(out)[-120:]}"
+        items += page
+        if len(page) < per_page:  # mut:short-page
+            return 0, items, ""
+    return 1, None, f"{path}: more than {max_pages} pages of {per_page}: refused, not truncated"
+
+

diff --git a/tools/audit/seat/instruments/figure_block.py.md b/tools/audit/seat/instruments/figure_block.py.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..a7d7d28af3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/audit/seat/instruments/figure_block.py.md
@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+# `figure_block.py`
+
+- `figure_block.py` (tools/pr/) — fills and checks the generated figure blocks
+  in a PR body (`<!-- figure-block: NAME -->` ... `<!-- /figure-block -->`).
+  When: a figure a registered instrument prints (scope-line, structure-ratchet,
+  merge-base), which must not be typed. Refusal: the registry is read from the
+  BASE's `tools/pr/figure_registry.json`, so the author chooses no command, only
+  a registered name; an unregistered name, or a block that differs from what
+  the instrument renders at the head, is refused. A body with no block passes.
+  `render NAME` prints one block; `refresh BODY` fills the blocks in a body
+  file at the head (what `seat/body_push.sh` and `prepr.sh --body-check` run);
+  `verify BODY --base SHA --head SHA` re-renders read-only and refuses a
+  difference (what `pr-contract` runs). `--self-test` runs offline over
+  fixtures and prints `figure_block self-test: N checks, 0 failed`.

 | hook | event | script | does | why it exists |

+| liveness | SessionStart, PostCompact, UserPromptSubmit | `hooks/liveness.py` | demands a fresh policy re-read (`policy_reread_check.py`; always on PostCompact); prints `DEAD`/`ALARM` per late beat job and for a free `beatd.lock` (`beatd.py status`, so the loop list is the job table), `STALE` for an alive file under `$HPO_STATE_DIR/alive/` and for a digest whose `digest.txt` and beat journal both stood still, `DEAD beatd` is relaunched (`RESTARTED`/`auto-restart FAILED`) from `beatd/launch.json` under the seat venv's PATH, beatd only; `DEAD relay` when `cloud-relay.log` is stale; `MISSING` for an absent checkout in the state overlay; on PostCompact it writes `policy-corpus.txt` and a `compact-owed` marker that every UserPromptSubmit re-raises until `--prove <sha256>` clears it; then the digest, then one `ARM:` line | after a compaction nobody re-armed the wake loop and owed lines stood unread for hours (2026-11-01) |
 | seat-interpreter | SessionStart | `hooks/seat_interpreter.py` | runs `seat_venv.sh --check`; one `SEAT-INTERPRETER` line when it refuses | a temp cleanup deleted the seat venv unnoticed (2026-10-03) |
 | git-identity | SessionStart | `hooks/git_identity.py` | sets the orchestrator checkout's local `user.name`/`user.email` from `$HPO_STATE_DIR/git-identity` when they differ | a commit under the host's default identity is refused only after the push (decision 0011) |
 | Bash guard | PreToolUse, project-level | `.claude/hooks/pre-bash.sh`, second arm | exit 2 for `git checkout/switch/reset/pull/merge/rebase/stash/clean/restore` whose cwd, `cd` or `-C` resolves to the checkout named in `$HPO_STATE_DIR/orch-checkout`, read through the hook's one command-position parser (`HPO_PRE_BASH_PARSE_PY`), so `bash -c`, `eval`, `( )` and `$( )` bodies count | `beatd`, `tick_loop.sh` and `cloud_relay.sh` run from that checkout and bash reads a script incrementally |

diff --git a/tools/audit/seat/instruments/scorecard.py.md b/tools/audit/seat/instruments/scorecard.py.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..ee69987209
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/audit/seat/instruments/scorecard.py.md
@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+# `scorecard.py`
+
+- `scorecard.py` — the convergence scorecard (R10-MACH-SCORECARD): ten
+  report-only lines, one per signal, the baseline from which thresholds can
+  later be set. No line sets an exit code or holds a merge. It is read-only on
+  every input and makes no GitHub call; an input it cannot read prints
+  `<line>  unread (<why>)`, never a guessed value. The lines:
+  - `A_gate` — the share of the last 20 concluded main `CI` runs whose job
+    `gate` succeeded (a run with no cached job listing is `unread`).
+  - `A_run` — the share of the same runs whose run conclusion is success.
+  - `Y_rev` — over the last 50 pull requests, the share whose first review
+    verdict (the earliest by `t`, whatever the order of `verdicts.json`) is `merge`.
+  - `M_first` — over the same 50, the share whose first verdict is `blocked`
+    in a machinery family (carry, body, CI state, merge state, root-cause
+    form, ruling or roster).
+  - `Y_train` — over the last 50 merges the merge train named, the share
+    never on a `SKIP #n` or `PARK` line.
+  - `H` — hotfix-token merges among the last 50 code merges (production or
+    instrument), with the production merges among them beside it. It has no
+    null control: it is a naming measure, a branch token, read with that caveat.
+  - `S` — size: `machinery_ratchet.py --measure` (non-production merges per
+    window, churn per 1 000 product lines) and machinery lines over product lines.
+  - `E` — roster groups whose source is `outside` and hotfix or bug groups
+    touching the product, and how many of both are still open.
+  - `C` — the longest run of consecutive cancelled main runs in the last 50.
+  - `K` — `recycle` lines of the standing dispatch and triage seats in the
+    day's sweep record.
+
+  Every line but `H` is held in `--self-test` to a null control (a case whose
+  right answer is the quiet one). Inputs sit under `<state>/scorecard/`
+  (`runs.json`, `jobs/jobs_<id>.json`, `verdicts.json`, `merges.tsv`,
+  `roster.json`) beside the overlay's `train_log` and the optional
+  `sweep_record`. When: the beat's `scorecard` row runs `report --dir
+  <state>/scorecard --train-log <train_log> --repo <checkout>` (plus
+  `--sweep-record` when the overlay names one) once a day and writes the
+  output to `S/beatd/scorecard.txt`; the digest hears only
+  `scorecard: UNREADABLE rc=<n>: <why>` when the run fails. `--self-test`:
+  planted and null cases per line, and one mutant per predicate.

   non-numeric `--interval` or an unknown option; a failing relay pass or tick
   is reported and the loop goes on. `--self-test` drives it over stubs.
+  The self-test reads and moves no checkout but scratch clones of its own:
+  `--self-test`'s first statement re-runs it under `env -i` carrying no
+  caller variable (`PATH` a literal of system directories and the running
+  bash's, `HOME` and `TMPDIR` fresh), and the rows run only from the
+  `--self-test-rows` entry that re-exec names. The barrier fails closed: a
+  `--self-test` the re-exec did not replace (a caller's function named
+  `exec`, exported or defined by a `BASH_ENV` file, shadows the builtin)

+  command a function could shadow; rows pin both shadows and the null
+  control. So no caller variable, nor a value computed from one, reaches a
+  row, unless a caller's own code runs the rows entry itself (a
+  `BASH_ENV` file is code run inside this process, out of any script
+  line's reach); its poison row exports every name the

+  branch and a detached clone behind origin/main to pin that, so it is safe

+def rollup_states(entries) -> "dict[str, str]":

+def quiet_log(full: Path, out=print, tail: int = QUIET_TAIL):
+    """The train's quiet log (owner card 2026-10-24): every line goes to `full`;
+    stdout gets every line but the named chatter (QUIET_CHATTER), and a
+    `TRAIN STOPPED` line first prints the last `tail` chatter lines, the
+    failing step's tail. `--verbose`/TRAIN_VERBOSE=1 skips it."""
+    held: list[str] = []
+    fh = open(full, "a", buffering=1)
+
+    def log(m) -> None:
+        m = str(m)
+        fh.write(m + "\n")
+        if QUIET_CHATTER_RE.match(m):
+            held.append(m)
+            del held[:-tail]
+            return
+        if "TRAIN STOPPED" in m:
+            for h in held:
+                out("  | " + h)
+            held.clear()
+        out(m)
+    out(f"quiet output: the full log is {full} (--verbose or TRAIN_VERBOSE=1 prints it)")
+    return log

+    one run of the listing is unfinished, else None. The baseline is the p50 and
+    max duration of the last BASELINE_JOBS completed runs of the same name in the
+    SAME listing (no extra API call); a name with none completed prints
+    `no baseline`. Elapsed over the max reads `over max`, never a verdict to
+    cancel (2026-11-11: two near-complete 2173-3623 s python jobs were cancelled
+    as hung)."""
+    runs = list(runs or ())
+    open_ = [r for r in runs if r.get("status") != "completed"]
+    if len(open_) != 1:
+        return None
+    job = open_[0]
+    name = job.get("name", "?")
+
+    def ts(v):
+        try:
+            return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(v.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()
+        except (AttributeError, ValueError):
+            return None
+
+    def secs(r):
+        a, b = ts(r.get("started_at")), ts(r.get("completed_at"))
+        return None if a is None or b is None else b - a
+

+                   and secs(r) is not None), key=lambda r: r.get("completed_at") or "")

+#: One planted reader per spelling every review found passing a caller scan:
+#: (name, source). Each defines `reader(latest, required)` reading the gate
+#: conclusion with no deferral; `_F` is FINAL, the only spelling of that read.
+PLANTED_READERS = [
+    ("direct call", "def reader(latest, required):\n    return classify(latest, required, _F)\n"),
+    ("import alias", "def reader(latest, required):\n    from merge_train import classify as judge\n    return judge(latest, required, _F)\n"),
+    ("rebinding", "judge = classify\ndef reader(latest, required):\n    return judge(latest, required, _F)\n"),
+    ("getattr", "import sys\ndef reader(latest, required):\n    return getattr(sys.modules['merge_train'], 'classify')(latest, required, _F)\n"),
+    ("functools.partial", "import functools\ndef reader(latest, required):\n    return functools.partial(classify, latest, required)(_F)\n"),
+    ("a function named *self_test*", "def reader_self_test(latest, required):\n    return classify(latest, required, _F)\nreader = reader_self_test\n"),
+    ("busy omitted", "def reader(latest, required):\n    return classify(latest, required)\n"),
+    ("busy a literal ()", "def reader(latest, required):\n    return classify(latest, required, ())\n"),
+    ("busy rebound to an empty Busy", "def reader(latest, required):\n    b = Busy()\n    return classify(latest, required, b)\n"),
+]

+def plant(src: str, filename: str) -> dict:
+    """<src> run as a module of its own whose code objects carry <filename>, with
+    merge_train's names in scope: its functions' frames are <filename>'s."""
+    ns = {k: v for k, v in globals().items() if not k.startswith("__")} | {"_F": FINAL, "__name__": "planted"}
+    exec(compile(src, filename, "exec"), ns)
+    return ns
+

+    here = str(Path(__file__).resolve())

+    def blind(fn) -> bool:
+        try:

+            return True

+    places = {"merge_train.py": here, "orchestrator_tick.py": str(ROOT / "tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py"),

+              "a module outside the tree": "/nonexistent/elsewhere.py"}

+    check(f"P436 barrier: each of the {len(PLANTED_READERS)} planted deferral-blind readers, planted in each of "
+          f"{len(places)} modules, refuses a red gate (BlindRead, or TypeError for no busy) -- passed: {passed[:4]}", not passed)
+    def at(path: str, qual: str):
+        """A FINAL reader whose frame is (path, qual)."""
+        cls, _, fn = qual.rpartition(".")

+        if cls:

+        ns = plant(body, str(ROOT / path))

+#: Self-test only: Train wraps an injected `run` so a stub refuses a paged read
+#: whose `--jq` is not the object key the path serves (mutation proof for the
+#: `key` argument of Train.pages and each call site).
+_JQ_CHECK = False
+_PAGED_KEY = (("check-runs", "check_runs"), ("/jobs?", "jobs"), ("actions/", "workflow_runs"))
+
+
+def _jq_checked(run):
+    def checked(argv, *a, **k):
+        if argv[:2] == ["gh", "api"] and "--jq" in argv and re.search(r"[?&]page=\d+", argv[2]):
+            want = next((key for frag, key in _PAGED_KEY if frag in argv[2]), None)
+            jq = argv[argv.index("--jq") + 1]
+            if want and jq != f".{want}[]":
+                return 1, f"unexpected --jq {jq!r} for {argv[2]}"
+        return run(argv, *a, **k)
+    return checked
+
+
+def _jl(items) -> str:
+    """A paged read's stub answer: one compact JSON item per line (`--jq .[]`)."""
+    return "".join(json.dumps(x) + "\n" for x in items)
+
+

+FORK CAP (R10-MUTANT-RUN-FORKCAP). The command runs in its own session; its family (session, process group, every process
+carrying the run's MUTANT_RUN_TOKEN, and every descendant of the driver, which is a child
+subreaper (PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER) while the command runs, so a descendant that setsid'd,
+setpgid'd, cleared its environment or was orphaned still counts) is polled every 0.5 s and killed whole, also at exit; a family holding more than `--fork-cap` processes (default 256, 0
+turns the cap off) is SIGKILLed whole and reported `FORKCAP <name>` (diff mode:
+`FORKCAP file:line OPERATOR  <mutated line>`), never KILLED: a mutant that makes
+a self-test re-enter itself (a chain 700 deep once exhausted a host's `ulimit -u`)
+was stopped by the cap, not by a test pinning it, so it is unresolved. A diff

+reads only SURVIVED lines. A FORKCAP on the NULL run is rc 3, as KILLED NULL is.

+dev/, not inside a multi-line string) and mutates each with six operators:

@@ -33,6 +44,14 @@ dev/, not inside a multi-line string) and mutates each with five operators:
               are left alone: they pin no behaviour)
   CONST_SWAP  the first number moves (n to n+1, 0.0 to 1.0) or, with none,
               the first True/False flips
+  STMT_DEL    from the head file's ast, each simple statement (assignment,
+              expression, delete, raise, assert, return) an added line falls in
+              is replaced whole, however many lines it spans, by `pass` at its
+              indent; the report line is `SURVIVED <file>:<first line> STMT_DEL  pass`.
+              Left alone: a statement sharing its lines with other code, a
+              docstring or bare constant, print and _LOGGER calls, imports and
+              compound headers, and any statement CALL_DEL or RETURN_DEL already
+              deletes to the same text

+NO PROCFS. Where /proc is absent (macOS, the BSDs) the process table comes from
+`ps -axo pid=,stat=,ppid=,pgid=` with the session from os.getsid; the token leg
+reads nothing, and with no subreaper there either, a descendant that left the
+session is not followed.
+
+The procfs root is `MUTANT_RUN_PROCFS` (default /proc): a path that does not
+exist makes the host one without procfs, in this process and every driver it
+starts, so a Linux host runs the macOS path.
+
+`--self-test` builds throwaway repositories and runs every arm above. It reads
+the process table three ways on every host: with no procfs root, through a faked
+root it writes from the live table, and through the host's own /proc. A case the
+host cannot run (its own /proc where there is none, a child subreaper where
+prctl is absent) prints one `skip` line naming why and is counted on the
+`skipped` line above the summary.

+def _subreaper(on: int) -> int:
+    """Set this process's child-subreaper flag (PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER: an orphaned descendant is

+    a host without procfs (macOS, the BSDs) from `ps`, the session from os.getsid (None where refused)."""

+def family(sid: int, token: str, skip: frozenset = frozenset(), root: int = 0) -> list[int]:
+    """Live processes of the command `sid` started: its session, its process group, any that still
+    carries the run's token in its environment, and, given `root` (this driver, a subreaper while

+    had before the command). The ppid leg is the one a descendant cannot leave: setsid, setpgid,
+    a cleared environment and an exited parent all keep it under `root`. Zombies are not counted."""

+def _stmt_del(rel: str, src: str, lines: list[str], nums: list[int], have: set[str]) -> list[tuple]:
+    """STMT_DEL: each simple statement an added line falls in, whole, becomes `pass` at its indent.
+
+    Skipped: a statement sharing its lines with other code (`a = 1; b = 2`, `if x: y = 1`),
+    a docstring or bare constant, a print or _LOGGER call, and any text another operator already
+    produced (a single-line CALL_DEL or RETURN_DEL), so a statement is one mutant, not two.
+    """
+    try:
+        tree = ast.parse(src)
+    except SyntaxError:
+        return []
+    out = []
+    for node in sorted((x for x in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(x, _SIMPLE)), key=lambda x: x.lineno):
+        lo, hi = node.lineno, node.end_lineno
+        if not any(lo <= n <= hi for n in nums):
+            continue
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Expr):
+            v = node.value
+            if isinstance(v, ast.Constant):
+                continue
+            if isinstance(v, ast.Call) and ast.unparse(v.func).split(".")[0] in ("print", "_LOGGER"):
+                continue
+        first, last = lines[lo - 1].rstrip("\r\n"), lines[hi - 1].rstrip("\r\n")
+        head = first.encode()[: node.col_offset].decode()
+        tail = last.encode()[node.end_col_offset:].decode().strip()
+        if head.strip() or (tail and not tail.startswith("#")):
+            continue
+        eol = lines[lo - 1][len(first):]
+        text = "".join(lines[: lo - 1]) + head + "pass" + eol + "".join(lines[hi:])
+        if text == src or text in have:
+            continue
+        try:
+            compile(text, rel, "exec")
+        except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
+            continue
+        have.add(text)
+        out.append((rel, lo, "STMT_DEL", text, "pass"))
+    return out
+

+# Whose refusal a refused row push is (R10-HOTFIX-OPENPR-HOST-REFUSAL): the HOST's only when the refused
+# step, run again here on the refused head and on a pristine origin/main tree, fails the same way at
+# both -- one exit status, one set of FAIL rows. It is measured, never read from the refusal's text
+# or the diff's paths: #3508 was closed for a self-test that failed on the orchestrator host at
+# origin/main too, and a path guard on prepr.sh called a head that broke any other self-test input
+# the host's. The log only names WHICH step refused; prepr's self-test is the one step with a form
+# that runs on a tree alone, so a row naming any other step (a body, figure or carry check reads the
+# head's body) is the head's. Both trees are detached worktrees under <cache>, run alike, and each
+# measurement owns its tree: a directory mktemp makes for that one call, which no other run names,
+# removes or reuses (two refusals measured at once in one shared tree read each other's files, and
+# called a head's break the host's). A run that did not end whole is no measurement: its tree gone
+# or off <sha> when the self-test returns, or the self-test ended by a signal. Main's answer is
+# kept per origin/main sha in <cache>/<sha>.sig, written from a whole run under this process's own
+# name and renamed into place, one run per main move; whatever cannot be measured (no tree of its
+# own, no worktree, no self-test in the tree, no cache directory) is the head's, and closes. A run
+# killed mid-measurement leaves its <cache>/tree.* directory: nothing here removes another run's.
+pr_step_sig() { # <checkout> <sha> <scratch dir> -> the self-test's exit status and FAIL rows at <sha>; rc 1 = not measured
+  local w st rc=0 out="" at
+  w=$(mktemp -d "$3/tree.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) || return 1  # ret:sigpriv
+  git -C "$1" worktree add -q --detach "$w" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -rf "$w"; false; } || return 1  # ret:sigtree
+  st=tools/pr/prepr.sh
+  [ ! -f "$w/tools/audit/prepr.sh" ] || st=tools/audit/prepr.sh  # the copy tools/pr/prepr.sh itself runs when a tree holds one  # mut:sigold
+  if [ -f "$w/$st" ]; then out=$(cd "$w" && PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub bash "$st" --self-test 2>&1) || rc=$?; else rc=unrun; fi
+  at=$(git -C "$w" rev-parse -q --verify HEAD 2>/dev/null) || at=gone
+  git -C "$1" worktree remove --force "$w" >/dev/null 2>&1 || :; rm -rf "$w" || :
+  [ "$rc" != unrun ] || return 1  # ret:signone
+  [ "$at" = "$(git -C "$1" rev-parse -q --verify "$2^{commit}" 2>/dev/null)" ] || return 1  # ret:sigwhole
+  [ "$rc" -le 128 ] || return 1  # ret:sigkilled
+  printf 'rc=%s\n' "$rc"; grep -E '^  FAIL ' <<<"$out" | sort -u || :
+}
+pr_host_refusal() { # <checkout> <refusal log> <refused head> <origin/main sha> <cache dir>: 0 = the host's, 1 = the head's
+  local c=$5 other sh sm
+  other=$(grep REFUSE "$2" 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '^  REFUSE +self-test( |$)|^app_push: REFUSE: the body did not pass tools/pr/prepr\.sh' | grep -c . || :)
+  [ "$other" = 0 ] || return 1  # mut:hostother
+  grep -qE '^  REFUSE +self-test( |$)' "$2" 2>/dev/null || return 1  # mut:hostrows
+  [ -n "$3" ] && [ -n "$4" ] && mkdir -p "$c" 2>/dev/null || return 1  # ret:hostdir
+  sh=$(pr_step_sig "$1" "$3" "$c") || return 1  # ret:hosthead
+  sm=$(cat "$c/$4.sig" 2>/dev/null) || sm=  # mut:hostcache
+  [ -n "$sm" ] || { sm=$(pr_step_sig "$1" "$4" "$c") && printf '%s\n' "$sm" > "$c/$4.tmp.$$" && { rm -f "$c"/*.sig; mv -f "$c/$4.tmp.$$" "$c/$4.sig"; }; } || return 1  # ret:hostmain
+  [ "${sh%%$'\n'*}" != rc=0 ] || return 1  # mut:hostfails
+  [ "$sh" = "$sm" ]  # mut:hostsame
+}

new file mode 100755
index 0000000000..d7b41fd0f6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/audit/seat/r10_disinfection_setpoint_mutants.py
@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""R10-OUTSIDE-DISINFECTION-SETPOINT's named mutants, each run against tests/block_duty.py.
+
+    python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_disinfection_setpoint_mutants.py [NAME ...]
+
+Each mutant is applied to a detached worktree of HEAD (removed after), and
+tests/block_duty.py run there under PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub. Prints
+<name>: KILLED|SURVIVED and the checks that failed. NULL changes
+nothing and must survive; every other mutant must be killed.
+"""
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+SRC = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3])
+A = "custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_arbiter.py"
+T = "custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py"
+P = "custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/setpoint_check.py"
+MUTANTS = [
+    ("NULL", A, "", ""),
+    ("M1-no-cycle-write", A, "cycle = inp.params.dhw_cycle_temp if booked or inp.disinfecting else None", "cycle = None"),
+    ("M2-round-up", A, 'return _bounded(inp, "dhw_setpoint", float(cycle), hi=inp.params.dhw_hard_max_temp)',
+     'return _bounded(inp, "dhw_setpoint", float(cycle), rounding="up")'),
+    ("M12-no-hard-max", A, 'return _bounded(inp, "dhw_setpoint", float(cycle), hi=inp.params.dhw_hard_max_temp)',
+     'return _bounded(inp, "dhw_setpoint", float(cycle))'),
+    ("M13-cap-cycle-not-hard-max", A, 'hi=inp.params.dhw_hard_max_temp)', 'hi=float(cycle))'),
+    ("M14-limit-hard-max", A, 'everyday, hi=inp.params.dhw_max_temp)', 'everyday, hi=inp.params.dhw_hard_max_temp)'),
+    ("M15-limit-dropped", A, 'everyday, hi=inp.params.dhw_max_temp)', 'everyday)'),
+    ("M16-limit-round-up", A, 'everyday, hi=inp.params.dhw_max_temp)', 'everyday, rounding="up")'),
+    ("M17-fix-uncapped", P, 'rounding="up", hi_c=params.dhw_hard_max_temp)', 'rounding="up")'),
+    ("M18-active-raw-floor", P, "and pump < on_step_c - MIXING_VALVE_WRITE_EPSILON", "and pump < floor - MIXING_VALVE_WRITE_EPSILON"),
+    ("M19-ceiling-under-min", A, "if hi is not None and (low is None or hi >= quantise_setpoint_c(inp.hass, entity, low, rounding=\"up\")):",
+     "if hi is not None:"),
+    ("M20-ceiling-under-raw-min", A, "hi >= quantise_setpoint_c(inp.hass, entity, low, rounding=\"up\")", "hi >= low"),
+    ("M3-booking-ignored", A, "if booked or inp.disinfecting else None", "if inp.disinfecting else None"),
+    ("M4-hold-ignored", A, "if booked or inp.disinfecting else None", "if booked else None"),
+    ("M5-gate-only-excuse", A, 'return not (reading is None or written is None or _differs("dhw_setpoint", reading, written[0]))',
+     'return not (reading is None or written is None or _differs("dhw_setpoint", reading, written[0])) and written[0] < float(coord.arbiter_inputs().params.dhw_setpoint) - SETPOINT_TOLERANCE'),
+    ("M6-excuse-any-reading", A, 'return not (reading is None or written is None or _differs("dhw_setpoint", reading, written[0]))',
+     'return not (reading is None or written is None)'),
+    # M11-everyday-cycle-nearest (route a cycle at or below the everyday set-point through the
+    # no-cycle return) is retired as equivalent since part 2: there the cycle's temperature is the
+    # everyday set-point and dhw_hard_max_temp equals dhw_max_temp, so both returns are one call.
+    ("M7-flag-ignored", T, "return self.dhw_legionella_temp if self.legionella_cycle_active else None", "return self.dhw_legionella_temp"),
+    ("M10-enabled-not-active", T, "return self.dhw_legionella_temp if self.legionella_cycle_active else None",
+     "return self.dhw_legionella_temp if self.dhw_legionella_enabled else None"),
+    ("M8-cycle-not-max", T, "return None if target is None else max(self.dhw_setpoint, target)", "return target"),
+    ("M9-floor-no-disinfection", P, "return floor if disinfection is None else max(floor, float(disinfection))", "return floor"),
+]
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    names = sys.argv[1:] or [m[0] for m in MUTANTS]
+    bad = 0
+    for name, path, old, new in MUTANTS:
+        if name not in names:
+            continue
+        d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
+        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", SRC, "worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", d, "HEAD"], check=True)
+        try:
+            f = os.path.join(d, path)
+            s = open(f).read()
+            if old:
+                assert s.count(old) == 1, (name, s.count(old))
+                open(f, "w").write(s.replace(old, new))
+            r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "tests/block_duty.py"], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True,
+                               env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": "tests/hastub"})
+            fails = [l.strip() for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip().startswith("FAIL")]
+            print(f"{name}: {'KILLED' if r.returncode else 'SURVIVED'} rc={r.returncode}")
+            bad += (name == "NULL") == bool(r.returncode)
+            for l in fails:
+                print("   ", l[:150])
+        finally:
+            subprocess.run(["git", "-C", SRC, "worktree", "remove", "--force", d])
+    return 1 if bad else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
diff --git a/tools/audit/seat/replay_draws.py b/tools/audit/seat/replay_draws.py
index 2afa6b2628..5fb743ac9e 100644
--- a/tools/audit/seat/replay_draws.py
+++ b/tools/audit/seat/replay_draws.py
@@ -12,6 +12,8 @@ draws is re-derived by running it, not by reading a body.
     replay_draws.py parse --cache DIR --out FILE.tsv
     replay_draws.py window --cache DIR --runs N --until 2026-11-05T23:59:59Z
     replay_draws.py grade --job ID [--ruler MS] [--clean-from ARM]
+    replay_draws.py shift [--table FILE.tsv] [--no-cuts]
+    replay_draws.py interleave --pre DIR --post DIR [--pairs N]
 
 ``fetch`` lists the runs (newest first), each run's jobs on every page and
 every attempt, and downloads each concluded job's log once into ``DIR``,
@@ -24,6 +26,14 @@ grades one job of ``tests/replay_cost_draws.tsv`` exactly as the lane does
 (``replay.job_cost``) and exits 1 iff a clean run offends or a doubled arm is
 not over budget: ``--ruler`` moves the job's ruler (a draw moved across a
 border), ``--clean-from cpu`` grades the doubled arm as if it were clean.
+``shift`` runs ``replay.level_shift_offenders`` over a draw table (default the
+committed one; ``--table`` reads another, e.g. one ``git show <sha>:`` wrote),
+prints the classes examined and every class resting wholly on draws before a
+shift, and exits 1 iff it names one; ``--no-cuts`` drops ``COST_CUTS``.
+``interleave`` measures a declared cut's factor on this box: the synthetic
+fixture's clean replay (``replay.py --one``) in two checkouts, a commit's parent
+(``--pre``) and the commit (``--post``), ``N`` pairs in alternating order,
+printing each run's ``cpu_ratio`` and ruler and the ratio of the medians.
 Needs an authenticated ``gh``.
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
@@ -176,6 +186,48 @@ def grade(job: str, ruler: float | None, clean_from: str | None) -> int:
     return 1 if bad else 0
 
 
+def shift(table: Path | None, cuts: bool) -> int:
+    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+    sys.path[:0] = [str(root / "tests"), str(root / "tests" / "hastub")]
+    import replay
+    path = table or replay.COST_DRAWS
+    out = 0
+    for name in replay.COST_CLASS_BUDGETS:
+        examined, offenders = replay.level_shift_offenders(
+            replay.cost_draws(path, cuts=()), replay.cost_draw_created(path), name,
+            cuts=replay.COST_CUTS if cuts else ())
+        print(f"{name}: classes examined {len(examined)} {examined}")
+        for o in offenders:
+            print(f"  {o}")
+        out |= bool(offenders)
+    return out
+
+
+def interleave(pre: Path, post: Path, pairs: int) -> int:
+    import os
+    import statistics
+    got: dict[str, list[float]] = {"pre": [], "post": []}
+    for i in range(pairs):
+        for arm in (("pre", "post") if i % 2 == 0 else ("post", "pre")):
+            tree = pre if arm == "pre" else post
+            run = subprocess.run(
+                [sys.executable, "tests/replay.py", "--one", "tests/replay/synthetic-dhw-only.json"],
+                cwd=tree, capture_output=True, text=True,
+                env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": "tests/hastub"})
+            line = next((ln for ln in run.stdout.splitlines()
+                         if ln.startswith("<<<replay-json>>>")), None)
+            if line is None:
+                print(f"pair {i + 1} {arm}: no replay-json line (exit {run.returncode})")
+                return 2
+            cost = json.loads(line[len("<<<replay-json>>>"):])["cost"]
+            got[arm].append(cost["cpu_ratio"])
+            print(f"pair {i + 1} {arm} cpu_ratio {cost['cpu_ratio']} ref_ms {cost['ref_ms']:.2f}",
+                  flush=True)
+    a, b = statistics.median(got["pre"]), statistics.median(got["post"])
+    print(f"medians pre {a} post {b}; post/pre {b / a:.4f}")
+    return 0
+
+
 def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
     sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
@@ -194,7 +246,18 @@ def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
     g.add_argument("--job", required=True)
     g.add_argument("--ruler", type=float)
     g.add_argument("--clean-from", choices=("cpu", "memory", "loop"))
+    h = sub.add_parser("shift")
+    h.add_argument("--table", type=Path)
+    h.add_argument("--no-cuts", action="store_true")
+    i = sub.add_parser("interleave")
+    i.add_argument("--pre", type=Path, required=True)
+    i.add_argument("--post", type=Path, required=True)
+    i.add_argument("--pairs", type=int, default=12)
     args = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    if args.cmd == "interleave":
+        return interleave(args.pre, args.post, args.pairs)
+    if args.cmd == "shift":
+        return shift(args.table, not args.no_cuts)
     if args.cmd == "grade":
         return grade(args.job, args.ruler, args.clean_from)
     if args.cmd == "fetch":

-           "handoff-not-applied", "carry-landed")

 def git(*a: str, cwd: Path | None = None, check: bool = True) -> str:
@@ -224,6 +224,51 @@ def required_reading(pr: int, head: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
     return "RED", f"classify unreadable (rc {r.returncode}): {last[:200]}"
 
 
+def introduced_reading(head: str, base: str, read=None) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
+    """(INTRODUCED step names, how read) of the head's instrument-self-tests job
+    against the merge base's, by merge_train.introduced_at: the one rule, which
+    `classify --pr` reads too: one filtered check-run read per side and one
+    job-step read per side through `gh`, and only the head's listing when its
+    job is not red. An input with no reading (unreadable, a job-level cancelled,
+    a job still running) is ([], "unreadable: ..."), which `build` refuses: fail closed."""
+    import merge_train
+    read = read or gh
+
+    def get(path):
+        try:
+            return read(path)
+        except Unavailable:
+            return None

diff --git a/tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py b/tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py
index 72418af63e..f12d47539e 100644
--- a/tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py
+++ b/tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py
@@ -128,6 +128,40 @@ def sizes(durations: dict) -> tuple:
     except (KeyError, TypeError) as e:
         raise SchemaError(f"{DURATIONS} carries no sizes_hours table: {e}")
 
+#: A group's owner-stated price (R10-HOTFIX-PLAN-OWNER-PRICE): minutes the
+#: owner ruled for the group, and the text of the ruling. The planner reads
+#: them (`replan.group_hours`), the editor writes them (`roster_edit set-price`),
+#: and both ask `owner_price_why` -- one definition of a writable price.
+OWNER_PRICE_MINUTES = "owner_price_minutes"
+OWNER_PRICE_CITE = "owner_price_cite"
+
+
+def owner_price_why(minutes, cite) -> str | None:
+    """Why (`minutes`, `cite`) is not an owner-stated price, or None. A price
+    is a positive number of minutes (a bool is no number) beside a non-blank
+    citation text: a price nobody can trace to the owner is a fabricated
+    measurement."""
+    if isinstance(minutes, bool) or not isinstance(minutes, (int, float)) \
+            or not minutes > 0 or minutes == float("inf"):
+        return f"an owner price is a positive number of minutes, not {minutes!r}"
+    if not isinstance(cite, str) or not cite.strip():
+        return "an owner price needs a citation text naming the owner's words"
+    return None
+
+
+def owner_price(group: dict) -> tuple[float, str] | None:
+    """(minutes, citation) of a group's owner-stated price, None when it has
+    none. One field without the other, or an invalid pair, is a SchemaError:
+    a half-written price is never read as no price."""
+    m, c = group.get(OWNER_PRICE_MINUTES), group.get(OWNER_PRICE_CITE)
+    if m is None and c is None:
+        return None
+    why = owner_price_why(m, c)
+    if why:
+        raise SchemaError(f"{group.get('group')}: {why}")
+    return float(m), c.strip()
+
+
 # WHICH ROSTER -- the one owner (R10-TICK b, d). Every seat tool that reads or
 # edits a roster asks `roster_path()`; none carries a path of its own. A round's
 # roster is `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r<N>-groups.json`, the programme-record
@@ -661,6 +695,10 @@ def one_line_brief(group: dict, limit: int = 160) -> str:
     longer than `limit` is cut with an ellipsis.
     """
     text = (group.get("brief") or "").strip()
+    # A brief written as a markdown document opens with a heading marker; the
+    # row is plain text, so the marker goes and the lines join.
+    text = re.sub(r"\A\s*#{1,6}[ \t]*", "", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"\s*\n\s*", " ", text)
     text = _ATTRIBUTION.sub("", text)
     cut = re.split(r"(?<=\.)\s", text, maxsplit=1)[0]
     cut = cut.replace("|", "/")
diff --git a/tools/audit/seat/scorecard.py b/tools/audit/seat/scorecard.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..97b4b64f48
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/audit/seat/scorecard.py
@@ -0,0 +1,276 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Convergence scorecard: ten report-only lines, one per signal, each with its null control.
+
+    python3 -I scorecard.py report --dir D --train-log PATH [--repo DIR] [--sweep-record PATH]
+    python3 -I scorecard.py --self-test [--no-mutants]
+
+Report-only (R10-MACH-SCORECARD): no line sets an exit code or holds a merge. It
+is the baseline from which thresholds can later be set. Read-only on every
+input and no GitHub call; the inputs are refreshed elsewhere and an input it
+cannot read prints `<line>  unread (<why>)`, never a guessed value.
+
+INPUTS, all under D (the beat's `<state>/scorecard/`) except the train log:
+  runs.json      [{id, t, c}] main `CI` push runs: id, UTC stamp, run conclusion
+  jobs/jobs_<id>.json   the run's job listing (`{"jobs": [{name, conclusion}]}`)
+  verdicts.json  {"verdicts": [{pr, head, kind, cls, t}]} review verdicts
+  merges.tsv     TSV with columns pr, ct, class, tokens (merge order by ct)
+  roster.json    {"groups": [...]} the round's roster
+  ../study/work/yield.py  holds `FAMILY = [(name, regex), ...]`, read as a
+                 literal (never executed), the class-word to family map of M_first
+
+THE LINES (rule, then the null control the self-test holds it to):
+  A_gate   share of the last 20 concluded (success or failure) main runs whose
+           job named `gate` concluded success; a run with no cached job listing
+           is `unread`, reported and not guessed.
+           NULL: a run whose only failed job is `governance / instrument-self-tests`
+           counts green here and red in A_run.
+  A_run    share of the same runs whose run conclusion is success.
+           NULL: the same run counts red.
+  Y_rev    over the last 50 pull requests by first verdict (the earliest verdict by `t`,
+           whatever the order of verdicts.json): share whose first verdict is `merge`.
+           NULL: a bus of merge verdicts only prints 100%.
+  M_first  same 50: share whose first verdict is `blocked` in a machinery family
+           (MACH: carry, body, CI state, merge state, root-cause form, ruling or roster).
+           NULL: the same bus prints 0%.
+  Y_train  over the last 50 merged pull requests the merge train named: share
+           never on a `SKIP #n` or `PARK` line. A pull request the train never
+           named is not counted.
+           NULL: a log with no SKIP or PARK line prints 100%.
+  H        hotfix-token merges among the last 50 code merges (class production
+           or instrument), with the production merges among those 50 beside it.
+           NO NULL CONTROL: it is a naming measure (a branch token), read with
+           that caveat. The study's own text gives it none and none is invented.
+  S        size: `machinery_ratchet.py --measure --head origin/main` (its JSON's
+           non-production merges per window and churn per 1 000 product lines),
+           and machinery lines over product lines from `git grep -c ''` over
+           `tools .github .claude dev/governance` against `custom_components blueprints`.
+           NULL: a frozen machinery gives a flat or falling ratio (the ratio
+           of two unchanged counts is unchanged).
+  E        escapes: roster groups whose source is `outside`, and hotfix or bug
+           groups (group names HOTFIX, or kind bug|hotfix) whose files include
+           the product (`custom_components/`); and how many of both are still
+           open (resume.stage not `done`).
+           NULL: a round with no escape adds none.
+  C        detection delay: the longest run of consecutive cancelled main runs
+           in the last 50 runs (cancelled runs included, ordered by stamp).
+           NULL: C is 0 when no main run is cancelled.
+  K        seat cost: `recycle` lines of the standing dispatch and triage seats
+           in the day's sweep record.
+           NULL: K is 0 with no recycle line.
+C and K are one row of the study's table and print on one line.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import ast
+import collections
+import csv
+import io
+import json
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+WINDOW_RUNS = 20
+WINDOW_PRS = 50
+WINDOW_MERGES = 50
+WINDOW_CANCEL = 50
+MACH = {"carry-bookkeeping", "body-bookkeeping", "ci-state", "merge-state", "root-cause-form", "ruling-or-roster"}
+RECYCLE = re.compile(r"\brecycle", re.I)
+SEATS = re.compile(r"standing[- ](?:dispatch|triage)|\b(?:dispatch|triage)\b", re.I)
+
+
+def pct(n: int, d: int) -> str:
+    return f"{100 * n / d:.0f}%" if d else "n/a"
+
+
+def family_of(cls: str, fam: list) -> str:
+    for name, rx in fam:
+        if re.match(rx, cls):
+            return name
+    return "unmapped"
+
+
+def load_family(text: str) -> list:
+    """FAMILY from yield.py's source, as a literal; nothing is executed."""
+    i = text.index("FAMILY = [")
+    j = text.index("def fam(", i)
+    return ast.literal_eval(text[i:j].split("=", 1)[1].strip())
+
+
+def line_a(runs: list, gate: dict) -> list[str]:
+    ok = [r for r in sorted(runs, key=lambda r: r["t"]) if r["c"] in ("success", "failure")][-WINDOW_RUNS:]
+    if not ok:
+        return ["A_gate  unread (no concluded main run)", "A_run   unread (no concluded main run)"]
+    g = collections.Counter("success" if r["c"] == "success" else gate.get(r["id"], "unread") for r in ok)
+    read = g["success"] + g["failure"]
+    run_ok = sum(r["c"] == "success" for r in ok)
+    gate_part = f"{g['success']}/{read} read = {pct(g['success'], read)}" if read else "0/0 read"
+    return [f"A_gate  {gate_part}  (unread {g['unread']} of {len(ok)}; window {ok[0]['t']} .. {ok[-1]['t']})",
+            f"A_run   {run_ok}/{len(ok)} = {pct(run_ok, len(ok))}"]
+
+
+def line_review(verdicts: list, fam: list | None) -> list[str]:
+    first: dict = {}
+    for v in sorted(verdicts, key=lambda v: v["t"]):  # the first verdict is the earliest by t, whatever the file order
+        first.setdefault(v["pr"], v)
+    last = list(first.values())[-WINDOW_PRS:]
+    if not last:
+        return ["Y_rev   unread (no verdict)", "M_first unread (no verdict)"]
+    n = len(last)
+    first_merge = sum(v["kind"] == "merge" for v in last)
+    span = f"first verdicts {last[0]['t'][:16]} .. {last[-1]['t'][:16]}"
+    y = f"Y_rev   first verdict merge {first_merge}/{n} = {pct(first_merge, n)}  ({span})"
+    if fam is None:
+        return [y, "M_first unread (no family map)"]
+    mf = sum(v["kind"] == "blocked" and family_of(v["cls"], fam) in MACH for v in last)
+    return [y, f"M_first {mf}/{n} = {pct(mf, n)}  ({span})"]
+
+
+def line_train(merged: list[str], train_text: str) -> str:
+    skipped, named = set(), set()
+    for ln in train_text.splitlines():
+        m = re.match(r"SKIP #(\d+)", ln)
+        if m:
+            skipped.add(m[1])
+        if ln.startswith("PARK"):
+            skipped |= set(re.findall(r"#(\d{4})", ln)[:1])
+        if re.match(r"(BATCH|SKIP|PARK|MERGED|ADMIT|ALREADY)", ln):
+            named |= set(re.findall(r"#(\d{4})", ln))
+    tn = [p for p in merged if p in named][-WINDOW_MERGES:]
+    clean = sum(p not in skipped for p in tn)
+    return f"Y_train never skipped or parked {clean}/{len(tn)} = {pct(clean, len(tn))}  (last {WINDOW_MERGES} train-named merged PRs)"
+
+
+def line_hotfix(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
+    code = [r for r in rows if r["class"] in ("production", "instrument")][-WINDOW_MERGES:]
+    hot = sum("hotfix" in r["tokens"] for r in code)
+    prod = sum(r["class"] == "production" for r in code)
+    return (f"H       hotfix-token merges {hot}/{len(code)} of the last {WINDOW_MERGES} code merges; "
+            f"production merges among them {prod}  (naming measure, no null control)")
+
+
+def line_escapes(groups: list[dict]) -> str:
+    out = [x for x in groups if x.get("source") == "outside"]
+    ph = [x for x in groups if ("HOTFIX" in x["group"] or x.get("kind") in ("bug", "hotfix"))
+          and any(f.startswith("custom_components/") for f in (x.get("files") or []))]
+    openn = sum((x.get("resume") or {}).get("stage") != "done" for x in out + ph)
+    return (f"E       roster groups from outside reports {len(out)}; hotfix or bug groups touching the product "
+            f"{len(ph)}; open among both {openn}")
+
+
+def cancel_streak(runs: list) -> int:
+    best = cur = 0
+    for r in sorted(runs, key=lambda r: r["t"])[-WINDOW_CANCEL:]:
+        cur = cur + 1 if r["c"] == "cancelled" else 0
+        best = max(best, cur)
+    return best
+
+
+def recycle_count(record: str) -> int:
+    return sum(bool(RECYCLE.search(ln) and SEATS.search(ln)) for ln in record.splitlines())
+
+
+def line_ck(runs: list | None, record: str | None) -> str:
+    c = f"C {cancel_streak(runs)}" if runs is not None else "C unread"
+    k = f"K {recycle_count(record)}" if record is not None else "K unread"
+    return f"C, K    {c}; {k}  (longest cancelled main-run streak; recycle lines of the dispatch and triage seats)"
+
+
+def sh_out(argv: list[str], cwd: Path) -> tuple[int, str]:
+    try:
+        p = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
+    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
+        return 127, str(e)
+    return p.returncode, p.stdout
+
+
+def count_lines(repo: Path, paths: list[str], run=sh_out) -> int | None:
+    rc, out = run(["git", "grep", "-c", "", "origin/main", "--", *paths], repo)
+    if rc not in (0, 1):
+        return None
+    return sum(int(ln.rsplit(":", 1)[1]) for ln in out.splitlines() if ":" in ln and ln.rsplit(":", 1)[1].isdigit())
+
+
+def line_size(repo: Path, run=sh_out) -> list[str]:
+    rc, out = run([sys.executable, "-I", "tools/audit/machinery_ratchet.py", "--measure", "--head", "origin/main"], repo)
+    mach = count_lines(repo, ["tools", ".github", ".claude", "dev/governance"], run)
+    prod = count_lines(repo, ["custom_components", "blueprints"], run)
+    try:
+        m = json.loads(out) if rc == 0 else None
+        lines = [f"S       non-production merges {m['nonproduction_merges']} per {m['window']}; "
+                 f"churn {m['churn_per_kilo_product_lines']} per 1 000 product lines"]
+    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
+        lines = ["S       ratchet unread"]
+    if mach is None or not prod:
+        lines.append("S       machinery/product unread")
+    else:
+        lines.append(f"S       machinery {mach} / product {prod} = {mach / prod:.2f}")
+    return lines
+
+
+def rd(path: Path):
+    try:
+        return path.read_text()
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+
+
+def report(d: Path, train_log: Path, repo: Path | None, record: Path | None, run=sh_out) -> list[str]:
+    out: list[str] = []
+
+    def load(name):
+        t = rd(d / name)
+        try:
+            return None if t is None else json.loads(t)
+        except ValueError:
+            return None
+
+    runs = load("runs.json")
+    gate: dict = {}
+    for f in sorted((d / "jobs").glob("jobs_*.json")) if (d / "jobs").is_dir() else []:
+        try:
+            for j in json.loads(f.read_text()).get("jobs", []):
+                if j["name"] == "gate":
+                    gate[int(f.stem.split("_")[1])] = j["conclusion"]
+        except (ValueError, KeyError, IndexError):
+            continue
+    out += line_a(runs, gate) if runs else ["A_gate  unread (runs.json)", "A_run   unread (runs.json)"]
+    v = load("verdicts.json")
+    ytxt = rd(d.parent / "study" / "work" / "yield.py")
+    try:
+        fam = load_family(ytxt) if ytxt else None
+    except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
+        fam = None
+    out += line_review(v["verdicts"], fam) if v else ["Y_rev   unread (verdicts.json)", "M_first unread (verdicts.json)"]
+    mt, tt = rd(d / "merges.tsv"), rd(train_log)
+    rows = sorted(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(mt), delimiter="\t"), key=lambda r: int(r["ct"])) if mt else None
+    out.append(line_train([r["pr"] for r in rows if r["pr"]], tt) if rows is not None and tt is not None
+               else "Y_train unread (merges.tsv or train log)")
+    out.append(line_hotfix(rows) if rows is not None else "H       unread (merges.tsv)")
+    out += line_size(repo, run) if repo else ["S       unread (no checkout)"]
+    ro = load("roster.json")
+    out.append(line_escapes(ro["groups"]) if ro else "E       unread (roster.json)")
+    out.append(line_ck(runs, rd(record) if record else None))
+    return out
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    if argv[:1] == ["--self-test"]:
+        import scorecard_selftest
+        return scorecard_selftest.run(Path(__file__), mutants="--no-mutants" not in argv)
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n", 1)[0])
+    ap.add_argument("cmd", choices=["report"])
+    ap.add_argument("--dir", required=True, type=Path)
+    ap.add_argument("--train-log", required=True, type=Path)
+    ap.add_argument("--repo", type=Path)
+    ap.add_argument("--sweep-record", type=Path)
+    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    print("\n".join(report(a.dir, a.train_log, a.repo, a.sweep_record)))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
diff --git a/tools/audit/seat/scorecard_selftest.py b/tools/audit/seat/scorecard_selftest.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..494fe70b3f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/audit/seat/scorecard_selftest.py
@@ -0,0 +1,218 @@
+"""Self-test of scorecard.py: a null control and a planted case per line, and one mutant per predicate.
+
+Run through scorecard.py's own test mode, with or without the mutants. Offline, in-process over
+planted inputs; the mutants edit a temp copy of scorecard.py, and a mutant that survives, or whose
+copy does not run, fails the test.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+H = "a" * 40
+
+
+def load(path: Path):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("scorecard_under_test", path)
+    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
+    return mod
+
+
+def runs(spec):
+    """[(conclusion, id)] -> run rows with ascending stamps."""
+    return [{"id": i, "t": f"2026-11-{1 + k // 24:02d}T{k % 24:02d}:00:00Z", "c": c} for k, (c, i) in enumerate(spec)]
+
+
+def verdicts(spec):
+    return [{"pr": p, "head": H, "kind": k, "cls": c, "t": f"2026-11-01T00:{n % 60:02d}:{n // 60:02d}Z"}
+            for n, (p, k, c) in enumerate(spec)]
+
+
+FAM = [("carry-bookkeeping", r"carry"), ("code", r"code")]
+TRAIN_CLEAN = "BATCH #1001 #1002\nMERGED #1001\nMERGED #1002\n"
+
+
+def cases(sc) -> dict[str, bool]:
+    r: dict[str, bool] = {}
+    # A_gate / A_run
+    rs = runs([("success", 1)] * 4 + [("failure", 5)])
+    ag, ar = sc.line_a(rs, {5: "success"})  # only a non-gate job failed
+    r["A_gate null: a run failing only outside the gate job counts green"] = "5/5 read = 100%" in ag
+    r["A_run null: the same run counts red"] = ar.startswith("A_run   4/5 = 80%")
+    ag, _ = sc.line_a(rs, {5: "failure"})
+    r["A_gate planted: a run whose gate job failed counts red"] = "4/5 read = 80%" in ag
+    ag, _ = sc.line_a(rs, {})
+    r["A_gate: a failed run with no job listing is unread, not guessed"] = "4/4 read = 100%" in ag and "unread 1 of 5" in ag
+    ag, ar = sc.line_a(runs([("cancelled", 9)] + [("success", 1)] * 2), {})
+    r["A_*: a cancelled run is not a concluded run"] = "2/2" in ag and "2/2" in ar
+    ag, ar = sc.line_a(runs([("failure", 100 + i) for i in range(5)] + [("success", i) for i in range(20)]), {})
+    r["A_*: only the last 20 concluded runs are read"] = "20/20 read = 100%" in ag and "20/20 = 100%" in ar
+    # Y_rev / M_first
+    bus = verdicts([(i, "merge", "none") for i in range(60)])
+    y, m = sc.line_review(bus, FAM)
+    r["Y_rev null: a bus of merge verdicts prints 100% over the last 50"] = "50/50 = 100%" in y
+    r["M_first null: the same bus prints 0%"] = m.startswith("M_first 0/50 = 0%")
+    mix = verdicts([(1, "blocked", "carry-x"), (2, "blocked", "code-x"), (3, "merge", "carry-x"), (4, "blocked", "zzz"),
+                    (1, "merge", "none"), (1, "blocked", "carry-x")])
+    y, m = sc.line_review(mix, FAM)
+    r["Y_rev planted: one merge first in four pull requests"] = "merge 1/4 = 25%" in y
+    r["M_first planted: only a blocked first verdict in a machinery family counts"] = m.startswith("M_first 1/4 = 25%")
+    # the first verdict is the earliest by t, in any file order; the window is the 50 latest first verdicts
+    shuf = [{"pr": 1, "head": H, "kind": "blocked", "cls": "carry-x", "t": "2026-11-03T00:00:00Z"},
+            {"pr": 1, "head": H, "kind": "merge", "cls": "none", "t": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z"},
+            {"pr": 2, "head": H, "kind": "blocked", "cls": "zzz", "t": "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z"}]
+    y, m = sc.line_review(shuf, FAM)
+    r["Y_rev unordered: the earliest verdict by t is the first, not the first in the file"] = \
+        "merge 1/2 = 50%" in y and "first verdicts 2026-11-01T00:00 .. 2026-11-02T00:00" in y and m.startswith("M_first 0/2 = 0%")
+    rev = [{"pr": i, "head": H, "kind": "merge" if i < 50 else "blocked", "cls": "none",
+            "t": f"2026-11-{1 + (99 - i) // 24:02d}T{(99 - i) % 24:02d}:00:00Z"} for i in range(60)]
+    y, _ = sc.line_review(rev, FAM)
+    r["Y_rev unordered window: the 50 latest first verdicts, whatever the file order"] = "merge 50/50 = 100%" in y
+    y, _ = sc.line_review([{"pr": 1, "head": H, "kind": "blocked", "cls": "zzz", "t": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z"},
+                           {"pr": 1, "head": H, "kind": "merge", "cls": "none", "t": "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z"}], FAM)
+    r["Y_rev first verdict: a later merge does not make a blocked first verdict a merge"] = "merge 0/1 = 0%" in y
+    y, m = sc.line_review(mix, None)
+    r["M_first without a family map is unread, Y_rev still prints"] = "unread" in m and "1/4" in y
+    # Y_train
+    mg = ["1001", "1002", "1003"]
+    t = sc.line_train(mg, TRAIN_CLEAN)
+    r["Y_train null: a log with no SKIP or PARK line prints 100%; an unnamed pull request is not counted"] = "2/2 = 100%" in t
+    t = sc.line_train(mg, TRAIN_CLEAN + "SKIP #1001 red\nPARK #1002 held\n")
+    r["Y_train planted: a SKIP line and a PARK line each cost the pull request"] = "0/2 = 0%" in t
+    t = sc.line_train(["1003"], "MERGED #1003\n")
+    r["Y_train named: a pull request named only on a MERGED line is counted"] = "1/1 = 100%" in t
+    # H
+    rows = [{"class": "production", "tokens": "hotfix-x"}, {"class": "instrument", "tokens": "hotfix"},
+            {"class": "docs", "tokens": "hotfix"}, {"class": "production", "tokens": "feat"}]
+    r["H: hotfix-token merges over code merges, docs not counted, production beside"] = \
+        "2/3 of the last 50 code merges; production merges among them 2" in sc.line_hotfix(rows)
+    r["H states it has no null control"] = "no null control" in sc.line_hotfix(rows)
+    # E
+    g = [{"group": "A", "source": "outside", "resume": {"stage": "done"}},
+         {"group": "R10-HOTFIX-X", "files": ["custom_components/a.py"], "resume": {"stage": "fix"}},
+         {"group": "B", "kind": "bug", "files": ["custom_components/b.py"]},
+         {"group": "C", "kind": "bug", "files": ["tools/x.py"]},
+         {"group": "D", "files": ["custom_components/d.py"]}]
+    e = sc.line_escapes(g)
+    r["E planted: one outside, two product hotfix or bug groups, two open"] = "outside reports 1;" in e and "product 2;" in e and "open among both 2" in e
+    r["E null: a round with no escape adds none"] = "reports 0; hotfix or bug groups touching the product 0; open among both 0" in sc.line_escapes([{"group": "D"}])
+    # C / K
+    cn = sc.line_ck(runs([("success", 1)] * 4), "all fine\n")
+    r["C, K null: no cancelled run and no recycle line are both 0"] = "C 0; K 0" in cn
+    cp = sc.line_ck(runs([("cancelled", 1), ("success", 2), ("cancelled", 3), ("cancelled", 4), ("cancelled", 5), ("success", 6)]),
+                    "standing-dispatch recycle at 10:00\nstanding triage RECYCLE\nroster recycle\nstanding-dispatch ok\n")
+    r["C planted: the longest consecutive cancelled streak"] = "C 3;" in cp
+    r["K planted: only recycle lines of the dispatch and triage seats"] = "K 2" in cp
+    r["C, K unread input is named, never 0"] = "C unread; K unread" in sc.line_ck(None, None)
+    # S
+    def fake(argv, cwd):
+        if "machinery_ratchet.py" in argv[2]:
+            return 0, '{"nonproduction_merges": 498, "window": 580, "churn_per_kilo_product_lines": 12299}\n'
+        paths = argv[-1:] if False else argv
+        n = "100" if "custom_components" in argv else "300"
+        return 0, f"origin/main:f:{n}\n"
+    s = sc.line_size(Path("."), fake)
+    r["S: the ratchet line verbatim and machinery over product"] = any("merges 498 per 580; churn 12299 per" in x for x in s) and any("300 / product 100 = 3.00" in x for x in s)
+    s2 = sc.line_size(Path("."), lambda argv, cwd: (0, "x:1\n") if "machinery_ratchet.py" not in argv[2] else (0, '{"nonproduction_merges": 1, "window": 2, "churn_per_kilo_product_lines": 3}'))
+    r["S null: frozen machinery and product give an unchanged ratio"] = s2[-1] == sc.line_size(Path("."), lambda argv, cwd: (0, "x:1\n") if "machinery_ratchet.py" not in argv[2] else (0, '{"nonproduction_merges": 1, "window": 2, "churn_per_kilo_product_lines": 3}'))[-1]
+    s3 = sc.line_size(Path("."), lambda argv, cwd: (2, ""))
+    s4 = sc.line_size(Path("."), lambda argv, cwd: fake(argv, cwd) if "machinery_ratchet.py" in argv[2] else (2, "origin/main:f:5\n"))
+    r["S: an unreadable ratchet is unread, never a number"] = "ratchet unread" in s3[0]
+    s5 = sc.line_size(Path("."), lambda argv, cwd: (3, '{"nonproduction_merges": 1, "window": 2, "churn_per_kilo_product_lines": 3}\n')
+                      if "machinery_ratchet.py" in argv[2] else fake(argv, cwd))
+    r["S: a ratchet that exits non-zero is unread even when it printed JSON"] = "ratchet unread" in s5[0]
+    r["S: an unreadable line count is unread, never a ratio"] = "498 per 580" in s4[0] and s4[-1].endswith("unread")
+    # the whole report over a planted state dir, and over an empty one
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        d = Path(td) / "scorecard"
+        (d / "jobs").mkdir(parents=True)
+        (d / "runs.json").write_text(json.dumps(rs))
+        (d / "jobs" / "jobs_5.json").write_text(json.dumps({"jobs": [{"name": "gate", "conclusion": "success"},
+                                                                    {"name": "governance / instrument-self-tests", "conclusion": "failure"}]}))
+        (d / "verdicts.json").write_text(json.dumps({"verdicts": mix}))
+        (d / "merges.tsv").write_text("pr\tct\tclass\ttokens\n1001\t1\tproduction\thotfix\n1002\t2\tproduction\tx\n")
+        (d / "roster.json").write_text(json.dumps({"groups": g}))
+        (Path(td) / "study" / "work").mkdir(parents=True)
+        (Path(td) / "study" / "work" / "yield.py").write_text(f"FAMILY = {FAM!r}\ndef fam(c):\n    pass\n")
+        (Path(td) / "train.log").write_text(TRAIN_CLEAN)
+        (Path(td) / "sweep.txt").write_text("dispatch recycle\n")
+        out = sc.report(d, Path(td) / "train.log", None, Path(td) / "sweep.txt")
+        r["report: ten lines' worth over a planted state dir (S unread without a checkout)"] = \
+            len(out) == 9 and not any("unread (" in x for x in out if x[:2] != "S ") and out[0].startswith("A_gate  5/5")
+        r["report: A_gate reads the job named gate, not the last job listed"] = out[0].startswith("A_gate  5/5 read = 100%") and out[1].startswith("A_run   4/5")
+        r["report: K reads the sweep record it is given"] = "K 1 " in out[-1] and "K unread" not in out[-1]
+        empty = sc.report(Path(td) / "none", Path(td) / "none.log", None, None)
+        r["report: an empty state dir prints unread on every line, none a number"] = \
+            all("unread" in x for x in empty if not x.startswith("C, K")) and "C unread; K unread" in empty[-1]
+    return r
+
+
+#: (needle, replacement, the case that must fail). One per predicate.
+MUTANTS = {
+    "A_gate reads the run conclusion": ('"success" if r["c"] == "success" else gate.get(r["id"], "unread")', 'r["c"]', "A_gate null"),
+    "A_gate window": ("WINDOW_RUNS = 20", "WINDOW_RUNS = 21", "only the last 20"),
+    "A_run counts cancelled green": ('sum(r["c"] == "success" for r in ok)', 'sum(r["c"] != "cancelled" for r in ok)', "A_run null"),
+    "Y_rev not merge": ('first_merge = sum(v["kind"] == "merge"', 'first_merge = sum(v["kind"] != "merge"', "Y_rev null"),
+    "Y_rev window": ("WINDOW_PRS = 50", "WINDOW_PRS = 51", "Y_rev null"),
+    "M_first ignores kind": ('v["kind"] == "blocked" and family_of', 'True and family_of', "M_first planted"),
+    "M_first family inverted": ("in MACH for v in last", "not in MACH for v in last", "M_first planted"),
+    "Y_rev first verdict kept": ("first.setdefault(v[\"pr\"], v)", "first[v[\"pr\"]] = v", "Y_rev first verdict"),
+    "Y_rev ordered by t": ('sorted(verdicts, key=lambda v: v["t"])', "list(verdicts)", "Y_rev unordered"),
+    "A_gate job named gate": ('if j["name"] == "gate":', "if True:", "report: A_gate reads the job named gate"),
+    "report passes the record": ("rd(record) if record else None", "None", "report: K reads"),
+    "Y_train MERGED names": ('(BATCH|SKIP|PARK|MERGED|ADMIT|ALREADY)', '(BATCH|SKIP|PARK|ADMIT|ALREADY)', "Y_train named"),
+    "S ratchet exit": ("json.loads(out) if rc == 0 else None", "json.loads(out)", "S: a ratchet that exits non-zero"),
+    "Y_train SKIP": ('r"SKIP #(\\d+)"', 'r"SKIPX #(\\d+)"', "Y_train planted"),
+    "Y_train PARK": ('ln.startswith("PARK")', 'ln.startswith("PARKX")', "Y_train planted"),
+    "Y_train unnamed counted": ("tn = [p for p in merged if p in named]", "tn = [p for p in merged]", "Y_train null"),
+    "H token": ('"hotfix" in r["tokens"]', '"hotfixx" in r["tokens"]', "H: hotfix"),
+    "H class filter": ('("production", "instrument")', '("production",)', "H: hotfix"),
+    "H production beside": ('r["class"] == "production" for r in code', 'r["class"] != "x" for r in code', "H: hotfix"),
+    "E outside": ('x.get("source") == "outside"', 'x.get("source") != "outside"', "E planted"),
+    "E hotfix name": ('"HOTFIX" in x["group"]', '"HOTFIXX" in x["group"]', "E planted"),
+    "E product files": ('f.startswith("custom_components/")', 'f.startswith("custom_componentsX/")', "E planted"),
+    "E open": ('.get("stage") != "done"', '.get("stage") == "done"', "E planted"),
+    "C streak": ('cur = cur + 1 if r["c"] == "cancelled" else 0', 'cur = cur + 1 if r["c"] == "cancelled" else cur', "C planted"),
+    "K seats": ("RECYCLE.search(ln) and SEATS.search(ln)", "RECYCLE.search(ln) or SEATS.search(ln)", "K planted"),
+    "S ratio inverted": ("mach / prod:.2f", "prod / mach:.2f", "S: the ratchet"),
+    "S unreadable count": ("if rc not in (0, 1):\n        return None", "if False:\n        return None", "S: an unreadable line count"),
+}
+
+
+def run(path: Path, mutants: bool = True) -> int:
+    bad: list[str] = []
+
+    def show(res: dict[str, bool]) -> None:
+        for name, ok in res.items():
+            print(("ok   " if ok else "FAIL ") + name)
+            if not ok:
+                bad.append(name)
+
+    show(cases(load(path)))
+    if mutants:
+        src = path.read_text()
+        here = Path(__file__).resolve()
+        for name, (old, new, case) in MUTANTS.items():
+            if src.count(old) != 1:
+                print(f"FAIL mutant {name}: needle found {src.count(old)} times")
+                bad.append(name)
+                continue
+            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+                (Path(td) / path.name).write_text(src.replace(old, new))
+                (Path(td) / here.name).write_text(here.read_text())
+                p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", str(Path(td) / here.name)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
+            killed = p.returncode != 0 and any(ln.startswith("FAIL") and case in ln for ln in p.stdout.splitlines())
+            print(("ok   " if killed else "FAIL ") + f"mutant killed: {name} (by '{case}')")
+            if not killed:
+                bad.append("mutant " + name)
+    print("scorecard self-test: " + ("FAIL " + "; ".join(bad) if bad else f"ok ({'with' if mutants else 'without'} mutants)"))
+    return 1 if bad else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":  # a mutant copy runs its cases only
+    sys.exit(run(Path(__file__).with_name("scorecard.py"), mutants=False))

diff --git a/tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh b/tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh
index 9ca47ad5df..c691f3e161 100755
--- a/tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh
+++ b/tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh
@@ -123,7 +123,7 @@ esac

 # lives in that script alone, so a raw post bypassed it). DENY BY DEFAULT: a call that could
 # write a comment on a record issue (#201, or its continuation) is refused unless the caller is python running the
-# tree's own gh_comment.py (by real path); it is let through only when it is on an explicit
+# baked tree's gh_comment.py, or a checkout's tracked and unmodified one (by real path; below); it is let through only when it is on an explicit
 # list of calls that cannot. The list is gh's own command table, not a list of spellings:
 #   - no subcommand, or --version/--help alone: pass; any other leading flag: refused;
 #   - `issue`: view/list/status/create pass; comment, close, reopen, edit, delete, lock,
@@ -337,18 +337,19 @@ if [ -n "${hit:-}" ]; then
     done
     if [ -n "$script" ] && [ -n "$gcpy" ]; then
       a=$(rp "$script") && b=$(rp "$gcpy") && [ "$a" = "$b" ] && ok=1
-      # Another tree's gh_comment.py (R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE, P449): the daemons' PATH carries one
-      # install, run from any checkout. Admitted by real path when it is the tracked
-      # tools/pr/gh_comment.py of a worktree git registers beside the baked tree's; a file
-      # merely so named, in a directory git does not list, stays refused.
+      # Another checkout's gh_comment.py (R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE, P449; SHIM-COMMENT-GUARD-ONE-CHECKOUT,
+      # P591): the daemons' PATH carries one install, and three live checkouts run seat tools.
+      # Admitted by real path <root>/tools/pr/gh_comment.py when <root> is a checkout of this
+      # repository (it tracks this shim) and the script is tracked and unmodified against HEAD,
+      # so its mandate_guard is the committed one. A file merely so named, an untracked one, or
+      # one with a local edit stays refused.
       if [ -z "$ok" ] && [ -n "$a" ]; then
         case $a in */tools/pr/gh_comment.py)
-          troot=${a%/tools/pr/gh_comment.py} broot=${gcpy%/tools/pr/gh_comment.py}
-          if [ "$broot" != "$gcpy" ] && git -C "$troot" ls-files --error-unmatch tools/pr/gh_comment.py >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-            while IFS= read -r wl; do
-              [ "$wl" = "worktree $troot" ] && ok=1
-            done < <(git -C "$broot" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null)

+# ends a non-interactive bash.

 BR=$1; C=$2; B=$3; shift 3; ISS="$*"; R=tvofi/heatpump_optimizer
 WT=$P/upd-${BR//\//-}
 # The EXIT trap goes first, so the lock (pr_branch_lock) is freed by it after the reap: bash runs it
@@ -97,6 +97,15 @@ TTL=$(gh pr view "$N" -R $R --json title -q .title)
 _added=$(ensure_row . "$N" "$(row_line "$N" $R "$TTL")")
 ROW=""; [ -z "$_added" ] || ROW="adds one commit containing only this PR's own row, \`$_added\`"
 M=$(git rev-parse --short origin/main); H=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
+# A generated figure block names the head it was rendered at (figure_block.py refresh, as open_pr.sh's
+# op_figures), and the merges and the row above moved it: re-render at the head this run pushes or patches,
+# before either. A body with no block is untouched; a failed refresh refuses, pushing and patching nothing.
+upd_figures() { # <where>
+  grep -q '^<!-- figure-block: ' "$B" || return 0
+  python3 -I "$PRT/figure_block.py" refresh "$B" --base origin/main --head HEAD > $WT.fig.log 2>&1 && return 0
+  pr_refuse "the figure-block refresh $1 failed; nothing is pushed or patched:
+$(tail -n 20 $WT.fig.log)"
+}

@@ -117,6 +126,7 @@ import sys; from head_note import prefix
 p,H=sys.argv[1:3]; s=open(p).read()
 s=prefix(s,"`%s` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.\n\n"%H); open(p,'w').write(s)
 E
+  upd_figures "at the unmoved head"  # mut:updfig2

   cat $WT.log
   [ "$rc" = 0 ] || pr_refuse "body-only: body_patch.sh refused #$N at $H (exit $rc); its log is $WT.log"
@@ -131,6 +141,7 @@ if MM: pre="`%s` "%H + ((N+" and then ") if N else "") + "merges origin/main `%s
 else: pre="`%s` "%H + " and then ".join(x for x in (N, R) if x) + ".\n\n"  # main merged cleanly: not merged (R4)
 s=prefix(s,pre); open(p,'w').write(s)
 E
+upd_figures "at the head to push"  # mut:updfig1
 if test -f tools/audit/app_push.sh; then _push=tools/audit/app_push.sh; else _push=tools/pr/app_push.sh; fi
 RO=""; [ "$(git rev-parse "$H^@")" != "$LIVE" ] || RO=--row-only  # mut:rowonly
 [ -n "$RO" ] || RO=--reuse  # mut:updreuse

+// The offline half of the figure-block contract (tools/pr/figure_block.py is the
+// grammar's owner and `verify` the rendering half; this runs no instrument).
+// Same line scan as figure_block.parse: an open marker that does not parse, a
+// block never closed or opened inside another, a block outside `## Figures`, a
+// block rendered at another head or never rendered, a name the base's registry
+// does not hold.
+const FIGURE_OPEN = /^<!-- figure-block: ([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)((?: [a-z]+=[0-9a-f]{40})*) -->$/
+const FIGURE_CLOSE = '<!-- /figure-block -->'
+function figureBlockProblems(body, { base = '', head = '' } = {}) {
+  const msgs = []
+  const lines = body.split('\n')
+  const inFigures = new Set((sections(body).get('Figures') ?? '').split('\n'))
+  const headOk = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(head) && !/^0{40}$/.test(head)
+  let registry
+  if (base) {
+    try {
+      registry = Object.keys(JSON.parse(execFileSync('git', ['show', `${base}:tools/pr/figure_registry.json`], { cwd: ROOT, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'] })).instruments ?? {})
+    } catch { registry = undefined }
+  }
+  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
+    const m = FIGURE_OPEN.exec(lines[i])
+    if (!m) {
+      if (lines[i].startsWith('<!-- figure-block')) msgs.push(`line ${i + 1}: a figure-block marker that does not parse: ${JSON.stringify(lines[i].slice(0, 80))}`)
+      continue
+    }
+    let j = i + 1
+    while (j < lines.length && lines[j] !== FIGURE_CLOSE && !lines[j].startsWith('<!-- figure-block')) j++
+    if (j >= lines.length) { msgs.push(`line ${i + 1}: figure-block ${m[1]} is never closed`); break }
+    if (lines[j] !== FIGURE_CLOSE) { msgs.push(`line ${j + 1}: a figure-block opens inside another`); i = j - 1; continue }
+    if (!inFigures.has(lines[i]) || !inFigures.has(lines[j])) msgs.push(`line ${i + 1}: figure-block ${m[1]} lies outside \`## Figures\``)
+    const headAttr = /(?:^| )head=([0-9a-f]{40})/.exec(m[2])?.[1]
+    if (headOk && headAttr === undefined) msgs.push(`line ${i + 1}: figure-block ${m[1]} is unrendered: run figure_block.py refresh`)
+    else if (headOk && headAttr !== head) msgs.push(`line ${i + 1}: figure-block ${m[1]} names another head (${headAttr.slice(0, 12)}, this is ${head.slice(0, 12)}): run figure_block.py refresh`)
+    if (registry && !registry.includes(m[1])) msgs.push(`line ${i + 1}: figure-block ${m[1]} is not registered at base`)
+    i = j
+  }
+  return msgs
+}

+
+            def got():
