diff --git a/tools/pr/figure_block.py b/tools/pr/figure_block.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..4b0c392c5d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/pr/figure_block.py
@@ -0,0 +1,304 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Generated figure blocks for a pull-request body (owner's card 7, option B).
+
+A body's `## Figures` may carry a block whose text is *rendered*, not typed:
+
+    <!-- figure-block: scope-line mb=<40 hex> head=<40 hex> -->
+    ~~~text
+    <what the registered instrument printed>
+    ~~~
+    <!-- /figure-block -->
+
+``figure_registry.json`` names the instruments a block may come from. It is read
+from the BASE tree (``--base``), as ``.claude/workflows/*`` already is, so a pull
+request can neither add an instrument nor choose a command and use it in the
+same pull request: **the author chooses no command**, only a registered name.
+Each registered instrument runs in a throwaway worktree of the head, with the
+registry's ``files`` overlaid from the base, so the program is the base's and the
+tree it measures is the head's.
+
+    figure_block.py render NAME   [--base REF] [--head REF]   print one block
+    figure_block.py refresh BODY  [--base REF] [--head REF]   re-render every block in place
+    figure_block.py verify  BODY  [--base REF] [--head REF]   refuse a block that is not what the
+                                                               registry renders (read-only)
+    figure_block.py --self-test
+
+``refresh`` is the seat-side writer (``body_push.sh``, ``prepr.sh``): a body
+carries an empty marker and the writer fills it at the head with no agent turn.
+``verify`` (``pr-contract``) renders and compares; it writes nothing. Only a
+*registered* figure is structurally non-stale: a free-form figure under
+``## Figures`` stays as it was, well-formed and resolvable, never executed.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import re
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+REGISTRY = "tools/pr/figure_registry.json"
+OPEN_RE = re.compile(r"^<!-- figure-block: (?P<name>[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)(?P<attrs>(?: [a-z]+=[0-9a-f]{40})*) -->$")
+CLOSE = "<!-- /figure-block -->"
+FENCE = "~~~text"
+FENCE_END = "~~~"
+PLACEHOLDERS = ("mb", "head", "base", "workdir")
+
+
+class Refused(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def _git(root: str, *args: str) -> str:
+    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
+    if p.returncode:
+        raise Refused(f"git {' '.join(args)}: {p.stderr.strip() or 'failed'}")
+    return p.stdout.strip()
+
+
+def load_registry(root: str, base: str) -> dict:
+    """The registry as the BASE tree holds it; a base without one registers nothing."""
+    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "show", f"{base}:{REGISTRY}"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
+    if p.returncode:
+        return {}
+    data = json.loads(p.stdout)
+    return data.get("instruments", {})
+
+
+def parse(text: str):
+    """Yield (start, end, name, attrs, body) per block; line indexes are [start, end]."""
+    lines = text.split("\n")
+    out, i = [], 0
+    while i < len(lines):
+        m = OPEN_RE.match(lines[i])
+        if not m:
+            if lines[i].startswith("<!-- figure-block"):
+                raise Refused(f"line {i + 1}: a figure-block marker that does not parse: {lines[i][:80]!r}")
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        j = i + 1
+        while j < len(lines) and lines[j] != CLOSE:
+            if lines[j].startswith("<!-- figure-block"):
+                raise Refused(f"line {j + 1}: a figure-block opens inside another")
+            j += 1
+        if j >= len(lines):
+            raise Refused(f"line {i + 1}: figure-block {m['name']} is never closed")
+        attrs = dict(a.split("=") for a in m["attrs"].split())
+        out.append((i, j, m["name"], attrs, lines[i + 1:j]))
+        i = j + 1
+    return lines, out
+
+
+def render_text(name: str, attrs: dict, output: str) -> list[str]:
+    a = "".join(f" {k}={attrs[k]}" for k in ("mb", "head") if k in attrs)
+    return [f"<!-- figure-block: {name}{a} -->", FENCE, *output.rstrip("\n").split("\n"), FENCE_END, CLOSE]
+
+
+def run_instrument(root: str, base: str, head: str, mb: str, name: str, reg: dict) -> str:
+    """Run one registered instrument over the head's tree with the base's program."""
+    if name not in reg:
+        raise Refused(f"`{name}` is not in the registry at {base[:12]}:{REGISTRY} "
+                      f"({', '.join(sorted(reg)) or 'it registers nothing'}); a pull request cannot add an instrument and use it")
+    ent = reg[name]
+    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="figblock-")
+    wt = os.path.join(tmp, "wt")
+    workdir = os.path.join(tmp, "work")
+    os.mkdir(workdir)
+    try:
+        _git(root, "worktree", "add", "--detach", "-q", wt, head)
+        for f in ent.get("files", []):
+            _git(wt, "checkout", base, "--", f)  # the base's program, not the head's
+        sub = dict(mb=mb, head=head, base=base, workdir=workdir)
+        argv = [a.format(**sub) for a in ent["argv"]]
+        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k in ("PATH", "HOME", "LANG", "TMPDIR", "VIRTUAL_ENV")}
+        env["PYTHONPATH"] = "tests/hastub"
+        p = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=wt, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=ent.get("timeout_s", 300), check=False)
+        if p.returncode not in ent.get("ok_rc", [0]):
+            raise Refused(f"`{name}` exited {p.returncode}: {(p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-300:]}")
+        lines = p.stdout.rstrip("\n").split("\n")
+        if "grep" in ent:
+            lines = [ln for ln in lines if re.search(ent["grep"], ln)]
+        if "tail" in ent:
+            lines = lines[-int(ent["tail"]):]
+        if not lines or lines == [""]:
+            raise Refused(f"`{name}` printed nothing after its filter")
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+    finally:
+        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "worktree", "remove", "--force", wt], capture_output=True, check=False)
+        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
+
+
+def context(root: str, base: str, head: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    head_sha = _git(root, "rev-parse", "--verify", head + "^{commit}")
+    return head_sha, _git(root, "merge-base", base, head_sha)
+
+
+def cmd_render(root, base, head, name):
+    head_sha, mb = context(root, base, head)
+    out = run_instrument(root, base, head_sha, mb, name, load_registry(root, base))
+    print("\n".join(render_text(name, {"mb": mb, "head": head_sha}, out)))
+
+
+def cmd_refresh(root, base, head, body_path):
+    text = open(body_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
+    lines, blocks = parse(text)
+    if not blocks:
+        return 0
+    head_sha, mb = context(root, base, head)
+    reg = load_registry(root, base)
+    for i, j, name, _attrs, _b in reversed(blocks):
+        out = run_instrument(root, base, head_sha, mb, name, reg)
+        lines[i:j + 1] = render_text(name, {"mb": mb, "head": head_sha}, out)
+    open(body_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(lines))
+    print(f"figure_block: refreshed {len(blocks)} block(s) at {head_sha[:12]}")
+    return 0
+
+
+def verify_text(text: str, root: str, base: str, head: str) -> list[str]:
+    """Problems with the blocks in ``text``; none when every block is what the registry renders."""
+    _lines, blocks = parse(text)
+    if not blocks:
+        return []
+    head_sha, mb = context(root, base, head)
+    reg = load_registry(root, base)
+    problems = []
+    for i, _j, name, attrs, body in blocks:
+        if attrs.get("head") != head_sha or attrs.get("mb") != mb:
+            problems.append(f"line {i + 1}: block `{name}` names head={attrs.get('head', '-')[:12]} mb={attrs.get('mb', '-')[:12]}, "
+                            f"this run is head={head_sha[:12]} mb={mb[:12]}; re-render with `figure_block.py refresh <body>`")
+            continue
+        try:
+            want = render_text(name, attrs, run_instrument(root, base, head_sha, mb, name, reg))[1:-1]
+        except Refused as e:
+            problems.append(f"line {i + 1}: block `{name}`: {e}")
+            continue
+        if body != want:
+            problems.append(f"line {i + 1}: block `{name}` is not what the registered instrument printed at {head_sha[:12]}; "
+                            "a figure block is rendered, never typed -- run `figure_block.py refresh <body>`")
+    return problems
+
+
+def cmd_verify(root, base, head, body_path):
+    problems = verify_text(open(body_path, encoding="utf-8").read(), root, base, head)
+    for p in problems:
+        print(f"  ERROR   [figure-block] {p}")
+    n = len(parse(open(body_path, encoding="utf-8").read())[1])
+    print(f"figure_block verify: {n} block(s), {len(problems)} refused")
+    return 1 if problems else 0
+
+
+def _scope(root: str, mb: str, workdir: str) -> int:
+    """The registered `scope-line` instrument: the gate's MODE line for the diff since ``mb``."""
+    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "tests/closure.py", "select", "--diff", mb, "--workdir", workdir],
+                       cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
+    scope = os.path.join(workdir, "scope.txt")
+    if p.returncode or not os.path.exists(scope):
+        print(p.stderr[-300:], file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    mode = [ln for ln in open(scope, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n") if ln.strip().startswith("MODE:")]
+    print(mode[0].strip() if mode else "no MODE line")
+    return 0 if mode else 1
+
+
+def _self_test() -> int:
+    results = []
+
+    def check(name, ok):
+        results.append(bool(ok))
+        print(("  ok  " if ok else "  FAIL") + " " + name)
+
+    def refused(fn):
+        try:
+            fn()
+        except Refused:
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="figblock-st-")
+    try:
+        sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "..", "tests"))
+        from throwaway_git import throwaway_git_init
+        env = throwaway_git_init(tmp, "-q", "-b", "main")
+
+        def g(*a, cwd=tmp):
+            subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=cwd, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True)
+        os.makedirs(os.path.join(tmp, "tools/pr"))
+        reg = {"instruments": {"mb": {"argv": ["git", "merge-base", "{base}", "{head}"], "files": []},
+                               "bad": {"argv": ["false"], "files": []}}}
+        open(os.path.join(tmp, REGISTRY), "w").write(json.dumps(reg))
+        open(os.path.join(tmp, "f"), "w").write("1")
+        g("add", "-A"); g("commit", "-qm", "base")
+        g("checkout", "-qb", "topic")
+        open(os.path.join(tmp, "f"), "w").write("2")
+        # a head that adds an instrument the base lacks
+        reg["instruments"]["evil"] = {"argv": ["echo", "pwned"], "files": []}
+        open(os.path.join(tmp, REGISTRY), "w").write(json.dumps(reg))
+        g("commit", "-qam", "head")
+        head = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
+        mbsha = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "main"], cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
+        body = os.path.join(tmp, "body.md")
+        empty = f"## Figures\n<!-- figure-block: mb -->\n<!-- /figure-block -->\nfree-form: `git log`\n"
+        open(body, "w").write(empty)
+        check("refresh fills an empty marker at the head with no agent turn", cmd_refresh(tmp, "main", "HEAD", body) == 0
+              and mbsha in open(body).read() and head in open(body).read())
+        check("verify accepts the refreshed body and the free-form line beside it", verify_text(open(body).read(), tmp, "main", "HEAD") == []
+              and "free-form: `git log`" in open(body).read())
+        typed = open(body).read().replace(mbsha + "\n~~~", "0" * 40 + "\n~~~", 1)
+        check("a hand-typed value in a block is refused", len(verify_text(typed, tmp, "main", "HEAD")) == 1)
+        moved = open(body).read().replace(head, "1" * 40)
+        check("a block naming another head is refused as stale", len(verify_text(moved, tmp, "main", "HEAD")) == 1)
+        g("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "head2")
+        check("a moved head is stale until the writer re-renders it", len(verify_text(open(body).read(), tmp, "main", "HEAD")) == 1
+              and cmd_refresh(tmp, "main", "HEAD", body) == 0 and verify_text(open(body).read(), tmp, "main", "HEAD") == [])
+        evil = "<!-- figure-block: evil -->\n<!-- /figure-block -->\n"
+        check("an instrument registered only by the head is refused (null: the base's own mb passes above)",
+              refused(lambda: cmd_refresh(tmp, "main", "HEAD", _w(body, evil))))
+        check("an unknown name is refused", refused(lambda: cmd_refresh(tmp, "main", "HEAD", _w(body, "<!-- figure-block: nope -->\n<!-- /figure-block -->\n"))))
+        check("an instrument that exits non-zero is refused", refused(lambda: cmd_refresh(tmp, "main", "HEAD", _w(body, "<!-- figure-block: bad -->\n<!-- /figure-block -->\n"))))
+        check("an unclosed block is refused", refused(lambda: parse("<!-- figure-block: mb -->\nx\n")))
+        check("a malformed marker is refused", refused(lambda: parse("<!-- figure-block: Mb -->\n")))
+        check("a body with no block is untouched (null control)", verify_text("## Figures\nnone\n", tmp, "main", "HEAD") == [])
+    finally:
+        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
+    failed = results.count(False)
+    print(f"figure_block self-test: {len(results)} checks, {failed} failed")
+    return 1 if failed else 0
+
+
+def _w(path: str, text: str) -> str:
+    open(path, "w").write(text)
+    return path
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    if argv[:1] == ["--self-test"]:
+        return _self_test()
+    if argv[:1] == ["_scope"]:
+        return _scope(os.getcwd(), argv[1], argv[2])
+    opts = {"--base": "origin/main", "--head": "HEAD"}
+    pos = []
+    it = iter(argv)
+    for a in it:
+        if a in opts:
+            opts[a] = next(it, "")
+        else:
+            pos.append(a)
+    if len(pos) != 2 or pos[0] not in ("render", "refresh", "verify"):
+        print(__doc__)
+        return 2
+    root = _git(os.getcwd(), "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
+    try:
+        if pos[0] == "render":
+            cmd_render(root, opts["--base"], opts["--head"], pos[1])
+            return 0
+        fn = cmd_refresh if pos[0] == "refresh" else cmd_verify
+        return fn(root, opts["--base"], opts["--head"], pos[1])
+    except Refused as e:
+        print(f"  ERROR   [figure-block] {e}")
+        return 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

Grow by separate pull requests.",

+}
diff --git a/tools/pr/prepr.sh b/tools/pr/prepr.sh
index 07d5cb91fa..e0ffdff44d 100755
--- a/tools/pr/prepr.sh
+++ b/tools/pr/prepr.sh
@@ -257,6 +257,13 @@ pinned_touched() { # file of changed paths, pins (one per line)
   return 1
 }
 
+# Step 7a2's whole body, and --body-check's: a rendered figure block is re-rendered
+# from the base's registry at HEAD and compared (read-only, offline; pr-contract
+# runs the same verify). A body with no block passes untouched.
+figure_block_check() { # body file
+  python3 -I tools/pr/figure_block.py verify "$1" --base origin/main --head HEAD
+}
+
 # Step 7a's whole body, so `--self-test` drives the code the step runs rather
 # than a second copy of the command. A step wired into the run and demonstrated
 # by a sibling command is a step nothing pins: the assertion passes while the
@@ -1159,6 +1166,34 @@ moved_line() { # tree root, merge base -> one line; rc 0 clean, 1 refused, 3 ski
   return 1
 }
 
+# THE DIFF'S ADDED LINES MUTATED (R10-MUTANT-RUN-DRIVER, card 4; fixer.md step 2
+# makes running it the fixer's). `mutant_run.py --diff` applies its five
+# operators to each added Python line outside tests/ and dev/, the first
+# MUTANT_MAX (40) in file order, and runs MUTANT_CMD once per mutant. A run that
+# measured nothing -- the command failing on the unedited tree, a killed NULL, a
+# refusal -- is rc 1, never the "no survivor" an empty SURVIVED list would read
+# as: R10-FIXER-MD-SPELLING-CORPUS-P2 measured three of five fixer self-tests
+# failing in the git-archive copy, which `MUTANT_IN_PLACE=1` (`--in-place`) runs.
+mutants_line() { # tree root, base, command -> one line; rc 0 no survivor, 2 survivors (report only), 1 nothing measured, 3 skipped
+  [ -n "$3" ] || { echo "MUTANT_CMD unset -- set it to the group's self-test or features_block.py call (fixer.md step 2)"; return 3; }
+  [ -f "$1/tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py" ] || { echo "tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py is not in this tree"; return 3; }
+  local out r n
+  out=$(cd "$1" && python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff "$2...HEAD" --cmd "$3" \
+    --max-mutants "${MUTANT_MAX:-40}" --report-only ${MUTANT_IN_PLACE:+--in-place} 2>&1); r=$?
+  if [ "$r" -ne 0 ]; then
+    echo "mutant_run rc=$r measured nothing: $(grep -v '^SURVIVED ' <<<"$out" | grep . | tail -1 | cut -c1-160) -- fix MUTANT_CMD, or set MUTANT_IN_PLACE=1 for a self-test that needs a git checkout"
+    return 1
+  fi
+  n=$(grep -c '^SURVIVED ' <<<"$out")
+  if [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; then
+    grep '^SURVIVED ' <<<"$out"
+    echo "$n survivor(s) on the diff's added lines -- each owes a killing check or a line under ## Unpinned sites (fixer.md step 2)"
+    return 2
+  fi
+  echo "no survivor among the diff's first ${MUTANT_MAX:-40} mutant(s) under: $3" | cut -c1-200
+  return 0
+}
+
 # --- closure-reachability skips for the heavy steps ---------------------------
 # WHY THIS EXISTS. A pull request whose diff is one delivery row, or one file
 # under tools/ or docs/, paid for prepr's heavy battery -- the mutants drive,
@@ -1788,6 +1823,9 @@ if [ "${1:-}" = "--body-check" ]; then
   fout=$(figures_check "$2" 2>&1); fr=$?
   if [ "$fr" -eq 0 ]; then echo "figures ok: $(tail -1 <<<"$fout")"; else echo "REFUSE figures: $(tail -1 <<<"$fout")"; fi
   [ "$r" -ne 0 ] || r=$fr
+  gout=$(figure_block_check "$2" 2>&1); gr=$?

+    takes over a hold past its own age bound. `armed` False (no --push, a dry

@@ -0,0 +1,257 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env node
+// The product page's illustrative day (R10-PRODUCT-PAGE-REDESIGN).
+//
+// docs/index.html carries the chart as committed inline SVG, so it draws with
+// no script and tests/doc_claims.py reads what a visitor sees. This file owns
+// that markup: each layer sits between `<!-- chart:NAME -->` and
+// `<!-- /chart:NAME -->`, and is never edited by hand.
+//
+//   node tools/site/day_chart.mjs --write      rewrite every marker pair in the page
+//   node tools/site/day_chart.mjs --check      exit 1, naming the layer, where the page differs
+//   node tools/site/day_chart.mjs --self-test  assert the toy planner's invariants
+//   --page FILE                                a page other than docs/index.html
+//
+// --self-test and --check may be given together (tests/doc_claims.py does).
+import fs from "node:fs";
+import path from "node:path";
+import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
+
+/* The illustrative day and the toy planner behind every chart on this page.
+   Not the integration's solver: a 24-step dynamic programme over a house that
+   gains three units of stored heat in a heating hour and loses one in an idle
+   hour, with one hot-water run owed before each of two demand windows and one
+   compressor shared between the two. Prices are unitless. */
+const HPO = (() => {
+  const PRESETS = {
+    peaks: [3.0, 2.6, 2.3, 2.1, 2.0, 2.5, 4.2, 6.6, 8.6, 8.0, 6.9, 5.9, 5.4, 5.1, 5.6, 6.7, 8.8, 9.6, 9.1, 7.6, 6.2, 5.0, 4.4, 3.8],
+  };
+  const CAP = 9, START = 3, GAIN = 3;
+  const WINDOWS = [[6, 9], [18, 21]];          // hot-water demand windows, [from, to)
+  const DHW_SPANS = [[2, 6], [14, 18]];        // hours a run may sit in, inclusive
+
+  function baseline(p) {
+    const space = Array(24).fill(false), dhw = Array(24).fill(false), temp = [START];
+    let t = START;
+    for (let h = 0; h < 24; h++) {
+      if (h === 6 || h === 18) { dhw[h] = true; t -= 1; }
+      else if (t <= 1) { space[h] = true; t += GAIN; }
+      else t -= 1;
+      temp.push(t);
+    }
+    return finish(p, space, dhw, temp);
+  }
+
+  function finish(p, space, dhw, temp) {
+    let cost = 0, n = 0, cheap = 0;
+    const mean = p.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / 24;
+    for (let h = 0; h < 24; h++) if (space[h] || dhw[h]) { cost += p[h]; n++; if (p[h] < mean - 1e-9) cheap++; }
+    return { space, dhw, temp, cost, hours: n, cheap, mean };
+  }
+
+  function dp(p, dhwHours, endMin) {
+    const INF = 1e9;
+    let cur = Array(CAP + 1).fill(INF); cur[START] = 0;
+    const back = [];
+    for (let h = 0; h < 24; h++) {
+      const nxt = Array(CAP + 1).fill(INF), from = Array(CAP + 1).fill(null);
+      for (let t = 0; t <= CAP; t++) {
+        if (cur[t] >= INF) continue;
+        if (dhwHours.includes(h)) {
+          if (t - 1 >= 0 && cur[t] + p[h] < nxt[t - 1]) { nxt[t - 1] = cur[t] + p[h]; from[t - 1] = [t, false]; }
+          continue;
+        }
+        if (t - 1 >= 0 && cur[t] < nxt[t - 1] - 1e-9) { nxt[t - 1] = cur[t]; from[t - 1] = [t, false]; }
+        if (t + GAIN <= CAP && cur[t] + p[h] < nxt[t + GAIN] - 1e-9) { nxt[t + GAIN] = cur[t] + p[h]; from[t + GAIN] = [t, true]; }
+      }
+      back.push(from); cur = nxt;
+    }
+    let best = -1;
+    for (let t = endMin; t <= CAP; t++) if (cur[t] < INF && (best < 0 || cur[t] < cur[best] - 1e-9)) best = t;
+    if (best < 0) return null;
+    const space = Array(24).fill(false), temp = Array(25).fill(0);
+    let t = best; temp[24] = t;
+    for (let h = 23; h >= 0; h--) { const [pt, on] = back[h][t]; space[h] = on; t = pt; temp[h] = t; }
+    return { cost: cur[best], space, temp };
+  }
+
+  function solve(p) {
+    const base = baseline(p);
+    const endMin = base.temp[24];
+    let best = null;
+    for (let a = DHW_SPANS[0][0]; a <= DHW_SPANS[0][1]; a++)
+      for (let b = DHW_SPANS[1][0]; b <= DHW_SPANS[1][1]; b++) {
+        const r = dp(p, [a, b], endMin);
+        if (r && (!best || r.cost < best.r.cost - 1e-9)) best = { r, a, b };
+      }
+    const dhw = Array(24).fill(false); dhw[best.a] = dhw[best.b] = true;
+    return { plan: finish(p, best.r.space, dhw, best.r.temp), base };
+  }
+
+  /* Geometry: a 720 x 380 drawing, no text in it. */
+  const G = { W: 720, H: 380, L: 10, cw: 700 / 24, pTop: 22, pBase: 214, tFloor: 356, tStep: 9 };
+  const x = h => +(G.L + h * G.cw).toFixed(2);
+  const py = v => +(G.pBase - 62 - v * 13).toFixed(2);
+  const ty = t => +(G.tFloor - 6 - t * G.tStep).toFixed(2);
+
+  function grid() {
+    let s = "";
+    for (let h = 0; h <= 24; h++) s += `<line class="g${h % 6 ? "" : " g6"}" x1="${x(h)}" x2="${x(h)}" y1="${G.pTop}" y2="${G.pBase}"/>`;
+    s += `<line class="g g6" x1="${x(0)}" x2="${x(24)}" y1="${G.pBase}" y2="${G.pBase}"/>`;
+    return s;
+  }
+  function windows() {
+    return WINDOWS.map(([a, b]) => `<rect class="c-win" x="${x(a)}" y="${G.pTop}" width="${+(x(b) - x(a)).toFixed(2)}" height="${G.pBase - G.pTop}"/>`).join("");
+  }
+  function price(p) {
+    let d = `M${x(0)} ${py(p[0])}`;
+    for (let h = 0; h < 24; h++) d += ` V${py(p[h])} H${x(h + 1)}`;
+    return `<path class="c-price-fill" d="${d} V${G.pBase} H${x(0)} Z"/><path class="c-price" d="${d}"/>`;
+  }
+  function bars(s, cls) {
+    let out = "", i = 0;
+    for (let h = 0; h < 24; h++) {
+      if (!s.space[h] && !s.dhw[h]) continue;
+      const hh = s.space[h] ? 50 : 32;
+      out += `<rect class="bar ${s.space[h] ? "c-heat" : "c-dhw"}${cls ? " " + cls : ""}" style="--i:${i++}" x="${+(x(h) + 4).toFixed(2)}" y="${G.pBase - 4 - hh}" width="${+(G.cw - 8).toFixed(2)}" height="${hh}" rx="4"/>`;
+    }
+    return out;
+  }
+  function comfort(s) {
+    const pts = s.temp.map((t, h) => `${x(h)} ${ty(t)}`).join(" L");
+    return `<path class="c-house" d="M${pts}"/>`;
+  }
+  function floor() {
+    return `<line class="c-floor" x1="${x(0)}" x2="${x(24)}" y1="${G.tFloor}" y2="${G.tFloor}"/>`;
+  }
+  function outdoor() {
+    let d = "";
+    for (let h = 0; h <= 24; h++) { const v = 250 + 9 * Math.cos((h - 15) / 24 * 2 * Math.PI) * -1 + 9; d += (h ? " L" : "M") + x(h) + " " + v.toFixed(1); }
+    return `<path class="c-out" d="${d}"/>`;
+  }
+  /* What the house then did: the prediction, a little off, as the learners see it. */
+  function measured(s) {
+    let out = "";
+    const off = [0, 2, 3, 1, -2, -3, -1, 2, 3, 2, 0, -2, -3, -2, 1, 2, 3, 1, -1, -2, -3, -1, 1, 2, 1];
+    for (let h = 1; h <= 24; h++) out += `<circle class="c-meas" style="--i:${h}" cx="${x(h)}" cy="${(ty(s.temp[h]) + off[h]).toFixed(1)}" r="3.2"/>`;
+    return out;
+  }
+  function layers(p, s) {
+    return { grid: grid(), windows: windows(), price: price(p), bars: bars(s), comfort: comfort(s), floor: floor(), outdoor: outdoor(), measured: measured(s) };
+  }
+  return { PRESETS, WINDOWS, G, solve, layers };
+})();
+if (typeof module !== "undefined") module.exports = HPO;
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// The page writer. The drawn day is the first preset.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+const ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "..");
+const PAGE = path.join(ROOT, "docs", "index.html");
+// How many marker pairs the page owes per layer: the story draws all eight, and
+// the hero strip repeats the price and the bars. A page with fewer cannot pass
+// the check by carrying nothing to compare.
+const PAIRS = { grid: 1, windows: 1, price: 2, outdoor: 1, bars: 2, floor: 1, comfort: 1, measured: 1 };
+const MARKER = /<!-- chart:([a-z]+) -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- \/chart:\1 -->/g;
+
+function drawn(prices = Object.values(HPO.PRESETS)[0]) {
+  return HPO.layers(prices, HPO.solve(prices).plan);
+}
+
+/** { text, problems }: the page with every pair rewritten, and what was wrong with the page as given. */
+function render(src, want = drawn()) {
+  const seen = {}, problems = [];
+  const text = src.replace(MARKER, (whole, name, body) => {
+    seen[name] = (seen[name] || 0) + 1;
+    if (!(name in want)) { problems.push(`${name}: not a layer the generator draws`); return whole; }
+    if (body !== want[name]) problems.push(`${name}: the page's markup is not the generator's`);
+    return `<!-- chart:${name} -->${want[name]}<!-- /chart:${name} -->`;
+  });
+  for (const [name, n] of Object.entries(PAIRS)) {
+    if ((seen[name] || 0) !== n) problems.push(`${name}: ${seen[name] || 0} marker pair(s) in the page, ${n} owed`);
+  }
+  return { text, problems };
+}
+
+function selfTest() {
+  const fails = [];
+  const ok = (cond, what) => { if (!cond) fails.push(what); };
+  const eq = (a, b) => JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b);
+  const hours = flags => flags.flatMap((on, h) => (on ? [h] : []));
+  const p = Object.values(HPO.PRESETS)[0];
+  const { plan, base } = HPO.solve(p);
+
+  ok(plan.temp.length === 25 && plan.temp.every(t => t >= 0), "stored heat is never below zero");
+  const spans = [[2, 6], [14, 18]];
+  HPO.WINDOWS.forEach(([opens], k) => {
+    const runs = hours(plan.dhw).filter(h => h >= spans[k][0] && h <= spans[k][1]);
+    ok(runs.length === 1, `exactly one hot-water run in span ${k}`);
+    ok(runs.length === 1 && runs[0] + 1 <= opens, `the hot-water run of span ${k} ends before its demand window opens`);
+  });
+  ok(hours(plan.dhw).length === 2, "two hot-water runs in the day");
+  ok(!plan.space.some((on, h) => on && plan.dhw[h]), "one compressor: no hour heats both");
+  ok(plan.cost <= base.cost + 1e-9, "the plan costs no more than the unoptimized schedule on the drawn day");
+  const flat = HPO.solve(Array(24).fill(5));
+  ok(Math.abs(flat.plan.cost - flat.base.cost) < 1e-9, "a flat price gives equal cost for both");
+  // The drawn day, as the design note states it for the reviewer.
+  ok(eq(hours(plan.space), [3, 4, 5, 12, 13, 23]), "space heating sits in the hours the design note names");
+  ok(eq(hours(plan.dhw), [2, 14]), "hot water sits in the hours the design note names");
+  ok(eq(plan.temp, [3, 2, 1, 0, 3, 6, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 6, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, 3]), "stored heat by hour is the design note's");
+
+  const a = drawn(), b = drawn();
+  ok(eq(a, b), "two runs give byte-identical output");
+  ok(eq(Object.keys(a).sort(), Object.keys(PAIRS).sort()), "the layers drawn are the layers the page owes");
+  const all = Object.values(a).join("");
+  ok(!/<text|<tspan|<title|<desc/.test(all) && !/>[^<]+</.test(all), "no text in the drawing: nothing can be read off it");
+  ok(!/<line[^>]*[^/]>/.test(all), "every line element is self-closed (the page parser closes nothing else)");
+
+  // The check's own controls: a clean page passes, and each way of being wrong is named.
+  const page = `<svg>${Object.entries(PAIRS).map(([n, k]) => `<!-- chart:${n} --><!-- /chart:${n} -->`.repeat(k)).join("")}</svg>`;
+  const written = render(page).text;
+  ok(written !== page && render(written).problems.length === 0, "a written page passes the check");
+  ok(render(written).text === written, "writing a written page changes nothing");
+  const moved = p.slice(); moved[7] += 0.5;
+  const other = render(written, drawn(moved)).problems;
+  ok(other.some(m => m.startsWith("price:")), "one changed price is refused, naming the price layer");
+  ok(render(written.replace(/<!-- chart:grid -->[\s\S]*?<!-- \/chart:grid -->/, "")).problems.some(m => m.startsWith("grid: 0 marker")), "a missing marker pair is refused");
+  ok(render(written.replace('r="3.2"', 'r="3.3"')).problems.some(m => m.startsWith("measured:")), "a hand edit inside a pair is refused");
+  return fails;
+}
+
+function main(argv) {
+  const flags = new Set(argv.filter(a => a.startsWith("--") && a !== "--page"));
+  const at = argv.indexOf("--page");
+  const page = at >= 0 ? path.resolve(argv[at + 1] || "") : PAGE;
+  const known = ["--write", "--check", "--self-test"];
+  if (!flags.size || [...flags].some(f => !known.includes(f)) || (flags.has("--write") && flags.has("--check"))) {
+    console.error("usage: day_chart.mjs (--write | --check) [--self-test] [--page FILE]  |  day_chart.mjs --self-test");
+    return 2;
+  }
+  let rc = 0;
+  if (flags.has("--self-test")) {
+    const fails = selfTest();
+    for (const f of fails) console.log(`FAIL self-test: ${f}`);
+    if (fails.length) rc = 1; else console.log("day_chart: self-test OK");
+  }
+  if (flags.has("--write") || flags.has("--check")) {
+    let src;
+    try { src = fs.readFileSync(page, "utf8"); } catch (e) {
+      if (e.code !== "ENOENT") throw e;
+      console.log(`FAIL ${page}: no such page`); return 1;
+    }
+    const { text, problems } = render(src);
+    if (flags.has("--write")) {
+      const structural = problems.filter(m => !m.endsWith("is not the generator's"));
+      for (const m of structural) console.log(`FAIL ${m}`);
+      if (structural.length) return 1;
+      if (text !== src) fs.writeFileSync(page, text);
+      console.log(`day_chart: ${text !== src ? "wrote" : "unchanged"} ${path.relative(ROOT, page)}`);
+    } else {
+      for (const m of problems) console.log(`FAIL ${m}`);
+      if (problems.length) rc = 1; else console.log(`day_chart: ${path.relative(ROOT, page)} carries the generator's chart`);
+    }
+  }
+  return rc;
+}
+
+process.exitCode = main(process.argv.slice(2));

## Before you return the verdict (P275)
Run `python3 -I tools/audit/carry_audit.py check --body <PR body file> --comments <file holding [{"id": 0, "body": <verdict.md text>}]>`. Give every reported item its own `Carry: <GROUP> | #<issue> | O<n> | dismissed: <reason>`;
an evidence line flagged by its wording takes `Carry: dismissed: evidence, not a finding`. Return the verdict only at rc 0.
